I too am a mortal human being, like everyone else, descended from that earthly one who was made first, and in my mother’s womb I was formed as flesh.

For ten months I was solidified in human blood, through the pleasure of sleep and the accompanying union.

I too, once born, received the common air, fell upon the earth made in the same way, and uttered my first voice, crying like everyone else.

I was raised in swaddling clothes and amid great cares.

For no king has had any other beginning of birth.

There is therefore one entrance into life for all, and the departure is similar.

For this reason I prayed, and understanding was given to me; [Col. 0410D] I called, and the spirit of wisdom came into me.

I preferred her to kingdoms and thrones, and I considered riches as nothing in comparison with her.

I did not compare any precious stone with her, for all gold in comparison with her is a little sand, and silver in her sight will be reckoned as mud.

Beyond health and beauty I loved her, and I resolved to have her for my light, because her radiance cannot be extinguished.

All good things came to me together with her, and innumerable riches through her hands.

I rejoiced in all these things, because wisdom went before me, although I did not know that she was the mother of them all.

Without deceit I learned her, and without envy I share her; I do not hide her wealth.

For she is an unfailing treasure for human beings; those who use it become participants in God’s friendship, commended by the gifts of discipline.

But God gave me the ability to speak with understanding and to form worthy judgments about the things given to me, because he himself is the guide of wisdom and the corrector of the wise.

For in his hand are we and our words, and all wisdom, and knowledge and discipline concerning works.

For he gave me true knowledge of what exists, so that I might know the arrangement of the world and the powers of the elements;

the beginning, the end, and the middle of times; the changes of their cycles and the alterations of seasons;

the courses of years and the arrangements of the stars;

the natures of animals and the fury of beasts; the force of winds; the thoughts of human beings; the varieties of plants; and the powers of roots.

Whatever things are hidden and unforeseen, I learned, for wisdom, the maker of all things, taught me.

[Col. 0411B] For in her is a spirit intelligent, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, eloquent, mobile, undefiled, certain, gentle, loving what is good, acute, unhindered, beneficent,

humane, kind, steadfast, sure, secure, possessing every power, observing all things, and entering into all spirits; intelligent, pure, and subtle.

For wisdom is more mobile than anything that moves, and because of her purity she reaches everywhere.

For she is a vapor of the power of God and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty; therefore nothing defiled enters into her.

For she is the brightness of eternal light, the spotless mirror of God’s majesty, and the image of his goodness.

Though she is one, she can do all things; remaining in herself, she renews all things, and from generation to generation she passes into holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets.

For God loves no one except the one who dwells with wisdom.

For she is more beautiful than the sun and, compared with the arrangement of the stars, is found to be prior to light.

For night follows upon light, but wickedness does not overcome wisdom.

CHAPTER EIGHT.

Therefore she reaches from end to end with strength and orders all things gently.

I loved her and sought her from my youth; I desired to take her as my bride and became a lover of her beauty.

She glorifies her noble birth by having God as her companion; indeed, the Lord of all things also loved her [Al. omits “also”].

For she is the instructress of God’s discipline and the chooser of his works.

If riches are desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, which produces all things?

If understanding is at work, who among existing things is a greater craftsman than she?

And if anyone loves righteousness, her labors possess great virtues [Col. 0411D]; for she teaches sobriety and prudence, justice and [Note: [Col. 0411D] Other printed books read “truth,” but this is farther from the Greek *andreia* (ἀνδρεία), “courage” or “virtue.”] virtue, than which nothing is more useful for human beings in life.

If anyone desires an abundance of knowledge, she knows the things of the past and judges the future; she knows the intricacies of speech and the resolutions of arguments; she knows signs and marvels before they occur, and the outcomes of times and ages.

Therefore I resolved to take her to live with me, knowing that she would share my good things and be the companion of my thoughts and weariness.

Because of her I shall have glory among the crowds and honor among the elders, though young.

I shall be found keen in judgment, and shall be admired in the presence of the powerful, and the faces of princes shall marvel at me.

When I am silent, they will wait for me; when I speak, they will look toward me; and when I speak at length, [Col. 0412A] they will place their hands upon their mouths.

Moreover, through her I shall possess immortality, and shall leave an everlasting remembrance to those who are to come after me.

I shall govern peoples, and nations shall be subject to me.

Hearing of me, terrible kings will fear; among the multitude I shall appear good, and in war courageous.

When I enter my house, I shall rest with her; for her companionship has no bitterness, nor does her association bring weariness, but joy and gladness.

Considering these things within myself and recalling them in my heart—for immortality is found in kinship with wisdom,

and in her friendship there is good delight, in the works of her hands unfailing honor, in the contest of her speech wisdom, and in the exchange of her words distinction—I went about seeking to take her for myself.

[Col. 0412B] I was a child of keen understanding, and I received a good soul.

And when I was more virtuous, I entered an undefiled body.  
[Note: [Col. 0412D] Hentenius’s codices wrongly read “defiled.”]

And when I knew that I could not otherwise be self-controlled unless God granted it—and that this too was wisdom: to know whose gift it was—I approached the Lord and entreated him, and said with all my heart:

## CHAPTER IX

God of my fathers and Lord of mercy, who made all things by your word,

and by your wisdom appointed humankind to rule the creatures made by you,

to order the inhabited world in equity and justice, and to judge judgment with uprightness of heart:

Give me wisdom, the attendant at your thrones, and do not reject me from among your children.

For I am your servant and the son of your maidservant, a weak man, of short life, and inferior in understanding [Col. 0412C] of judgment and laws.

For even if someone among human beings is perfect, if your wisdom is absent from him, he will be counted as nothing.

You chose me as king over your people and as judge of your sons and daughters.

You commanded me to build a temple on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of your dwelling, like the tabernacle of your holy sanctuary, which you prepared from the beginning.

And with you was your wisdom, which knows your works, which was also present when you made the world and knew what was pleasing to your eyes and what was right according to your commandments.

Send her from your holy heavens, and from the throne of your majesty, so that she may be with me and labor with me, so that I may know what is acceptable to you.

For she knows and understands all things, and will guide me prudently in my works and guard me by her power.

Then my works will be acceptable, and I shall govern your people [Col. 0412D] justly, and shall be worthy of my father’s thrones.

For what human being can know the counsel of God? Or who can conceive what God wills?

For mortal thoughts are fearful, and our deliberations are uncertain.

For the corruptible body weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling presses down the mind that thinks of many things.

We scarcely estimate the things that are on earth, and we discover with labor the things that are before us. But who will investigate the things that are in heaven?

Who will know your mind, unless you give wisdom and send your holy spirit from on high?

And thus the paths of those who are on earth may be made straight, and people may learn what is pleasing to you?

[Col. 0413A] For from the beginning, Lord, all who were pleasing to you were saved through wisdom.

## CHAPTER X

She guarded the one who was first formed by God, the father of the world, when he alone had been created.

She brought him out of his transgression and gave him the power to master all things.

When the unrighteous man withdrew from her in his anger, he perished through the anger of fraternal murder.

Because of him, when water destroyed the earth, wisdom again saved it, steering the righteous man by means of contemptible wood.

When nations had joined together in a conspiracy of wickedness, she knew the righteous man and preserved him blameless before God, and kept him strong despite pity for his son.

She delivered the righteous man when the wicked were perishing, as he fled when fire descended upon the Five Cities.

Their deserted land remains smoking as a testimony to their wickedness, with trees bearing [Col. 0413B] fruit at uncertain seasons and a pillar of salt standing as a memorial of the unbelieving soul.

For those who passed wisdom by fell not only into the error of failing to know good things, but also left human beings a memorial of their folly, so that they could not remain hidden in the things in which they had sinned.

But wisdom delivered from sufferings those who kept watch over themselves.

She led the righteous man, a fugitive from his brother’s anger, along straight paths; she showed him the kingdom of God and gave him knowledge of holy things; she honored him in his labors and completed his labors.

In the deceit of those who surrounded him, she stood by him and made him honorable.

She guarded him from his enemies and protected him from deceivers; she gave him a strong contest so that he might conquer and know that wisdom is more powerful than all things.

She did not abandon the righteous man when he was sold, but delivered him from sinners; she descended with him into the pit.

[Col. 0413C] And in his chains she did not abandon him, until she brought him the scepter of the kingdom and power over those who oppressed him; she exposed as liars those who had stained him, and gave him everlasting glory.

She delivered the righteous people and the blameless offspring from the nations that oppressed them.

She entered the soul of the servant of God and stood against terrible kings with portents and signs.

She repaid the righteous for their labors, led them along a wondrous road, and was a shelter for them by day and a light of stars through the night.

She brought them across the Red Sea and carried them through the vast waters.

But she drowned their enemies in the sea and brought them up from the depth of the underworld.

Therefore the righteous took the spoils of the ungodly.

And they sang, Lord, your holy name, and together praised your victorious hand.

For wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues [Col. 0413D] of infants eloquent.

## CHAPTER XI

She directed their works by the hands of the holy prophet.

They traveled through deserts that were uninhabited and fixed their dwellings in deserted places.

They stood against their enemies and took vengeance on their foes.

They thirsted and called upon you, and water was given them from the highest rock, and relief from thirst from the hard stone.

For by the very things through which their enemies suffered punishment because of the failure of their drink, through those same things, when the children of Israel had abundance, they rejoiced:

through those same things, when the Israelites lacked them, they were treated well.

For instead of the fountain of an everlasting river, you gave the unjust human blood.

When they were diminished through the killing of infants, you unexpectedly gave them abundant water,

[Col. 0414A] showing through the thirst that then afflicted them how you exalted your own and destroyed their adversaries.

For when they were tested—and indeed received discipline with mercy—they learned how the ungodly, judged in anger, suffered torments.

You tested these as a father admonishing them, but condemned those as a stern king questioning them.

Whether absent or present, they were tortured alike.

For a twofold weariness had seized them, and groaning was joined to the memory of what had gone before.

For when they heard that things were going well for them through their own torments, they remembered the Lord and marveled at the outcome in the end.

For the one whom they had mocked when he was exposed and cast out, at the end of events they marveled at; yet they did not thirst in the same way as the righteous.

In return for the senseless thoughts of their wickedness—because some, having gone astray, worshiped mute serpents and worthless animals—you sent upon them a multitude of mute [Col. 0414B] animals as punishment:

so that they might know that by the things through which anyone sins, by those same things he is tormented.

For your almighty hand, which created the world from invisible matter, was not unable to send against them a multitude of bears or bold lions,

or unfamiliar beasts of a new kind, full of anger, or breathing fiery vapors, or emitting the smell of smoke, or sending terrifying sparks from their eyes.

Their assault could not merely destroy them, but even their appearance could kill them through fear.

Yet even without these, they could have been killed by one breath, suffering persecution from their own deeds and being scattered by the breath of your power; but you have ordered all things by measure, number, and weight.

For it was always within your power alone to exercise great strength, and who can resist the strength of your arm?

For before you the whole world is like a moment on a balance, and like a drop of morning dew descending upon the earth.

[Col. 0414C] But you have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of human beings for the sake of repentance.

For you love all things that exist, and hate nothing that you have made; for you neither established nor made anything while hating it.

How could anything endure unless you had willed it? Or how could what had not been called by you be preserved?

But you spare all things, because they are yours, Lord, lover of souls.

## CHAPTER XII

O how good and gentle, Lord, is your spirit in all things!

Therefore you correct those who go astray little by little, admonishing them in the things through which they sin, and addressing them so that, having abandoned wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord.

For you hated the ancient inhabitants of your holy land,

[Col. 0414D] because they performed hateful works against you through magical drugs and unjust sacrifices,

and were merciless murderers of their children, eaters of human entrails, and devourers of blood in the midst of your sacred rite.

They were parents who gave birth to helpless souls, and you wished to destroy them by the hands of our ancestors,

so that they might receive a fitting settlement from the children of God, the land more beloved by you than all others.

Yet even with these, as with human beings, you were sparing, and sent wasps as forerunners of your army, so that they might destroy them little by little.

Not because you were unable in battle to subject the ungodly to the righteous, or to destroy them all at once by savage beasts or by a harsh word,

but by judging them in stages, you gave them room for repentance, though you did not fail to know that their race was wicked, that their malice was natural, and that their way of thinking could not be changed forever.

[Col. 0415A] For their seed was accursed from the beginning; and, though you feared no one, you gave them pardon for their sins.

For who will say to you, “What have you done?” Or who will stand against your judgment? Or who will come before you as an avenger of unrighteous people? Or who will charge you if nations perish that you yourself made?

For there is no other God besides you, who cares for all things, so that you may show that you do not judge unjustly.

Neither king nor tyrant will inquire in your presence concerning those whom you have destroyed.

Since you are righteous, you order all things righteously; you consider it foreign to your power to condemn even one who does not deserve punishment.

For your power is the beginning of righteousness, and because you are Lord of all, you make yourself sparing toward all.

You show your power when people do not believe that you are perfect in power, and you expose the boldness of those who do not know you.

But you, master of power, judge with tranquility [Col. 0415B] and govern us with great forbearance, for the ability to act is yours whenever you will.

Through such works you taught your people that the righteous person must be humane, and you made your children hopeful, because when you judge, you grant room for repentance in sins.

For if you punished the enemies of your servants, who deserved death, with such care, giving them time and opportunity by which they might be changed from wickedness,

with how much care did you judge your children, whose ancestors you had given oaths and covenants of good promises?

Therefore, while disciplining us, you scourge our enemies in many ways, so that in judging we may think upon your goodness; and when judgment is passed upon us, we may hope in your mercy.

Thus, even to those who lived senselessly and unjustly in their lifetime, through the very things they worshiped, you gave the most severe torments.

[Col. 0415C] For they wandered longer in the way of error, judging the worthless things found among animals to be gods, living like senseless infants.

Therefore, as though they were senseless children, you gave them judgment as a mockery.

But those who were not corrected by mockeries and interpretations experienced a judgment worthy of God.

For through the things by which they had suffered patiently and indignantly, when they saw those whom they had thought to be gods being destroyed in the very things, they recognized as the true God the one whom formerly they denied that they knew; and for this reason the end of their condemnation came upon them.

## CHAPTER XIII

But all human beings are foolish in whom there is no knowledge of God; and from the good things that are seen they were unable to understand the one who exists, nor, by attending to his works, did they recognize who the craftsman was.

Instead, they judged either fire, or wind, or swift air, [Col. 0415D] or the circle of stars, or the vast water, or the sun and moon, the rulers of the world, to be gods.

If, delighted by their beauty, they judged them to be gods, let them know how much more beautiful than these is their Lord; for the author of beauty created all these things.

And if they were amazed at their power and works, let them understand from them how much more powerful is the one who made them.

For from the greatness of beauty and of creation, their creator can correspondingly be seen.

Yet their fault is still less serious. For perhaps they too go astray while seeking God and wishing to find him.

For while they live among his works, they investigate them and are persuaded that the things they see are good.

Yet even these cannot be excused.

For if they were able to know enough to estimate [Col. 0416A] the age of the world, how did they not more easily find its Lord?

Unhappy are those, and their hope is among the dead, who called the works of human hands gods: gold and silver, the invention of art, representations of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.

Or if some craftsman, a woodworker, cuts a straight piece of wood from the forest and skillfully scrapes away all its bark, and, using his art, carefully fashions it into a useful vessel for the needs of life,

and then uses the remnants of his work to prepare food,

and takes what remains of these—a crooked piece of wood full of knots, useful for nothing—and carefully carves it in his spare time, and shapes it by the knowledge of his art, making it resemble the image of a human being,

or compares it with one of the animals, coating it with red pigment, making its color red with paint, and covering every blemish that is on it,

and makes a fitting dwelling for it, setting it on a wall and securing it with iron,

[Col. 0416B] lest it should fall, taking care of it because he knows that it cannot help itself—for it is an image, and it needs assistance—

and then, for his property, his children, and his marriage, makes vows and inquires of it. He is not ashamed to speak with something that has no soul.

For health he entreats the sick object; for life he begs the dead; and he calls upon something useless for help.

For a journey he asks the one who cannot walk; and concerning acquisition, work, and the outcome of all things, he seeks an answer from one who is useless in every respect.

## CHAPTER XIV

Again, another person, intending to sail and beginning to travel through savage waves, calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the wood that carries him.

[Col. 0416C] For desire for gain devised it, and the craftsman fashioned it by his skill.

But your providence, Father, governs all things, because you gave a way even in the sea and a most secure path among the waves.

And by showing that you are able to save from all things, even when someone approaches the sea without skill,

so that the works of your wisdom would not be without purpose, therefore human beings also entrust their lives to a small piece of wood and, crossing the sea on a raft, are saved.

But from the beginning, when proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world, taking refuge in a raft, preserved for the age the seed of a new generation, guided by your hand.

Blessed is the wood through which righteousness comes.

But the idol made by human hands is accursed, both it and the one who made it, because the maker indeed performed the work, but the fragile object was called a god.

Likewise, the ungodly person and his ungodliness [Col. 0416D] are hateful to God.

For what was made will suffer torment together with the one who made it.

Therefore there will be no regard even for the idols of the nations, because they were made as objects of hatred, as a temptation to human souls, and as a snare for the feet of the foolish.

For the devising of idols is the beginning of fornication, and their invention is the corruption of life.

For they did not exist from the beginning, nor will they exist forever.

Human vanity invented these things in the world, and therefore their end was quickly found.

For a father, grieving with bitter mourning over his son who had been snatched away too soon, quickly made an image of him; and the one who had then died like a human being he now began to worship as a god, and established sacred rites and sacrifices for him among his servants.

Then, as time passed and the wicked [Col. 0417A] custom grew strong, this error was kept as law, and images were worshiped by the command of tyrants.

And those whom people could not honor openly because they were far away, they brought their likeness from a distance and made a visible image of the king whom they wished to honor, so that they might worship the absent one as though he were present, with all their diligence.

The exceptional care of the craftsman also advanced the worship of these objects among those who did not know better.

For, wishing to please the one who had employed him, he labored with his art to fashion the likeness as beautifully as possible.

And the multitude of people, carried away by the beauty of the work, now judged him who had previously been honored as a human being to be a god.

And this was the deception of human life: whether serving affection or kings, people bestowed an incommunicable name upon stones and wood.

Nor was it enough for them to err concerning the knowledge of God; but while living amid a great war of ignorance, they called such great and numerous evils peace.

[Col. 0417B] For either they sacrifice their children, or perform secret rites, or keep watchful celebrations full of madness,

and they no longer preserve either life or pure marriages; but one kills another through envy, or, committing adultery, causes grief.

Everything is mingled together: blood, murder, theft, deceit, corruption and faithlessness, disturbance and perjury, turmoil among the good,

forgetfulness of God, defilement of souls, alteration of birth, instability of marriages, disorder of adultery and shamelessness.

For the worship of unspeakable idols is the cause, beginning, and end of every evil.

For either, while rejoicing, they go mad; or certainly they prophesy falsehoods; or they live unjustly; or they quickly swear falsely.

For while they trust in idols that have no soul, they do not expect to suffer harm for swearing falsely.

Therefore both things will rightly befall them, because they thought wrongly about God, paying attention to idols and swearing unjustly,

[Col. 0417C] deceitfully despising justice.

For it is not the power of those who swear, but the punishment of sinners, that continually pursues the transgression of the unjust.

## CHAPTER XV

But you, our God, are good and true, patient and ordering all things in mercy.

For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your greatness; and if we do not sin, we know that we are counted as belonging to you.

For to know you is perfect righteousness, and to know your justice and power is the root of immortality.

For neither the invention of human beings’ evil craft nor the labor of a painting’s shadow without fruit led us into error—the carved image fashioned in various colors—

whose appearance gives the senseless person desire, and he loves the lifeless form of a dead image without a soul.

Those who love evil are worthy of such hopes, as are those who make them, love them, and worship them.

[Col. 0417D] Yet the potter also, laboriously pressing soft earth, fashions each vessel for our use; from the same clay he fashions vessels for clean uses, and likewise those intended for the opposite purposes. But the potter is the judge of the use of these vessels.

And with vain labor he fashions a god from the same clay—he who shortly before had himself been made from earth and, after a little while, returns to the place from which he was taken, reclaiming the debt owed by his soul.  
[Note: [Col. 0417D] Other printed books have *repertus* (“found”) instead of *repetitus* (“reclaimed”).]

Yet his concern is not that he is about to labor, nor that his life is short, but that he competes with goldsmiths and silversmiths; he also imitates bronze-workers and boasts of his fame because he fashions useless things.

For his heart is ashes, his hope is more worthless than earth, and his life is more contemptible than clay.

For he did not know the one who formed him, who breathed into him the soul that works, and who infused into him a living spirit.

[Col. 0418A] Yet they also considered our life a game, and the conduct of life something arranged for profit, and held that gain must be acquired from every source, even from evil.

For he knows that he is committing the greatest offense of all, the one who fashions fragile vessels and carved images from earthly matter.

All the foolish and desperately unhappy, proud in soul beyond measure, are enemies of your people and rule over them.

For they judged all the idols of the nations to be gods, though they have neither eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for perceiving breath, nor ears for hearing, nor fingers of hands for touching; and their feet are too sluggish for walking.

For a human being made them, and one who borrowed breath fashioned them. No human being can fashion a god like himself.

Since he is mortal, with wicked hands he fashions something dead. For he himself is better than those whom he worships, since he has lived, though mortal, whereas they have never lived.

Yet they also worship the most miserable animals; for, compared with these, the animals are [Col. 0418B] senseless and even worse.

Nor can anyone obtain anything good from the sight of these animals. They have fled from the praise of God and from his blessing.

## CHAPTER XVI

For these things and for others like them they deservedly suffered torments and were destroyed by a multitude of beasts.

In place of those torments, you ordered things well for your people, to whom you gave a new taste of the desire for their delight, preparing a meal of quails for them.

Thus those people, desiring food because of what had been shown and sent to them, were turned away even from necessary desire; while these, having quickly become needy, tasted a new food.

For it was necessary that destruction should come upon those who practiced tyranny without excuse, while to these you showed only how their enemies were being destroyed.

[Col. 0418C] For when the savage fury of beasts came upon them, they were destroyed by the bites of crooked serpents.

But your anger did not remain forever; for a short time they were troubled for correction, having a sign of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of your law.

For the one who turned toward it was not healed by what he saw, but by you, the savior of all.

And by this you showed our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil.

The bites of locusts and flies killed them, and no cure was found for their souls, because they deserved to be destroyed by such creatures.

But the teeth of poisonous dragons did not overcome your children, because your mercy came and healed them.

For they were examined by remembrance of your words, and were quickly saved, lest, falling into deep forgetfulness, they should be unable to use your help.

For neither herb nor poultice healed them,

[Col. 0418D] but your word, Lord, which heals all things.

For you, Lord, have power over life and death; you lead down to the gates of death and bring back.

Human beings may indeed kill through wickedness, but when the spirit has gone out, it does not return, nor can they recall the soul that has been received away.

But it is impossible to escape your hand.

For the ungodly who denied knowing you were scourged by the strength of your arm, suffering persecution through strange waters, hailstorms, and rains, and being consumed by fire.

For, astonishingly, in the water that extinguishes everything, fire was more powerful; for it is the avenger of the world on behalf of the righteous.

At one time the fire was restrained so that the animals sent against the ungodly would not be burned; but this was so that, seeing it, they might know that they were suffering persecution by the judgment of God.

At another time, in the water, fire blazed everywhere beyond its power,

[Col. 0419A] so as to destroy the nation of the unjust land.

In place of these things, you nourished your people with angelic food and supplied them with bread prepared from heaven without labor, containing every delight and the sweetness of every taste.

For your substance displayed your sweetness toward your children; and, serving the will of each one, it was changed into whatever each person desired.

But snow and ice endured the force of fire and did not melt, so that they might know that the fire blazing in hail and flashing in rain destroyed the produce of their enemies.

But this fire, again, forgot its own power when it was needed to nourish the righteous.

For creation, serving you, its Maker, blazes into punishment against the unjust and becomes gentler in doing good for those who trust in you.

Therefore, even then, transformed into all things, it served your grace, the nourisher of all, according to the desire of those who sought something from you,

[Col. 0419B] so that your children, whom you loved, Lord, might know that it is not the fruits of creation that nourish human beings, but your word preserves those who believe in you.

For what could not be destroyed by fire melted immediately when warmed by a slight ray of the sun,

so that it might be known to all that one must anticipate the sun to receive your blessing and worship you at the rising of the light.

For the hope of the ungrateful will melt like winter ice and vanish like useless water.

## CHAPTER XVII

For great are your judgments, Lord, and your words are beyond description; therefore undisciplined souls went astray.

While the ungodly thought that they could rule over a holy nation, bound with the chains of darkness and the fetters of a long night, shut up beneath roofs, they lay as fugitives from eternal providence [Col. 0419C].

And while they thought they were hidden in dark sins, they were scattered beneath the dark covering of oblivion, trembling terribly and thrown into great confusion by overwhelming astonishment.

For the cave that enclosed them did not guard them without fear; a sound descending from above disturbed them, and gloomy apparitions appearing to them produced terror.

No power of fire could give them light, nor could the clear flames of the stars illuminate that dreadful night.

A sudden fire appeared to them, full of fear; and, struck with terror at the unseen face, they judged the things that were visible to be worse.

The practitioners of magic were also made a laughingstock, and the boast of their wisdom was rebuked with disgrace.

For those who promised that they themselves could drive fears and disturbances from the suffering soul, these, filled with mockery, languished in fear.

[Col. 0419D] For even if no monstrous apparition disturbed them, they were shaken by the passage of animals and the hissing of serpents and perished trembling; and they denied seeing the air, from which no one could escape by any means.

For wickedness is timid and gives testimony to its condemnation; a troubled conscience always presumes the worst.

For fear is nothing other than the betrayal of the resources of thought.

And when expectation within is lesser, it reckons as greater its ignorance of the cause from which the torment comes.

But those who, sleeping the same sleep during the truly powerless night that came upon them from the lowest [Col. 0420A] and highest depths of the underworld,

were sometimes driven into terror by monstrous apparitions, and sometimes their souls failed through their agitation; for sudden and unexpected fear had come upon them.

Then, if any one of them fell, he was kept in prison, shut in without iron.

For if someone was a farmer, shepherd, or laborer occupied in fieldwork, he endured an inescapable necessity.

They were all bound by one chain of darkness. Whether it was a whistling spirit, the sweet sound of birds among the dense branches of trees, the overwhelming force of rushing water,

the powerful noise of falling rocks, the unseen running of playful animals, the mighty roar of bellowing beasts, or an echo resounding from the highest mountains—all these made them faint with fear.

For the whole world was illuminated by clear light, and its activities continued without hindrance.

But for those alone a heavy night had been spread over them, an image [Col. 0420B] of the darkness that was to overtake them. Thus they were heavier to themselves than the darkness.

## CHAPTER XVIII

But for your holy ones there was the greatest light. They heard these people’s voices but did not see their form; and because they themselves had not suffered the same things, they praised you.

And those who had previously been harmed gave thanks because they were no longer harmed, and they asked for the gift that there might be a distinction.

Therefore they had a flaming pillar of fire as a guide for an unknown road, and you provided the sun for them without harm as a means of their honorable hospitality.

Those deserved to be deprived of light and to suffer imprisonment in darkness, who had kept your children confined, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was beginning to be given to the world.

When they had resolved to kill the infants of the righteous, and one child had been exposed and saved to bring about their downfall,

[Col. 0420C] you carried away a multitude of children and destroyed them all together in mighty water.

For that night was known beforehand by our fathers, so that, truly knowing in what oaths they had placed their trust, they might be more confident.

The salvation of the righteous was received by your people, but the destruction of the unjust.

For just as you harmed their adversaries, so also, calling us to yourself, you glorified us.

For the righteous children of the good secretly offered sacrifices and established in harmony the law of righteousness, agreeing that the righteous would alike receive both good and evil, while already singing beforehand the praises of the fathers.

But the discordant voice of the enemies resounded, and the lamentation of the children’s mourners was heard in grief.

Servant and master were afflicted by a similar punishment, and commoner and king suffered alike.

Thus all alike held countless dead under one name of death. The living were not sufficient even to bury them, because in a single moment their most illustrious nation was destroyed.

For, not believing in everything because of their sorceries—  
[Note: [Col. 0419D] Some other books wrongly read *beneficia* (“benefits”). The Greek has *pharmakias* (φαρμακίας, “sorceries”).]

—then, at the first destruction of the firstborn, they promised that the people belonged to God.

When quiet silence held everything, and night had reached the midpoint of its course,

your almighty word, Lord, leaping from heaven, from the royal throne,

—these two words, “Lord, leaping,” are not recognized by the older printed books, nor are they found in the Greek text, which has only: “Your all-powerful word from the heavens, from the royal thrones,” and so forth—  
[Note: [Col. 0419D–0420D] The longer reading “Lord, leaping” is absent from the older printed editions and from the Greek text.]

—like a stern warrior leapt into the midst of the land of destruction.

Carrying your unfeigned command as a sharp sword, it stood and filled everything with death, and, standing upon the earth, reached even to heaven.

[Col. 0421A] Then sudden visions of evil dreams troubled them, and unexpected fears came upon them.

One person, thrown down half-dead in one place, and another elsewhere, demonstrated the reason for which he was dying.  
[Note: [Col. 0421C] The Greek likewise has “in another place” (ἀλλαχῆ); most Latin books, however, read “there.”]

For the visions that troubled them foretold this, so that they would not perish without knowing why they were suffering evil.

Then the trial of death also touched the righteous, and a disturbance of the multitude arose in the wilderness; but your anger did not continue long.

For the blameless man hastened to intercede for the peoples, bringing forward the shield of his service—prayer—and making his petition effective through incense. He resisted the anger and put an end to the necessity, showing that he was your servant.

He overcame the multitude, not by bodily strength or the power of weapons, but by the word he subdued the one who was tormenting them, recalling the oaths of the ancestors and the covenant.

For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between them, cut off the onslaught, and divided [Col. 0421B] the path that led to the living.

For upon the robe reaching to the feet that he wore was the whole world, and the glories of the ancestors were engraved in four rows of stones, while your majesty was engraved upon the diadem of his head.

The destroyer yielded to these things and was afraid of them, for this alone was sufficient to test the anger.

## CHAPTER XIX

But upon the ungodly, anger came without mercy to the very end.  
[Note: [Col. 0422D] Some printed books add *sua* (“its own”), although the Greek text omits the pronoun.]

For he knew beforehand also what would happen to them.

Because they had allowed them to depart, and had let them go with great anxiety, they were pursued by remorse.

For while they still held mourning in their hands and lamented at the tombs of the dead, they adopted another thought of folly: those whom they had driven away while pleading with them, they now pursued as fugitives.

For a fitting necessity led them to this end, and they lost the recollection of what had happened, so that punishment might fill up whatever the torments had left undone.

And while your people passed through wonderfully, they found a new death.

For every creature was reshaped according to its own kind from the beginning, serving your commands, so that your children might be kept unharmed.

For a cloud overshadowed their camps, and dry land appeared from the water that had previously covered it; in the Red Sea there was an unobstructed road, and a field bearing vegetation emerged from the immeasurable depth.

Through it every nation passed, sheltered by your hand, seeing your wonders and marvels.

For like horses they grazed on food, and like lambs they leaped for joy, magnifying you, Lord, who had delivered them.

For they still remembered what had happened during their sojourn: how, instead of animals for the nations, the earth produced swarms of flies, and instead of fish, the river spewed forth a multitude of frogs.

Finally they saw a new kind of birds, when, driven by desire, they asked for food for their feasting.

For, in response to their craving, quails rose up from the sea; and punishments came upon the sinners, [Col. 0422B] not without the former signs, through the force of lightning—for they were justly suffering according to their wickedness.

Indeed, they had established a more detestable lack of hospitality: some would not receive strangers, while others reduced good guests to slavery.

And not only this, but another consideration also applied to them: they received foreigners unwillingly.

But those who had joyfully received them, since they themselves had enjoyed the same justice, they afflicted with the most savage pains.

They were struck with blindness, just as those men at the doors of the righteous were: when they had suddenly been covered with darkness, each sought the passage to his own doorway.

For the elements, as they are changed within themselves, are like the sound of an instrument when its quality is altered, while all preserve their own sound; from this, the result can certainly be judged by sight itself.

For things of the land were changed into aquatic creatures, and whatever had been swimming passed onto the land.

Fire exercised power over water beyond its own nature, and water forgot its nature as an extinguisher. [Col. 0422C]

Conversely, the flames did not torment the flesh of perishable animals that walked among them, nor did they dissolve that good food which was easily dissolved like ice. For in everything you magnified your people, Lord, and honored them, and did not despise them, assisting them at all times and in every place.

[Col. 0421] Here ends the Book of Wisdom.

## PROLOGUE TO ECCLESIASTICUS, JESUS SON OF SIRACH

[Col. 0421]

[Col. 0421D] The wisdom of many great matters has been made known to us through the Law and the Prophets, and through the others who followed them. In these things Israel ought to be praised for instruction and wisdom, because it is necessary not only that those who speak be skilled, but also that outsiders may become highly skilled, both in speaking [Alternative: learning] and in writing.

My grandfather Jesus, after devoting himself more fully to the diligent reading of the Law, the Prophets, and the other books handed down to us by our ancestors, wished himself also to write something concerning instruction and wisdom, so that those who desire to learn, and who have become proficient in those works, might attend more and more closely with their minds and be strengthened for a life according to the Law.

Therefore I exhort you to come with goodwill and to undertake the reading with attentive application, and to grant indulgence in those places where, while following the model of wisdom, we seem to fall short in the composition of our words. [Col. 0422D] For Hebrew words lose force when they have been translated into another language. And not only this, but the Law itself, the Prophets, and the remaining books differ considerably when they are spoken in relation to one another.

For in the thirty-eighth year, in the reign of King Ptolemy Euergetes, after I had come to Egypt and had remained there for a considerable time, I found books that had been left there, containing instruction of no small or negligible value. Therefore I myself considered it good and necessary to add some diligence and labor in translating this book, and with much wakefulness I devoted learning, over the course of time, to bringing this book to completion for those who wish to give their minds to it and learn how they ought to order their conduct—those who have resolved [Alternative: resolved] to live according to the Law of the Lord.

## THE BOOK OF ECCLESIASTICUS BEGINS

[Col. 0423]

## CHAPTER ONE

[Col. 0423A]

All wisdom is from the Lord God, and it has always been with him and exists before the age.

Who has counted the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of the age? Who has measured the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss?

Who has investigated the wisdom of God that precedes all things? Wisdom was created before everything, and the understanding of prudence is from eternity.

The fountain of wisdom is the word of God in the heights, and its ways are eternal commandments.

To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed, and who has recognized its subtlety?

To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed and made manifest? And who has understood the multiplicity of its ways?

One is the Most High, the almighty Creator, a powerful King, and exceedingly fearsome, sitting upon his throne and ruling as God.

He himself created her in the Holy Spirit, and saw her, counted her, [Col. 0423B] and measured her.

And he poured her out over all his works and over all flesh according to his gift, and bestowed her upon those who love him.

The fear of the Lord is glory, boasting, joy, and a crown of exultation.

The fear of the Lord delights the heart and gives gladness, joy, and length of days.

It will be well with the one who fears the Lord at the end, and he will be blessed on the day of his death.

The love of God is honorable wisdom.

Those to whom she appears in vision love her when they see her and when they recognize her great works.

The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; she was conceived with the faithful in the womb, walks with chosen women, and is recognized among the righteous and faithful.

The fear of the Lord is the religiousness of knowledge.

Religious devotion will guard and justify the heart; it will give delight and joy.

It will be well with the one who fears the Lord, and he will be blessed in the days of his completion.

The fullness of wisdom is to fear God, and its fullness comes from its fruits.

She will fill his whole house through the generations, and his storehouses with her treasures.

The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, filling one with peace and the fruit of salvation.

He saw and counted her; both are gifts of God.

Wisdom will distribute knowledge and understanding of prudence, and she exalts those who hold her in honor.

The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are long-lived.

In the treasuries of wisdom are understanding and the religiousness of knowledge; but wisdom is an abomination to sinners.

The fear of the Lord drives away sin.

For the one who is without fear cannot be justified; the anger of his temper is his own overthrow.

The patient person will endure until the appointed time, and afterward comes the return of joy. [Col. 0423D]

Good sense will conceal his words for a time, and the lips of many will declare his understanding.

In the treasuries of wisdom is the expression of discipline;

but to the sinner, the worship of God is an abomination.

My child, if you desire wisdom, preserve justice, and God will give it to you.

For wisdom and discipline are the fear of the Lord, and what is pleasing to him—

[Col. 0424A] faith and gentleness—and he will fill his treasures.

Do not be distrustful of the fear of the Lord, and do not approach him with a divided heart.

Do not be hypocritical before men, and do not stumble through your lips.

Pay attention to these things, lest you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul.

Then God may reveal your hidden things and overthrow you in the midst of the assembly.

For you have approached the Lord deceitfully, and your heart is full of treachery and fraud.

## CHAPTER TWO

My child, when you approach the service of God, stand in justice and fear, and prepare your soul for trial.

Humble your heart and endure; incline your ear and receive words of understanding, and do not hurry in the time of distress.

Endure the supports of God; cling to God and endure, [Col. 0424B] so that your life may increase at the end.

Whatever is brought upon you, accept it, and endure in pain; in your humiliation, have patience.

For gold and silver are tested in fire, but acceptable people in the furnace of humiliation.

Trust in God, and he will restore you; direct your way and hope in him. Keep his fear, and grow old in it.

You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and do not turn away from him, lest you fall.

You who fear the Lord, believe him, and your reward will not be lost.

You who fear the Lord, hope in him, and his mercy will come to you as a delight.

You who fear the Lord, love him, and your hearts will be enlightened.

Look at the nations, children, and know that no one who hoped in the Lord was put to shame.

For who has remained in his commandments and been forsaken? Or who has called upon him and been despised?

[Col. 0424C] For God is gracious and merciful, and he will forgive sins on the day of tribulation; he is a protector to all who seek him in truth.

Woe to the double-hearted, the deceitful in speech, the hands that do evil, and the sinner who walks the earth by two paths.

Woe to those who are fainthearted and do not trust God; therefore they will not be protected by him.

Woe to those who have lost endurance, who have abandoned straight ways, and who have turned aside into crooked paths.

What will they do when the Lord begins to inspect them?

Those who fear the Lord will not distrust his word, and those who love him will keep his way.

Those who fear the Lord will seek what pleases him, and those who love him will be filled with his law.

Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and sanctify their souls in his presence.

Those who fear the Lord keep his commandments and will have patience until his visitation.

Saying: “If we do not repent, we shall fall into the hands of the Lord, [Col. 0424D] and not into the hands of men.”

For as great as he is, so great also is his mercy with him.

## CHAPTER THREE

The children of wisdom are the assembly of the righteous, and their community is obedience and love.

Listen, children, to the judgment of your father, and act accordingly, so that you may be saved.

[Col. 0425A] For God has honored the father in his children, and, in seeking the judgment of the mother, he has established it among the children.

Whoever loves God will pray for sins and will restrain himself from them; he will be heard in the prayer of his days.

As one who stores up treasure, so is one who honors his mother.

Whoever honors his father will rejoice in children, and on the day of his prayer he will be heard.

Whoever honors his father will live a longer life, and whoever obeys his father will refresh his mother.

Whoever fears the Lord honors his parents and serves those who begot him as though they were masters.

Honor your father in deed and word and with all patience,

so that blessing from him may come upon you, and his blessing may remain at the end.

The blessing of a father strengthens the houses of children, but the curse of a mother uproots their foundations.

Do not glory in the disgrace of your father, for his dishonor is not your glory.

[Col. 0425B] A person’s glory comes from the honor of his father, and a father without honor is the disgrace of his son.

My child, support your father’s old age, and do not grieve him during his life.

And if he should fail in understanding, grant him pardon, and do not despise him in your strength; for kindness shown to a father will not be forgotten.

For the good done on account of your mother’s sin will be restored to you.

It will be established for you in justice, and on the day of tribulation you will be remembered; as ice melts in clear weather, so your sins will melt away.

How evil in reputation is the one who abandons his father; and [Alternative: omitted: “and”] he is accursed by God who exasperates his mother.

My child, complete your works in gentleness, and you will be loved more than the glory of men.

The greater you are, humble yourself in everything, and you will find grace before God.

For great is the power of God alone, and he is honored by the humble.

Do not seek things higher than you, and do not investigate matters stronger than you; but always consider what God has commanded you, and do not be curious about his many works.

For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes the things that are hidden.

Do not investigate superfluous matters excessively, and do not be curious about his many works.

For many things beyond human understanding have been shown to you.

Suspicion of them has also overthrown many and held their minds captive in vanity.

A hard heart will fare badly at the end, and whoever loves danger will perish in it.

A heart that enters upon two paths will have no success, and the perverse-hearted will stumble on them.

A wicked heart will be weighed down with sorrows, and the sinner will add sin to sin.

There is no healing for the assembly of the proud; for the plant of sin will be rooted in them, and it will not be understood.

[Col. 0425D] The heart of the wise understands wisdom, and a good ear hears wisdom with complete desire.

A wise and understanding heart will refrain from sins, and in works of justice it will have success. [Note: [Col. 0425D] Other books read “approaches.”]

Water extinguishes a burning fire, and almsgiving resists sins.

God watches over the one who repays a kindness; he remembers him afterward, and at the time of his fall he will find support.

## CHAPTER FOUR

My child, do not defraud the poor of alms, and do not turn your eyes away from the poor.

Do not despise a hungry soul, and do not exasperate the poor in his need.

[Col. 0426A] Do not afflict the heart of the needy, and do not delay giving to one in distress.

Do not reject the plea of the afflicted, and do not turn your face away from the needy.

Do not turn your eyes away from the poor because of anger, and do not leave those who ask you behind, so that they curse you.

For the prayer of the one who curses you in the bitterness of his soul will be heard; the one who made him will hear him.

Make yourself approachable to the assembly of the poor; humble your soul before the presbyter, and bow your head before the great.

Incline your ear to the poor without sadness, repay what you owe, and answer him peaceably and gently.

Rescue the one who suffers injury from the hand of the proud, and do not bear it bitterly in your soul.

In judging, be merciful to orphans like a father, and be like a husband to their mother.

Then you will be like an obedient son of the Most High, and he will have mercy on you more than a mother.

Wisdom gives life to her children as to her own, receives those who seek her, and goes before them on the way of justice.

Whoever loves her loves life, and those who keep watch for her will embrace her favor.

Those who hold her will inherit life, and wherever she enters, God will bless.

Those who serve her will serve the Holy One obediently, and God loves those who love her.

Whoever listens to her will judge nations, and whoever gazes upon her will remain confident.

If he trusts her, he will inherit her, and his descendants will be established,

because she walks with him in trial and chooses him first.

She will bring fear, dread, and testing upon him, and afflict him with the discipline of her instruction until she tests him in his thoughts and trusts his soul.

[Col. 0426C] Then she will strengthen him, lead him onto a straight path, and make him glad.

She will uncover her hidden things to him and store up in him knowledge and understanding of justice.

But if he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to his enemy.

My child, preserve the time and avoid evil.

For your life’s sake, do not be ashamed to speak the truth.

For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace.

Do not show partiality against your own face, and do not lie against your own soul.

Do not fear your neighbor in his fall.

Do not hold back a word at the time of salvation. Do not hide your wisdom in its beauty.

For wisdom is recognized in the tongue; understanding, knowledge, and instruction are found in the word of the intelligent, and strength in works of justice.

Do not contradict the word of truth in any way, and be ashamed of the falsehood arising from your ignorance.

[Col. 0426D] Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not submit yourself to every person because of sin.

Do not resist the face of the powerful, nor strive against the current of a river.

Fight for justice for your soul, and contend for justice even unto death, and God will fight your enemies for you.

Do not be hasty with your tongue, useless, or slack in your works.

Do not be like a lion in your house, overturning your household and oppressing those subject to you.

Let your hand not be extended to receive and closed when it is time to give.

## CHAPTER FIVE

Do not rely on unjust possessions, and do not say: [Col. 0427A] “My life is sufficient”; for they will be of no benefit at the time of vengeance and distress.

Do not follow the desire of your heart in your strength.

And do not say: “How have I prevailed?” or “Who will subject me because of my deeds?” For God will surely take vengeance.

Do not say: “I have sinned, and what sad thing has happened to me?” For the Most High is patient in repaying.

Do not be without fear because your sin has been forgiven, nor add sin upon sin.

And do not say: “The Lord’s mercy is great; he will have mercy on the multitude of my sins.”

For mercy and wrath quickly draw near from him, and his wrath looks upon sinners.

Do not delay turning to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day.

For his wrath will come suddenly, and at the time of vengeance he will destroy you.

Do not be anxious about unjust wealth, for it will not benefit you on the day of distress and vengeance.

[Col. 0427B] Do not toss yourself about in every wind, and do not go down every path; for every sinner is tested by double speech.

Stand firm in the way of the Lord, in the truth of your understanding and knowledge, and let the word of peace and justice pursue you.

Be gentle in hearing the word, so that you may understand; and with wisdom give a true answer.

If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; otherwise, let your hand be over your mouth, lest you be caught in an undisciplined word and be put to shame.

Honor and glory belong to the intelligent speaker, but the tongue of the imprudent is his own overthrow.

Do not be called a whisperer, and do not let your tongue entrap you and put you to shame.

For the thief there is shame and repentance, and for the double-tongued the worst disgrace; but for the whisperer, hatred, hostility, and reproach.

Justify the small person and the great alike.

## CHAPTER SIX

[Col. 0427C]

Do not become an enemy to your neighbor for the sake of a friend; for the wicked will inherit reproach and insult, and every sinful person is envious and double-tongued.

Do not exalt yourself in the thought of your soul like a bull, lest your strength be overthrown through folly.

Then it may eat your leaves, destroy your fruits, and leave you like a dry tree in the wilderness.

For a wicked soul destroys its possessor, gives him as a joy to his enemies, and leads him into the lot of the impious.

Sweet speech multiplies friends and calms enemies, and a gracious tongue abounds in a good person.

Let many be your peacemakers, but let one out of a thousand be your counselor.

If you acquire a friend, acquire him in trial, and do not trust him too quickly.

For there is a friend according to his appointed time, and he will not remain on the day of tribulation.

There is also a friend who turns to hostility, and there is a friend who will expose hatred, strife, and insults. [Col. 0427D]

There is also a friend who is a companion at table, but he will not remain on the day of need.

If a friend remains steadfast, he will be like your equal, and he will act confidently among your household.

If he humbles himself before you and hides himself from your face, you will have a good friendship united in one mind.

Separate yourself from your enemies, and pay attention to your friends.

A faithful friend is a strong protection; whoever finds him has found a treasure.

Nothing compares with a faithful friend, and gold and silver are not worth weighing against the goodness of his faithfulness.

A faithful friend is a medicine of life and immortality, and those who fear the Lord will find him.

Whoever fears God will have a good friendship, for his friend will be like him.

My child, receive instruction from your youth, and you will find wisdom even to gray hairs.

[Col. 0428A] Approach her like one who plows and sows, and await her good fruits.

For you will labor little in her work, and soon you will eat of her produce through the generations.

How exceedingly harsh wisdom is to the learned, and the senseless person will not remain in her.

To them she will be like the testing of a stone’s strength, and they will not delay casting her away.

For the wisdom of instruction is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many; but to those who know her she remains until the sight of God.

Listen, my child, and accept the counsel of understanding, and do not reject my counsel.

Put your foot into her fetters and your neck into her chains.

Submit your shoulder and carry her, and do not be wearied by her bonds.

Approach her with all your soul, and preserve her ways with all your strength.

Seek her, and she will be revealed to you; and once you have taken hold of her, do not abandon her.

For at the end you will find rest in her, and she will turn into delight for you.

Her fetters will become for you a protection of strength, her bases a source of power, and her chains a robe of glory.

For beauty of life is in her, and her bonds are a saving attachment.

You will put her on as a robe of glory and place a crown of rejoicing upon yourself.

My child, if you attend to me, you will learn; and if you apply your mind, you will become wise.

If you incline your ear, you will receive instruction; and if you love listening, you will become wise.

Stand in the company of prudent elders, and join yourself wholeheartedly to their wisdom, so that you may be able to hear every account of God, and that sayings worthy of praise may not escape you.

If you see an intelligent person, rise early to seek him, and let your foot wear down the steps of his doors. [Col. 0428C]

Keep your thoughts on the commandments of God, and be especially constant in his commands; he himself will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom will be given to you.

## CHAPTER SEVEN

Do not do evil, and it will not seize you.

Depart from injustice, and evils will withdraw from you.

My child, do not sow evils in the furrows of injustice, and you will not reap them sevenfold.

Do not seek leadership from the ruler, nor a seat of honor from the king.

Do not justify yourself before God, for he knows the heart; and before the king do not wish to appear wise.

Do not seek to become a judge unless you are able by your strength to break through injustices, lest you fear the face of the powerful and place a stumbling block in your justice.

Do not sin amid the multitude of the city, nor thrust yourself into the crowd.

Do not bind two sins together, for you will not be free from even one.

Do not be fainthearted in your soul.

Do not neglect prayer or almsgiving.

Do not say: “God will look upon me because of the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer gifts to God Most High, he will accept mine.”

Do not mock a person in the bitterness of his soul; for there is one who humbles and exalts, God who observes all.

Do not plow falsehood against your brother, nor do the same against your friend.

Do not wish to lie every kind of lie; for constant lying is not good.

Do not be wordy in the assembly of elders, and do not repeat yourself in your prayer.

Do not hate laborious work or farming created by the Most High.

[Col. 0429A] Do not count yourself among the undisciplined. [Note: The published books of Hentenius read “among the disciplinarians,” but both sound sense and the Greek text itself have ἁμαρτωλῶν, “of sinners.”]

Remember wrath, for it will not delay.

Humble your spirit greatly, for the vengeance of the impious flesh is fire and worm.

Do not break faith with a friend over money he has delayed returning, nor despise your beloved brother for gold.

Do not depart from a sensible and good wife whom you received in the fear of the Lord, for the grace of her modesty is worth more than gold.

Do not wrong a servant who works faithfully, nor a hired worker who gives his life to his work.

Let a sensible servant be dear to you like your own soul; do not defraud him of his freedom, nor abandon him in need.

Do you have cattle? Attend to them; and if they are useful, let them remain with you.

Do you have children? Instruct them, and bend them from their youth.

Do you have daughters? Guard their bodies, and do not show them a smiling face.

Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great work; and give her to a sensible man.

If you have a wife according to your soul, do not cast her away; and do not entrust yourself to one who is hateful. With your whole heart,

honor your father, and do not forget the groans of your mother.

Remember that you would not have been born unless through them, and repay them as they repaid you.

With all your soul fear the Lord, and sanctify his priests.

With all your strength love the one who made you, and do not abandon his ministers.

Honor God with all your soul, and honor the priests, and purify yourself with your arms.

Give them their portion, as it has been commanded you, of firstfruits and purification; and cleanse yourself from your negligence with a little.

You shall offer to the Lord the gift of your arms and the sacrifice of sanctification [Col. 0429C], and the first portions of holy things.

Stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your atonement and your blessing may be brought to completion.

The grace of a gift is before every living person, and do not withhold kindness from the dead.

Do not cease from consoling those who weep, and walk with those who mourn.

Do not be reluctant to visit the sick; for through such acts you will be strengthened in love.

In all your works remember your last things, and you will never sin.

## CHAPTER EIGHT

Do not quarrel with a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands.

Do not contend with a wealthy man, lest he bring a lawsuit against you.

For gold and silver have destroyed many, reached even to the heart of kings, and perverted them.

Do not quarrel with a talkative man, and do not pile wood onto his fire. [Alternative: “in his fire.”]

Do not associate with an uneducated person, lest he speak evil of your lineage.

Do not despise one who turns away from sin, nor reproach him; remember that we are all under correction.

Do not despise a person in his old age, for some of us also grow old.

Do not rejoice over the death of your enemy, knowing that we all die and do not wish to enter into rejoicing.

Do not neglect the account of wise elders, and occupy yourself with their proverbs.

For from them you will learn wisdom, understanding, and how to serve the great without complaint.

Do not let the account of the elders pass you by; for they themselves learned from their fathers.

[Col. 0430A] For from them you will learn understanding and how to give an answer in time of need.

Do not kindle the coals of sinners by rebuking them, lest you be kindled by the flame of their fire.

Do not stand before an abusive person, lest he sit as an ambusher at your mouth.

Do not lend to one stronger than you; and if you lend, regard it as lost.

Do not give surety beyond your means; and if you have given surety, consider how you will repay.

Do not judge against a judge, for he judges according to what is just.

Do not go on the road with a bold man, lest he burden you with his evils; for he goes according to his own will, and you will perish together with his folly.

Do not quarrel with an angry man, and do not go into the wilderness with a bold man; for blood is as nothing before him, and where there is no help, he will overthrow you.

Do not take counsel with fools, for they cannot love anything except what pleases them.

[Col. 0430B] Do not make plans before a stranger, for you do not know what he will produce.

Do not reveal your heart to every person, lest he bring you false favor and reproach you.

## CHAPTER NINE

Do not be jealous of the wife who shares your bosom, lest she display against you the malice of evil instruction.

Do not give a woman power over your soul, lest she enter into your strength and you be put to shame.

Do not look upon a fickle woman, lest you fall into her snares.

Do not keep company with a dancer, nor listen to her, lest you perish through her arts.

Do not gaze upon a virgin, lest you stumble because of her beauty.

Do not give your soul in any way to prostitutes, lest you destroy yourself and your inheritance.

Do not look around in the streets of the city, lest you wander in its squares. [Col. 0430C]

Turn your face away from a well-adorned woman, and do not look closely at another’s beauty.

Because of a woman’s beauty many have perished, and from it desire blazes like fire.

Every woman who is a prostitute will be trampled like dung in the street.

Many, admiring another woman’s beauty, have become rejected; for her conversation blazes like fire.

Do not sit at all with a strange woman, nor recline beside her on a couch.

And do not quarrel with her over wine, lest your heart incline toward her and you slip into destruction through your blood.

Do not abandon an old friend, for a new one will not be like him.

New wine is a new friend; it will grow old, and you will drink it with pleasure.

Do not be jealous of glory or the wealth of sinners, for you do not know what their overthrow will be.

Do not let the injury of the unjust please you, knowing that the impious will not please even to the underworld.

Keep far away from a man who has power to kill, and you will not suspect the fear of death.

And if you approach him, commit nothing, lest he take your life.

Know that you are sharing death, for you will walk amid snares and tread upon the weapons of those in pain.

According to your ability, guard yourself from your neighbor, and deal with the wise and prudent.

Let righteous men be your table companions, and let your glorying be in the fear of God.

Let your thoughts be occupied with the understanding of God, and let all your discourse be wholly in the commandments of the Most High.

[Col. 0431A] In the hands of craftsmen, works will be praised; and the leader of the people will be praised for the wisdom of his speech; but the word belongs to the understanding of elders.

A talkative man is terrifying in his city, and one reckless in speech will be hated.

## CHAPTER TEN

A wise judge will judge his people, and the rule of an intelligent person will be stable.

As is the judge of the people, so are his ministers; and what the ruler of the city is like, so are its inhabitants.

An foolish king will destroy his people, but cities will be inhabited through the understanding of the powerful.

The power of the earth is in the hand of God, and he will raise up a useful ruler over it in due time.

Human prosperity is in the hand of God, and upon the face of the scribe he places his honor.

Do not remember any injury done by your neighbor, and do nothing in works of injury.

[Col. 0431B] Pride is hateful before God and men, and every injustice of the nations is an abomination.

A kingdom is transferred [Alternative: will be transferred] from nation to nation because of injustices, injuries, insults, and various deceits.

Nothing is more wicked than a miser. Why should earth and ashes be proud?

Nothing is more unjust than loving money; for such a person has even sold his own soul, because during his life he cast away his inmost self.

Every position of power has a short life. A prolonged illness burdens the physician.

The physician cuts short a brief illness; so the king exists today and will die tomorrow.

For when a person dies, he will inherit serpents, beasts, and worms.

The beginning of human pride is apostasy from God.

For his heart has departed from the one who made him, because pride is the beginning of every sin. Whoever clings to it will be filled with curses, and it will overthrow him at the end.

Therefore the Lord dishonored the gatherings of the wicked and destroyed them completely.

God destroyed the seats of proud leaders and made the gentle sit in their place.

God dried up the roots of proud nations and planted the humble among those nations.

The Lord overturned the lands of the nations and destroyed them to their foundations.

He dried them up from among themselves, destroyed them, and caused their memory to cease from the earth.

God erased the memory of the proud and left the memory of the humble in understanding.

Pride was not created for human beings, nor anger for the race of women.

The offspring of human beings who fear God will be honored; but the offspring that passes over the commandments of the Lord will be dishonored.

In the midst of the brothers their ruler is in honor, and those who fear the Lord are in his eyes.

The glory of the rich, the honored, and the poor is the fear of God.

Do not despise a poor righteous man, and do not magnify a rich sinful man.

The great, the judge, and the powerful are held in honor; yet there is none greater than the one who fears God.

Free persons will serve a sensible servant, and a prudent and disciplined man will not grumble when corrected, while the ignorant will not be honored.

Do not exalt yourself while doing your work, and do not delay in time of distress.

Better is the one who works and abounds in everything than the one who boasts and lacks bread.

My child, preserve your soul in gentleness, and give it honor according to its worth.

Who will justify one who sins against his own soul? And who will honor one who dishonors his own soul?

[Col. 0432A] The poor man boasts through his discipline and fear, while there is a man who is honored because of his wealth.

But whoever boasts of poverty—how much more should he boast of wealth! And whoever boasts of wealth should fear poverty.

## CHAPTER XI

Wisdom will exalt the head of the humble [Al. exalted it], and will make him sit in the midst of the great.

Do not praise a man for his appearance, nor despise a person for his looks.

The bee is small among flying creatures, but its fruit is the beginning of sweetness.

Never boast in clothing, nor exalt yourself on the day of your honor; for the works of the Most High alone are marvelous—glorious, hidden, and beyond sight are his works.

Many tyrants have sat upon a throne, and one whom no one expected has worn the crown.

Many powerful men have been utterly oppressed, and the glorious have been delivered into the hands of others.

[Col. 0432B] Before you question anyone, do not reproach him; and when you have questioned him, correct him justly.

Before you hear, do not answer a word; and in the midst of speeches do not add your own words.

Do not contend over a matter that does not trouble you, and do not stand in judgment concerning sinners.

My son, do not let your activities be many; and if you become rich, you will not be free from wrongdoing. For if you pursue too much, you will not overtake it; and if you run ahead, you will not escape.

There is a man who labors, hurries, and suffers—an impious man—and the more so he will not prosper.

There is a man who is corrupt and in need of recovery, more and more failing in strength and abounding in poverty.

And the eye of God looked upon him for good, and raised him from his lowliness, and exalted his head; and many were amazed at him, and they honored God because of him.

Good and evil, life and death, poverty and honor are from God.

[Col. 0432C] Wisdom, discipline, and knowledge of the law are with God. Love and the ways of the good are with him.

Error and darkness were created together with sinners; but those who rejoice in evils grow old in evil.

God’s gift remains with the righteous, and his prosperity will have lasting success forever.

There is one who becomes wealthy by acting sparingly, and this is the portion of his reward:

in that he says, “I have found rest for myself, and now I shall eat alone of my goods.”

And he does not know that time will pass, death will draw near, he will leave everything to others, and he will die.

Stand by your covenant, converse in it, and grow old in the work of your commandments.

Do not remain in the works of sinners.

But trust in God, and remain in your place.

For it is easy in the eyes of God suddenly to make a poor man honorable.

God’s blessing hastens as the reward of the righteous, and in a swift hour his progress bears fruit.

[Col. 0432D] Do not say, “What need have I, and what good will come to me from this?”

Do not say, “I have enough for myself; and what could make me worse because of it?”

On a day of good things, do not be forgetful of evils; and on a day of evils, do not be forgetful of good things,

for it is easy before God, on the day of death, to repay each one according to his ways.

The evil of the hour causes the forgetting of great luxury, and at the end of a man his works are stripped bare.

Before death, praise no one, for a man is recognized through his children.

Do not bring every person into your house, for there are many snares of the deceitful.

For just as the entrails of stinking things belch forth, and as a partridge is led into a cage, and a doe into a snare, so is the heart of the proud—and like a lookout who sees the fall of his neighbor.
