[Col. 0433A] For one who turns good things into evil lies in wait, and will place a blemish even upon the chosen.

From one spark a fire grows, and from one deceitful man bloodshed increases; the sinful man, however, lies in wait for blood.

Beware of the pestilent man, for he fabricates evils, lest he bring ridicule upon you forever.

Admit a stranger to yourself, and he will overthrow you in a whirlwind and estrange you from your own people.

## CHAPTER XII

If you do good, know for whom you do it; and there will be much gratitude in your good deeds.

Do good to the righteous, and you will find a great reward—not from him, perhaps, but certainly from the Lord.

For it is not well with one who persists in evils and does not give alms, because the Most High also hates sinners and has mercy on the repentant.

Give to the merciful, and do not support the sinner; and he will repay the impious and sinners with vengeance, keeping them for the day of vengeance.

[Col. 0433B] Give to the good, and do not receive the sinner.

Do good to the humble, and do not give to the impious; prevent bread from being given to him, lest he become stronger than you through it.

For you will find double evils in all the good things you do for him, because the Most High also hates sinners and will repay the impious with vengeance.

A friend will not be recognized in prosperity, and an enemy will not remain hidden in adversity.

In a man’s prosperity, his enemies are sorrowful; and in his adversity, his friend is recognized.

Do not trust your enemy forever, for his wickedness rusts like bronze.

And if he goes humbled and bent over, give him your attention and guard yourself from him.

Do not place him beside you, nor let him sit at your right hand, lest he turn into your place, seek your chair, and at last you recognize my words and be pricked by my sayings.

Who will pity a serpent-charmer bitten by a serpent, or any of those who approach wild beasts? So it is with one who associates with an unjust man and is wrapped up in his sins.

He will remain with you for one hour; but if you turn aside, he will not support you.

The enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he lies in wait to throw you into a pit.

The enemy weeps with his eyes; and if he finds an opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.

And if evils befall you, you will find him there first.

The enemy weeps with his eyes, and, as though helping, he will dig beneath your feet.

He will shake his head and clap his hands; and, whispering much, he will change his expression.

## CHAPTER XIII

Whoever touches pitch will be defiled by it, and whoever associates with the proud will put on pride.

He will take a burden upon himself who associates with one more honorable than himself. Do not become a companion to one richer than you.

[Col. 0433D] What fellowship can a pot have with a kettle? For when they collide, it will be broken [Al. they will be broken].

The rich man acts unjustly and rages, but the poor man who has been wronged remains silent.

If you are generous, he will take you in; and if you have nothing, he will abandon you.

If you have possessions, he will live with you, empty you out, and not grieve over you.

If you become necessary to him, he will trip you up; and, smiling, he will give you hope, telling you good things and saying, “What do you need?”

And he will shame you with his food until he has emptied you twice and three times; and at last he will mock you. Then, seeing you afterward, he will abandon you and shake his head at you.

Submit yourself to God, and await his hand.

Take care lest, deceived into folly, you be humbled.

[Col. 0434A] Do not be humble in your own wisdom, lest, being humbled, you be led astray into folly.

Withdraw from an advocate more powerful than yourself; for by this he will all the more summon you to court.

Do not be insolent, lest you stumble; and do not remain far from him, lest you fall into oblivion.

Do not presume to speak with him on equal terms, nor trust his many words; for through much speech he will test you, and, smiling, will question you about your secrets.

His harsh spirit will preserve your words, and will not spare either wickedness or bonds.

Beware for yourself, and pay close attention to your hearing, for you walk with your overthrow.

When hearing such things, regard them as though in a dream, and you will remain awake.

Love God throughout your whole life, and call upon him for your salvation.

Every animal loves its own kind; so also every person loves his neighbor.

Every creature joins itself to its kind, and every person associates with one like himself.

[Col. 0434B] If a wolf ever associates with a lamb, so does a sinner with a righteous person.

What fellowship has a holy man with a dog? [Note: [Col. 0433D] Formerly, “with flesh” stood corruptly in place of “with a dog.”] Or what portion has a rich man with a poor man?

The wild ass in the wilderness is the lion’s prey; so also the poor are the pasture of the rich.

And as humility is an abomination to the proud, so the poor man is a curse to the rich.

When a rich man is shaken, he is supported by his friends; but when a humble man falls, he is driven away by his acquaintances.

Many are the rescuers of a deceived rich man: he has spoken proudly, and they have justified him.

The humble man is deceived and is also reproved; he has spoken sensibly, and no place has been given him.

The rich man speaks, and everyone is silent, and they carry his word up to the clouds.

The poor man speaks, and they say, “Who is this?” And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him.

Good is wealth when there is no sin in the conscience; but poverty is most evil in the mouth of the impious.

A person’s heart changes his appearance, whether for good or for evil.

The mark of a good heart and a good face you will find only with difficulty and labor.

## CHAPTER XIV

Blessed is the man who has not fallen through a word from his mouth and has not been stung by sorrow over sin.

Happy is the one who has not had sorrow in his heart and has not fallen away from his hope.

For a greedy and grasping man, possessions are without reason; and for an envious man, what use is gold?

Whoever gathers unjustly from his heart gathers for others, and another will revel in his goods.

Whoever is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? He will not rejoice in his possessions.

There is none worse than one who envies himself; and this is the recompense of his wickedness:

even if he does good, he does it unknowingly and unwillingly; and at last he reveals his wickedness.

The eye of the envious man is evil, and he turns away his face and despises his own soul.

The greedy eye is insatiable in a portion of iniquity; it will not be satisfied until it consumes and dries up the soul.

An evil eye is directed toward evils and will not be satisfied with bread; he will be needy and sorrowful at his own table.

My son, if you have possessions, do good to yourself, and offer God offerings worthy of him.

Remember that death does not delay, and the covenant of the underworld has been shown to you; for the covenant of this world will end in death.

Before your death, do good to your friend, and according to your strength extend your hand and give to the poor.

Do not let a good day pass you by, and do not let a portion of a good gift escape you.

[Col. 0435A] Will you not leave your pains and labors to others at the division of the lot?

Give, and receive, and justify your soul.

Before your death, practice righteousness, for food is not found in the underworld.

Every creature will grow old like grass, and like a leaf bearing fruit on a green tree.

Some are born and others are cast down; so it is with the generation of flesh and blood: one comes to an end and another is born.

Every corruptible work will fail at the end, and the one who performs it will go with it.

But every chosen work will be justified, and the one who performs it will be honored in it.

Blessed is the man who will dwell in wisdom, who will meditate on his righteousness, and who will consider the prudence of God with understanding.

He who devises his ways in his heart, and in his secret places understands, walking after her like an investigator and remaining in her ways;

he who looks through her windows and listens at her doors;

who rests beside her house and fixes a stake in her walls, will set up his tent in her hands, and good things will rest in his tent forever.

He will place his children beneath her shelter, and under her branches he will dwell.

He will be protected beneath her shelter from the heat, and in her glory he will rest.

## CHAPTER XV

Whoever fears God will do good, and whoever is devoted to righteousness will seize it.

And it will meet him like an honored mother, and like a wife from her virginity she will receive him.

She will feed him with the bread of life and understanding, and give him drink from the water of saving wisdom. He will be established in her and will not be shaken.

She will hold him, and he will not be put to shame; she will exalt him among his neighbors.

[Col. 0435C] In the midst of the assembly she will open his mouth, fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothe him with a robe of glory.

She will store up delight and rejoicing for him, and he will inherit an eternal name.

Foolish men will not seize her, but sensible men will meet her. Foolish men will not see her, for she is far from pride and deceit.

Lying men will not remember her, but truthful men will be found in her and will prosper until they behold God.

Praise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner.

For wisdom has proceeded from God; the praise of God’s wisdom will stand, and it will abound in a faithful mouth, and the ruler will give it to him.

Do not say, “It is because of God that she is absent”; for do not do what he hates.

Do not say, “He has caused me to stumble”; for impious men are not necessary to him.

The Lord hates every abomination of error, and it will not be beloved by those who fear him.

From the beginning God established humankind and left them in the hand of their own counsel.

He added his commandments and precepts.

If you wish to keep the commandments, they will preserve you and enable you to practice acceptable faithfulness forever.

He has placed before you water and fire; stretch out your hand toward whichever you choose.

Before a person are life and death, good and evil; whichever pleases him will be given to him.

For the wisdom of God is great, and he is mighty in power, seeing all things without interruption.

The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him, and he knows every work of a human being.

He commanded no one to act impiously, and he gave no one room to sin.

For he does not desire a multitude of faithless and useless children.

## CHAPTER XVI

[Col. 0436A]

Do not rejoice in impious children, even if they multiply, nor delight in them if the fear of God is not in them.

Do not trust their life, and do not regard their labors.

For one who fears God is better than a thousand impious children.

And it is better to die without children than to leave behind impious children.

One sensible person will inhabit a homeland, while a tribe of impious people will be deserted.

My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard things stronger than these.

In the assembly of sinners fire will blaze, and in an unbelieving nation anger will burn.

The ancient giants, who trusted in their own strength and were destroyed, did not pray for their sins.

Nor did he spare the sojourn of Lot, and he cursed them because of the arrogance of their speech.

[Col. 0436B] He did not have mercy on them, destroying the whole nation that exalted itself in its sins.

And as with six hundred thousand foot soldiers who were gathered in the hardness of their heart: if even one had been stiff-necked, it would have been astonishing if he had remained unharmed.

For mercy and wrath belong to him; he is mighty to pardon and to pour out wrath.

According to his mercy, so is his correction; he judges a person according to his works.

The sinner will not escape through plunder, and the patience of the merciful will not delay.

Every mercy will make a place for each person according to the merit of his works and according to the understanding of his pilgrimage.

Do not say, “I shall be hidden from God, and who from above will remember me?”

In a great people I shall not be recognized; for what is my soul among such an immense creation?

Behold heaven and the heaven of heavens, the abyss, and the whole earth, and the things in them: they will be shaken in his sight.

The mountains together, the hills, and the foundations of the earth—when God looks upon them, they will be shaken with trembling.

And among all these things the heart is without understanding, but every heart is understood by him.

Who understands his ways, and the storm which no human eye will see?

For his works are very many and hidden; but who can declare the works of his righteousness? Or who can endure them? For the covenant is far from some, and the examination of all comes at the consummation.

One who is fainthearted devises empty things; the imprudent and erring man devises foolish things.

Hear me, my son, and learn the discipline of understanding, and attend in your heart to my words.

I will speak discipline with equity, and I will search out how to recount wisdom. Attend in your heart to my words; and I speak with uprightness of spirit of the powers that God established in his works from the beginning, and in truth I proclaim his knowledge.

In God’s judgment he distinguished their portions from the beginning, from the establishment of his works, and their beginnings among their nations.

He adorned their works forever; they neither hungered nor labored, and they did not cease from their works.

No one will oppress his neighbor forever.

Do not be unbelieving toward his word.

After this God looked upon the earth and filled it with his good things.

Every living soul declared before his face, and their return is again into it.

## CHAPTER XVII

God created humankind from the earth and made them according to his image.

[Col. 0437A] And again he turns them back into it, and clothes them with strength according to himself.

He gave them a number of days and a fixed time, and gave them authority over the things that are upon the earth.

He placed the fear of them over all flesh, and they ruled the beasts and the birds.

From them he created a helper like themselves; he gave them counsel, a tongue, eyes, ears, and a heart for thinking, and filled them with the discipline of understanding.

He created in them knowledge of the spirit, filled their hearts with understanding, and showed them good and evil.

He set his eye upon their hearts, to show them the greatness of his works [Al. and to show them],

so that they might praise together the name of holiness, boast in his wonders, and recount the greatness of his works.

He added discipline to them and inherited to them the law of life.

He established an eternal covenant with them and showed them his judgments and righteousness.

Their eyes saw the greatness of his glory, and their ears heard the honor of his voice; and he said to them, “Beware of every injustice.”

And he commanded each one concerning his neighbor.

Their ways are always before him; they are not hidden from his eyes.

He appointed a ruler over each nation.

And the portion of God, Israel, was made manifest.

All their works are like the sun in God’s sight, and his eyes continually watch their ways.

The covenants are not hidden from God because of their iniquities.

A person’s almsgiving is like a seal with him, and he will preserve a person’s grace like the apple of the eye.

Afterward he will rise and repay them, recompensing each one upon their heads, and he will turn them back into the innermost parts of the earth.

But to those who repent he gave the way of righteousness, strengthened those who were failing to endure, and appointed for them the portion of truth.

[Col. 0437C] Return to the Lord and abandon your sins.

Pray before the face of the Lord, and lessen your offenses.

Return to the Lord and turn away from your injustice, and hate the abomination exceedingly.

Know the righteous acts and judgments of God; stand in the appointed portion and in the prayer of the Most High God.

Go into the portions of the holy age, with the living and those who give confession to God.

Do not linger in the error of the impious. Confess before death; from the dead, confession perishes as though it were nothing.

You shall confess and praise God; you shall boast and praise God, and you shall boast in his mercies.

How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his propitiation toward those who turn to him!

For not all things can be in human beings, since the son of humankind is not immortal, and they have delighted in the vanity of wickedness.

What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it will fail. Or what is worse than what flesh and blood has devised? Even this will be reproved.

He himself beholds the power of the height of heaven, while all human beings are earth and ashes.

## CHAPTER XVIII

He who lives forever created all things together. God alone will be justified, and he remains the unconquered king forever.

Who is sufficient to recount his works?

For who will investigate his greatness?

Who will declare the power of his majesty, or who will add to the telling of his mercy?

It is not possible to diminish or add to it, nor is it possible to discover the greatness of God.

When a person has finished, then he will begin; and when he has rested, he will be perplexed.

What is a human being, and what is his grace? What is his good, or what is his evil?

[Col. 0438A] The number of human days is, at most, a hundred years; they are counted as a drop of seawater, and the years are as few as a grain of sand compared with the day of eternity.

Therefore God is patient with them and pours out his mercy upon them.

He saw the presumption of their hearts, that it was evil, and he knew their overthrow, that it was wicked.

Therefore he filled them with his propitiation and showed them the way of uprightness.

A human being’s mercy is toward his neighbor, but God’s mercy is over all flesh.

The merciful person teaches and instructs like a shepherd his flock.

He has mercy on the one who receives instruction in mercy, and on the one who hastens in his judgments.

My son, do not give cause for complaint in good things, and with every gift do not give sorrow through an evil word.

Does not dew cool the heat? So a good word is better than a gift.

Is not a word indeed better than a good gift? Yet both are found with a justified person.

A fool will reproach sharply, and a gift from an undisciplined person makes the eyes waste away.

Before judgment, prepare righteousness for yourself, and before you speak, learn.

Before illness, apply medicine; and before judgment, examine yourself, and you will find propitiation in the sight of God.

Before illness, humble yourself, and in the time of sickness show your conduct.

Do not be prevented from praying always, and do not fear being justified even unto death, for God’s reward remains forever.

Before prayer, prepare your soul, and do not be like a person who tempts God.

Remember wrath on the day of consummation, and the time of retribution when the face is turned away.

Remember poverty in a time of abundance, and the needs of poverty on the day of riches.

From morning until evening time changes, and all these things are swift in the eyes of God.

A wise person will fear in all things, and in days of offenses will beware of negligence.

Every clever person recognizes wisdom, and to the one who finds it he will give praise.

Those who are sensible in words also act wisely; they understand truth and righteousness, and fulfill proverbs and judgments.

Do not go after your desires, and turn away from your will.

If you grant your soul its desires, it will make you a joy to your enemies.

Do not [Al. Do not] delight in crowds or in small things, for their commission is continual.

Do not be mediocre in contention arising from interest, while you have nothing in your purse; for you will be envious of your own life.

## CHAPTER XIX

[Col. 0438D] A drunken laborer will not become rich, and whoever despises small things will gradually fall.

Wine and women make wise men apostatize, and they reprove the sensible.

Whoever joins himself to prostitutes will become worthless; decay and worms will inherit him, and he will be raised up as a great example and removed from the number of the living.

Whoever believes too quickly is lighthearted and will be diminished; and whoever sins against his own soul will be held guilty besides.

Whoever rejoices in iniquity will be marked out; and whoever hates correction will have his life shortened; whoever hates talkativeness destroys wickedness.

Whoever sins against his own soul will repent; and whoever delights in wickedness will be marked out.

Do not repeat a wicked and harsh word, and you will not be diminished.

Do not tell your understanding to friend or enemy; and if you have committed a fault, do not expose it.

[Col. 0439A] For he will hear you, guard it, and, as though defending the sin, hate you; and so he will always be present against you.

Have you heard a word against your neighbor? Let it die within you, trusting that it will not burst you.

At the face of a word the fool gives birth, like the groaning of a woman giving birth to a child.

A word in the heart of a fool is like an arrow fixed in the thigh of flesh.

Correct your friend, lest he perhaps has not understood and says, “I did not do it”; or, if he did it, lest he do it again.

Correct your neighbor, lest he perhaps has not said it; and, if he has said it, lest he repeat it.

Correct your friend, for a fault often occurs.

And do not believe every word: there is one who slips with his tongue but not from his heart.

For who is there who has not sinned with his tongue? Correct your neighbor before you threaten him.

And give place to the fear of the Most High, for all wisdom is the fear of God: in it is fearing God, and in all wisdom is the ordering of the law.

[Col. 0439B] There is no discipline in wickedness, and the thought of sinners is not prudence.

There is wickedness, and in it there is abomination; and there is a foolish person who diminishes wisdom.

Better is a person who is deficient in wisdom and lacking in understanding but fears God than one who abounds in understanding and transgresses the law of the Most High.

There is a certain cleverness, and it itself is unjust; and there is one who utters a reliable word while proclaiming truth.

There is one who humbles himself wickedly, while his inward parts are full of deceit.

There is one who submits himself excessively through much humility; and there is one who inclines his face and pretends not to see what he does not know.

Even if prevented from sinning by weakness of strength, if he finds an opportunity to do evil, he will do it.

A man is recognized by his appearance, and a sensible person is recognized by the encounter with his face.

A person’s clothing, the laughter of his teeth, and his manner of walking [Col. 0439C] declare what he is.

There is a false correction in the anger of an abusive person; there is a judgment that is not proved to be good; and there is one who remains silent, and he is prudent.

## CHAPTER XX

How good it is to rebuke rather than to become angry, and not to prevent one who confesses in prayer!

The desire of a eunuch will deflower a young girl.

So does one who uses force to carry out an unjust judgment.

How good it is to reveal repentance after being corrected! For thus you will escape deliberate sin.

There is one who remains silent and is found wise; and there is one who is hateful because he is bold in speaking.

There is one who remains silent because he lacks the sense for speech; and there is one who remains silent because he knows the proper time.

A wise person will remain silent until the proper time; but the licentious and imprudent will not observe the time.

Whoever uses many words injures his soul, and whoever unjustly assumes authority will be hated.

There is a progression into evils for an undisciplined person, and there is a discovery resulting in harm.

There is a gift that is not useful, and there is a gift whose repayment is double.

There is one who is diminished because of glory, and there is one who lifts up his head from humiliation.

There is one who buys back many things for a small price and restores them sevenfold.

A wise person makes himself loved by his words, but the graces of fools will be poured out.

A gift from a fool will not benefit you, for his eyes are sevenfold [i.e. watchful].

He will give little and reproach much, and the opening of his mouth is an inflammation.

Today someone lends at interest, and tomorrow he demands repayment; such a person is hateful.

A fool will have no friend, and there will be no gratitude for his good things.

[Col. 0440A] For those who eat his bread are false-tongued. How often, and by how much, will they mock him! For he did not distribute directly, with sound judgment, what was meant to be possessed; and likewise what was not meant to be possessed [Al. omits “was”].

The fall of a false tongue is like one who falls on a pavement; so the downfall of the wicked will come swiftly.

An ungracious man, like an empty tale, will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.

A proverb will be rejected from the mouth of a fool, for he does not speak it at its proper time.

There is one who is prevented from sinning because of poverty, and in his rest he will be stung.

There is one who will lose his soul through shame, and will lose it because of an imprudent person; but through showing partiality to persons he will destroy himself.

There is one who, through shame, makes a promise to a friend and gains an enemy for nothing.

A wicked reproach is falsehood in a person, and it will continually be in the mouth of the undisciplined.

A thief is better than the persistence of a lying person; but both will inherit destruction.

The conduct of lying people is without honor, and their shame is with them without interruption.

A wise person will advance himself through words, and a prudent man will please the great.

Whoever cultivates his land will heap up a harvest, and whoever practices righteousness will himself be exalted; but whoever pleases the great will escape injustice.

Gifts and presents blind the eyes of judges, and, like a muzzle on the mouth, turn away their corrections [Al. correction].

What use are hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure in either case?

Better is one who conceals his folly than a person who hides his wisdom.

## CHAPTER XXI

My son, have you sinned? Do not add to it again; but pray concerning your former sins [Col. 0440C], that they may be forgiven you.

Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent; for if you approach them, they will seize you.

His teeth are the teeth of a lion, killing human souls.

Every iniquity is like a two-edged sword; there is no healing for its wound.

Reproach and insult will annul wealth, and a house that is excessively rich will be brought to nothing by pride; so the wealth of the proud will be uprooted.

The prayer of the poor comes from his mouth to his ears, and judgment will quickly come upon him.

Whoever hates correction is a sinner’s footprint; but whoever fears God will turn back to his heart.

One powerful in bold speech is known from afar, and the sensible man knows that he himself may slip.

Whoever builds his house at another’s expense is like one who gathers his stones in winter.

The gathering of sinners is stubble, and their end is a flame of fire.

The way of sinners is paved with stones, but at their end are the underworld, darkness, and punishments.

Whoever guards righteousness will preserve his understanding.

The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding.

One who is not wise will not be instructed in goodness.

But there is wisdom that abounds in evil, and there is no understanding where there is bitterness.

The knowledge of the wise will abound like a flood, and his counsel will remain like a fountain of life.

The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel; it will retain no wisdom.

Whatever wise word he hears, the learned person will praise and add it to himself; the licentious person hears it, dislikes it, and throws it behind his back.

The account of a fool is like a burden on the road, but grace will be found on the lips of the sensible.

The mouth of the prudent is sought in the assembly, and they will ponder his words in their hearts.

[Col. 0441A] Wisdom is like a demolished house to a fool, and the knowledge of the senseless consists of unutterable words.

Instruction is fetters on a fool’s feet, and like manacles upon his right hand.

A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a wise man will scarcely laugh quietly.

Instruction is an ornament of gold to the prudent, and like a bracelet on the right arm.

A fool’s foot is quick to enter his neighbor’s house, but a knowledgeable person will be ashamed before a powerful person.

A fool looks through the window into the house, but an educated person will stand outside.

It is folly for a person to listen at the door; a prudent person will be burdened by the insult.

The lips of the imprudent will tell foolish things, but the words of the prudent will be weighed on a balance.

In the mouth of fools is their heart, but in the heart of the wise is their mouth.

While the impious curses the devil, he curses his own soul.

[Col. 0441B] A whisperer defiles his own soul and will be hated by all; whoever remains with him will be hateful. One who is silent and sensible will be honored.

## CHAPTER XXII

A lazy person is pelted with stones of clay, and everyone will speak of his contemptible condition.

A lazy person is pelted with cow dung, and everyone who touches him shakes his hands.

An undisciplined son is a disgrace to his father; but a daughter will become a diminishment.

A prudent daughter is an inheritance to her husband, but one who causes shame becomes a disgrace to her father.

The bold man disgraces both father and husband; he will not be lessened by the impious, but will be dishonored by both.

Music in mourning is an untimely tale; scourges and instruction are wisdom at every time.

Whoever teaches a fool is like one who glues together a potsherd.

Whoever tells a word to one who does not listen is like one who awakens [Col. 0441C] a sleeper from deep sleep.

One who recounts wisdom to a sleeping person speaks with a fool; and at the end of the account he says, “Who is this?”

Weep over the dead, for his light has failed; and weep over the fool, for his understanding has failed [Al. is failing].

Weep little over the dead, for he has found rest.

The life of the most wicked is worse than the death of a fool.

The mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for the fool and the impious it lasts all the days of their life.

Do not speak much with a fool, and do not walk with the senseless.

Keep yourself from him, lest you have trouble and be defiled by his sin.

Turn away from him, and you will find rest, and you will not be wearied by his folly.

What can be heavier than lead? And what other name does he have than “fool”?

It is easier to carry sand, salt, and a mass of iron than an imprudent, foolish, and impious person.

A wooden brace fastened in the foundation of a building will not be loosened; so is a heart established in the thought of counsel.

The thought of a sensible person will not be corrupted by fear at any time.

As stakes on high ground and masonry laid without expense will not stand against the face of the wind,

so a timid heart in the thought of a fool will not withstand the force of fear.

As a trembling heart in the thought of a fool fears at no time, so is the one who always remains in the commandments of God.

Pricking the eye brings forth tears, and one who pricks the heart brings forth understanding.

Throwing a stone at birds will bring them down; so whoever insults a friend dissolves friendship.

Even if you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back. To a friend—

If you open your mouth in sorrow, do not be afraid, for reconciliation is possible, [Col. 0442A] except in the case of insult, reproach, pride, revelation of a secret, or a treacherous wound; in all these cases a friend will flee.

Keep faith with a friend in his poverty, so that you may also rejoice in his prosperity.

Remain faithful to him in the time of his tribulation, so that you may also be a fellow-heir of his inheritance.

Before the fire of a furnace there is vapor, and the smoke of fire rises upward; so before bloodshed come curses, insults, and threats.

I will not be ashamed to greet a friend, nor hide myself from his face; and if evils come upon me through him, I will endure them.

Everyone who hears will beware of him.

Who will set a guard over my mouth and a sure seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall because of them and my tongue may not destroy me?

## CHAPTER XXIII
[Col. 0442B] Lord, Father and Ruler of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel, nor [Alt.: do not] let me fall into it.

Who will set scourges upon my thoughts and the instruction of wisdom in my heart, so that they may not spare me for their ignorances, and their offenses may not appear?

And so that my ignorance may not increase, my offenses multiply, my sins abound, and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me?

Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to their thoughts.

Do not give me haughtiness of eyes, and turn every desire away from me.

Take away from me the desires of the belly; do not let the lusts of sexual intercourse seize me, nor hand me over to a shameless and undisciplined soul.

Hear the teaching of the mouth, children; whoever guards it will not perish by his lips, nor stumble in the most wicked deeds.

[Col. 0442C] The sinner is caught in his vanity, and the proud and slanderous man will stumble through them.

Do not accustom your mouth to swearing, for many are the falls that come from it.

Let the naming of God not be constant in your mouth, and do not mix yourself with the names of the Holy Ones, for you will not be free from guilt concerning them.

For just as a servant who is constantly questioned is not freed from the whip, so everyone who swears and invokes God will not be cleansed entirely from sin.

A man who swears much will be filled with iniquity, and the scourge will not depart from his house.

If he fails in his undertaking, his offense will be upon him; and if he dissimulates, he sins twice over [Alt.: he will sin twice].

If he swears in vain, he will not be justified, for his household will be filled with retribution.

There is also another kind of speech that leads to death; let it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob.

[Col. 0442D] For all these things will be removed from the merciful, and they will not wallow in sins.

Do not accustom your mouth to undisciplined speech, for there is sinful speech in it.

Remember your father and your mother, for you sit in the midst of great men.

Lest God forget you in their presence, and, made foolish by your constant association with them, you suffer reproach, and wish that you had not been born, and curse the day of your birth.

A man accustomed to reproachful words will not be instructed throughout all his days.

Two kinds abound in sins, and a third brings anger and destruction.

A hot-tempered soul, like a burning fire, will not be extinguished until it has swallowed something;

and a wicked man, in the mouth of his flesh, will not cease until he has kindled a fire.

[Col. 0443A] Every bread is sweet to the fornicator; he will not tire of transgressing to the end.

Every man who transgresses against his marriage-bed, despising his own soul and saying, “Who sees me?

Darkness surrounds me, and the walls cover me, and no one looks around me; whom should I fear? The Most High will not remember my sins.”

He does not understand that the eye of God sees everything, that the fear of such a man drives the fear of God from him, and that he fears the eyes of men;

nor does he know that the eyes of the Lord are much brighter than the sun, observing all the ways of men, and the depth of the abyss, and looking into the hearts of men in their hidden places.

For all things are known to the Lord God before they were created; so also, after completion, he observes everything.

This man will be punished in the streets of the city, and will be driven away like a young horse; where he does not expect it, he will be seized.

[Col. 0443B] And he will be a disgrace to all, because he did not understand the fear of the Lord.

So too every woman who abandons her husband and establishes an inheritance from another marriage.

For first she was unfaithful to the law of the Most High; second, she sinned against her husband; third, she committed fornication in adultery and established children for herself by another man.

She will be brought into the assembly, and attention will be paid to her children.

Her children will not put down roots, and her branches will not bear fruit.

She will leave her memory as a curse, and her disgrace will not be wiped away.

Those who are left behind will recognize that nothing is better than the fear of God, and nothing sweeter than to attend to the commandments of the Lord.

Great glory belongs to following the Lord, for length of days will be received from him.

## CHAPTER XXIV

[Col. 0443C]

Wisdom will praise herself and will be honored in God, and will glory in the midst of her people.

In the assemblies of the Most High she will open her mouth, and in the presence of his power she will glory.

She will be exalted in the midst of her people, and will be admired in the holy assembly.

Among the multitude of the elect she will receive praise, and among the blessed she will be blessed, saying:

“I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature.

I made the light arise in the heavens, unfailing, and like a mist I covered the whole earth.

I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.

Alone I traversed the circuit of heaven, and penetrated the depth of the abyss; I walked upon the waves of the sea.

I stood throughout the whole earth and among every people.

I held primacy among every nation.

[Col. 0443D] I trampled by my power the hearts of all the eminent and the humble; among all these I sought a place of rest, and I shall dwell in the inheritance of the Lord.

Then the Creator of all commanded and said to me—and he who created me rested in my tabernacle—

‘Dwell in Jacob, and receive your inheritance in Israel, and take root among my elect.’

From the beginning, before the ages, I was created, and until the age to come I shall not cease; in the holy dwelling-place I ministered before him.

And so I was established in Zion, and likewise I rested in the sanctified city, and my power was in Jerusalem.

I took root among an honored people, and my inheritance was in the portion of my God, and my dwelling was in the fullness of the holy ones.

I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and like a cypress on Mount Zion.

I was exalted like a palm tree in Kadesh, and like a rose planting in Jericho.

[Col. 0444A] Like a beautiful olive tree in the fields, and like a plane tree I was exalted beside the water in the streets.

Like cinnamon and balsam giving forth fragrance, I gave perfume; like chosen myrrh I gave sweetness of scent.

Like storax, galbanum, onycha, and aromatic resin, and like uncut frankincense, I gave forth fragrance in my dwelling; my scent was like unmixed balsam.

Like a terebinth I spread out my branches, and my branches were branches of honor and grace.

Like a vine I produced the sweetness of fragrance, and my blossoms were fruits of honor and beauty.

I am the mother of beautiful love, of fear, of knowledge, and of holy hope.

In me is every grace of the way and of truth; in me is every hope of life and virtue.

Come over to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits.

For my spirit is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

[Col. 0444B] My memory is for generations of ages.

Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst.

Whoever listens to me will not be put to shame, and those who work in me will not sin.

Those who make me shine forth will possess eternal life.

All this is the book of life, the covenant of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth.

Moses commanded the law in statutes of justice, as an inheritance for the house of Jacob and promises for Israel.

He appointed David his servant to raise up from him a most powerful king, seated forever upon a throne of honor.

He fills, like the Pishon, with wisdom, and like the Tigris in the days of new growth.

He fills, like the Euphrates, with understanding; he multiplies, like the Jordan in harvest time.

He sends instruction like light, and stands forth like the Gihon on the day of vintage.

[Col. 0444C] He was the first to know it fully, and one weaker will not investigate it.

For his thought overflowed from the sea, and his counsel from the great abyss.

I, Wisdom, poured out rivers.

I was like a channel of immense water from a river, like the channel of the Dioryx, and like an aqueduct I went forth in Paradise.

I said, ‘I will water my garden of plantations and saturate the fruit of my meadow.’

And behold, my channel became abundant, and my river approached the sea.

For I enlighten all with instruction like the dawn, and I shall declare it to the distant regions.

I shall penetrate all the lower parts of the earth, and inspect all who sleep, and enlighten all who hope in the Lord.

I shall still pour forth instruction like prophecy, and leave it for those who seek wisdom; I shall not cease through their generations, unto the holy age.

[Col. 0444D] See that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek out the truth.

## CHAPTER XXV

In three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and human beings:

The concord of brothers, the love of neighbors, and a husband and wife who agree well with one another.

My soul hates three kinds of people, and I am greatly burdened by their souls:

A proud poor man; a lying rich man; a foolish and senseless old man.

What you did not gather in your youth, how will you find in your old age?

How beautiful is the judgment of a song, and for elders to know counsel!

How beautiful is wisdom among the aged, and understanding and counsel among the honored!

[Col. 0445A] The crown of the aged is extensive experience, and their glory is the fear of God.

Nine things I have considered beyond suspicion in my heart, and I shall mention a tenth with my tongue to human beings:

A man who rejoices in his children, while living and seeing the downfall of his enemies.

Blessed is he who dwells with a sensible wife, who has not slipped with his tongue, and who has not served those unworthy of him.

Blessed is he who has found a true friend, and who declares righteousness to an ear that listens.

How great is the one who has found wisdom and knowledge! Yet none is above the one who fears the Lord.

The fear of God has placed itself above all things.

Blessed is the person to whom it has been granted to possess the fear of God; whoever holds it, with whom can he be compared?

The fear of God is the beginning of his love, but the beginning of faith must be joined to it.

Every wound is a wound of the heart, and every wickedness is the wickedness of a woman.

And every wound, but not a wound of the heart;

[Col. 0445B] every wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman;

every assault, but not the assault of those who hate;

and every vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies.

There is no head more wicked than the head of a serpent,

and there is no anger above the anger of a woman. I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon than live with a wicked woman.

The wickedness of a woman changes her face, and darkens her countenance like a bear, and she displays herself like a sack among her neighbors.

Her husband groans, and when he hears her he sighs faintly.

Every wickedness is brief compared with the wickedness of a woman; the lot of sinners will fall upon her.

As a sandy ascent is to the feet of an old man, so is a talkative woman to a quiet man.

Do not look upon a woman’s beauty, and do not desire a woman for her appearance.

A woman’s anger, irreverence, and great shame—

If a woman holds primacy, she is contrary to her husband.

[Col. 0445C] A humble heart, a sorrowful face, and a wounded heart: a wicked woman.

Weak hands and loosened knees: a woman who does not make her husband blessed.

From a woman sin had its beginning, and through her we all die.

Do not give your water an outlet, not even a little, nor grant a wicked woman leave to go out.

If she does not walk at your hand, she will shame you in the presence of your enemies.

Cut her off from your flesh, lest she continually abuse you.

## CHAPTER XXVI

Blessed is the husband of a good wife, for the number of his years is doubled.

A strong woman delights her husband, and will complete the years of his life in peace.

A good wife is a good portion; she will be given to a man in the portion of those who fear God, for his good deeds.

But the heart of both rich and poor is good when their faces are cheerful at all times.

Three things my heart feared, and at the fourth my face was afraid:

A city informer, and a gathering of the people;

a lying accusation—more grievous than death;

and the sorrow of the heart and mourning caused by a jealous woman.

In a jealous woman there is a scourge of the tongue, sharing itself with everyone.

As a good yoke that moves easily, so is a wicked woman to the one who holds her—like someone who has seized a scorpion.

An intoxicated woman causes great anger; her insult and disgrace will not be covered.

The fornication of a woman is recognized by the haughtiness of her eyes and by her eyelids.

[Col. 0446A] With a daughter who does not turn away, keep firm watch, lest she find an opportunity and use it.

Beware of all the irreverence of her eyes, and do not be surprised if she neglects you.

As a thirsty traveler opens his mouth toward a spring, so she will drink from every nearby water and sit down opposite every stake, and open her quiver against every arrow, until she is exhausted.

The grace of an attentive wife delights her husband, and will fatten his bones.

Her discipline is a gift from God.

A sensible and quiet woman: there is no exchange for a well-instructed soul.

Grace upon grace is a holy and modest woman.

But no weighing is worthy of a self-controlled soul.

As the rising sun is to the world in the heights of God, so is the appearance of a good woman an ornament to her house.

A shining lamp upon a holy lampstand, and a beautiful face upon a firm age.

[Col. 0446B] Golden columns upon silver bases, and firm feet upon the feet of a stable woman.

Eternal foundations upon solid rock, and the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman.

There are two things at which my heart was saddened, and at the third anger came upon me:

A warrior failing through poverty; and a sensible man despised;

and one who turns from righteousness to sin—God has prepared him for the sword.

Two kinds of people appeared to me difficult and dangerous. It is difficult for a merchant to strip himself of negligence, and a tavernkeeper will not be justified from sins of the lips.

## CHAPTER XXVII

Because of poverty many have sinned, and whoever seeks to grow rich turns away his eye.

As a peg is driven into the joint of stones, so sin will be wedged between the middle of selling and buying.

The offense will be crushed together with the offender.

If you do not hold yourself firmly in the fear of the Lord, your house will quickly be overthrown.

As dust remains in the shaking of a sieve, so a person’s uncertainty remains in his thoughts.

The furnace tests the potter’s vessels, and the trial of tribulation tests righteous people.

As a tree’s fruit reveals its cultivation, so a word reveals the thought of a person’s heart.

Do not praise a man before his speech; this is the testing of human beings.

If you pursue righteousness, you will grasp it, clothe yourself with it like an honored robe, and dwell with it; it will protect you forever, and on the day of knowledge you will find stability.

Birds flock to their own kind, and truth returns to those who practice it.

A lion always lies in wait for prey; so do sins for those who practice iniquities.

A holy man remains in wisdom like the sun, but a fool changes like the moon.

Among the senseless, keep your word according to the occasion; among thoughtful people, be constant.

The tale of sinners is hateful, and their laughter is in the delights of sin.

A tongue that swears much will set the hair on the head on end, and its irreverence is a stopping of the ears.

The shedding of blood in the quarrel of the proud, and their curse is grievous to hear.

Whoever exposes the secrets of a friend loses faithfulness and will not find a friend according to his heart.

Love your neighbor and join yourself to him in faith.

But if you expose his hidden matters, do not pursue him afterward.

For as a man who loses his friend, so is one who loses the friendship of his neighbor.

[Col. 0447A] And as one who releases a bird from his hand, so you have abandoned your neighbor and will not catch him.

Do not pursue him, for he is far away; he has fled like a doe from a snare, because his soul has been wounded.

You will no longer be able to bind him together with you; reconciliation is accursed.

But to expose a friend’s secrets is despair for an unhappy soul.

He who winks with his eye contrives wickedness, and no one will cast him off.

In the presence of your eyes he will trample his mouth, and will marvel at your words; but at last he will pervert his mouth and turn your words into a stumbling-block.

I have hated many things, but have not equated him with them, and the Lord will hate him.

Whoever throws a stone upward will have it fall upon his own head, and a treacherous blow will divide the wounds of the treacherous man.

Whoever digs a pit will fall into it; whoever sets a stone before his neighbor will stumble over it; whoever lays a snare for another will perish in it.

The wicked counsel he devises will roll back upon him, and he will not know where it came upon him from.

Mockery and reproach are for the proud, and vengeance will lie in wait for him like a lion.

Those who delight in the fall of the righteous will perish in a snare; pain will consume them before they die.

Anger and fury are both abominable, and the sinful man will be subject to them.

## CHAPTER XXVIII

Whoever wishes to take revenge will find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely preserve his sins.

Forgive your neighbor who has harmed you; then, when he entreats you, your sins will be forgiven.

A person reserves anger against another person, and seeks healing from God.

He has no mercy on a person like himself, [Col. 0447C] yet he entreats for his own sins?

Though he is flesh, he reserves anger, and asks for pardon from God? Who will plead for his offenses?

Remember the last things, and cease from enmity;

for decay and death threaten in his commandments.

Remember the fear of God, and do not be angry with your neighbor.

Remember the covenant of the Most High, and overlook your neighbor’s ignorance.

Abstain from strife, and you will lessen your sins.

For an angry person kindles strife, and a sinful man disturbs friends and casts enmity among those who have peace.

As wood determines the forest, so the fire blazes; according to a person’s strength, so will be his anger, and according to his substance he will exalt his wrath.

Hastiness in fighting kindles fire, and hasty quarrels shed blood, and a tongue that bears witness brings death.

If you blow upon a spark, it will blaze like a fire; if you spit upon it, it will be extinguished. Both proceed from the mouth.

The whisperer and the double-tongued are accursed, for they will disturb many who have peace.

The third tongue has stirred up many and scattered them from nation to nation.

It has destroyed the fortified cities of the rich and dug up the houses of great men.

It has overthrown the strength of peoples and dissolved mighty nations.

The third tongue has expelled married women and deprived them of their labors.

Whoever pays attention to it will have no rest, nor will he have a friend in whom he may rest.

The blow of a whip leaves a bruise, but the blow of the tongue crushes bones.

Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as those who have perished through their own tongue.

Blessed is he who is sheltered from a wicked tongue, who has not passed into its anger, who has not drawn its yoke upon himself, and who has not been bound in its chains.

For its yoke is an iron yoke, and its bond is a bronze bond.

Its death is a most evil death, and Sheol is more useful than it.

Its endurance will not last, but it will seize the ways of the unjust; in its flame it will not burn the righteous.

Those who abandon God will fall into it; it will blaze against them and not be extinguished, and it will be sent against them like a lion and injure them like a leopard.

Fence your ears with thorns; do not listen to a wicked tongue. Make doors and bolts for your mouth.

Refine your gold and silver, and make a balance for your words, and straight reins for your mouth.

Pay attention, lest you slip with your tongue, fall before enemies lying in wait for you, and your fall be incurable unto death.

## CHAPTER XXIX

[Col. 0448B]

Whoever shows mercy lends to his neighbor, and whoever prevails by his hand keeps the commandments.

Lend to your neighbor in his time of need, and repay your neighbor again at the proper time.

Confirm your word and act faithfully toward him, and at all times you will find what you need.

Many have regarded a loan as a windfall and caused trouble for those who helped them.

Until they receive it, they kiss the hands of the giver and humble their voice in promises.

But at the time of repayment he will ask for time, speak words of annoyance and murmuring, and make excuses about the time.

If he is able to repay, he will oppose him; he will scarcely return half the principal and will count that as a gain.

But if not, he will defraud him of his money and acquire him as an enemy for nothing.

[Col. 0448C] He will return feasts and curses to him, and for honor and benefit he will repay him with insult.

Many have not lent, not because of wickedness, but because they feared being defrauded for nothing.

Nevertheless, be more generous toward the humble in spirit, and do not keep him waiting for almsgiving.

For the sake of the commandment, take up the poor man, and because of his poverty do not send him away empty-handed.

Lose your money for the sake of your brother and friend, and do not hide it under a stone for destruction.

Place your treasure in the commandments of the Most High, and it will benefit you more than gold.

Enclose almsgiving in the heart of the poor, and it will plead for you against every evil.

More than a mighty shield and a spear, it will fight against your enemy.

A good man gives security for his neighbor,

but whoever loses his sense of shame abandons him.

Do not forget the gratitude due to a guarantor, for he gave his life for you.

[Col. 0448D] The sinner and the unclean man flee a pledge.

The sinner claims the guarantor’s goods for himself.

And ungrateful in understanding, he abandons the one who freed him.

A man gives security for his neighbor, and when he has lost respect, he will be abandoned by him.

A most wicked pledge has ruined many who were prospering and tossed them about like waves of the sea.

It has forced powerful men to migrate, and they have wandered among foreign nations.

The sinful transgressor of the Lord’s command will fall into a wicked promise, and whoever tries to do many things will fall into judgment.

Recover your neighbor according to your ability, and take care lest you fall.

The beginning of a person’s life is water and bread, clothing, and a house protecting his shame.

The poor man’s food beneath a shelter of boards is better than splendid feasts abroad without a dwelling.

[Col. 0449A] Let the little seem great to you, and you will not hear the reproach of exile.

Wretched is the life of lodging from house to house; wherever he lodges, he will not act confidently or open his mouth.

He will lodge, feed, and give drink to the ungrateful, and in addition to these things he will hear bitter words.

“Pass on, guest, and set the table; feed the others with what you have in your hand.”

“Go out from the presence of the honor of my friends; because of the necessity of my house, my brother has become a guest to me.”

These things are grievous to a sensible person: the correction of the household and the reproach of a moneylender.

## CHAPTER XXX

Whoever loves his son will frequently chastise him, so that he may rejoice at his end and not knock at the doors of his neighbors.

Whoever teaches his son will be praised through him and will glory in him among his household.

Whoever teaches his son provokes his enemy to jealousy, and will glory in him among his friends.

His father is dead, yet it is as though he were not dead, for he has left behind someone like himself.

During his life he saw him and rejoiced in him; at his death he was not saddened, nor was he ashamed before his enemies.

For he left a defender of the house against enemies and one who repays kindness to friends.

For the sake of his children’s lives he will bind up his wounds, and his inward parts will be disturbed at every cry.

An unbroken horse turns out stubborn, and an undisciplined son turns out headstrong.

Fondle your son, and he will make you afraid; play with him, and he will grieve you.

Do not smile at him, lest you suffer pain, and at the end your teeth chatter.

Do not give him power in his youth, and do not disregard his thoughts.

Bend his neck in his youth, and beat his sides while he is a child, lest he become stubborn and not believe you, and he become a grief to your soul.

Teach your son and discipline him, lest you stumble over his disgrace.

A poor man who is healthy and strong in bodily power is better than a rich man who is weak and afflicted by wickedness.

The health of the soul in the holiness of righteousness is better than all gold and silver, and a strong body than immense wealth.

There is no wealth greater than bodily health, and no pleasure greater than joy of heart.

Death is better than a bitter life, and eternal rest than persistent sickness.

Good things hidden in a closed mouth are like dishes of food set around a tomb.

What benefit is a libation to an idol? It will neither eat nor smell it.

So is one who is driven away by the Lord, carrying wages of iniquity,

seeing with his eyes and groaning, like a eunuch embracing a virgin and sighing.

[Col. 0449D] Do not give sadness to your soul, and do not afflict yourself by your own counsel.

The joy of the heart is the life of a person, and a treasure of unfailing holiness; the exultation of a person is longevity.

Have mercy on your soul by pleasing God, and exercise restraint. Gather your heart into his holiness, and drive sadness far from you.

For sadness has killed many, and there is no benefit in it.

Jealousy and anger shorten days, and anxiety brings old age before its time.

A bright heart and a good one is fitting at banquets, for its feasts are carefully prepared.

## CHAPTER XXXI

Wakefulness over wealth will waste away the flesh, and its anxiety will take away sleep.

[Col. 0450A] Anxiety about provision turns aside understanding, and severe illness makes the soul sober.

The rich man labored in gathering possessions, and in his repose he will be filled with his goods.

The poor man labored in the reduction of food, and in the end he becomes needy.

Whoever loves gold will not be justified, and whoever pursues corruption will be filled with it.

Many have been given over to ruin through gold, and their destruction has come through its appearance.

Gold is a stumbling-block to those who sacrifice to it; woe to those who pursue it, and every imprudent person will perish through it.

Blessed is the rich man who was found without blemish, who did not go after gold, nor hope in money and treasures.

Who is this, that we may praise him? For he has done wonders in his life.

Whoever has been tested in this matter and proved perfect will have eternal glory: he could transgress, but did not transgress; he could do evil, but did not do it.

Therefore his goods have been established in the Lord, and the whole assembly of the holy ones will recount his almsgiving.

Have you sat at a great table? Do not open your throat over it first.

Do not say, “There are many things upon it.”

Remember that the evil eye is wicked.

What has been created more wicked than the eye? Therefore it will weep from every face when it sees.

Do not stretch out your hand first, lest, contaminated by envy, you be ashamed.

Do not be squeezed at a banquet.

Understand your neighbor’s circumstances from your own.

Use, like a frugal person, what is set before you, lest, when you eat much, you become hateful.

Stop first for the sake of discipline, and do not be excessive, lest you offend.

And if you sit among many, do not stretch out your hand before them, [Col. 0450C] nor ask to drink first.

How sufficient a little wine is for an educated person! You will not be troubled by it in sleep, and you will not feel pain.

Wakefulness, biliousness, and torment belong to an undisciplined man.

Sleep is health for a frugal person; he will sleep until morning, and his soul will delight with him.

And if you are compelled to eat much, rise from the middle, vomit, and you will feel relief, and you will not bring illness upon your body.

Listen to me, son, and do not despise me; at the end you will find my words.

In all your works be swift, and no illness will overtake you.

The lips of many will bless one generous with bread, and the testimony to his generosity will be reliable.

The city will murmur against one miserly with bread, and its testimony to his wickedness is true.

Do not provoke those who love wine, for wine has destroyed many.

[Col. 0450D] Fire tests hard iron; so wine will expose the hearts of the proud when drunk in intoxication.

Wine is a fitting life for human beings when taken soberly; if you drink it moderately, you will be sober.

What life is there for one who is diminished by wine?

What deprives life? Death.

Wine was created for gladness, and not for drunkenness, from the beginning.

Wine drunk moderately is exultation of soul and heart.

Sober drinking is health to soul and body.

Wine drunk in excess causes irritation, anger, and many disasters.

Wine drunk in excess is bitterness of soul.

The violence of drunkenness is the offense of the imprudent; it diminishes strength and causes wounds.

At a banquet of wine do not rebuke your neighbor, and do not despise him in his enjoyment.

[Col. 0451A] Do not speak words of reproach to him, and do not press him by repeating the matter.

## CHAPTER XXXII

Have they appointed you ruler? Do not become proud; be among them as one of themselves.

Care for them, and then sit down confidently, having completed all your care,

so that you may rejoice because of them, receive the crown as an adornment of favor, and obtain the honor of the gathering.

Speak, elder, for it is fitting for you.

Let your first word be with careful knowledge, and do not interrupt the music.

Where there is no listening, do not pour out speech, and do not inopportunely exalt yourself in your wisdom.

A gem of carbuncle in a gold ornament, and the comparison of musicians at a banquet of wine.

As an emerald is a mark in a work of gold, so is the number of musicians in pleasant and moderate wine.

Listen silently, and good favor will come to you out of reverence.

[Col. 0451B] Young man, speak in your own cause only with difficulty.

If you are questioned twice, let your answer be brief.

In many matters be like one who does not know, and listen silently while also asking questions.

Do not presume among great men, and where there are elders do not speak much.

Before hail comes lightning; before shame comes grace, and because of reverence good favor will come to you.

At the time of rising do not delay; go ahead first to your house, and there amuse yourself there and play there,

and carry out your plans, but not in sins or arrogant speech.

And above all these things bless the Lord who made you and who satisfies you with all his goods.

Whoever fears the Lord will receive his instruction, and those who keep watch for him will find blessing.

Whoever seeks the law will be filled with it, and whoever acts treacherously will stumble in it.

Those who fear the Lord will find just judgment, and will kindle righteous judgments like a light.

A sinful man will avoid correction and will find a comparison according to his own will.

A man of counsel will not destroy understanding; a stranger and a proud man will not fear dread,

even after he has acted without counsel, and he will be convicted by his own pursuits.

Son, do nothing without counsel, and after acting you will not repent.

Do not go on the way of ruin, and do not stumble over stones. Do not trust yourself to a difficult road, lest you place a stumbling-block before your soul.

Beware of your children, and pay attention to your household.

In all your work trust with the faith of your soul, for this is the keeping of the commandments.

Whoever believes in God attends to the commandments, and whoever trusts in him will not be diminished.

## CHAPTER XXXIII

[Col. 0451D]

Evils will not meet the one who fears the Lord; in temptation God will preserve him and deliver him from evils.

The wise person does not hate commandments and statutes, and will not be tossed about like a ship in a storm.

A sensible person believes in God’s law, and the law is faithful to him.

Whoever makes his question known will prepare his statement; then, when he has entreated, he will be heard, and he will keep discipline, and then he will answer.

The innermost thoughts of a fool are like a cartwheel, and his thought like a turning axle.

An unbroken horse is like a mocking friend: it neighs under every rider.

Why does one day surpass another, and light again surpass light, and year surpass year by the sun?

By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished, when he made the sun that keeps the commandment.

[Col. 0452A] He changed their seasons and their festivals, and in them they celebrated festivals at the appointed time.

From among them God exalted and magnified some, and from among them he set some in the number of days. All human beings are from the soil, and from the earth, from which Adam was created.

In the abundance of discipline the Lord separated them and changed their ways.

From them he blessed and exalted; from them he sanctified and drew them to himself; from them he cursed and humbled them, and turned them away from their separation.

Like clay in the potter’s hand, to shape it and arrange it.

All his ways are according to his arrangement; so is a person in the hand of the one who made him, and he will repay him according to his judgment.

Good is opposite evil, and life opposite death; so is the sinner opposite the righteous man. Look likewise upon all the works of the Most High: two and two, and one opposite one.

And I was the last to awaken, and like one who gathers grapes after the grape-pickers.

I hoped in the blessing of God, and like one who gathers grapes I filled the winepress.

Look, for I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek discipline.

Listen to me, great men, and all peoples; rulers of the assembly, hear with your ears.

Do not give power over you in your lifetime to son, wife, brother, or friend, and do not give your possession to another, lest you later regret it and plead on their behalf.

While you still live and breathe, no flesh should change you.

For it is better that your children ask you than that you should look to the hands of your children.

In all your works be preeminent.

Do not give a blemish to your glory. On the day when the days of your life are completed, and at the time of your departure, distribute your inheritance.

Food, a rod, and a burden are for a donkey; bread, discipline, [Col. 0452C] and work are for a servant.

He works under discipline and seeks rest; loosen his hands, and he seeks freedom.

The yoke and the strap bend a stiff neck, and constant tasks bow down a servant.

For a malicious servant, torture and fetters; send him to work, lest he be idle.

For idleness has taught him much wickedness.

[Col. 0452D] Put him to work; for that is fitting for him. But if he does not obey, bend him with fetters, and do not be excessive toward any living being; nevertheless, do nothing severe without judgment.

If you have a faithful servant, let him be to you as your own soul; treat him like a brother, for you have acquired him at the price of your own blood.

If you wrong him unjustly, he will turn to flight.

And if he departs in a haughty spirit, whom will you seek, and on what road will you seek him? You do not know.

## CHAPTER 34

Vain hope and lying are proper to a senseless man, and dreams exalt the imprudent.

Like one who grasps at a shadow and pursues the wind, so is one who pays attention to lying visions.

This is the vision of dreams: one human likeness appearing before another human being.

What can be cleansed from what is unclean? And what truth can be spoken by what is false?

Divination is error, omens are lies, and the dreams of evildoers are vanity.

And just as a woman in labor suffers pangs, so your heart suffers fantasies; unless a visitation has been sent by the Most High, do not set your heart upon them.

For dreams have caused many to go astray, and those who hoped in them have fallen.

Without falsehood the word of the law will be fulfilled, and wisdom will be made plain in the mouth of the faithful.

[Col. 0453A] What does one who has not been tested know? A man experienced in many things will think about many things; and one who has learned much will explain understanding.

One who has not experienced things recognizes little; but one who has undergone many experiences multiplies wickedness.

What does one who has not been tested know? One who has been deceived will abound in wickedness.

I saw many things while wandering abroad, and my understanding surpassed my words. I often wandered, and encountered very many kinds of speech.

At times I was in danger of death because of these things, and I was delivered by the grace of God.

The spirit of those who fear God is sought, and in his regard they will be blessed.

For their hope is in the one who saves them, and the eyes of God are upon those who love him.

One who fears the Lord will fear nothing and will not be terrified, for he himself is his hope.

Blessed is the soul of one who fears the Lord.

Upon whom does he look, and who is his strength?

[Col. 0453B] The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him: he is their powerful protector, the support of their strength, a shelter from the heat, and a shade at midday;

he is a plea against offense, help in falling, raising up the soul, enlightening the eyes, giving health, life, and blessing.

The offering of one who sacrifices from injustice is defiled, and the mockeries of the unjust are not pleasing.

The Lord is only for those who wait for him on the way of truth and justice.

The Most High does not approve the gifts of the unjust, nor does he look upon the offerings of the wicked; he will not be appeased for sins by the multitude of their sacrifices.

One who offers a sacrifice from the property of the poor is like one who sacrifices a son before his father.

The bread of the needy is the life of the poor; whoever deprives him of it is a man of blood.

Whoever takes away bread earned through sweat is like one who kills his neighbor.

[Col. 0453C] Whoever sheds blood and whoever defrauds a hired laborer are brothers.

One builds and another destroys: what do they gain except labor?

One prays and another curses: whose voice will God hear?

One who purifies himself after contact with a dead person and then touches him again—what benefit is there in his washing?

So too, the person who fasts because of his sins and then does the same things again: what benefit is there in humbling himself? Who will hear his prayer?

## CHAPTER 35

Whoever keeps the law multiplies offerings.

A saving sacrifice is to heed the commandments and to depart from every iniquity.

To offer a sacrifice of atonement for injustices, and to make supplication for sins, is to withdraw from injustice.

He who offers fine flour repays gratitude; he who performs mercy offers a sacrifice.

[Col. 0453D] The Lord is pleased when one withdraws from iniquity, and supplication for sins is withdrawal from injustice.

You shall not appear before the presence of the Lord empty-handed.

For all these things are done because of God’s commandment.

The offering of the righteous fattens the altar, and its fragrance is sweet before the Most High.

The sacrifice of the righteous is acceptable, and the Lord will not forget its memorial.

With a good heart give glory to God, and do not diminish the firstfruits of your hands.

In every gift make your face cheerful, and sanctify your tithes with rejoicing.

Give to the Most High according to his gift, and with a generous eye make an offering from the work of your hands;

for the Lord is one who repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.

Do not offer corrupt gifts, for he will not accept them.

Do not look upon an unjust sacrifice, for the Lord [Col. 0454A] is judge, and with him there is no respect for persons.

The Lord will not show partiality against the poor, but he will hear the prayer of the one who has been wronged.

He will not despise the prayers of the orphan, nor those of the widow when she pours out her lament.

Do not the widow’s tears run down her cheek, and does not her cry rise against the one who causes them?

For from her cheek they rise up to heaven, and the Lord, who hears, will not be pleased by them.

Whoever worships God with goodwill will be accepted, and his prayer will draw near to the clouds.

The prayer of one who humbles himself will pierce the clouds; and until it draws near, he will not be consoled; nor will it depart until the Most High looks upon him.

And the Lord will not delay, but will judge the righteous and execute judgment; and the Mighty One will not be patient with them, so as to crush their backs.

He will repay the nations with vengeance until he removes the multitude of the proud, and he will crush the scepters of the unjust,

until he repays human beings according to their deeds, and [Col. 0454B] according to the works of Adam, and according to his presumption;

until he judges the judgment of his people and delights the righteous with his mercy.

The mercy of God is beautiful in the time of affliction, like a rain cloud in a time of drought.

## CHAPTER 36

Have mercy on us, God of all, and look upon us, and show us the light of your mercies.

Send your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, so that they may know that there is no God except you, and that they may recount your mighty deeds.

Raise your hand over foreign nations, so that they may see your power;

for just as you have been sanctified among us in their presence, so you will be magnified among them in our presence,

so that they may know you, as we also have known you: that there is no God besides you, Lord.

[Col. 0454C] Renew the signs and alter the wonders.

Glorify your hand and your right arm.

Arouse fury and pour out wrath.

Take away the adversary and afflict the enemy.

Hasten the time and remember the end, so that they may recount your wonders.

Let him who escapes be consumed in the flame of wrath; and let those who harm your people find destruction.

Crush the head of the enemy rulers who say, “There is no one besides us.”

Gather all the tribes of Jacob, so that they may know that there is no God except you, and may recount your mighty deeds; and you shall possess them as at the beginning.

Have mercy on your people, over whom your name has been invoked, and on Israel, whom you have made equal to your firstborn.

Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of your rest.

Fill Zion with your ineffable words, and your people with your glory.

Give testimony to those who have existed from the beginning of your creation, [Col. 0454D] and raise up the prophecies that earlier prophets spoke in your name.

Give a reward to those who wait for you, so that your prophets may be found faithful; and hear the prayers of your servants.

According to the blessing of Aaron, give blessing to your people, and guide us in the way of righteousness; then all who dwell on earth will know that you are God, the observer of the ages.

Every food will be eaten by the belly, yet one food is better than another.

The throat tastes the food of wild beasts, but a discerning heart understands lying words.

A perverse heart will cause sorrow, but an experienced person will resist it.

A woman will receive every male, yet one daughter is better than another.

The appearance of a woman makes her husband’s face cheerful, and beyond every human desire she brings forth longing.

[Col. 0455A] If there is a tongue of healing, there is also one of soothing and mercy; no man is like her among human beings.

Whoever possesses a good wife begins to acquire property; she is a helper corresponding to him and a pillar of rest.

Where there is no hedge, the property will be plundered; and where there is no wife, the needy man groans.

Who will trust one who has no nest, and who turns aside wherever darkness overtakes him, like a girded robber leaping from city to city?

## CHAPTER 37

Every friend will say, “I too have formed a friendship”; but there is a friend who is a friend in name only. Is there not sorrow even unto death?

A companion and a friend will turn into enemies.

O most wicked presumption! From where were you created, to cover the dry ground with his malice and deceit?

A companion rejoices with his friend in pleasures, [Col. 0455B] but in time of affliction he will become an adversary.

A companion shares his friend’s sorrow for the sake of his belly, and against the enemy he will take up a shield.

Do not forget your friend in your heart, and do not be unmindful of him amid your possessions.

Do not take counsel with one who lies in wait for you, and hide your plans from those who envy you.

Every counselor offers counsel, but there is a counselor who gives counsel for himself.

Guard your soul from a counselor; first learn what his need is, for he too will think according to his own interest.
