Otherwise he may drive a stake into the ground and say to you,

“Your road is good,” while standing opposite to see what happens to you.

Discuss holiness with an irreligious man, justice with an unjust man, and with a woman her rival; with a timid man, war; with a merchant, a business transaction; with a buyer, a sale; with an envious man, giving thanks;

[Col. 0455C] with an ungodly man, piety; with a dishonorable man, honor; with a farm laborer, every kind of work;

with a yearly laborer, the completion of the year; with a lazy servant, much work. Do not attend to these people in every counsel.

But be constant with a holy man, whoever you know to observe the fear of God,

whose soul is like your own, and who, when you stumble in darkness, will grieve with you.

Establish within yourself a heart of good counsel, for you have nothing more valuable than that.

The soul of a holy man sometimes declares the truth more than seven watchmen sitting high up to keep watch.

And in all these things pray to the Most High, that he may direct your way in truth.

Before all your works, let a truthful word go before you, and before every action, sound counsel.

A wicked word will change the heart; from it arise four outcomes: good and evil, life and death; and the tongue is their continual mistress. There is a man who is cunning and instructs many, but is useless to his own soul.

[Col. 0455D] An experienced man instructs many, and is pleasant to his own soul.

Whoever speaks sophistically is hateful; he will be deprived in every matter.

Grace has not been given to him by the Lord, for he has been deprived of all wisdom.

There is a man who is wise for his own soul, and the fruit of his understanding is praiseworthy.

A wise man teaches his people, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.

A wise man will be filled with blessings, and those who see him will praise him.

The life of a man is measured by the number of his days; but the days of Israel are without number.

The wise man will inherit honor among his people, and his name will live forever.

[Col. 0456A] My son, test your soul during your life; and if it is wicked, do not give it power over you.

For not everything is suitable for everyone, and not every kind of food pleases every soul.

Do not be greedy at every feast, and do not overindulge in every food.

For in many foods there will be illness, and greed will approach even to bile.

Because of gluttony many have died; but the one who is temperate will prolong life.

## CHAPTER 38

Honor the physician because of necessity, for the Most High created him.

For every healing is from God, and from the king he will receive gifts.

The physician’s skill will raise his head, and he will be praised in the presence of great men.

The Most High created medicines from the earth, and a prudent man will not reject them.

Was not bitter water sweetened by wood?

[Col. 0456B] The Most High has given human beings knowledge of their power, so that he may be honored in his wonderful works.

By these the physician soothes pain; the pharmacist makes compounds of sweetness and prepares ointments for healing, and his works will not come to an end.

For the peace of God is upon the face of the earth.

My son, in your illness do not neglect yourself, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.

Turn away from wrongdoing, and keep your hands right, and cleanse your heart from every sin.

Offer a sweet-smelling sacrifice and a memorial of fine flour; make the offering rich, and give a place to the physician.

For the Lord created him, and let him not depart from you, since his works are necessary.

For there is a time when you will fall into their hands.

[Col. 0456C] But they themselves will pray to the Lord to direct their repose and healing for the sake of their way of life.

Whoever sins before his Maker will fall into the hands of the physician.

My son, pour out tears for the dead, and begin to mourn as one who has suffered grievously; cover his body according to the judgment due him, and do not neglect his burial.

Because of the carrying out of the dead, bear his grief bitterly for one day, and console yourself on account of the sorrow.

Mourn according to his merit for one day, or two, because of the slander.

For sorrow hastens death, and sorrow covers strength; grief of heart bends the neck.

In bereavement grief remains, and the substance of the poor is according to his heart.

Do not give your heart over to grief, but drive it away from you, and remember the last things.

Do not forget, for there is no return, and you will do him no good; you will only harm yourself.

Remember my judgment, for so yours also will be: yesterday for me, and today for you.

In the resting-place of the dead, let his memory rest, and console him at the departure of his spirit.

[Col. 0456D] The wisdom of the scribe comes in a time of leisure; and whoever is less occupied with action will gain wisdom; with what wisdom will he be filled?

The one who holds the plow and the one who boasts of the goad drives the oxen with the stimulus, occupies himself with their work, and his discourse concerns the offspring of bulls.

He gives his heart to turning the furrows, and his watchfulness is over the fattening of the cows.

So too every craftsman and builder, who passes the night like the day, who carves engraved seals, and whose constant labor varies the design: he gives his heart to the likeness of the image, and his vigilance completes the work.

So too the ironsmith, sitting beside the anvil and examining the work of iron. The vapor of the fire burns his flesh, and he struggles in the heat of the furnace.

[Col. 0457A] The sound of the hammer renews his ear, and his eye is fixed on the likeness of the vessel.

He gives his heart to completing the work, and his vigilance adorns it to perfection.

So too the potter, sitting at his work and turning the wheel with his feet, who is always anxious because of his work, and all his activity is carefully measured.

With his arm he shapes the clay, and before his feet he bends his strength.

He gives his heart to completing the coating, and his vigilance cleans the furnace.

All these trust in their hands, and each is wise in his own craft.

Without these none of the cities would be built.

Yet they will not enter the assembly, nor walk about, nor enter the church.

They will not sit upon the judge’s seat, nor understand the covenant of judgment; they will not publicly expound discipline and judgment, nor will they be found among those who speak in parables.

But they will establish the created order of the age, applying their soul to the work of their craft and seeking out the law of the Most High.

## CHAPTER 39

The wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and will occupy himself with the prophets.

He will preserve the account of distinguished men and enter together into the subtleties of their parables.

He will seek out the hidden meanings of proverbs and dwell among the concealed things of parables.

He will serve among great men and appear before a ruler.

He will pass through the lands of foreign nations, for he will test what is good and evil among human beings.

He will give his heart to keeping watch from early morning for the Lord who made him, and he will pray in the presence of the Most High.

He will open his mouth in prayer and pray for his sins.

[Col. 0457C] For if the great Lord wills it, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding;

and he himself will pour forth words of wisdom like rain, and in prayer he will give thanks to the Lord.

He himself will direct his counsel and instruction, and he will deliberate upon his hidden things.

He himself will make plain the instruction of his teaching, and he will glory in the law of the Lord’s covenant.

Many will praise his wisdom, and it will not be erased forever.

His memory will not disappear, and his name will be sought from generation to generation.

The nations will recount his wisdom, and the assembly will proclaim his praise.

If he remains, he will leave a name greater than a thousand; and if he rests, it will benefit him.

I will continue to deliberate so that I may speak, for I am filled with fury.

In his speech he says: “Hear me, divine offspring, and bear fruit like a rose planted beside streams of water.

[Col. 0457D] Have an aroma of sweetness like Lebanon.

Blossom like flowers, like the lily; give forth fragrance, put forth leaves in grace, sing praise with a song, and bless the Lord in his works.

Give magnificence to his name, and give thanks to him with the voice of your lips, with songs of your lips and with lyres; and say this in your thanksgiving:

‘The works of the Lord are all exceedingly good.’

At his word the water stood like a heap, and at the word of his mouth like reservoirs of water.

For at his command pleasure is produced, and there is no diminishing of his salvation.

The works of all flesh are before him, and nothing is hidden from his eyes.

From age to age he looks, and nothing is wonderful in his presence.

Do not say, ‘What is this?’ or, ‘What is that?’ For everything will be sought in its proper time.

[Col. 0458A] His blessing overflowed like a river.

As a cataclysm drenched the dry land, so his wrath will possess the nations that have not sought him.

As he turned waters into dryness and the land became dry, and the power of his ways directed them, so offenses are directed against sinners in his wrath.

Good things were created for the good from the beginning, and likewise good and evil for the most wicked.

The beginning of what is necessary for human life is water, fire and iron, salt, milk and bread of fine flour, honey, a cluster of grapes, oil, and clothing.

All these things are good for the holy, but for the impious and sinners they will be turned into evil.

There are spirits created for vengeance, and in their fury they have strengthened their torments.

At the time of consummation they will pour out their power and appease the wrath of the one who made them.

Fire, hail, famine, and death—all these were created for vengeance;

the teeth of beasts, scorpions, serpents, and the avenging sword [Col. 0458B] for the destruction of the impious.

At his commands they will feast; they will be prepared upon the earth for times of need, and in their appointed times they will not transgress the word.

Therefore I was established from the beginning; I deliberated, reflected, and left these things in writing.

All the works of the Lord are good, and every work will supply what is needed in its proper hour.

Do not say, ‘This is worse than that’; for everything will be approved in its proper time.

And now, with all your heart and mouth, praise together and bless the name of the Lord.”

## CHAPTER 40

A great occupation has been created for all human beings, and a heavy yoke lies upon the children of Adam, from the day they leave their mother’s womb until the day of burial, into the mother of all.

[Col. 0458C] Their thoughts, the fears of their heart, the invention of expectation, and the day of completion.

From the one seated upon a glorious throne to the one humbled in earth and ashes;

from the one who wears hyacinth-colored clothing and bears a crown to the one covered with coarse linen: anger, jealousy, tumult, agitation, and fear of death; persistent rage and contention.

And at the time of rest in bed, the sleep of night changes his knowledge.

There is little rest, almost as though there were none; and in dreams he is watched as though it were day.

He is troubled in the vision of his heart, like one who has escaped on the day of battle. At the time of his deliverance he rises, astonished that there is no fear.

This is the lot of all flesh, from human beings to animals, and sevenfold for sinners.

In addition there are death, blood, contention, and the sword; oppression, famine, destruction, and scourges.

All these things were created for the unjust, and because of them the cataclysm came.

All things that are from the earth will return to the earth, and all waters will return to the sea.

Every gift and injustice will be erased, but faithfulness will stand forever.

The possessions of the unjust will dry up like a river, and like great thunder in a rainstorm they will resound.

When they open their hands, they will rejoice; so the transgressors will waste away at the end.

The descendants of the impious will not multiply branches, and unclean roots will resound upon the summit of a rock.

Green growth beside every water and on a riverbank will be plucked up before every grass.

Grace is like a paradise in blessings, and mercy endures forever.

The life of a self-sufficient laborer will be made sweet [Alternative: trampled], and in it you will find treasure.

Children and the building of a city will establish [Alternative: established] a name, [Col. 0459A] and above these an immaculate wife will be counted.

Wine and music gladden the heart, and the love of wisdom is above both.

Flutes and the psaltery make a sweet melody, and above both is a gracious tongue.

Your eye will desire grace and beauty, and above these, green plantings.

A friend and a companion are fitting in their time, and above both is a wife with her husband.

Brothers are a help in time of affliction, and above them mercy will deliver.

Gold and silver are a support for the feet, and above both is pleasing counsel.

Wealth and strength exalt the heart, and above these is the fear of the Lord.

There is no want in the fear of the Lord, and there is no need to seek help in it.

The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and above every glory they have covered him with it.

[Col. 0459B] My son, do not be in need during your lifetime; for it is better to die than to be in need.

A man who looks to another’s table has no life in the thought of his own food, for he nourishes his soul with another’s provisions.

But a disciplined and instructed man will guard himself.

In the mouth of the imprudent poverty will be trampled [Alternative: made sweet], and in his belly fire will burn.

## CHAPTER 41

O death, how bitter is your memory to the man who has peace in his possessions,

to the tranquil man whose ways are straight in everything, and who is still strong enough to receive food!

O death, your judgment is good for the needy man, and for one whose strength is failing,

whose age is exhausted, who is troubled about everything, and who is incredulous and has lost patience!

Do not fear the judgment of death. Remember what came before you and what will come after you; this is the judgment of the Lord upon all flesh.

And what will come upon you according to the pleasure of the Most High—whether ten years, or a hundred, or a thousand?

For there is no accusation of life in the underworld.

The children of abominations become the children of sinners, and those who dwell beside the houses of the impious.

The inheritance of sinful children will perish, and with their offspring there will be continual reproach.

The children complain about an impious father, because through him they are in disgrace.

Woe to you, impious men, who have abandoned the law of the Most High Lord.

If you are born, you will be born under a curse; and if you die, your portion will be under a curse.

Everything that is from the earth will return to the earth; so the impious will pass from the curse into destruction.

The mourning of human beings is for their bodies, but the name of the impious will be erased.

[Col. 0459D] Take care of a good name, for it will remain with you longer than a thousand precious and great treasures.

The number of the days of a good life is limited; but a good name will endure forever.

Preserve discipline in peace, children, for hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what benefit is there in either?

A man who hides his foolishness is better than a man who hides his wisdom.

Nevertheless, show reverence in the matters that proceed from my mouth.

For it is not good to observe every form of reverence, and not everything pleases everyone in faith.

Be ashamed before father and mother because of fornication; before a ruler and a powerful person because of lying;

before a prince and a judge because of wrongdoing; before the synagogue and the people because of iniquity;

before a companion and a friend because of injustice, and before the place where you dwell;

[Col. 0460A] because of theft, because of the truth of God and the covenant; because of reclining at table with bread, and because of concealment concerning what is given and received;

before those who greet you, because of silence; before the gaze of a promiscuous woman; and because of turning your face away from a relative.

Do not turn your face away from your neighbor, nor take away a portion and fail to return it.

Do not look upon another man’s wife, nor scrutinize his maidservant, nor stand beside his bed.

Be ashamed before friends because of insulting words; and when you give, do not reproach the recipient.

## CHAPTER 42

Do not repeat a word heard concerning the revelation of a hidden matter, and you will truly be without shame and will find favor in the sight of all people. Do not be ashamed because of any of these things, and do not show partiality so as to sin.

Do not be ashamed of the law of the Most High, the covenant, and judgment in acquitting the impious;

nor concerning the word of companions and travelers, or the distribution of the inheritance [Col. 0460B] of friends;

nor concerning equality in measures and weights, or the acquisition of much and little;

nor concerning the adulteration of goods, or merchants and traders; nor concerning strict discipline for children, or the bleeding of the side of a wicked servant.

A seal is good over a wicked woman.

Where there are many hands, lock things up; and whatever you give, count and weigh it. Record everything given and received.

Concerning the discipline of the senseless and the fool, and concerning elders who are judged by young men: in all things you will be instructed and approved in the sight of all living people.

A daughter is a hidden watch and concern for her father; her care removes sleep, lest she become mature in her youth and, living with a husband, become hateful;

lest she be defiled in her virginity and be found pregnant in her father’s house; lest, living with a husband, she transgress, or at least become barren.

[Col. 0460C] Over a lustful daughter strengthen your vigilance, lest she make you come into disgrace before your enemies, into slander in the city, reproach by the people, and shame you in the multitude of the assembly.

Do not fix your attention on every person because of appearance, and do not dwell among women.

For from clothing comes the moth, and from a woman comes a man’s iniquity.

A man’s iniquity is better than a woman who does good, and a woman who brings shame into disgrace.

Therefore I will remember the works of the Lord, and I will proclaim what I have seen. His works are in the words of the Lord.

The sun, shining upon everything, has looked upon it, and the work of the Lord is full of glory.

Has not the Lord caused his holy ones to proclaim all his wonders, which the Lord Almighty established to remain in his glory?

He searched out the abyss and the human heart, and he penetrated their subtleties.

For the Lord knows all knowledge, and he has looked into the sign of the age, declaring what has passed and revealing the traces of hidden things.

No thought escapes him, and no word is hidden from him.

He has adorned the great things of his wisdom, who is before the age and unto the age; nothing has been added,

nothing diminished, and he has no need of anyone’s counsel.

How desirable are all his works, and how like a spark it is to contemplate them!

All these things live and remain forever, and in every need they all obey him.

All things are twofold, one corresponding to another, and he has made nothing deficient.

He has established the good of each thing. And who can be satisfied when he sees his glory?

## CHAPTER 43

The beauty of the firmament on high is his splendor, the appearance of heaven in the vision of glory.

[Col. 0461A] The sun, announcing at its rising, is a marvelous vessel, the work of the Most High.

At noon it scorches the earth, and who can withstand its heat? One tending a furnace in works of burning—

Threefold is the sun’s scorching: it burns the mountains, breathes out fiery rays, and, shining with its rays, blinds the eyes.

Great is the Lord who made it, and at his word it hastens on its course.

The moon too, in all things, has its appointed time: a sign of the times and a sign of the age.

The moon marks the festival day, a light that diminishes at its completion.

The month is named according to it, increasing wonderfully at its completion.

It is a vessel of the armies on high, shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven.

The beauty of heaven is the glory of the stars, illuminating the world from on high; the Lord is the one who illumines it.

At his holy word they stand for judgment, and they do not fail in their watches.

Look at the rainbow and bless the one who made it; it is exceedingly beautiful in its brightness.

He has encircled heaven with the circle of his glory; the hands of the Most High have opened it.

By his command he hastens the snow, and he hastens to send forth flashes of lightning for his judgment.

Therefore the storehouses are opened, and the clouds fly out like birds.

By his greatness he has set the clouds in place, and the hailstones are broken.

At his presence the mountains will be shaken, and at his will the south wind will blow.

The sound of his thunder will strike the earth, as will the storm of the north wind and the gathering of the spirit.

And as a bird settling down to sit scatters snow, so the locust sinks down in its descent.

The eye will marvel at the beauty of its whiteness, and the heart will be terrified at its rain.

[Col. 0461C] He pours out frost like salt upon the earth; and when it freezes, it becomes like the tops of thistles.

The cold north wind blows, and the ice crystallizes from the water; it rests upon every gathering of waters, and clothes the waters like a breastplate.

It devours the mountains, burns the wilderness, and extinguishes the green growth like fire.

The healing of all things is in the swift-moving cloud; and dew, meeting the coming heat, makes the lowly one humble.

At his word the wind became silent, and by his thought he calmed the abyss; and the Lord planted islands in it.

Those who sail the sea should recount its dangers, and when we hear of them with our ears, we will marvel.

There are splendid works and wonders there: various kinds of beasts, all sorts of animals, and the creation of monsters.

Because of him the end of the journey was established, and at his word all things were ordered.

We shall say many things, but we shall fail in words; the conclusion of the discourse is that he is all things.

[Col. 0461D] What can we accomplish by boasting? He is almighty, above all his works.

The Lord is awesome and exceedingly great, and his power is wondrous.

Glorify the Lord as much as you are able [Alternative: as much as you can], for he will still surpass this, and his magnificence is astonishing.

Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can, for he is greater than every praise.

In exalting him, be filled with strength; do not grow weary, for you will not comprehend him.

Who has seen him and can describe him? Who can magnify him as he was from the beginning?

Many things are hidden, greater than these, for we have seen only a few of his works.

But the Lord has made everything, and he has given wisdom to those who act piously.

## CHAPTER 44

[Col. 0462A]

Let us praise glorious men, our ancestors in their generations.

The Lord bestowed great glory through his magnificence from of old.

Great men, ruling in their powers, people mighty in strength and endowed with prudence, proclaiming through the prophets the dignity of prophecy;

commanding the people in the present age, and giving the peoples the most holy words through the power of prudence;

seeking musical modes through their skill, and recounting the songs of the Scriptures;

wealthy men, mighty in strength, devoted to beauty, and bringing peace to their households.

All these obtained glory in their generations and were praised in their days.

Those born from them left behind a name by which their praises might be recounted.

There are also some whose memory has disappeared: they perished as though [Col. 0462B] they had never existed; they were born as though they had not been born, and so were their children after them.

But these were men of mercy, whose acts of piety did not fail.

Their good deeds remain with their offspring.

Their descendants are a holy inheritance, and their seed stood firm in the covenants.

Their children remain forever because of them; their offspring and their glory will not be abandoned.

Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name lives from generation to generation.

Let the peoples recount their wisdom, and let the assembly proclaim their praise.

Enoch pleased God and was transferred to paradise, so that he might give repentance to the nations.

No one was found perfect and righteous, and in the time of wrath he became a reconciliation.

Therefore a remnant was left for the earth when the flood occurred.

[Col. 0462C] The covenants of the age were established with him, so that no flesh might be destroyed by the flood.

Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations, and no one was found like him in glory. He kept the law of the Most High and was in covenant with him.

He established the covenant in his flesh, and in testing he was found faithful.

Therefore with an oath he gave him glory among his people, so that he might increase him like a heap of earth,

and exalt his offspring like the stars, and give them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.

And he acted in the same way toward Isaac, for the sake of Abraham his father.

The Lord gave him the blessing of all nations and confirmed the covenant upon the head of Jacob.

He acknowledged him through his blessings, gave him an inheritance, and divided his portion among the twelve tribes.

And he preserved for him men of mercy, who found favor in the sight of all flesh.

## CHAPTER 45

[Col. 0462D]

Beloved by God and by human beings was Moses, whose memory is held in blessing.

He made him like the holy ones in glory, magnified him in the fear of his enemies, and by his words made monsters cease.

He glorified him in the sight of kings, gave him commandments before his people, and showed him his glory.

In his faithfulness and gentleness he made him holy, and chose him from all flesh.

For he heard him, and his voice, and brought him into the cloud.

And he gave him commandments face to face, the law of life and discipline, to teach Jacob his covenant and his ordinances to Israel.

He exalted Aaron, his brother, and made him like himself, from the tribe of Levi.

[Col. 0463A]

He established for him an everlasting covenant and gave him the priesthood of the people; and he blessed him in glory.

He girded him with a glorious belt, clothed him in a glorious robe, and crowned him with emblems of strength.

He placed on him leggings, breeches, and a shoulder-piece, and girded him round about with very many golden bells,

so that they might make a sound as he walked and cause a sound to be heard in the Temple, as a memorial for the sons of his people.

A holy robe, of gold, hyacinth-blue, and purple, woven work, the work of a skillful man endowed with judgment and truth;

of twisted scarlet, the work of an artist, with precious stones set in a gold setting, and engraved by the work of a gem-cutter, as a memorial according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

A golden crown above his turban, impressed with the sign of holiness and the glory of honor: a work of strength, adorned with the desires of the eyes.

Such beautiful things as these had not existed before him, from the beginning.

No foreigner was ever clothed in them, but only his sons and his descendants throughout all time.

[Col. 0463B]

His sacrifices were consumed daily by fire.

Moses filled his hands and anointed him with holy oil.

An everlasting covenant was made for him and for his offspring, like the days of heaven: to perform the priesthood, to possess praise, and to glorify his people in his name.

He chose him from among all the living, to offer sacrifice to God, incense, and a pleasing fragrance, as an atonement in memory, for his people.

And in his commandments he gave him authority over the ordinances of judgment, to teach Jacob the testimonies and to give Israel light through his law.

For foreigners stood against him, and men who had been with Dathan and Abiram, and the assembly of Korah, surrounded him out of envy in the wilderness, in anger.

The Lord God saw it, and it did not please him, and they were consumed in the outburst of his anger.

He performed wonders against them and consumed them in the flame of fire.

[Col. 0463C]

And he added glory to Aaron, gave him an inheritance, and divided among him the firstfruits of the produce of the land.

He prepared bread for them first, in abundance; for they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and to his offspring.

Nevertheless, he shall have no inheritance among the nations in the land; he has no portion among the people, for he himself is his portion and inheritance.

Phinehas son of Eleazar is third in glory, because he imitated him in the fear of the Lord,

and stood in reverence before the people; by the goodness and eagerness of his soul he pleased God for Israel.

Therefore he established for him a covenant of peace, making him prince of the holy things and of his people, so that the dignity of the priesthood might belong to him and to his offspring forever.

And the covenant with David, king and son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah: an inheritance for him and for his offspring, so that he might give wisdom to our heart to judge his people in righteousness, lest their good things be abolished; and he made their glory everlasting among their people.

CHAPTER XLVI

[Col. 0463D]

Jesus son of Nave was mighty in war and successor to Moses among the prophets; he was great according to his name.

He was greatest for the salvation of God’s chosen, to defeat the enemies who rose up, so that he might obtain Israel’s inheritance.

What glory he gained when he lifted his hands and hurled weapons against the cities!

Who before him stood in such a manner? For the Lord himself brought the enemies low.

Was not the sun hindered by his anger, and one day made like two?

He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when he was attacking the enemies from every side, and the great and holy God heard him with very powerful hailstones.

[Col. 0464A]

He rushed against the hostile nation and, in the descent, destroyed his opponents,

so that the nations might know his power, because it is not easy to fight against God. And he followed behind the Mighty One.

And in the days of Moses he and Caleb son of Jephunneh showed mercy by standing against the enemy, restraining the people from sins, and breaking the murmur of wickedness.

These two were appointed and rescued from danger, out of the number of six hundred thousand foot soldiers, to bring them into the inheritance, into the land flowing with milk and honey.

And the Lord gave Caleb strength [alternative reading: “Caleb himself”], and his vigor remained even into old age, so that he might go up to the high place of the land; and his offspring obtained it as an inheritance,

so that all the sons of Israel might see that it is good to obey the holy God. [Note: [Col. 0463] Other Latin manuscripts insert “his”; the Greek text has only πορεύεσθαι ὀπίσω Κυρίου, “to walk after the Lord.”]

And the judges, each one by his own name, whose heart was not corrupted, who did not turn away from the Lord,

so that their memory might be in blessing, and their bones might flourish from their place.

And their name might endure forever, continuing to their children, the glory of holy men.

Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved by the Lord God, renewed the kingdom and anointed rulers among his people.

He judged the assembly according to the law of the Lord, and God looked upon Jacob; and by his faithfulness the prophet was proved.

He was known in his words as faithful, because he had seen the God of light.

And he called upon the Lord Almighty when attacking the enemies surrounding him on every side, with the offering of an unblemished lamb.

Then the Lord thundered from heaven, and made his voice heard with a great sound.

And he crushed the rulers of Tyre and all the commanders of the Philistines.

And before the time of the end of his life and of the age, he gave testimony in the sight of the Lord and of his Anointed. He accepted no money, not even as much as a sandal, from any human being, and no one accused him.

[Col. 0464C]

After this he slept, and made the king known; he showed him the end of his life, and raised his voice from the earth in prophecy, to wipe out the wickedness of the nation.

CHAPTER XLVII

After these things Nathan the prophet arose in the days of David.

And David was set apart from the sons of Israel like fat separated from flesh.

He played with lions as with lambs, and dealt with bears in the same way as with lambs of the flock in his youth.

Did he not kill the giant and remove reproach from the nation?

By lifting his hand, with a slingstone he cast down the boast of Goliath.

For he called upon the Lord Almighty, and he gave him power in his right hand to strike down a mighty man in war and to exalt the horn of his people.

Thus he glorified him among ten thousand, and praised him with the blessings of the Lord, offering him a crown of glory.

[Col. 0464D]

For he crushed the enemies on every side and exterminated the Philistines, his opponents, to the present day; he crushed their horn forever.

In every work he gave thanks to the Holy One and to the Most High in words of glory.

With all his heart he praised the Lord and loved God, who had made him; and he gave him power against his enemies.

He established singers before the altar and made sweet melodies in their sound.

And he gave beauty to the festivals and adorned the seasons until the completion of his life, so that they might praise the holy name of the Lord and magnify God’s holiness in the morning.

The Lord purged his sins and exalted his horn forever; he gave him the covenant of the kingdom and a throne of glory in Israel.

[Col. 0465A]

After him a wise son arose, and because of him he cast down all the power of the enemies.

Solomon ruled in days of peace; God subjected all the enemies to him, so that he might build a house in his name and prepare a sanctuary forever. How well trained you were in your youth!

You were filled with wisdom like a river, and your soul covered the earth.

You filled it with riddles in comparisons; your name was spread to distant islands, and you were loved in your peace.

The lands marveled at your songs, proverbs, comparisons, and interpretations,

and at the name of the Lord God, whose title is “God of Israel.”

You gathered gold as though it were bronze and filled silver as though it were lead.

And you bent your thighs toward women; you had power over your body.

[Col. 0465B]

You brought a stain upon your glory and profaned your offspring, bringing anger upon your children and provoking your folly,

so that you made the kingdom double and established a harsh kingdom over Ephraim.

But God will not abandon his mercy, nor corrupt [alternative reading adds: “and”]—nor will he erase—his works; he will not destroy the descendants of his chosen one, and he will not corrupt the offspring of the one who loves the Lord.

He left a remnant for Jacob, and David from the same stock.

And Solomon came to his end with his ancestors.

He left behind him, from his offspring, the folly of the nation:

Roboam, diminished in wisdom, who turned the people away by his counsel;

and Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin and gave Ephraim a way of sinning, and their sins multiplied greatly.

[Col. 0465C]

They turned them very far away from their land.

And he sought out every wickedness until defense came upon them, and he freed them from all their sins.

CHAPTER XLVIII

And Elijah the prophet arose like a fire, and his word burned like a torch.

He brought famine upon them, and those who provoked him by their envy became few; for they could not endure the commandments of the Lord.

By the word of the Lord he shut up heaven and brought down fire from heaven three times.

Thus Elijah was magnified in his wonders. Who can boast of being like you?

You raised the dead from the underworld, from the lot of death, by the word of the Lord God.

You cast kings down to destruction, and easily shattered their power, and the glorious from their beds.

You heard judgment on Sinai and judgments of vindication at Horeb.

[Col. 0465D]

You anointed kings for repentance and made prophets successors after you.

You were received in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of horses.

You were written in the judgments of the times, to turn aside the anger of the Lord, to reconcile the heart of a father to his son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

Blessed are those who saw you and were adorned by your friendship.

For we live only in this life; after death, our name will not be like this.

Elijah was indeed concealed in the whirlwind, and his spirit was filled in Elisha. In his days he did not fear a ruler, and no one overcame him by force;

no word defeated him, and in death his body prophesied.

In life he performed wonders, and in death he accomplished marvelous deeds.

In all these things the people did not repent and did not turn away

[Col. 0466A]

from their sins until they were expelled from their land and scattered throughout the whole earth.

And only a very small people remained, with a ruler in the house of David.

Some of them did what pleased God; others committed many sins.

Hezekiah fortified his city, brought water into its midst, cut through the rock with iron, and built a reservoir for the water.

In his days Sennacherib came up, sent the Rabshakeh, raised his hand against them, stretched out his hand against Zion, and became arrogant in his power.

Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they suffered like women in labor.

They called upon the merciful Lord, and, spreading out their hands, lifted them to heaven; and the holy Lord God quickly heard their voice.

He did not remember their sins, nor give them over to their enemies, but purged them by the hand of Isaiah, the holy prophet.

[Col. 0466B]

He overthrew the camp of the Assyrians, and the angel of the Lord crushed them.

For Hezekiah did what pleased God and walked courageously in the way of David his father, as the great and faithful prophet Isaiah had commanded him before God.

In his days the sun turned back and added life to the king.

With a great spirit he saw the final things and comforted those who mourned in Zion. Forever

he showed what was to come and what was hidden, before it happened.

CHAPTER XLIX

The memory of Josiah became like a composition of fragrance, the work of a perfumer.

His memory will be sweetened in every mouth like honey and like music at a banquet of wine.

He was divinely directed toward the repentance of the nation and removed the abominations of wickedness.

He directed his heart toward the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened piety.

Apart from David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all committed sin;

for the kings of Judah abandoned the law of the Most High and despised the fear of God.

They gave their kingdom to others and their glory to a foreign nation.

They burned the chosen city of holiness and made its streets desolate by the hand of Jeremiah.

For they treated badly the one who had been consecrated as a prophet from his mother’s womb, to uproot, tear down, destroy, and again build and renew.

Ezekiel saw the vision of glory that he showed him on the chariot of the cherubim.

For he remembered the enemies in the rain, to do good to those who had shown straight paths.

And may the bones of the twelve prophets flourish from their place;

[Col. 0466D]

for they strengthened Jacob and redeemed themselves by the faithfulness of their strength.

How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? For he too was like a signet ring on the right hand.

And so also Jeshua son of Jozadak, who in his days built the house and exalted the holy Temple for the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.

And Nehemiah, whose memory is great, who raised up for us the walls that had fallen, made the gates and bars stand firm, and rebuilt our houses.

No one was born on earth like Enoch, for he too was received from the earth.

Nor like Joseph, who was born a man, prince of his brothers, support of the nation, ruler of his brothers, and foundation of the people.

And his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied.

Seth and Shem gained glory among human beings, and Adam was above every living soul at the beginning.

CHAPTER L

[Col. 0467A]

Simon son of Onias, the great priest, who in his life supported the house and in his days strengthened the Temple.

He himself laid the foundation for the height of the Temple, the double structure of the Temple walls from the highest point.

In his days wells of water flowed out, and they were filled beyond measure, like the sea.

He cared for his people and delivered them from destruction.

He was powerful enough to enlarge the city and gained glory in the conduct of the people; he enlarged the entrance of the house and the court.

Like the morning star in the midst of clouds, and like the full moon shining in his days.

And like the sun shining forth, so he shone in the Temple of God.

Like a radiant rainbow among clouds of glory, like a rose blossom in the days of spring, like lilies beside running water, and like fragrant frankincense in the days of summer.

Like a shining fire and incense burning in the fire.

[Col. 0467B]

Like a solid golden vessel, adorned with every precious stone.

Like an olive sprouting, and like a cypress rising to the heights, when he received the robe of glory and clothed himself in the perfection of strength.

As he went up to the holy altar, he gave glory to holiness by his vesture.

When he received the portions from the hands of the priests, he himself stood beside the altar. Around him was a crown of brothers, like a plantation of cedars on Mount Lebanon.

Thus they stood around him like branches of palm, and all the sons of Aaron in their glory.

The offering of the Lord was in their hands before the whole assembly of Israel; and, completing his service at the altar, he magnified the offering of the Most High King.

He stretched out his hand over the libation and poured out some of the blood of the grape.

He poured a divine fragrance at the foundation of the altar to the Most High Prince.

[Col. 0467C]

Then the sons of Aaron shouted; they sounded on the long trumpets and made a great voice heard as a memorial before God.

Then all the people together hastened and fell on their faces upon the earth, to worship the Lord their God and offer prayers to God Almighty, the Most High.

And the psalmists magnified him with their voices, and in the great house the sound of sweetness grew full.

The people entreated the Most High Lord in prayer until the honor of the Lord was completed, and they fulfilled their service.

Then, descending, he lifted his hands over the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips and to glory in his name.

And he repeated his prayer, wishing to display the power of God.

And now pray to the God of all, who has done great things throughout the whole earth, who has increased our days from our mother’s womb and dealt with us according to his mercy:

May he give us gladness of heart and establish peace in our days in Israel for everlasting days.

May Israel believe that God’s mercy is with us, so that he may deliver us in his days.

There are two nations my soul hates, and the third is no nation:

those who dwell on Mount Seir, the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.

The teaching of wisdom and discipline was written in this book by Jesus son of Sirach, a Jerusalemite, who renewed wisdom from his heart.

Blessed is the one who occupies himself with these good things; whoever sets them in his heart will always be wise.

For if he does these things, he will be capable of everything, because the light of God is his path.

CHAPTER LI

The prayer of Jesus son of Sirach:

I will confess to you, Lord and King, and praise you, God my Savior.

[Col. 0468A]

I will confess your name, because you became my helper and protector.

You delivered my body from destruction, from the snare of an unrighteous tongue, from the lips of those who practice falsehood, and in the presence of those standing by you became my helper.

You delivered me, according to the abundance of the mercy of your name, from those who roar, prepared for prey,

from the hands of those seeking my life, and from the gates of affliction that surrounded me;

from the pressure of the flame that surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burned;

from the depth of the belly of the underworld, from a defiled tongue, from a lying word, from an unrighteous king, and from an unjust tongue.

My soul will praise the Lord until death.

And my life had drawn near to the underworld below.

They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help. I looked for human assistance, and there was none.

I remembered your mercy, Lord, and your work,

[Col. 0468B]

which has existed from of old.

For you rescue those who wait for you, Lord, and deliver them from the hands of the nations.

You exalted my dwelling above the earth, and for the death that was passing away I pleaded.

I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he might not abandon me in the day of my distress and in the time of the arrogant, when there was no help.

I will praise your name continually and praise it in thanksgiving; and my prayer was heard.

You delivered me from destruction and rescued me from an evil time.

Therefore I will confess and praise you, and bless the name of the Lord.

While I was still young, before I wandered, I openly sought wisdom in my prayer.

Before the Temple I asked for her, and until the end I will seek her. And she blossomed like an early grape.

[Col. 0468C]

My heart rejoiced in her. My foot walked on a straight path; from my youth I sought her.

I inclined my ear a little and received her.

I found much wisdom within myself and made great progress in it.

I will give glory to the one who gives me wisdom.

For I resolved to practice her; I was zealous for what is good, and I shall not be put to shame.

My soul wrestled with her, and in practicing her I was strengthened.

I stretched out my hands on high and lamented my ignorance of her.

I directed my soul toward her, and in knowledge I found her.

I possessed a heart with her from the beginning; therefore I shall not abandon her.

My belly was troubled as I sought her; therefore I shall possess a good possession.

The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise him.

[Col. 0468D]

Draw near to me, you who are uneducated, and gather yourselves into a house of discipline.

Why do you still delay, and why do you say these things? Your souls thirst exceedingly.

I opened my mouth and spoke: Acquire her for yourselves without silver.

Submit your necks to her yoke, and let your soul receive discipline, for it is near at hand to find her.

See with your eyes how little I labored and found for myself abundant rest.

Acquire discipline with much silver, and possess abundant gold through her.

Let your soul rejoice in her mercy, and you shall not be put to shame in praising her.

Perform your work before the appointed time, and she will give you your reward at its proper time.

[Col. 0467]

The book of Ecclesiasticus ends.

THE TWO BOOKS OF THE MACCABEES BEGIN.

BOOK ONE

[Col. 0469]

CHAPTER I

[Col. 0469A]

And it happened, after Alexander son of Philip the Macedonian had struck down Darius, king of the Persians and Medes—the first to rule in Greece, coming out from the land of Kittim—

that he fought many battles, captured all the fortified places, and killed the kings of the earth.

He crossed as far as the ends of the earth, seized the spoils of a multitude of nations, and the earth was silent before him.

He gathered a very great force and army, and his heart was exalted and lifted up.

He gained possession of the regions of the nations and of tyrants, and they became tributary to him.

After this he fell sick in bed and realized that he was going to die.

He called his noble servants, who had been brought up with him from youth, and while he was still alive he divided his kingdom among them.

Alexander reigned for twelve years and died.

[Col. 0469B]

And his servants took possession of the kingdom, each in his own place.

They all put diadems upon themselves after his death, and their sons after them for many years; and evils multiplied on the earth.

And there came forth from them a sinful root, Antiochus the Illustrious, son of King Antiochus, who had been a hostage at Rome; and he reigned in the one hundred and thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.

In those days lawless men came forth from Israel and persuaded many, saying: “Let us go and establish a covenant with the nations around us, because ever since we withdrew from them, many evils have overtaken us.”

And the proposal seemed good in their eyes.

Some of the people appointed themselves and went to the king; and he gave them authority to follow the customs of the nations.

They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the laws of the nations.

[Col. 0469C]

They made themselves foreskins, abandoned the holy covenant, joined themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.

And the kingdom was prepared before Antiochus, and he began to reign in the land of Egypt, so that he might rule over two kingdoms.

He entered Egypt with a large force, with chariots, elephants, cavalry, and a great multitude of ships.

He waged war against Ptolemy, king of Egypt; and Ptolemy was afraid before him and fled, and many wounded men fell.

He captured the fortified cities in the land of Egypt and took the spoils of the land of Egypt.

Then Antiochus turned back after he had struck Egypt, in the one hundred and forty-third year, and went up against Israel.

He went up to Jerusalem with a large force.

He entered the sanctuary in arrogance and took the golden altar, the lampstand of light and all its vessels, the table of the bread of the Presence, the libation vessels, the bowls, the golden mortars, the veil, the crowns, and the golden ornament that was before the Temple; he shattered everything.

[Col. 0469D]

He took the silver and gold, the desirable vessels, and the hidden treasures that he found. Having taken everything, he departed for his own land.

[Col. 0470A]

He carried out a slaughter of people and spoke with great arrogance.

And there was great mourning in Israel and in every place where they lived.

Princes and elders groaned; virgins and young men grew weak, and the beauty of the women was changed.

Every bridegroom took up lamentation, and those who sat on the marriage bed mourned.

The earth was shaken over its inhabitants, and the whole house of Jacob put on confusion.

After two years, the king sent the chief collector of tribute to the cities of Judah, and he came to Jerusalem with a great crowd.

He spoke peaceful words to them deceitfully, and they believed him.

Then he suddenly fell upon the city, struck it with a great blow, and destroyed many people in Israel.

He took the spoils of the city, burned it with fire, destroyed its houses, and demolished its walls all around.

[Col. 0470B]

They took the women captive and seized the children and livestock.

They built the City of David with a great and strong wall and strong towers, and it became a fortress for them.

They placed there a sinful people, wicked men; they established themselves in it, placed weapons and provisions there, and stored up the spoils of Jerusalem.

They stored them there, and they became a great snare.

This was done as a plot against the sanctuary and as an evil instrument against Israel.

They shed innocent blood around the sanctuary and defiled the sanctuary.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and it became a dwelling place of foreigners; it became foreign to its own offspring, and its children abandoned it.

Its sanctuary was desolated like a wilderness.

Its feast days were turned into mourning, its Sabbaths into reproach, and its honors into nothing.

[Col. 0470C]

According to its former glory, so its dishonor was multiplied, and its exaltation was turned into mourning.

King Antiochus wrote to his entire kingdom that all the people should be one, and that each person should abandon his own law.

All the nations consented according to the word of King Antiochus.

Many from Israel consented to his servitude, sacrificed to idols, and profaned the Sabbath.

The king sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem and to all the cities of Judah, ordering them to follow the laws of the nations of the land,

to prohibit burnt offerings, sacrifices, and offerings of atonement from being made in the Temple of God,

to prohibit the observance of the Sabbath and feast days,

and to order that the holy things and the holy people of Israel be defiled.

He ordered altars, temples, and idols to be built, and swine’s flesh and common animals to be sacrificed.

[Col. 0470D]

He ordered them to leave their sons uncircumcised and to defile their souls with every unclean thing and abomination, so that they might forget the law and alter all the ordinances of God.

And whoever did not act according to the word of King Antiochus was to die.

According to all these words he wrote to his entire kingdom,

[Col. 0471A]

and he appointed officers over the people to compel these things to be done.

And they ordered the cities of Judah to sacrifice.

Many from the people gathered to them—those who had abandoned the law of the Lord—and they committed evil throughout the land.

They drove the people of Israel into hiding, into secret places and places of refuge for fugitives.

On the fifteenth day of the month Kislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, King Antiochus built the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God, and throughout the cities of Judah all around they built altars.

Before the doors of the houses and in the streets they burned incense and sacrificed.

They burned the books of the law of God with fire, tearing them apart.

And whenever books of the covenant of the Lord were found with anyone, or anyone observed the law of the Lord, they slaughtered him according to the king’s decree.

They did these things by their power against the people of Israel who were found in every city, month after month.

On the twenty-fifth day of the month they sacrificed upon the altar that stood opposite the altar.

Women who circumcised their children were killed according to the command of King Antiochus.

They hung the infants by their necks throughout all their houses and slaughtered those who had circumcised them.

Many of the people of Israel resolved among themselves not to eat unclean things, and chose rather to die than to be defiled by unclean foods.

They refused to violate the holy law of God, and they were slaughtered.

And great anger came upon the people.

CHAPTER II

In those days Mathathias son of John, son of Simeon, a priest from the sons of Joarib, rose up from Jerusalem and settled on Mount Modin.

[Col. 0471C]

He had five sons: John, who was called Gaddis;

Simon, who was called Thassi;

Judas, who was called Maccabaeus;

Eleazar, who was called Abaron;

and Jonathan, who was called Apphus.

They saw the evils that were taking place among the people of Judah and in Jerusalem.

And Mathathias said: “Woe is me! Why was I born to see the ruin of my people and the ruin of the holy city, and to sit there while it is being given into the hands of enemies?

The holy things have fallen into the hands of foreigners; its Temple has become like a man without honor.

Its vessels of glory have been carried away captive; its old men have been slaughtered in the streets, and its young men have fallen by the sword of the enemies.

What nation has not inherited its kingdom or obtained its spoils?

[Col. 0471D]

All its adornment has been taken away. She who was free has become a slave.

And behold, our holy place, our beauty, and our glory have been desolated, and the nations have defiled them.

Why, then, should we continue to live?”

And Mathathias and his sons tore their garments, covered themselves with sackcloth, and mourned greatly.

Then those who had been sent by King Antiochus came there to compel those who had taken refuge in the city of Modin to sacrifice, burn incense, and depart from the law of God.

Many from the people of Israel, consenting, approached them, but Mathathias and his sons stood firm.

Those who had been sent by Antiochus answered and said to Mathathias: “You are a prince, illustrious and great in this city, adorned with sons and brothers.

Come first and carry out the king’s command, as all the nations, the men of Judah, and those who remained [alternative reading: “stayed”] in Jerusalem have done. Then you and your sons will be among the friends of the king, and you will be enriched with gold, silver, and many gifts.”

And Mathathias answered and said in a loud voice: “Even if all the nations obey King Antiochus, so that each one abandons the service of the law of his fathers and consents to his commands,

I, my sons, and my brothers will obey the law of our fathers.

May God be gracious to us! It is not useful for us to abandon the law and the ordinances of God.

We will not listen to the words of King Antiochus, nor sacrifice by transgressing the commandments of our law and going by another way.”

And when he had finished speaking these words, a certain Jew came forward in the sight of everyone to sacrifice to idols upon the altar in the city of Modin, according to the king’s command.

When Mathathias saw this, he was grieved; his kidneys trembled, and his anger was kindled according to the judgment of the law. He rushed upon him and slaughtered him upon the altar.

[Col. 0472B]

He also killed at that very moment the man whom King Antiochus had sent to compel them to sacrifice, and he destroyed the altar.

And he was zealous for the law, as Phinehas had been for Zimri son of Salu.

And Mathathias cried out in a loud voice in the city, saying: “Everyone who is zealous for the law and establishes the covenant, let him come out after me.”

Then he and his sons fled into the mountains and abandoned everything they had in the city.

At that time many who were seeking judgment and righteousness went down into the wilderness.

They and their sons, their wives, and their livestock settled there, because evils had overwhelmed them.

It was reported to the king’s men and to the army that was in Jerusalem, the City of David, that certain men had departed, had rejected the king’s command in secret places in the wilderness, and that many had gone after them.

They immediately went out against them and engaged them in battle on the Sabbath.

[Col. 0472C]

And they said to them: “Are you still resisting? Come out and do according to the word of King Antiochus, and you shall live.”

They said: “We will not come out, nor will we do the word of the king, to profane the Sabbath day.”

And they began battle against them.

They did not answer them, nor throw a stone at them, nor block up the secret places,

saying: “Let us all die in our innocence; heaven and earth will testify against us that you are destroying us unjustly.”

They waged war against them on the Sabbaths, and they died—along with their wives, children, and livestock—up to a thousand human beings.

Mathathias and his friends learned of it and mourned over them greatly.

And one man said to his neighbor: “If we all do as our brothers have done, and do not fight against the nations for our lives and our ordinances,

[Col. 0472D]

they will now quickly destroy us from the earth.”

And on that day they resolved, saying: “Let us fight against anyone who comes against us in battle on the Sabbath, and let us not all die as our brothers died in the secret places.”

Then the assembly of the Hasideans, strong in power, gathered to them from Israel—everyone willing in the law.

And all who were fleeing from the evils joined them and became their support.

They assembled an army, struck down sinners in their anger, and wicked men in their indignation; the rest fled to the nations to escape.

Mathathias and his friends went throughout the land and destroyed the altars.

They circumcised all the uncircumcised boys whom they found within the borders of Israel, and did so with strength.

They pursued the sons of arrogance, and the work prospered in their hands.

[Col. 0473A] And they secured the law from the hands of the nations and from the hands of kings, and they did not give power to the sinner.

Now the days of Mattathias’s death drew near, and he said to his sons: “Now arrogance, chastisement, the time of overthrow, and the wrath of indignation have grown strong.

“Therefore, my sons, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.

“Remember the deeds of our fathers, which they performed in their generations, and you will receive great glory and an everlasting name.

“Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and was it not reckoned to him as righteousness?

“Joseph kept the commandment in the time of his distress, and he became lord of Egypt.

“Phinehas our father, by showing zeal for the zeal of God, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

“Joshua, when he fulfilled the word, became leader in Israel.”

“Caleb, when he bore witness in the assembly, received an inheritance.

[Col. 0473B] “David, in his mercy, obtained the throne of the kingdom forever.

“Elijah, while he was zealous for the zeal of the law, was taken up into heaven.

“Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, because they believed, were delivered from the flame.

“Daniel, in his innocence, was delivered from the lions’ mouth.

“And so consider this from generation to generation: [Al. tac. et] for all who hope in him do not grow weak.

“And do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and a worm.

“Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his own earth, and his thought has perished.

“Therefore, my sons, be strong and act manfully in the law, for in it you will be glorified.

“And behold, Simon your brother: I know that he is a man of counsel. Always listen to him, and he will be your father.

“And Judas Maccabaeus, mighty in strength from his youth, [Col. 0473C] shall be your commander in the army, and he shall conduct the war of the people.

“You shall bring to yourselves all who practice the law, and avenge the vengeance of your people.

“Repay the nations with repayment, and attend to the commandment of the law.”

And he blessed them and was gathered to his fathers.

He died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year and was buried by his sons in the tombs of his fathers at Modein. All Israel mourned for him with a great mourning.

## CHAPTER III

And Judas, who was called Maccabaeus, his son, rose up in his place.

All his brothers helped him, as did all who had joined themselves to his father, and they fought Israel’s battle with joy.

He enlarged the glory of his people, put on a breastplate like a giant, and girded himself with his weapons for battle; [Col. 0473D] he protected the camp with his sword.

He became like a lion in his deeds and like a lion’s cub roaring in the hunt.

He pursued the wicked, searching them out, and he burned with fire those who troubled his people.

His enemies were driven back before his fear, and all the workers of iniquity were thrown into confusion; salvation was directed by his hand.

He embittered many kings, gladdened Jacob by his deeds, and his memory is blessed forever.

He traversed the cities of Judah, destroyed the impious among them, and turned away wrath from Israel.

His name was known to the ends of the earth, and he gathered together those who were perishing.

Apollonius gathered the nations and, from Samaria, a large and powerful force to fight against Israel.

Judas learned of this and went out to meet him. He struck and killed him; many wounded men fell, and the rest fled.

He took their spoils, and Judas took away the sword of Apollonius, and he fought with it all his days.

Seron, commander of the army of Syria, heard that Judas had gathered an assembly of the faithful and a congregation with him.

And he said: “I will make a name for myself and be glorified in the kingdom. I will defeat Judas and those who are with him, who have despised the king’s word.”

He prepared himself, and the camps of the wicked went up with him—strong auxiliaries—to take vengeance on the children of Israel.

They approached as far as Beth-horon, and Judas went out to meet him with a few men.

When they saw the army coming against them, they said to Judas: “How can we, being few, fight against so great and powerful a multitude? We are exhausted today by fasting.”

Judas said: “It is easy for many to be shut up in the hands of a few, [Col. 0474B] and in the sight of the God of heaven there is no difference between saving by means of many and by means of few.

“For victory in battle does not depend on the multitude of the army, but strength comes from heaven.

“They come against us in their insolent multitude and arrogance, to destroy us and our wives and our children, and to plunder us.

“But we shall fight for our lives and our laws.

“And the Lord himself will crush them before our face. But you must not fear them.”

As soon as he had finished speaking, he suddenly rushed upon them. Seron and his army were crushed before him.

He pursued him down the descent of Beth-horon as far as the plain, and eight hundred of them fell. The rest fled into the land of the Philistines.

Fear of Judas and his brothers fell upon them, and terror upon all the nations around them.

[Col. 0474C] His name reached the king, and all the nations reported the battles of Judas.

When King Antiochus heard these reports, he became angry in spirit. He sent for and gathered the army of his entire kingdom, very strong camps.

He opened his treasury, paid the army’s wages for a year, and ordered them to be ready for every undertaking.

He saw that money had run out of his treasuries, and that the revenues of the region were small because of the dissension and the plague he had brought upon the land by abolishing the ordinances that had existed from former days.

He feared that he would no longer have enough for the expenses and gifts which he had previously bestowed with a lavish hand, surpassing the kings who had preceded him.

He was greatly dismayed and resolved to go to Persia, collect the revenues of the regions, and gather a large amount of silver.

He left Lysias, a nobleman of royal descent, in charge of the royal affairs, from the Euphrates River as far as [Col. 0474D] the river of Egypt,

and to raise his son Antiochus until he returned.

He entrusted to him half the army and the elephants, and gave him orders concerning everything he wanted, including the inhabitants of Judea and Jerusalem,

and ordering him to send an army against them to crush and uproot the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to remove their memory from the place,

and to establish foreign inhabitants throughout all their territory and distribute their land by lot.

The king took the remaining part of the army and left Antioch, the city of his kingdom, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year. He crossed the Euphrates River and traversed the upper regions.

Lysias chose Ptolemy son of Dorymenus, Nicanor, and Gorgias, powerful men among the king’s friends,

[Col. 0475A] and sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand cavalry, to enter the land of Judah and destroy it according to the king’s word.

They advanced with all their strength, came, and encamped at Emmaus in the plain.

The merchants of the regions heard of their name, and they took a great deal of silver and gold, as well as boys. They came to the camp to take the children of Israel as slaves. The armies of Syria and of foreign lands joined them.

Judas and his brothers saw that the evils had multiplied and that the armies were approaching their borders. They learned the king’s orders, which commanded the people to be destroyed and annihilated.

And each said to his neighbor: “Let us raise up the downfall of our people and fight for our people and our holy places.”

An assembly gathered to prepare for battle, to pray, and to seek mercy and compassion.

[Col. 0475B] Jerusalem was uninhabited, but was like a desert. None of its children entered or left it. The sanctuary was trampled underfoot; foreigners’ children were in the citadel, and the habitation of the nations was there. Joy had been taken away from Jacob, and there the flute and lyre had ceased.

They gathered and came to Mizpah, opposite Jerusalem, because Mizpah had formerly been a place of prayer in Israel.

They fasted that day, put on sackcloth, placed ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.

They opened the books of the law, in which the nations had sought a likeness to their idols.

They brought the priestly ornaments, the firstfruits, and the tithes. They summoned the Nazirites whose days had been completed.

They cried out to heaven with a loud voice, saying: “What shall we do with these people, and where shall we lead them?

“Your holy places have been trampled underfoot and polluted, [Col. 0475C] and your priests have been brought into mourning and humiliation.

“And behold, the nations have assembled against us to destroy us. You know what they are plotting against us.

“How shall we be able to stand before them unless you, God, help us?”

And they sounded the trumpets and cried out with a loud voice.

After this Judas appointed commanders of the people: tribunes, centurions, commanders of fifty, and commanders of ten.

He told those who were building houses, betrothing wives, planting vineyards, and those who were fearful, to return each to his own house according to the law.

They moved the camp and stationed it south of Emmaus.

Judas said: “Gird yourselves and be valiant men, and be ready by morning to fight against these nations that have assembled against us to destroy us and our holy places.

“For it is better for us to die in battle than to see the evils of our nation and of the holy places.”

[Col. 0475D] “As it shall be the will in heaven, so let it be.”

## CHAPTER IV

Gorgias took five thousand men and one thousand chosen cavalry, and they moved the camp by night,

to approach the camp of the Jews and strike them suddenly. The children who were in the citadel served as their guides.

Judas heard of this, rose up himself, and set out to strike the king’s army, which was in Emmaus.

For the army was still dispersed from the camp.

Gorgias came by night into Judas’s camp, found no one, and searched for them in the mountains, saying: “These men are fleeing from us.”

When day had dawned, Judas appeared in the plain with only three thousand men, who had neither coverings nor swords.

[Col. 0476A] They saw the strong camp of the nations, the men in breastplates, and the cavalry around them, all trained for battle.

Judas said to the men who were with him: “Do not fear their multitude, and do not dread their assault.

“Remember how our fathers were saved in the Red Sea when Pharaoh pursued them with a great army.

“And now let us cry out to heaven, and the Lord will have mercy on us, remember the covenant of our fathers, and crush this army before our face today.

“And all the nations shall know that there is one who redeems and delivers Israel.”

The foreigners lifted their eyes and saw them coming against them.

They came out of the camp for battle, and those who were with Judas sounded the trumpet.

They joined battle; the nations were crushed and fled into the plain.

The last of them all fell by the sword. They pursued them as far as Gazera and as far as the plains of Idumea, Azotus, and Jamnia, and as many as three thousand of them fell.

[Col. 0476B] Judas and his army returned, following them.

He said to the people: “Do not covet the spoils, for battle is still against us.

“Gorgias and his army are near us in the mountain. But now stand against our enemies and defeat them; afterward you may safely take the spoils.”

While Judas was still saying this, a certain part of the army appeared, looking out from the mountain.

Gorgias saw that his own men had been put to flight and that the camp had been burned, for the smoke that was visible showed what had happened.

When they saw this, they were greatly afraid, looking at Judas and at the army prepared for battle in the plain at the same time.

They all fled into the plain of the foreigners.

Judas returned to the spoils of the camp, and they took a great deal of gold, silver, hyacinth-colored cloth, sea-purple cloth, and great riches.

They returned, singing a hymn and blessing God in heaven, “for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.”

And great deliverance occurred in Israel on that day.

Those of the foreigners who escaped came and reported to Lysias everything that had happened.

When he heard this, he was dismayed and faint with anxiety, because things had not happened [Al. omits “in”] in Israel as he had intended and as the king had ordered.

The following year Lysias gathered sixty thousand chosen men and five thousand cavalry to defeat them.

They came into Judea and encamped at Beth-horon, and Judas went out to meet them with ten thousand men.

They saw the powerful army, and Judas prayed and said: “Blessed are you, Savior of Israel, who crushed the attack of the mighty by the hand of your servant David, and delivered the camp of the foreigners into the hand of Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer. [Col. 0476D]

“Deliver this army into the hand of your people Israel, and let them be put to shame in their army and cavalry.

“Strike them with terror, melt the boldness of their strength, and let them be shaken by their downfall.

“Cast them down by the sword of those who love you, and let all who know your name praise you in hymns.”

They joined battle, and five thousand men of Lysias’s army fell.

When Lysias saw the flight of his men, the courage of the Jews, and that they were prepared either to live or to die bravely, he went away to Antioch and chose soldiers so that he might return again with a larger force to Judea.

Judas and his brothers said: “Behold, our enemies have been crushed. Let us now go up to cleanse the holy places and renew them.”

All the army gathered, and they went up to Mount Zion.

[Col. 0477A] They saw the sanctuary deserted, the altar profaned, the gates burned, the courtyards overgrown with shrubs like a forest or the mountains, and the chambers in ruins.

They tore their garments, mourned with great mourning, and placed ashes [Al. ashes] upon their heads.

They fell on their faces to the ground, sounded the trumpets of the signals, and cried out to heaven.

Then Judas appointed men to fight against those who were in the citadel until they had cleansed the holy places.

He chose priests without blemish, who desired the law of God.

They cleansed the holy places and carried the stones of defilement to an unclean place.

He considered what should be done with the altar of burnt offerings, which had been profaned.

And a good counsel occurred to them: to destroy it, lest it become a reproach to them, because the nations had polluted it and demolished it.

[Col. 0477B] They stored the stones on the temple mount in a suitable place until a prophet should come and give an answer concerning them.

They took whole stones according to the law and built a new altar like the former one.

They built the holy places and the interior rooms of the temple, and they sanctified the building and the courtyards.

They made new sacred vessels and brought in the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.

They placed incense upon the altar, lit the lamps that were on the lampstand, and they shone in the temple.

They placed loaves upon the table, hung up the curtains, and completed all the work they had undertaken.

Before dawn, on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month—which is the month of Casleu—in the one hundred and forty-eighth year, they rose.

They offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings that they had made.

[Col. 0477C] At the season and on the day when the nations had profaned it, it was renewed with songs, lyres, harps, and cymbals.

All the people fell on their faces, worshiped, and blessed in heaven the one who had prospered them.

They celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days and offered burnt offerings with joy, as well as a sacrifice of well-being and of praise.

They adorned the front of the temple with golden crowns and shields. They dedicated the gates and the chambers and set doors upon them.

There was exceedingly great joy among the people, and the reproach of the nations was removed.

Judas, his brothers, and the entire assembly of Israel decreed that the days of the dedication of the altar should be observed at their appointed time, year after year, for eight days beginning on the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, with joy and gladness.

At that time they built up Mount Zion, surrounding it with high walls and strong towers, lest the nations should come and trample it as they had done before.

[Col. 0477D] He stationed an army there to guard it and fortified it to protect Beth-zur, [Al. add. and] so that the people might have a stronghold against the face of Idumea.

## CHAPTER V

When the nations around them heard that the altar and the sanctuary had been rebuilt as before, they became exceedingly angry.

They plotted to destroy the race of Jacob who lived among them, and they began to kill and persecute some of the people.

Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea and those who were in Acrabattane, because they were surrounding the Israelites; and he struck them with a great blow.

He remembered the wickedness of the children of Bean, who had been a snare and a stumbling-block to the people, lying in wait for them on the road.

They were shut up in towers, and he approached them, placed them under the ban, and burned their towers with fire, together with everyone who was in them.

He passed over to the children of Ammon and found a strong force, a numerous people, and Timothy as their commander.

He fought many battles with them; they were crushed before him, and he struck them.

He captured Gazer, with its villages, and returned to Judea.
