[CLI, 10.] Peter answered and said: “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you over the waters.” He said: “Come.” Peter got down from the boat and walked on the water to come to Jesus. But when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid; and when he began to sink, he cried out, saying: “Lord, save me!” Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him: “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

[CLII, 6.] When they had climbed into the boat, the wind ceased. Those who were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying: “Truly, you are the Son of God.”

[CLIII, 2.] When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret. When the men of that place recognized him, they sent word throughout the whole region and brought him all who were ill. They begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And all who touched it were healed.

## Chapter XV

[CLIV, 6.] Then scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem approached him, saying: “Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.”

But he answered them: “Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition? For God said: ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever curses father or mother must surely die.’ But you say: ‘Whoever says to his father or mother, “Whatever gift comes from me will benefit you,”’—and he will not honor his father or his mother. Thus you have nullified the commandment of God because of your tradition.

“Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well about you, saying:

[Note: The Greek text has more: Ἐγγίζει μοι ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τῷ στόματι, καὶ τοῖς χείλεσί με τιμᾷ etc.; ‘This people draws near to me with its mouth, and honors me with its lips,’ etc.]

‘This people honors me with its lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and commandments of men.’”

After calling the crowds to him, he said to them: “Hear and understand. It is not what enters the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth—this defiles a person.”

[CLV, 10.] Then his disciples approached and said to him: “Do you know that the Pharisees, when they heard this saying, took offense?”

But he answered: “Every planting that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted.”

[CLVI, 5.] “Leave them. They are blind guides of the blind. And if the blind leads the blind, both will fall into a pit.”

[CLVII, 6.] Peter answered and said to him: “Explain this parable to us.” But he said: “Are you also still without understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine? But the things that come out of the mouth proceed from the heart, and these defile a person. For from the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies. These are the things that defile a person. But eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried out to him, saying: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is grievously tormented by a demon.” But he did not answer her a word. His disciples approached and begged him, saying: “Send her away, because she is crying out after us.”

[CLVIII, 5.] But he answered: “I was sent only to the sheep that have perished from the house of Israel.”

[CLIX, 6.] But she came and worshiped him, saying: “Lord, help me.” He answered: “It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to dogs.” But she said: “Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”

Then Jesus answered and said to her: “O woman, great is your faith. Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.

[CLX, 6.] When Jesus had departed from there, he came beside the Sea of Galilee. He went up the mountain and sat there. Great crowds came to him, bringing with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the disabled, and many others. They cast them at his feet, and he healed them, so that the crowds marveled when they saw the mute speaking, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples to him and said: “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have remained with me for three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away fasting, lest they faint on the way.”

The disciples said to him: “Where, then, could we get so many loaves in the desert as to satisfy so great a crowd?” Jesus said to them: “How many loaves do you have?” They said: “Seven, and a few small fish.”

He ordered the crowd to recline on the ground. He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples; and the disciples gave them to the people. They all ate and were satisfied. They took up what remained of the fragments: seven baskets full. Those who ate numbered four thousand men, besides children and women.

After dismissing the crowd, he went up into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.

## Chapter XVI

[CLXI, 4.] The Pharisees and Sadducees approached him, testing him, and asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

[CLXII, 5.] But he answered them: “In the evening you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’ And in the morning, ‘Today there will be a storm, for the sky is red and gloomy.’ You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times [Note: The word ‘know’ is also omitted by the Regina manuscripts along with most Greek manuscripts.]?”

[CLXIII, 6.] “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” And he left them and went away.

When his disciples had come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.

[CLXIV, 2.] He said to them: “Pay attention and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

[CLXV, 6.] They reasoned among themselves, saying: “It is because we did not take bread.” But Jesus, knowing this, said: “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up? Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up? Why do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread when I said, ‘Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees’?”

Then they understood that he had not said to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

[CLXVI, 1.] Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi and questioned his disciples, saying: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” They said: “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

Jesus said to them: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

[CLXVII, 10.] Jesus answered and said to him: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed also in heaven.”

[CLXVIII, 2.] Then he commanded his disciples to tell no one that he was Jesus Christ.

From that time Jesus began to show his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, scribes, and chief priests, be killed, and rise again on the third day.

[CLXIX, 6.] Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying: “Far be it from you, Lord; this shall never happen to you.” But he turned and said to Peter: “Get behind me, Satan; you are a stumbling block to me, because you do not understand the things of God, but those of men.”

[CLXX, 2.] Then Jesus said to his disciples: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?”

[CLXXI, 10.] “For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each person according to his works.”

[CLXXII, 2.] “Amen, I say to you: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”

## Chapter XVII

After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and his brother John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became white like snow. And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, speaking with him.

Peter answered and said to Jesus: “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, I will make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice from the cloud said: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”

When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid. Jesus approached, touched them, and said: “Rise; do not be afraid.” When they lifted their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.

As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: “Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”

[CLXXIII, 6.] The disciples questioned him, saying: “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

He answered them: “Elijah will indeed come and restore all things. But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands.”

Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.

[CLXXIV, 2.] When he had come to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling before him, and said: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire and frequently into the water. I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him.”

Jesus answered: “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I endure you? Bring him here to me.” Jesus rebuked him, and the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.

[CLXXV, 5.] Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said: “Why could we not cast him out?”

He said to them [Note: The Regina manuscripts have here the name ‘Jesus,’ along with several Greek manuscripts; and shortly afterward, where it reads ‘Pass from here to there,’ they omit the second adverb]: “Because of your unbelief. For truly I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Pass from here to there,’ and it will pass; and nothing will be impossible for you. But this kind is not cast out except by prayer and fasting.”

[CLXXVI, 2.] While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: “The Son of Man is going to be delivered into the hands of men; they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.” And they were greatly grieved.

[CLXXVII, 10.] When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma approached Peter and said to him: “Does your teacher not pay the didrachma?” He said: “Yes.”

When he had entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect tribute or tax—from their own sons or from strangers?” He said: “From strangers.” Jesus said to him: “Then the sons are free. But so that we do not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. When you open its mouth, you will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and for yourself.”

## Chapter XVIII

[CLXXVIII, 2.] At that hour the disciples approached Jesus, saying: “Who, do you think, is greater in the kingdom of heaven?”

Jesus called a little child and set him in their midst, saying: “Amen, I say to you: unless you turn and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven. Therefore whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greater in the kingdom of heaven. And whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me.

[CXXIX, 2.] “But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a millstone turned by an ass be hung around his neck and that he be drowned in the depths of the sea. Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks. For stumbling blocks must come; nevertheless, woe to that person through whom the stumbling block comes.

[CLXXX, 6.] “If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life maimed or lame than, possessing two hands or two feet, to be cast into eternal fire. And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than, possessing two eyes, to be cast into the fire of Gehenna.

[CLXXXI, 10.] “See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. For the Son of Man came to save what had perished.

[CLXXXII, 5.] “What do you think? If someone has a hundred sheep and one of them strays, does he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go in search of the one that strayed? And if it happens that he finds it, amen, I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not stray. So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.

[CLXXXIII, 5.] “If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother.

[CLXXXIV, 10.] “But if he does not listen to you, take one or two others with you, so that every word may stand on the testimony of two or three witnesses. If he does not listen to them, tell it to the church. But if he does not listen even to the church, let him be to you as a pagan, and a eunuch, and a tax collector.

[CLXXXV, 7.] “Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

[CLXXXVI, 10.] “Again I say to you, if two of you agree on earth about any matter that they ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in their midst.”

[CLXXXVII, 5.] Then Peter approached him and said: “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?”

Jesus said to him: “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.”

[CLXXXVIII, 10.] “Therefore the kingdom of heaven has been compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. When he began to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents. Since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered him to be sold, together with his wife, his children, and everything he had, and payment to be made.

“Then that servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’ Moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the debt.

“But when that servant had gone out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He seized him and began to choke him, saying: ‘Pay what you owe.’ Then his fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying: ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’ But he was unwilling. Instead, he went and put him in prison until he should repay the debt.

“When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved. They came and reported to their master everything that had taken place. Then his master summoned him and said to him: ‘Wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?’

“And in anger his master handed him over to the torturers until he should repay the entire debt.

“So also my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.”

## Chapter XIX

[CLXXXIX, 6.] When Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee and came into the regions of Judea beyond the Jordan. Great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

The Pharisees approached him, testing him and saying: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

He answered them: “Have you not read that the one who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said: ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh’? Therefore they are no longer two but one flesh. What God has joined together, let no person separate.”

They said to him: “Why, then, did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and dismissing her?”

He said to them: “Because of the hardness of your hearts Moses permitted you to divorce your wives; but from the beginning it was not so.

[CXC, 2.] “I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of fornication, and marries another, commits adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”

[CXCI, 10.] His disciples said to him: “If the situation of a man with his wife is such, it is not expedient to marry.” He said to them: “Not everyone grasps this saying, but only those to whom it has been given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb; there are eunuchs who were made so by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let anyone who can grasp it, grasp it.”

[CXCII, 2.] Then little children were brought to him so that he might lay his hands on them and pray. But the disciples rebuked them. Jesus said to them: “Allow the little children, and do not prevent them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” And after laying his hands on them, he departed from there.

[CXCIII, 2.] And behold, one approached him and said: “Good Teacher, what good shall I do to have eternal life?” He said to him: “Why do you ask me about what is good? One is good—God. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.”

He said to him: “Which ones?” Jesus said: “You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not give false testimony; honor your father and your mother; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

The young man said to him: “I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?”

[CXCIV, 2.] Jesus said to him: “If you wish to be perfect, go, sell what you have, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”

[CXCV, 2.] When the young man heard the saying, he went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions.

Jesus said to his disciples: “Amen, I say to you: a rich person will enter the kingdom of heaven with difficulty. And again I say to you: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.”

When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished, saying: “Who, then, can be saved?”

Jesus looked at them and said: “With human beings this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

Then Peter answered and said to him: “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. [CXCVI, 10.] What, then, will there be for us?”

Jesus said to them: “Amen, I say to you: you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his majesty, [CXCVII, 5.] you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

[CXCVIII, 2.] “And everyone who has left [alternative: leaves] a house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundredfold and will possess eternal life.

[CXCIX, 2.] “But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

## Chapter XX

[CC, 10.] “The kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard. After agreeing with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

“Going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace and said to them: ‘You also go into my vineyard [Note: The pronoun ‘my’ is absent here, and shortly afterward where the same passage recurs, in two Regina manuscripts as well as in the Greek text.], and I will give you whatever is just.’ They went.

“Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hours and did likewise. About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing there, and he said to them: ‘Why are you standing here idle all day?’ They said to him: ‘Because no one has hired us.’ He said to them: ‘You also go into my vineyard.’

“When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward: ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last and ending with the first.’

“When those who had come about the eleventh hour arrived, they each received a denarius. When the first also came, they thought that they would receive more; but they too received a denarius each. On receiving it, they grumbled against the householder, saying: ‘These last worked for one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who bore the burden of the day and the heat.’

“But he answered one of them: ‘Friend, I am not doing you an injustice. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go. I want to give this last one the same as I give you. Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good?’

“So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

[CCI, 2.] As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside privately and said to them: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked, scourged, and crucified; and on the third day he will rise.”

[CCII, 6.] Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshiping and asking something of him. He said to her: “What do you want?” She said to him: “Say that these two sons of mine will sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.”

Jesus answered: “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink?” They said to him: “We can.”

He said to them: “You will indeed drink my cup, but to sit at my right or left is not mine to give, except to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”

[CCIII, 2.] When the ten heard this, they were indignant at the two brothers. Jesus called them to himself and said: “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are great exercise authority over them. It will not be so among you. Whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your slave.

[CCIV, 4.] “Just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

[CCV, 2.] As they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road heard that Jesus was passing by, and they cried out, saying: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

The crowd rebuked them so that they would be silent. But they cried out all the more, saying: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David.”

Jesus stopped, called them, and said: “What do you want me to do for you?”

They said to him: “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”

Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes. Immediately they saw, and they followed him.

## Chapter XXI

**CCVI, 2.** When they had drawn near to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus then sent two disciples, saying to them: “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with it. Untie them and bring them to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say, ‘The Lord has need of them,’ and immediately he will let them go.” [Col. 0568D]

**CCVII, 7.** Now all this happened so that what had been spoken through the Prophet might be fulfilled, saying: “Tell the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek, seated upon a donkey, and a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.”

[Note: [Col. 0568D] The words “Now all this” (*Istud totum*) are omitted by the cited Greek manuscripts of better quality, as well as by the Royal manuscripts.]

**CCVIII, 2.** The disciples, going, did as Jesus had commanded them. And they brought the donkey and the colt, and placed their garments upon them, and made him sit upon them. But the very large crowd spread their garments on the road; others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.

**CCIX, 1.** The crowds that went before and those that followed were crying out, saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest.”

**CCX, 10.** And when he had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred, saying: “Who is this?” But the people were saying: “This is Jesus, the Prophet from Nazareth of Galilee.”

**CCXI, 1.** And Jesus entered the temple of God and drove out all who were selling and buying in the temple; and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves. And he said to them: “It is written: ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of thieves.”

[Note: [Col. 0569D] Instead of *shall be called*, which is also found in the Greek text, the Royal manuscripts prefer *is called*.]

**CCXII, 10.** And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.

**CCXIII, 5.** But when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders that he performed, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant and said to him: “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them: “Certainly. Have you never read: ‘From the mouth of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise’?”

**CCXIV, 6.** And leaving them, he went out beyond the city to Bethany, and there he remained. In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he became hungry. And seeing a single fig tree beside the road, he went to it and found nothing on it except leaves. And he said to it: “May no fruit ever come from you again.” And immediately the fig tree withered. When the disciples saw this, they marveled, saying: “How did it wither immediately?”

**CCXV, 6.** Jesus answered and said to them: “Amen I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will do not only what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Lift yourself up and throw yourself into the sea,’ it will happen.”

**CCXVI, 4.** And everything that you ask for in prayer, believing, you will receive.

**CCXVII, 2.** And when he had come into the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people approached him as he was teaching, saying: “By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?” Jesus answered and said to them: “I too will ask you one question; if you answer me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John—where was it from, from heaven or from human beings?”

But they reasoned among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we fear the crowd, for they all regarded John as a prophet.” And answering Jesus, they said: “We do not know.” He also said to them: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.” [Col. 0569D]

**CCXVIII, 10.** “But what do you think? A certain man had two sons. Approaching the first, he said, ‘Son, go today and work in my vineyard.’ But he answered, ‘I do not want to.’ Afterwards, moved by repentance, he went. Approaching the other, he said the same thing. But he answered, ‘I am going, sir,’ and did not go. Which of the two did the will of the father?” They said to him: “The first.” Jesus said to them: “Amen I tell you, tax collectors and prostitutes will go before you into the kingdom of God. For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Yet you, seeing this, did not even afterward repent so as to believe him.”

**CCXIX, 2.** “Hear another parable. There was a householder who planted a vineyard, fenced it around, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to farmers, and went abroad. When the time of the fruits approached, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect its fruits. But the farmers seized his servants, struck one, killed another, and stoned another. Again he sent other servants, more numerous than the first, and they treated them in the same way. Finally he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’ But when the farmers saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.’ And they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him. Therefore, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?” They said to him: “He will destroy those wicked men wickedly, and lease his vineyard to other farmers who will give him its fruit at the proper seasons.”

Jesus said to them: “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the cornerstone. This was done by the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’? Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits. And whoever falls upon this stone will be shattered; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

**CCXX, 1.** When the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they understood that he was speaking about them. And seeking to seize him, they feared the crowds, because they regarded him as a prophet.

## Chapter XXII

**CCXXI, 5.** Jesus answered and again spoke to them in parables, saying: “The kingdom of heaven has become like a king who made a wedding feast for his son. And he sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding, but they were unwilling to come. Again he sent other servants, saying: ‘Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my meal; my bulls and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding.’ But they disregarded it and went away, one to his farm and another to his business. The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

“When the king heard this, he was angry; and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers and burned their city. Then he said to his servants: ‘The wedding is indeed ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go, therefore, to the crossroads, and invite to the wedding whomever you find.’ And his servants went out onto the roads and gathered everyone whom they found, bad and good; and the wedding hall was filled with those reclining at table.”

**CCXXII, 10.** But the king entered to see those reclining at table, and he saw there a man not dressed in a wedding garment. And he said to him: “Friend, how did you come in here without having a wedding garment?” But he was speechless. Then the king said to the attendants: “Bind his hands and feet and throw him into the outer darkness.” [Col. 0571A] “There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

[Note: [Col. 0570D] The Greek has more: **ἄρατε αὐτὸν, καὶ ἐκβάλετε**—“Take him and throw him out,” and so forth.]

**CCXXIII, 2.** Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel in order to trap him in his speech. And they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying: “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and that you do not care about anyone; for you do not regard people’s status. Tell us, therefore, what do you think: is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar, or not?”

But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said: “Why are you testing me, hypocrites? Show me the coin of the tax.” And they offered him a denarius. And Jesus said to them: “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said to him: “Caesar’s.” Then he said to them: “Therefore repay to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And hearing this, they marveled, left him, and went away.

On that day Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, approached him and questioned him, saying: “Teacher, Moses said: ‘If someone dies without having a son, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’ Now there were among us seven brothers. The first, after marrying, died; and having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second and the third, down to the seventh. Last of all, the woman also died. In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they will be like the angels of God in heaven.”

[Note: [Col. 0571D] More precisely, the Greek **εἰσὶ** means “they are presently”; two Royal manuscripts read this.]

“And concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken by God when he said to you: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” And when the crowds heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.

**CCXXIV, 6.** But when the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together. And one of them, a lawyer, questioning him to test him, said: “Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?” Jesus said to him: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the greatest and first commandment. And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments the whole Law and the Prophets depend.”

**CCXXV, 2.** When the Pharisees had gathered, Jesus questioned them, saying: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him: “David’s.” He said to them: “How then does David, in the Spirit, call him ‘Lord,’ saying: ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I place your enemies as a footstool for your feet’? Therefore, if David calls him ‘Lord,’ how is he his son?”

**CCXXVI, 2.** And no one could answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day onward to question him further.

## Chapter XXIII

**CCXXVII, 10.** Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, saying: “The scribes and Pharisees have taken their seat on Moses’ chair. Therefore observe and do everything they tell you; but do not act according to their works, for they say things and do not do them.

**CCXXVIII, 5.** For they bind heavy and unbearable burdens and place them on people’s shoulders, but they themselves are unwilling to move them with their finger.

**CCXIX, 2.** They perform all their works in order to be seen by people. For they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge their tassels. They love the places of honor at banquets, the first seats in the synagogues, greetings in the marketplace, and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by people.

**CCXXX, 10.** But do not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for one is your Teacher, and you are all brothers. And do not call anyone your father on earth, for one is your Father, who is in heaven. Nor be called instructors, for one is your Instructor, the Christ.

**CCXXXI, 5.** The greater among you shall be your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

**CCXXXII, 5.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before people. For you yourselves do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to enter.

**CCXXXIII, 10.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel around sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he has been made one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.

Woe to you, blind guides, who say: “Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is obligated.” Fools and blind! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold? And whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is upon it is obligated. Blind! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that sanctifies the gift? Therefore whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything that is upon it. And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it; and whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits upon it.

[Note: [Col. 0571D] Some more recent manuscripts, along with the printed editions, add here: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour widows’ houses while making long prayers; for this reason you will receive a greater judgment.” But that these words are foreign to this passage and have been transferred here from chapters CXXXVI of Mark and CCXLVII of Luke—that is, from Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47—with some additions and some alterations to complete the connection, is suggested first by the very variation of their position in the manuscripts that contain them. Some place them before the saying concerning the keys, as does the manuscript of our monastery, Saint Taurinus of Évreux, containing the four Gospels in Greek with commentaries; others place them afterward.

“Second, they cannot have a place in the Eusebian and Hieronymian canons of the Gospels. They cannot be placed in Canon Ten, since they are not proper to Matthew but are common to the aforementioned passages of Mark and Luke; those passages, however, are assigned to Canon Eight, which contains nothing from Matthew.

“Third, these words are absent from the older and better manuscripts, of which we have many before us, written eight hundred years ago or more: one of the Royal Library, no. 3564; six from Saint-Germain-des-Prés, designated by the numbers 4, 6, 15, 18, 19, and 32; one Corbie manuscript preserved in our Saint-Germain library, no. 2; one from the monastery of Saint-William in the Desert; and another from the monastery of Crassus. MART.

“The Vulgate books, however, place this entire verse here: ‘Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour widows’ houses while making long prayers; for this reason you will receive a greater judgment.’ It is also found word for word in the Greek archetype:

**Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταὶ, ὅτι κατεσθίετε τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν, καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι· διὰ τοῦτο λήψεσθε περισσότερον κρίμα.**

“‘Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the houses of widows and, under pretext, make long prayers; for this reason you will receive a greater judgment.’ Yet it is found in none of our own ancient Latin books, nor in others that we consulted for this passage. See also the Sacred Critics discussing this interpolation, and Martianay himself in the Notes at the end of the book.

“Shortly afterward, however, the older Royal manuscript contains more: ‘Woe to you, scribes, blind guides,’ and so forth.”]

**CCXXXIV, 5.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who tithe mint, dill, and cumin, yet have abandoned the weightier matters of the Law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These you ought to have done, without omitting the others.

**CCXXXV, 10.** Blind guides, who strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.

**CCXXXVI, 5.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse what is outside the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of plunder and uncleanness. Blind Pharisee, first cleanse what is inside the cup and the dish, so that what is outside may also become clean.

**CCXXXVII, 5.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful to people on the outside, but inside are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of filth. So you also appear outwardly righteous to people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

**CCXXXVIII, 5.** Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, and say: “If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets.” Thus you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who killed the prophets.

**CCXXXIX, 10.** And you—fill up the measure of your fathers. Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?

**CCXL, 5.** Therefore, behold, I am sending you prophets, wise men, and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city, so that all the righteous blood poured out upon the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

**CCXLI, 5.** Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks beneath her wings, and you were unwilling! Behold, your house will be left desolate. For I tell you, you will not see me from now on until you say: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.”

## Chapter XXIV

**CCXLII, 2.** And Jesus went out from the temple and was departing. His disciples approached him to point out the temple buildings to him. But he answered and said to them: “Do you see all these things? Amen I tell you, not one stone here will be left upon another that will not be destroyed.”

**CCXLIII, 2.** As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached him privately, saying: “Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the consummation of the age?” Jesus answered and said to them: “See that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray. For you will hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not troubled, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be pestilences, famines, and earthquakes in various places. But all these things are the beginning of sorrows.

**CCXLIV, 1.** Then they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.

**CCXLV, 10.** Then many will be scandalized, and they will hand one another over and hate one another. Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray. And because iniquity has abounded, the love of many will grow cold. But whoever perseveres to the end will be saved.

**CCXLVI, 6.** And this Gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world, as a testimony to all nations; and then the consummation will come.

**CCXLVII, 6.** Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place—let the one who reads understand—

**CCXLVIII, 2.** then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let the one who is on the rooftop not come down to take anything from his house; and let the one who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

**CCXLIX, 2.** Woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days.

**CCL, 6.** Pray, however, that your flight may not occur in winter or on the Sabbath.

**CCLI, 2.** For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be.

**CCLII, 6.** And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.

**CCLIII, 2.** Then if anyone says to you: “Behold, here is the Christ,” or “There,” do not believe it.

**CCLIV, 6.** For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so that, if it were possible, even the elect would be led astray. Behold, I have foretold it to you.

**CCLV, 5.** Therefore, if they say to you: “Behold, he is in the desert,” do not go out; “Behold, in the inner rooms,” do not believe it.

**CCLVI, 5.** For just as lightning comes out from the east and appears even to the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

**CCLVII, 5.** Wherever the body is, there the eagles will also gather.

**CCLVIII, 2.** Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven.

**CCLIX, 2.** And then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. And he will send his angels with a trumpet and a great voice, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens to their farthest boundaries.

“Learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and its leaves have appeared, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors. Amen I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

**CCLX, 6.** But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of heaven, but the Father alone.

**CCLXI, 5.** For just as it was in the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of Man. For just as they were in the days before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

**CCLXII, 5.** Then two will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left. Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.

[Note: [Col. 0575D] Some printed books add: “Two in one bed: one will be taken and one will be left.” Several Greek copies also have this: **δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς· εἷς παραλαμβάνεται, καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται**—“two upon one bed; one is taken and one is left.”]

**CCLXIII, 6.** Therefore keep watch, because you do not know at what hour your Lord will come.

**CCLXIV, 2.** But know this: if the householder had known at what hour the thief would come, he would certainly have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be broken into. Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not know.

**CCLXV, 5.** Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent servant whom his master appointed over his household, to give them food at the proper time?

**CCLXVI, 5.** Blessed is that servant whom, when his master comes, he finds doing so. Amen I tell you, he will appoint him over all his possessions.

**CCLXVII, 5.** But if that wicked servant says in his heart: “My master is delaying his coming,” and begins to beat his fellow servants, while eating and drinking with drunkards, the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know. And he will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the hypocrites; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

## Chapter XXV

**CCLXVIII, 10.** Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride. Five of them were foolish and five prudent. But the five foolish ones, having taken their lamps, did not take oil with them; whereas the prudent took oil in their vessels along with their lamps. As the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep. But at midnight a cry arose: “Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him.”

Then all those virgins arose and trimmed their lamps. But the foolish said to the prudent: “Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.” The prudent answered, saying: “Perhaps there will not be enough for us and you; go instead to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.”

But while they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door was shut. Finally the remaining virgins also came, saying: “Lord, Lord, open to us.” But he answered and said: “Amen I tell you, I do not know you.” Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour. [Col. 0576A]

**CCLXIX, 2.** For it is like a man going abroad who called his servants and entrusted his possessions to them.

**CCLXX, 5.** To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability, and immediately he departed. The one who had received five talents went away, worked with them, and gained another five. Likewise, the one who had received two gained another two. But the one who had received one went away, dug in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. The one who had received five talents approached, offered another five talents, and said: “Master, you entrusted five talents to me; behold, I have gained another five.” His master said to him: “Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.”

The one who had received two talents also approached and said: “Master, you entrusted two talents to me; behold, I have gained another two.” His master said to him: “Well done, good and faithful servant. Because you were faithful over little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.”

But the one who had received one talent approached and said: “Master, I know that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter. And being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Behold, you have what is yours.”

But his master answered and said to him: “Wicked and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I did not scatter. Therefore you ought to have entrusted my money to the money-changers, so that when I came I would certainly have received what was mine with interest. Take the talent from him, therefore, and give it to the one who has ten talents.

**CCLXXI, 2.** For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will abound; but from the one who does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away.

**CCLXXII, 5.** And throw the useless servant into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

**CCLXXIII, 10.** But when the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he will sit upon the throne of his majesty. And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. And he will place the sheep at his right hand, but the goats at his left.

Then the king will say to those at his right hand: “Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me; naked, and you clothed me; ill, and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me.”

Then the righteous will answer him, saying: “Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you? Or when did we see you ill or in prison and come to you?”

And the king answering will say to them: “Amen I tell you, insofar as you did it for one of the least of these my brothers, you did it for me.”

Then he will also say to those at his left hand: “Depart from me, accursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink; I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me; naked, and you did not clothe me; ill and in prison, and you did not visit me.”

Then they too will answer him, saying: “Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or ill, or in prison, and did not minister to you?”

Then he will answer them, saying: “Amen I tell you, insofar as you did not do it for one of these least, neither did you do it for me.”

And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

[Chapter XXVI. CCLXXIV, 1.] And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples: “You know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

[CCLXXV, 6.] Then the chief priests and the elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the chief priest, who was called Caiaphas, and they took counsel to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him. But they said: “Not on the feast day, lest perhaps a tumult arise among the people.”

[CCLXXVI, 1.] Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, a woman approached him carrying an alabaster vessel of expensive ointment, and poured it over his head as he reclined. But when the disciples saw this [Another reading: “his disciples”], they were indignant, saying: “Why this waste? For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.”

But Jesus, knowing this, said to them: “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has performed a good work for me. For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”

[Note: In the future tense, “you will have” is read in the Regina manuscripts and in the Sixtine edition, just as in one or another Greek exemplar there is ἕξετε (“you will have”) instead of ἔχετε (“you have”). A little farther on, the same manuscripts read “who is called Judas Scarioth” instead of “Judas Iscariot was called.”]

[CCLXXVII, 4.] For by putting this ointment on my body, she has done it for my burial. Amen I say to you, wherever this Gospel is preached throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

[CCLXXVIII, 2.] Then one of the Twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests and said to them: “What do you wish to give me, and I will hand him over to you?” And they appointed for him thirty pieces of silver. From then on he sought an opportunity to hand him over.

On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying: “Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?” But Jesus said: “Go into the city, to a certain man, and say to him: ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover with you at your house, with my disciples.’” And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and prepared the Passover.

When evening came, he reclined with his twelve disciples. [CCLXXIX, 4.] And while they were eating, he said: “Amen I say to you, one of you is going to hand me over.”

[CCLXXX, 1.] And being greatly saddened, they began each to say: “Surely it is not I, Lord?”

[CCLXXXI, 2.] But he answered and said: “He who dips his hand with me into the dish will hand me over. The Son of Man indeed goes, [Col. 0578A] as it is written concerning him; but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be handed over.”

[CCLXXXII, 6.] It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.

[CCLXXXIII, 10.] But Judas, who handed him over, answering, said: “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him: “You have said it.”

[CCLXXXIV, 1.] While they were dining, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: “Take and eat: this is my body.”

[CCLXXXV, 2.] And taking the cup, he gave thanks and gave it to them, saying: “Drink from it, all of you. For this is my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. But I say to you: From now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I shall drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.”

[CCLXXXVI, 6.] And after singing a hymn, [Col. 0578B] they went out to the Mount of Olives.

[CCLXXXVII, 4.] Then Jesus says to them: “You will all suffer offense because of me on this night.”

[CCLXXXVIII, 6.] For it is written: “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.” But after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.

[CCLXXXIX, 1.] But Peter answered and said to him: “Even if all are offended because of you, I will never be offended.” Jesus said to him: “Amen I say to you, on this night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.”

[CCXC, 6.] Peter said to him: “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the disciples said likewise.

[CCXCI, 1.] Then Jesus came with them to a country place called Gethsemane.

[CCXCII, 6.] And he said to his disciples: “Sit here until I go over there and pray.” And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be saddened and distressed.

[CCXCIII, 4.] Then he said to them: “My soul is sorrowful unto death; remain here and keep watch with me.”

[CCXCIV, 1.] And going forward a little, he fell on his face, praying and saying: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me.”

[CCXCV, 1.] “Nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.”

[CCXCVI, 2.] And he came to his disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter: “So, you were not able to keep watch with me for one hour? Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation.”

[CCXCVII, 4.] “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

[CCXCVIII, 6.] Again, for the second time, he went away and prayed, saying: “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.” And he came again and found them sleeping, [Col. 0578D] for their eyes were weighed down. And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.

Then he came to his disciples and said to them: “Sleep now and rest. [CCXCIX, 4.] Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go. Behold, he who will hand me over has drawn near.”

[CCC, 1.] While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a great crowd sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people, with swords and clubs.

[CCCI, 2.] Now the one who handed him over had given them a sign, saying: “Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.” And immediately approaching Jesus, he said: “Hail, Rabbi.” And he kissed him. And Jesus said to him: “Friend, for what purpose have you come?” Then they approached, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him.

[CCCII, 1.] And behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and striking the servant of the chief priest, cut off his ear.

[CCCIII, 10.] Then Jesus said to him: “Return your sword to its place. For all who take up the sword will perish by the sword. Or do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he will provide me at once with more than twelve legions of angels? How then will the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen in this way?”

[CCCIV, 1.] At that hour Jesus said to the crowds: “As though against a robber you have come out with swords and clubs to seize me. Every day I sat teaching in the temple among you, and you did not seize me?”

[CCCV, 6.] But all this happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples, abandoning him, fled.

[CCCVI, 1.] But those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the chief priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.

[CCCVII, 4.] Peter, however, was following him from a distance, as far as the courtyard of the chief priest. And entering inside, he sat with the attendants, to see the outcome.

[CCCVIII, 2.] Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus, so that they might hand him over to death; and they did not find any, although many false witnesses had come forward.

[CCCIX, 6.] Finally two false witnesses came forward and said: “He said: ‘I can destroy the temple of God and rebuild it after three days.’”

And the chief priest rose and said to him: “Do you answer nothing to the things these men testify against you?” But Jesus remained silent. And the chief priest said to him: “I adjure you by the living God, tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”

Jesus says to him: “You have said it.”

[CCCX, 1.] “Nevertheless, I say to you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of God and coming in the clouds of heaven.”

[CCCXI, 6.] Then the chief priest tore his garments, saying: “He has blasphemed.”

[CCCXII, 2.] “What further need have we of witnesses? Behold, now you have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?” And they answered: “He is liable to death.”

[CCCXIII, 1.] Then they spat in his face and struck him with blows; others slapped his face, saying: “Prophesy to us, Christ: who is the one who struck you?”

[CCCXIV, 1.] Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. And one maidservant approached him, saying: “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.” But he denied it before everyone, saying: “I do not know what you are saying.”

[CCCXV, 1.] As he was going out through the gate, another maidservant saw him and said to those who were there: “This man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.” And again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man.”

And after a little while those who were standing there approached and said to Peter: “Truly, you too are one of them, for your speech makes you evident.” Then he began to curse and swear that he did not know the man. And immediately the cock crowed.

[CCCXVI, 2.] And Peter remembered Jesus’ word, which he had said: “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” And going outside, he wept bitterly.

[Chapter XXVII. CCCXVII, 2.] When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, so that they might hand him over to death.

[CCCXVIII, 1.] And having bound him, they led him away and handed him over to the governor Pontius Pilate.

[CCCXIX, 10.] Then Judas, who handed him over, seeing that he had been condemned, was moved to repentance and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying: “I sinned by handing over innocent blood.”

But they said: [Col. 0580B] “What is that to us? You see to it.”

And throwing the silver pieces into the temple, he withdrew; and going away, [Note: In the Regina manuscript: “he hanged himself with a noose”; in Greek alone is found ἀπήγξατο (“he hanged himself”).] he hanged himself.

But the chief priests, taking the silver pieces, said: “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.” And after taking counsel, they bought with them the potter’s field, for the burial of foreigners. Therefore that field was called Haceldama, that is, “Field of Blood,” to this day.

Then was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah, saying: “And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was valued, whom they valued from the children of Israel; and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed for me.”

[CCCXX, 1.] Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying: “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus says to him: “You say so.”

[CCCXXI, 4.] And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then Pilate says to him: “Do you not hear how many testimonies they bring against you?” And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.

[CCCXXII, 2.] On the solemn day, the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whomever they wished.

[CCCXXIII, 4.] At that time he had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas. Therefore, when they had assembled, Pilate said to them: “Whom do you wish me to release for you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?” For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.

[CCCXXIV, 10.] As he was sitting on the tribunal, his wife sent to him, saying: “Have nothing to do with that righteous man. For today I have suffered many things in a dream because of him.”

[CCCXXV, 10.] But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus. And the governor answered and said to them: “Which of the two do you wish me to release for you?” And they said: “Barabbas.”

[CCCXXVI, 1.] Pilate says to them: “What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all say: “Let him be crucified.” The governor said to them: “For what evil has he done?” But they shouted even more, saying: “Let him be crucified.”

[CCCXXVII, 10.] But Pilate, seeing that he was accomplishing nothing, and that rather a tumult was arising, took water and washed his hands before the people, saying: “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; you see to it.”

And the whole people answered and said: [Col. 0581A] “His blood be upon us and upon our children.”

[CCCXXVIII, 1.] Then he released Barabbas for them; but Jesus, after scourging him, he handed over to them to be crucified.

[CCCXXIX, 4.] Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around him. And stripping him, they placed a scarlet cloak around him, and twisting a crown of thorns, they put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying: “Hail, king of the Jews.”

[CCCXXX, 6.] And spitting upon him, they took the reed and struck his head. And after they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak and dressed him in his garments, and led him away to crucify him.

[CCCXXXI, 1.] As they were going out, they found a Cyrenian man named [Col. 0581B] Simon. They compelled this man to carry his cross.

[CCCXXXII, 1.] And they came to a place called Golgotha, which is the place of the Skull.

[CCCXXXIII, 4.] And they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall. And when he had tasted it, he did not wish to drink.

[CCCXXXIV, 1.] After they had crucified him, they divided his garments among themselves by casting lots.

[Note: This entire passage—“so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: They divided my garments among themselves, and over my clothing they cast a lot”—is added at this point in none of our manuscripts. It is also absent from other ancient Latin manuscripts and from several Greek books, and finally from the Complutensian edition and the Syriac version. On this matter, consult the sacred critics.]

“So that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: They divided my garments among themselves, and over my clothing they cast a lot.” And sitting down, they kept watch over him.

[CCCXXXV, 1.] And they placed above his head the charge against him, written: “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”

[CCCXXXVI, 1.] Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.

[CCCXXXVII, 6.] But those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads [Col. 0581C] and saying: “Ah! You who destroy the temple [Note: The Regina manuscripts add the name “of God,” which is nevertheless absent from the Greek archetype and other printed books.] and rebuild it in three days, save yourself. If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”

[CCCXXXVIII, 2.] Likewise the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes and elders, said: “He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is the king of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he wishes him—for he said: ‘I am the Son of God.’”

[CCCXXXIX, 2.] The robbers who had been crucified with him also reproached him in the same way.

[CCCXL, 2.] From the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

[CCCXLI, 6.] And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: “Eli, Eli,” [Note: In the older Regina codex, somewhat more corruptly, “Lema Zaptani.”] “lamma sabactani?”—that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

But some of those standing there, hearing this, were saying: “This man is calling Elijah.”

[CCCXLII, 2.] And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, placed it on a reed, and gave him a drink. But the others were saying: “Let be; let us see whether Elijah will come to save him.”

[CCCXLIII, 1.] But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up his spirit.

[CCCXLIV, 1.] And behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

[CCCXLV, 10.] And the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split, and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep arose. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they came into the holy city and appeared to many.

[CCCXLVI, 2.] Now the centurion and those who were with him guarding Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that were happening, were greatly afraid, saying: “Truly, this was the Son of God.”

[CCCXLVII, 6.] There were also many women there at a distance [Another reading adds: “watching”], who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

[CCCXLVIII, 1.] When evening had come, a certain rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who himself also was a disciple of Jesus, came. He approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. He approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered that the body be handed over.

[CCCXLIX, 1.] And having received the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth. And he placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock. And he rolled a large stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.

[CCCL, 6.] Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.

[CCCLI, 10.] On the next day, which is after the day of preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate, saying: “Lord, we remember that that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’ Therefore command that the tomb be guarded until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him and say to the people: ‘He has risen from the dead.’ And the last error will be worse than the first.”

Pilate said to them: “You have a guard; go, guard it as you know how.” But they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone, with the guards.

[Chapter XXVIII. CCCLII, 2.] On the evening of the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was beginning to dawn, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. And behold, there was a great earthquake. For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven; and approaching, he rolled away the stone and sat upon it. His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing like snow.

[CCCLIII, 2.] From fear of him the guards were terrified and became like dead men. But the angel answered and said to the women: “Do not be afraid. For I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord had been laid. And going quickly, tell his disciples that he has risen; and behold, he goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him. Behold, I have told you.”

[CCCLIV, 2.] And they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to announce it to his disciples.

[CCCLV, 10.] And behold, Jesus met them, saying: “Greetings.” They approached, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him. Then Jesus said to them: “Do not be afraid. Go, announce to my brothers that they should go into Galilee; there they will see me.”

When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened. And after assembling with the elders and taking counsel, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money, saying: “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping. And if this reaches the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you secure.”

[Col. 0584A] They, having received the money, did as they had been instructed. And this report has been spread among the Jews to this day.

Now the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them. And seeing him, they worshiped him; but some doubted. And Jesus approached and spoke to them, saying: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go, therefore, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; teaching them to keep everything that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you all the days, until the consummation of the age.”

[Col. 0583] The Gospel according to Matthew ends here.

[Col. 0583]

THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MARK BEGINS.

[Col. 0583B] [Chapter I. I, 2.] The beginning [Note: One of the Regina codices inserts the word “holy” before this. A little farther on, where it says “he will prepare his way before you,” all agree in omitting the words “before you”; these words are also absent at this point from several Greek manuscripts.] of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I send my angel before your face, who will prepare your way before you.”

[II, 1.] “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.”

[III, 6.] John was in the wilderness, baptizing and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. And the whole region of Judea and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.

And John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.

[IV, 1.] And he preached, saying: “After me comes one stronger than I, whose sandal strap I am not worthy, stooping down, to untie. I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

[Col. 0583C] [V, 1.] And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan. And immediately, as he was coming up from the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit [Note: Here one Regina manuscript, together with the Sixtine edition, adds “Holy,” that is, “the Holy Spirit.”] descending like a dove and remaining upon him. And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”

[VI, 2.] And immediately the Spirit drove him into the wilderness. And he was in the wilderness forty days and forty nights, and he was tempted by Satan.

[VII, 6.] And he was with the beasts, and angels ministered to him.

[VIII, 4.] But after John had been handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, [IX, 6.] preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God and saying: “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the Gospel.”

And as he was passing beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting nets into the sea—for they were fishermen.

[X, 2.] And Jesus said to them: “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men.” And immediately leaving their nets, they followed him.

[XI, 6.] And going on a little from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who themselves also were mending the nets in the boat. And immediately he called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, they followed him.

[XII, 8.] And they enter Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath, entering the synagogue, he taught them.

[XIII, 2.] And they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

[XIV, 8.] And in their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out, saying: “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.”

And Jesus rebuked him, saying: “Be silent and come out of the man.” And the unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.

And they were all amazed, so that they discussed it among themselves, saying: “What is this? What is this new teaching? For with authority he even commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him.” And his fame immediately spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.

[XV, 2.] And immediately, leaving the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John. Simon’s mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her. And approaching, he raised her up, taking her by the hand; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered to them.

When evening came, after the sun had set, they brought to him all who were ill and those possessed by demons; and the whole city was gathered at the door. And he healed many who were afflicted with various [Col. 0584D] illnesses,

[XVI, 8.] and he cast out many demons and did not allow them to speak, because they knew him.

[XVII, 8.] And rising very early, he went out and departed into a deserted place, and there he prayed. And Simon and those who were with him followed him. And when they had found him, they said to him: “Everyone is looking for you.”

And he said to them: “Let us go to the neighboring villages and towns, so that I may preach there also; for this is why I came.” And he was preaching in their synagogues and throughout all Galilee, and casting out demons.

[XVIII, 2.] And a leper came to him, beseeching him; and kneeling, he said to him: “If you wish, you can cleanse me.” But Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him: “I wish it. Be cleansed.”

And when he had spoken, immediately the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed. And rebuking him, he immediately drove him out, and said to him: “See that you tell no one. But go, show yourself to the chief priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded as a testimony to them.”

[XIX, 10.] But he went out and began to proclaim and spread the report of the matter, so that he could no longer enter a city openly, but remained outside in deserted places [Another reading: “to be”]; and they came to him from everywhere.

[Chapter II. XX, 1.] And again he entered Capernaum after some days. And it was heard that he was in the house, and many gathered, so that there was no room—not even at the door—and he was speaking the word to them.
