And they came to him bringing a paralytic, who was carried by four men. And when they could not bring him to him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was. And having opened it, they lowered the pallet on which the paralytic lay.

And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

[Note: Two Regina manuscripts omit the pronoun “your,” although it is echoed in the Greek.]

Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts: “Why does this man speak in this way? He blasphemes.”

[Another reading: “Why does he speak blasphemies?”]

“Who can forgive sins except God alone?”

And Jesus immediately knew in his spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, and he said to them: “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts? Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise, take up your pallet, and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—“I say to you: Rise, take up your pallet, and go to your house.”

And immediately he rose, and taking up the pallet, he went out before everyone, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying: “We have never seen anything like this.”

[XXI, 2.] And he went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd came to him, and he taught them. And as he was passing by, he saw [Note: The manuscripts read “Levin,” closer to the Greek Λευΐν.] Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him: [Col. 0585D] “Follow me.” And rising, he followed him.

[XXII, 2.] And it came to pass, while he reclined at his house, that many tax collectors and sinners were reclining together with Jesus and his disciples; for there were many who also followed him.

And when the scribes and Pharisees saw that he was eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples: “Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

[XXIII, 2.] When Jesus heard this, he said to them: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. And they came and said to him: “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”

And Jesus said to them: “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.

“No one sews a patch of unprocessed cloth onto an old garment; otherwise the new patch tears away from the old, and a worse tear results. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine will be spilled, and the wineskins will be ruined. Rather, new wine must be put into new wineskins.”

[XXIV, 2.] And it came to pass again that, while [Note: Our manuscripts omit the name “the Lord”; the Greek has αὐτόν (“him”).] the Lord was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, his disciples [Col. 0586B] began to go ahead and pluck the ears of grain.

But the Pharisees said to him: “Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not permitted?”

And he said to them: “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and became hungry, he and those who were with him—how he entered the house of God under Abiathar the chief priest, and ate the bread of the Presence, which it was not permitted for anyone to eat except the priests, and gave it also to those who were with him?”

[XXV, 2.] And he said to them: “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath. Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

[Chapter III.] And he entered the synagogue again, and there was a man who had a withered hand. And they watched him to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.

[Col. 0586C] And he said to the man who had the withered hand: “Rise and stand in the midst.” And he says to them: “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.

And looking around at them with anger, grieved over the blindness of their hearts, he says to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.

[XXVI, 4.] But the Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

[XXVII, 1.] But Jesus withdrew with his disciples toward the sea. And a great crowd from Galilee and Judea followed him, and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan. And those from around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing what he was doing, came to him.

And he told his disciples to have a little boat ready for him because of the crowd, lest they should press upon him. For he healed many, so that all who had afflictions rushed upon him to touch him.

[XXVIII, 8.] And when the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying: “You are the Son of God.” And he sternly rebuked them, so that they would not reveal who he was.

[XXIX, 2.] And going up onto the mountain, he called to himself those whom he wished, and they came to him. And he appointed twelve to be with him and to send them out to preach. And he gave them authority to cure illnesses and to cast out demons.

[XXX, 2.] And he gave Simon the name Peter. And to James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James he gave the names Boanerges, which means “Sons of Thunder”; and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot [Another reading: “Scarioth”], who also handed him over.

[XXXI, 10.] And they come to the house, and again a crowd gathers, so that they could not even eat bread. And when his own people heard, they went out to seize him, for they were saying: “He has become deranged.”

[XXXII, 2.] And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying: “He has Beelzebub,” and “By the prince of demons he casts out demons.”

[XXXIII, 2.] And calling them together, he spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan? And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand. And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.

“No one can enter the house of a strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.

[XXXIV, 2.] Amen I say to you: All sins and blasphemies will be forgiven the children of men, whatever blasphemies they may utter. But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not have forgiveness forever, but will be liable to an eternal offense.”

For they were saying: “He has an unclean spirit.”

[XXXV, 2.] And his mother and brothers come. And standing outside, they sent to him, calling him. And a crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him: “Behold, your mother and your brothers are outside seeking you.”

And answering them, he said: “Who is my mother and my brothers?” And looking around at those sitting around him, he said: “Behold my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of God is my brother, and my sister, and is mother.” [Note: One Regina manuscript, together with most Greek books, omits the pronoun “my.”]

### [Chapter IV. XXXVI, 2.]

And again he began to teach beside the sea. A very large crowd gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat on the sea, while the whole crowd was on the land beside the sea. And he taught them many things in parables, and said to them in his teaching:

“Listen. Behold, a sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds [Note: [Col. 0587D] Here the word “sky” is lacking in the manuscripts of Regina, as also in most Greek copies.] of the sky came and ate it. Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil [Col. 0587D]. And when the sun rose, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered. Other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no fruit. Other seed fell on good soil; and it produced fruit, growing up and increasing; and it yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

And he said: “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

And when he was alone, those who were with him, together with the Twelve, questioned him [Col. 0588A] about the parable [Variant: “parables”]. And he said to them:

“To you has been given knowledge [Note: [Col. 0587D] The manuscripts of Regina have *scire* (“to know”) instead of *nosse* (“to have knowledge of”).] of the mystery of the kingdom of God;

### [XXXVII, 1.]

but for those who are outside, everything is given in parables, so that, seeing, they may see and not perceive, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, lest they should ever turn and their sins be forgiven.”

And he said to them: “You do not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?

### [XXXVIII, 2.]

“The sower sows the word. These, then, are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear it, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that was sown in their hearts. Likewise, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy; but they have no root in themselves and are temporary [Col. 0588B]. Then, when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, they immediately fall away. Others are those sown among thorns: these are the ones who hear the word, but the anxieties of the age, the deceitfulness of riches, and desires concerning other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes fruitless. And these are the ones sown on good soil: they hear the word, receive it, and bear fruit—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.

### [XXXIX, 2.]

“And he said to them: “Does a lamp come in order to be placed under a bushel or under a bed, and not rather to be placed on a lampstand?

### [XL, 2.]

“For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed; nor has anything been concealed except so that it may come into the open. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.

### [XLI, 2.]

“And he said to them: “Consider what you hear [Col. 0588C]. With the measure you use, it will be measured out to you, and more will be added to you.

### [XLII, 2.]

“For to the one who has, it will be given; and from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

### [XLIII, 10.]

“And he said:

“So is the kingdom of God: as if a man were to cast seed upon the ground, and sleep and rise, night and day, while the seed sprouts and grows, although he does not know how. For the earth bears fruit by itself: first the stalk, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear. And when it has produced fruit, immediately he sends out the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.

[Note: [Col. 0588D] In the manuscripts of Regina the reading is “And when it has come forth,” etc., as also in the Louvain edition and others. The Sixtine edition has still more: “When it has brought forth from itself,” etc. In Greek there is only Ὅταν δὲ παραδῷ, “but when it yields.”]

### [XLIV, 2.]

“And he said: “To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, or with what parable shall we compare it? It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds that are in the earth; and when it has been sown [Col. 0588D], it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and produces great branches, so that the birds of the sky can dwell under its shade.”

### [XLV, 6.]

And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it. Without a parable, however, he did not speak to them;

### [XLVI, 10.]

but privately he explained everything to his disciples.

### [XLVII, 2.]

And he said to them on that day, when evening had come: “Let us cross over to the other side.” And leaving the crowd, they took him with them just as he was in the boat; and other boats were with him.

And a great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling [Col. 0589A]. He himself was in the stern, sleeping on a cushion. And they woke him and said to him: “Teacher, does it not concern you that we are perishing?”

And rising, he rebuked the wind and said to the sea: “Be silent; be still.” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

And he said to them: “Why are you so fearful? Do you still have no faith?”

And they were filled with great fear and said to one another: “Who, then, is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

## [Chapter V.]

And they came across the sea to the region of the Gerasenes. And when he had disembarked from the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs. He lived among the tombs, and no one could any longer bind him, not even with chains; for he had often been bound with fetters and chains [Col. 0589B], but had broken the chains and shattered the fetters, and no one was able to subdue him.

And continually, night and day, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones. When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and worshiped him. And crying out with a loud voice, he said:

“What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” [Note: [Col. 0589D] In our manuscripts, “Son of the Most High God” occurs instead of “Son of the Highest.”] “I adjure you by God, do not torment me.”

For he was saying to him: “Come out of the man, unclean spirit.” And he asked him: “What is your name?” And he said to him: “My name is Legion, because we are many.” And he pleaded with him earnestly not to drive him out of the region.

Now there was there, near the mountain, a large herd of pigs grazing. And the spirits pleaded with him, saying: “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

And he immediately granted their request [Col. 0589C]. And the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs; and the herd—about two thousand in number—rushed down a steep slope into the sea and were drowned in the sea.

But those who were tending them fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside. And people went out to see what had happened [Variant: “what had been done”]; and they came to Jesus and saw the man who had had the demon sitting there, clothed, and in his right mind, and they were afraid.

And those who had seen it told them how it had happened to the man who had had the demon, and about the pigs. And they began to beg him to leave their territory.

### [XLVIII, 8.]

And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demon began to plead with him that he might remain with him. But he did not allow him, and said to him:

“Go to your house and to your own people, and announce to them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you [Col. 0589D].”

And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.

### [XLIX, 2.]

And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him, and he was beside the sea.

And one of the rulers of the synagogue, named Jairus, came. When he saw him, he fell at his feet and pleaded with him earnestly, saying:

“My little daughter is at the point of death. Come, lay your hand upon her, so that she may be saved and live.”

And he went with him, and a large crowd followed him and pressed around him.

And a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years, and had endured much from many physicians, and had spent all that she had without receiving any benefit—in fact, she had grown worse [Col. 0590A]—when she heard about Jesus, came behind him in the crowd and touched his garment. For she said:

“If I touch even his garment, I shall be saved.”

And immediately the source of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she had been healed of the affliction.

And Jesus, immediately recognizing in himself the power that had gone out from him, turned toward the crowd and said: “Who touched my garments?”

And his disciples said to him: “You see the crowd pressing around you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

And he kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.

But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.

And he said to her: “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace and be healed of your affliction.”

While he was still speaking, people came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house, saying: “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?”

But Jesus, hearing the message that was spoken, said to the ruler of the synagogue: “Do not fear; only believe [Col. 0590B].”

And he did not allow anyone to accompany him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.

And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and he saw the commotion, and people weeping and wailing greatly. And entering, he said to them: “Why are you disturbed and weeping? The girl has not died but is sleeping.”

And they laughed at him. But he, having put everyone out, took the girl’s father and mother and those who were with him, and entered where the girl was lying.

And taking the girl by the hand, he said to her: “Talitha cumi”—which is translated: “Girl, I say to you, arise.”

And immediately the girl rose and began walking; she was twelve years old. And they were overcome with great amazement [Col. 0590C]. And he strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and he said that something should be given her to eat.

## [Chapter VI. L, 1.]

And he went out from there and came to his native place, and his disciples followed him. When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard him were astonished at his teaching, saying:

“Where did this man get all this? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, and such mighty works that are performed by his hands? Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, Joseph, Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us?”

And they took offense at him.

### [LI, 1.]

And Jesus said to them: “A prophet is not without honor except in his native place, among his relatives, and in his own house [Col. 0590D].”

And he could perform no mighty work there, except that he healed a few sick people by laying his hands upon them. And he marveled because of their unbelief.

### [LII, 2.]

And he went around the villages in the surrounding area, teaching.

### [LIII, 2.]

And he called the Twelve and began to send them out two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits.

And he commanded them to take nothing for the journey except a staff: no bag, no bread, and no money in their belt; but to wear sandals and not to put on two tunics.

### [LIV, 2.]

And he said to them: “Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you leave that place.

### [LV, 2.]

“And whoever does not receive you or listen to you, when you leave that place, shake the dust from your feet as a testimony to them [Col. 0591A].”

### [LVI, 8.]

And going out, they preached that people should repent. And they cast out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.

### [LVII, 2.]

And King Herod heard—for his name had become known—and he said: “John the Baptist has risen from the dead; therefore these powers are at work in him.”

But others were saying: “He is Elijah.”

Others, however, were saying: “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”

### [LVIII, 10.]

When Herod heard this, he said: “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead.”

### [LIX, 2.]

For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her [Col. 0591B].

For John had said to Herod: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”

Herodias, however, was plotting against him and wanted to kill him, but could not. For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. And when he heard him, he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.

### [LX, 6.]

And when an opportune day came, Herod made a dinner for the nobles, military tribunes, and leading men of Galilee. And when the daughter of Herodias herself had entered and danced and pleased Herod and those reclining with him, the king said to the girl:

“Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”

And he swore to her: “Whatever you ask me, I will give you, even half of my kingdom.”

When she had gone out, she said to her mother: “What should I ask for?”

But she said: “The head of John the Baptist.”

And immediately she entered hurriedly before the king and made her request, saying: “I want you to give me at once, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist [Col. 0591C].”

And the king was grieved; but because of his oath and those reclining with him, he did not want to refuse her. Rather, he sent an executioner and ordered John’s head to be brought on a platter.

And he beheaded him in the prison and brought his head on a platter. And he gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

When his disciples heard this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.

### [LXI, 8.]

And the Apostles gathered around Jesus and reported to him everything they had done and taught.

### [LXII, 10.]

And he said to them: “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.”

For there were many who were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

### [LXIII, 6.]

And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves. Many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the cities and arrived before them [Col. 0591D].

And when Jesus came out, he saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.

### [LXIV, 1.]

And when it had already become quite late, his disciples approached him, saying:

“This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late. Send them away, so that they may go to the neighboring farms and villages and buy food for themselves to eat.”

But he answered them: “You give them something to eat.”

And they said to him: “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii’ worth of bread and give them something to eat?”

And he said to them: “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.”

And when they had found out, they said: “Five, and two fish.”

And he commanded them to have everyone recline [Col. 0592A] in groups on the green grass. And they reclined in groups of one hundred and of fifty.

And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all.

And they all ate and were satisfied. And they collected twelve baskets full of the leftover fragments and of the fish.

Now those who had eaten were five thousand men.

### [LXV, 6.]

And immediately he compelled his disciples to get into the boat, so that they might go ahead of him across to Bethsaida, while he dismissed the people.

### [LXVI, 2.]

And when he had dismissed them, he went up onto the mountain to pray.

### [LXVII, 4.]

And when evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

And seeing them laboring at the oars—for the wind was against them—around the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking upon the sea, and he intended to pass them by [Col. 0592B].

But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out. For they all saw him and were terrified.

And immediately he spoke with them and said to them: “Take courage; it is I. Do not be afraid.”

### [LXVIII, 6.]

And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were utterly astonished within themselves, for they had not understood about the loaves, because their heart was hardened.

### [LXIX, 2.]

And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored there.

And when they had disembarked from the boat, people immediately recognized him. And running through that whole region, they began to carry on pallets those who were ill [Col. 0592C], wherever they heard that he was.

And wherever he entered, whether villages, farms, or cities, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched him were saved.

## [Chapter VII. LXX, 10.]

And the Pharisees and some scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him. And when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with common—that is, unwashed—hands, they found fault.

For the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash their hands frequently, do not eat, holding to the tradition of the elders. And when they return from the marketplace, unless they wash themselves, they do not eat. And there are many other things that they have received to observe: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and beds.

### [LXXI, 6.]

And the Pharisees and scribes questioned him [Col. 0592D]:

“Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common hands?”

But he answered them:

“Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written:

‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain do they worship me, teaching human doctrines and commandments.’

“For abandoning the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men—washings of pitchers and cups—and you do many other things like these.

“And he said to them: “You set aside the commandment of God very effectively in order to maintain your tradition.

“For Moses said: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ And: ‘Whoever curses father or mother must surely die.’

“But you say: ‘If a man says to his father or mother, “Corban”—that is, “a gift”—“whatever benefit you might have received from me,”’ then you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or mother, nullifying the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down [Col. 0593A]. And you do many other things of this kind.”

And calling the crowd to him again, he said to them:

“Listen to me, all of you, and understand. Nothing outside a person that enters into him can defile him; rather, the things that come out of a person are what defile the person. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”

### [LXXIII, 6.]

And when he had entered the house away from the crowd, his disciples questioned him about the parable.

And he said to them: “Are you also so without understanding? Do you not understand that everything external that enters a person cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart [Col. 0593B] but goes into the stomach and passes out into the latrine, cleansing all foods?”

[Note: [Col. 0593D] The word *vadit* (“goes”) appears to be superfluous here. Certainly it is absent from the manuscripts we use, nor is it present in the Greek text itself.]

But he said that the things that come out of a person defile the person. For from within, out of the human heart, come evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, greed, wickedness, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and folly. All these evils come from within and defile the person.

And rising from there, he went into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And entering a house, he wanted no one to know, but he could not remain hidden.

For as soon as a woman heard about him—whose daughter had an unclean spirit—she entered and fell at his feet. The woman was a gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth.

### [LXXIII, 6.]

And she begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.

He said to her: “Let the children be fed first, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs [Col. 0593C].”

But she answered and said to him: “Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs under the table eat from the children’s crumbs.”

And he said to her: “Because of this saying, go. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”

And when she had gone to her house, she found the girl lying on the bed, and the demon gone out.

### [LXXIV, 10.]

And again, leaving the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis.

And they brought him a deaf man who also had a speech impediment, and they begged him to lay his hand upon him [Note: [Col. 0594D] One manuscript of Regina has “they immediately begged,” as also does the Greek, παρακαλοῦσιν.].

And taking him aside from the crowd, he put his fingers into his ears; and spitting, he touched his tongue.

And looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him: “Ephphatha”—that is, “Be opened.”

And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was released, and he spoke correctly [Col. 0593D]. And he commanded them not to tell anyone.

### [LXXV, 8.]

And the more he commanded them, the more they proclaimed it; and they were astonished all the more, saying:

### [LXXVI, 6.]

“He has done all things well. He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”

## [Chapter VIII.]

In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called his disciples and said to them:

“I have compassion on the crowd, because they have already remained with me for three days and have nothing to eat. And if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will faint on the way [Col. 0594A]; for some of them have come from far away.”

And his disciples answered him: “How can anyone satisfy these people with bread here in the wilderness?”

And he asked them: “How many loaves do you have?”

They said: “Seven.”

And he commanded the crowd to recline on the ground.

And taking the seven loaves, giving thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to distribute; and they distributed them to the crowd.

They also had a few small fish. He blessed these as well and ordered them to be distributed.

And they ate and were satisfied. And they collected what remained of the fragments: seven baskets.

Now those who had eaten were about four thousand. And he dismissed them.

And immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the district of Dalmanutha.

### [LXXVII, 4.]

And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven and testing him [Col. 0594B].

### [LXXVIII, 6.]

And sighing deeply in spirit, he said: “Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

And leaving them, he got into the boat again and went across to the other side.

And they had forgotten to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.

### [LXXIX, 2.]

And he warned them, saying: “Look out, and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”

### [LXXX, 6.]

And they reasoned with one another, saying: “It is because we have no bread.”

Knowing this, Jesus said to them: “Why are you reasoning that you have no bread? Do you still neither know nor understand? Is your heart still hardened? Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? Do you not remember, when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments you collected [Col. 0594C]?”

They said to him: “Twelve.”

“And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets of fragments did you collect?”

And they said to him: “Seven.”

And he said to them: “Do you still not understand?”

### [LXXXI, 10.]

And they came to Bethsaida. And they brought him a blind man and begged him to touch him.

And taking the blind man by the hand, he led him outside the village. And spitting on his eyes and laying his hands upon him, he asked him whether he saw anything.

And looking up, he said: “I see people, like trees, walking.”

Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes, and he began to see; and his sight was restored, so that he saw everything clearly.

And he sent him to his house, saying: “Go to your house, and if you enter the village, tell no one.”

### [LXXXII, 1.]

And Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the way he questioned his disciples, saying to them: “Who do people say that I am?”

They answered him, saying: “John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”

Then he said to them: “But who do you say that I am?”

Peter answered and said to him: “You are the Christ.”

### [LXXXIII, 2.]

And he sternly ordered them not to tell anyone about him.

And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise again after three days.

And he spoke the word openly [Col. 0595A].

### [LXXXIV, 6.]

And Peter took him aside [Col. 0595A] and began to rebuke him.

But he turned and, seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, saying: “Get behind me, Satan, because you do not think the things of God, but the things of men.”

### [LXXXV, 2.]

And calling the crowd together with his disciples, he said to them:

“If anyone wishes to follow me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

“For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the Gospel will save it.

“For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his soul? Or what can a person give in exchange for his soul?”

### [LXXXVI, 2.]

“For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels [Col. 0595B].”

### [LXXXVII, 2.]

And he said to them: “Amen, I say to you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God coming in power.”

## [Chapter IX.]

And after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves, alone; and he was transfigured before them.

And his garments became shining and exceedingly white, like snow, such as no fuller on earth could make them white.

And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking with Jesus.

And Peter answered and said to Jesus: “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified with fear [Col. 0595C].

And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

And immediately, looking around, they saw no one any longer except Jesus alone with them.

And as they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them to tell no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

### [LXXXVIII, 10.]

And they kept the matter to themselves, questioning what “when he had risen from the dead” meant.

### [LXXXIX, 6.]

And they questioned him, saying: “Why then do the Pharisees and scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

[Note: [Col. 0595D] In the Greek manuscripts this opinion is attributed to the scribes alone, not also to the Pharisees: ὅτι λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς, “because the scribes say,” etc. [Col. 0596D]]

He answered them: “Elijah, when he comes first, will restore all things. And how is it written concerning the Son of Man—that he should suffer many things and be despised?

“But I say to you that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they wished [Col. 0595D], just as it is written concerning him.”

### [XC, 10.]

And coming to his disciples, he saw a large crowd around them, and scribes disputing with them.

And immediately all the people, seeing Jesus, were astonished and greatly alarmed; and running up, they greeted him.

And he asked them: “What are you disputing about with them?”

### [XCI, 2.]

And one person from the crowd answered: “Teacher, I brought my son to you, who has a mute spirit. Wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. And I told your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”

He answered them: “O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I endure you? Bring him to me.”

And they brought him. And when it saw him, the spirit immediately convulsed him; and falling to the ground, he rolled about foaming.

And he asked his father: “How long has this been happening to him?”

He said: “From childhood. And often it has thrown him into fire and into water in order to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us and have compassion on us.”

Jesus said to him: “If you can believe, all things are possible for the one who believes.”

And immediately the boy’s father cried out with tears and said: “I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.”

And when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: “Deaf and mute spirit, I command you: come out of him, and never enter him again.”

And crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out [Col. 0596B]. And he became like a dead man, so that many said: “He is dead.”

But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him up, and he stood.

### [XCII, 10.]

And when he had entered the house, his disciples questioned him privately: “Why could we not cast it out?”

And he said to them: “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer and fasting.”

### [XCIII, 2.]

And departing from there, they passed through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.

For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them: “The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and after he has been killed, he will rise on the third day.”

But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to question him.

### [XCIV, 10.]

And they came to Capernaum. When they were in the house, he questioned them: “What were you discussing on the way?”

### [XCV, 2.]

But they were silent, for on the way they had argued among themselves about which of them was the greatest [Col. 0596C].

And sitting down, he called the Twelve and said to them:

“If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”

And taking a child, he placed him in their midst. And when he had embraced him, he said to them:

“Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me.”

### [XCVI, 1.]

“And whoever receives me does not receive me, but the one who sent me.”

### [XCVII, 8.]

John answered him, saying: “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, one who does not follow us, and we forbade him.”

But Jesus said: “Do not forbid him. For no one who performs a mighty work in my name can soon speak evil of me. For whoever is not against us is for us [Col. 0596D].”

### [XCVIII, 6.]

“For whoever gives you a cup of water in my name, because you belong to Christ: amen, I say to you, he will certainly not lose his reward.”

### [XCIX, 2.]

“And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble: it would be better for him if a millstone drawn by an ass were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.

### [C, 6.]

“And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than, having two hands, to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,

### [CI, 10.]

“where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.

“And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter eternal life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into the Gehenna of unquenchable fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished [Col. 0597A].

“And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the fire of Gehenna, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished.

“For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.

[Note: [Col. 0597D] “With salt” is not added in our manuscripts, although in most Greek copies the noun is present.]

### [CII, 2.]

“Salt is good. But if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

## Chapter X

**[CIII, 6.]** From there he arose and went into the regions of Judea beyond the Jordan. Crowds again gathered around him, and, as he was accustomed to do, he again taught them. The Pharisees approached and asked him [Note: [Col. 0598D] Here two manuscripts of Regina add the pronoun “him,” which the Greek books also retain]: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”—testing him.

But he answered and said to them: “What did Moses command you?” They said: “Moses permitted a man to write a bill of divorce and to dismiss her.” Jesus answered them: “Because of the hardness of your hearts he wrote this commandment for you. But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female. For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh. Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

**[CIV, 10.]** And in the house his disciples again questioned him about the same matter.

**[CV, 2.]** And he said to them: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her. And if a wife divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”

**[CVI, 2.]** And they were bringing little children to him, so that he might touch them. But the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them. When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them: “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them; for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these. Truly I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will not enter it.” And he embraced them and laid his hands upon them and blessed them.

**[CVII, 2.]** And as he was setting out on the road, someone ran up, knelt before him, and asked him: “Good Teacher, what must I do to receive eternal life?” But Jesus said to him: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God. You know the commandments: You shall not commit adultery; you shall not kill; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; you shall not defraud; honor your father and your mother.”

He answered and said to him: “Teacher, I have kept all these things from my youth.”

**[CVIII, 2.]** Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him: “You lack one thing: go, sell whatever you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”

**[CIX, 2.]** But he was saddened by the saying and went away grieving, for he had many possessions. And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples: “How difficult it is for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God!”

The disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answered again and said to them: “Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God when one trusts in riches! It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

They were even more astonished, saying to one another: “Then who can be saved?” Looking at them, Jesus said: “With human beings it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”

And Peter began to say to him: “Behold, we have left everything and followed you.”

**[CX, 2.]** Jesus answered and said: “Truly I tell you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields, for my sake and for the sake of the Gospel, who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this present time—houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and fields, together with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.”

**[CXI, 2.]** But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

**[CXII, 2.]** They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them. They were astonished, and those who followed were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:

“Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles. They will mock him, spit upon him, flog him, and kill him; and on the third day he will rise again.”

**[CXIII, 6.]** James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approached him and said: “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.”

He said to them: “What do you want me to do for you?”

They said: “Grant us that one of us may sit at your right hand and the other at your left in your glory.”

But Jesus said to them: “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”

They said to him: “We can.”

Jesus said to them: “The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized. But to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to grant; it belongs to those for whom it has been prepared.”

**[CXIV, 2.]** When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant at James and John. Jesus called them and said to them: “You know that those who appear to rule the Gentiles lord it over them, and their rulers exercise authority over them. It is not so among you. Rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be the slave of all.

**[CXV, 4.]** For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

**[CXVI, 2.]** And they came to Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho, together with his disciples and a very large crowd, Bartimaeus, the blind man, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road begging. When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”

Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent. But he cried out all the more: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. They called the blind man, saying to him: “Take courage; get up, he is calling you.”

He threw off his cloak, sprang up, and came to him. Jesus answered and said to him: “What do you want me to do for you?”

The blind man said to him: “Rabboni, that I may see.”

Jesus said to him: “Go; your faith has saved you.”

Immediately he received his sight and followed him on the road.

## Chapter XI

**[CXVII, 2.]** As they were approaching Jerusalem and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples and said to them: “Go into the village opposite you, and as soon as you enter it you will find a colt tied up, on which no human being has yet sat. Untie it and bring it here. And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it,’ and immediately he will send it here.”

**[CXVIII, 2.]** They went away and found the colt tied outside by the door, at the crossroads, and they untied it. Some of those standing there said to them: “What are you doing, untying the colt?”

They told them what Jesus had commanded, and the men let them take it. They brought the colt to Jesus, laid their garments upon it, and he sat on it. Many spread their garments on the road; others cut leafy branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

**[CXIX, 1.]** Those going ahead and those following cried out, saying:

“Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”

**[CXX, 6.]** He entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After looking around at everything, and since it was already evening, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.

The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, he was hungry. Seeing from a distance a fig tree with leaves, he went to see whether perhaps he might find something on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.

He answered and said to it: “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples heard this.

**[CXXI, 1.]** He came to Jerusalem. Having entered the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves. He would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. And he taught, saying to them:

“Is it not written: ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of thieves.”

**[CXXII, 1.]** When the chief priests and the scribes heard this, they sought how they might destroy him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was astonished at his teaching.

**[CXXIII, 10.]** When evening came, he went out of the city. As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree dried up from its roots.

**[CXXIV, 6.]** Peter remembered and said to him: “Rabbi, look—the fig tree that you cursed has withered.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Have faith in God. Truly I tell you: whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and cast into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will be done for him.

**[CXXV, 4.]** Therefore I tell you: whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you will receive it, and it will be granted to you.

**[CXXVI, 6.]** And whenever you stand to pray, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your sins.”

**[CXXVII, 2.]** They came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders approached him and said to him: “By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority to do them?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “I will ask you one question; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things. Was the baptism of John from heaven or from human beings? Answer me.”

They reasoned among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ [Note: [Col. 0599] One manuscript of Regina has *dicemus* (‘we shall say’) instead; then, together with another older manuscript, it reads *timebant* (‘they feared’) instead of *timemus* (‘we fear’), in agreement with the Greek ἐφοβοῦντο (‘they were afraid’).]

“But if we say, ‘From human beings’—we fear the people.” For everyone held that John truly was a prophet.

They answered Jesus: “We do not know.”

And Jesus answered and said to them: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

## Chapter XII

**[CXXVIII, 5.]** He began to speak to them in parables:

“A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, leased it to tenant farmers, and went abroad. At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers, to receive from them some of the vineyard’s produce. But they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

Again he sent them another servant; they wounded him on the head and treated him shamefully. He sent another, and they killed him; and many others—some they beat, others they killed.

He still had one son, a beloved one. Finally he sent him to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’ But the tenant farmers said to one another: ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’ And they seized him, killed him, and threw him outside the vineyard.

What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.

Have you not read this Scripture:

‘The stone that the builders rejected,
this has become the cornerstone.
This was done by the Lord,
and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

**[CXXIX, 1.]** They sought to seize him, but they feared the crowd. For they understood that he had told this parable against them. They left him and went away.

**[CXXX, 2.]** They sent some Pharisees and Herodians to him, to trap him in his words. They came and said to him:

“Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not care about anyone; for you do not regard people’s status, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not? Shall we pay, or shall we not?”

Knowing their cunning, he said to them: “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius, so that I may see it.”

They brought one. And he said to them: “Whose image and inscription is this?”

They said to him: “Caesar’s.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Then give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.”

And they were amazed at him.

The Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying:

“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves a wife but leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

There were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died, leaving no offspring. The second took her and died, and he too left no offspring. The third likewise. All seven took her, and they left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.

At the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Is this not why you are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God? For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like the angels in heaven.

As for the dead being raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are therefore greatly mistaken.”

**[CXXXI, 6.]** One of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing, and, seeing that he had answered them well [Note: [Col. 0601D] In Martianay’s edition it read *plurium numero* (‘in the plural’) and *videntes* (‘seeing’), which conflicts both with the other Latin and with all the Greek books, as well as with the proper sense], asked him which commandment was first of all.

Jesus answered him: “The first of all the commandments is: ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God [Note: [Col. 0601D] One manuscript of Regina has *noster* (‘our’) instead of *tuus* (‘your’), as do most Greek codices], the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.

“The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

**[CXXXII, 10.]** The scribe said to him: “Well said, Teacher; you have spoken truthfully, for there is one God [Note: [Col. 0601D] Our manuscripts omit the noun *Deus* (‘God’) here, which is also absent in some Greek copies], and there is no other besides him. And to love him with all the heart, all the understanding, all the soul, and all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is greater than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”

**[CXXXIII, 2.]** And no one dared to question him any longer.

**[CXX IV, 2.]** Jesus answered and taught in the temple, saying:

“How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David? For David himself says in the Holy Spirit:

‘The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right hand,
until I place your enemies beneath your feet.’

“David himself therefore calls him Lord; so how is he his son?”

And the large crowd listened to him gladly.

**[CXXXV, 2.]** In his teaching he said to them:

“Beware of the scribes, who want to walk about in long robes, to be greeted in the marketplace, to sit in the front seats in the synagogues, and to have the places of honor at banquets;

**[CXXXVI, 8.]** they devour widows’ houses under the pretext of lengthy prayer. They will receive a more severe judgment.”

Jesus sat opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put money into the treasury. Many rich people were putting in large amounts. A poor widow came and put in two small coins, which is a quadrans.

Calling his disciples to him, he said to them: “Truly I tell you: this poor widow has put in more than all those who have contributed to the treasury. For they all contributed out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had—all she had to live on.”

## Chapter XIII

**[CXXXVII, 2.]** As he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him: “Teacher, look at what stones and what buildings!”

Jesus answered and said to him: “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down.”

**[CXXXVIII, 2.]** As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned him privately:

“Tell us, when will these things happen, and what sign will there be when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”

Jesus began to say to them:

“See that no one leads you astray. Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will lead many astray.

“When you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be frightened. These things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places and famines. These things are the beginning of the birth-pangs.

**[CXXXIX, 1.]** But watch yourselves. For they will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them.

**[CXL, 6.]** And the Gospel must first be proclaimed to all nations.

**[CXLI, 2.]** And when they lead you away, handing you over, do not think beforehand about what you are to say; instead, say whatever is given to you in that hour. For it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.

“Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his daughter; children will rise against their parents and put them to death. You will be hated by everyone because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.

**[CXLII, 6.]** “When you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be—let the reader understand—

**[CXLIII, 2.]** then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; let the one who is on the housetop not come down into the house, nor enter it to take anything from his house; and let the one who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.

**[CXLIV, 2.]** Woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days.

**[CXLV, 6.]** Pray that it may not happen in winter.

**[CXLVI, 2.]** For those days will be such tribulations [Note: [Col. 0602D] Two manuscripts of Regina read: “those days of tribulation will be such,” and so on. Moreover, the better-quality Greek copies immediately preceding this passage read differently: ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος, “so that your flight may not take place in winter”], as has not been from the beginning of creation, which God created, until now, nor ever will be.

**[CXLVII, 6.]** And if the Lord had not shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect, whom he chose, he shortened the days.

**[CXLVIII, 2.]** And then, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there he is!’ do not believe it.

**[CXLIX, 6.]** For false Christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders in order to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. So be watchful; behold, I have foretold everything to you.

**[CL, 2.]** But in those days, after that tribulation [Note: [Col. 0603D] In Martianay’s edition, incorrectly, *sed contenebrabitur* (‘but it will be darkened’) instead of ‘the sun,’ and so forth], the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light. The stars of heaven will fall, and the powers that are in heaven will be shaken.

**[CLI, 2.]** And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory. Then he will send his angels and gather his elect from the four winds, from the farthest end of earth to the farthest end of heaven.

“Learn a parable from the fig tree. When its branch becomes tender and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.

“Truly I tell you: this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

**[CLII, 6.]** But concerning that day or hour no one knows—not the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.

**[CLIII, 6.]** Watch, stay awake, and pray, for you do not know when the time will be.

**[CLIV, 2.]** It is like a man who went abroad, left his house, gave authority to his servants, each for his own task, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.

**[CLV, 2.]** Therefore keep watch—for you do not know when the master of the house will come, in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning—lest, coming suddenly, he find you asleep.

“What I say to you I say to all: Keep watch.”

## Chapter XIV

**[CLVI, 1.]** It was two days before Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

**[CLVII, 6.]** The chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize him by deceit and kill him. They were saying: “Not during the feast, lest there be a disturbance among the people.”

**[CLVIII, 1.]** While he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, and reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of costly spikenard ointment. She broke the alabaster jar and poured it over his head.

Some were indignant among themselves and said: “Why has this ointment been wasted? This ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they were angry with her.

But Jesus said: “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has performed a good work for me. For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish you can do good to them; but you do not always have me.

**[CLIX, 4.]** She has done what she could. She has anticipated anointing my body for burial. Truly I tell you: wherever this Gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

**[CLX, 2.]** Judas Iscariot [Alternative: Scariothes], one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests in order to betray him to them. When they heard this, they rejoiced and promised to give him money. And he sought an opportunity to hand him over.

On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, the disciples said to him: “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

He sent two of his disciples and said to them: “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him. Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is my dining room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’ And he will show you a large upper room furnished and prepared. Make the preparations for us there.”

The disciples went out and came into the city. They found everything as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

**[CLXI, 4.]** When evening came, he arrived with the Twelve. While they were reclining and eating, Jesus said:

“Truly I tell you: one of you will betray me—one who is eating with me.”

**[CLXII, 1.]** They began to be saddened and to say to him one by one: “Surely not I?”

**[CLXIII, 2.]** He said to them: “One of the Twelve, the one who dips his hand with me into the bowl. For the Son of Man goes, as it is written concerning him; but woe to that person through whom the Son of Man is betrayed.

**[CLXIV, 6.]** It would have been better for that person if he had not been born.”

**[CLXV, 1.]** As they were eating, Jesus took bread; and after blessing it, he broke it and gave it to them and said: “Take; this is my body.”

**[CLXVI, 2.]** Then he took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it. And he said to them:

“This is my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many [Note: [Col. 0603D] One manuscript of Regina adds, in a later correction, *pro vobis et pro* (‘for you and for’), and so forth. Although these words are not in the Greek exemplar, they occur frequently in the Latin books].

“Truly I tell you: I shall no longer drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”

**[CLXVII, 6.]** After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

**[CLXVIII, 4.]** Jesus said to them: “You will all be scandalized because of me this night,

**[CLXIX, 6.]** for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’ But after I have risen, I will go before you into Galilee.”

**[CLXX, 1.]** Peter said to him: “Even if all are scandalized, yet I will not be.”

Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you: today, this very night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

**[CLXXI, 6.]** But he continued to speak more vehemently: “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the others said the same.

**[CLXXII, 1.]** They came to an estate called Gethsemane.

**[CLXXIII, 6.]** And he said to his disciples: “Sit here while I pray.” He took Peter, James, and John with him, and he began to be fearful and troubled.

**[CLXXIV, 4.]** And he said to them: “My soul is sorrowful even to death. Remain here and keep watch.”

**[CLXXV, 1.]** Going forward a little, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him. And he said: “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; take this cup from me,

**[CLXXVI, 1.]** yet not what I will, but what you will.”

He came and found them sleeping.

**[CLXXVII, 2.]** He said to Peter: “Simon, are you sleeping? Were you unable to keep watch for one hour? Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.”

**[CLXXVIII, 4.]** The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.

**[CLXXIX, 6.]** Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words. When he returned, he again found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer him.

He came a third time and said to them: “Sleep now and rest. Enough.

**[CLXXX, 4.]** The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go. Behold, the one who betrays me is near.”

**[CLXXXI, 1.]** While he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot [Alternative: Scarioth], one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.

**[CLXXXII, 2.]** His betrayer had given them a sign, saying: “The one whom I kiss is he; seize him and lead him away carefully.”

When he arrived, he immediately approached him and said: “Hail, Rabbi!” And he kissed him.

They laid hands on him and seized him.

**[CLXXXIII, 1.]** One of those standing nearby drew a sword, struck the servant of the chief priest, and cut off his ear.

**[CLXXXIV, 1.]** Jesus answered and said to them: “Have you come out with swords and clubs to seize me as though I were a robber? Every day I was among you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.

**[CLXXXV, 6.]** But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”

Then all his disciples abandoned him and fled.

**[CLXXXVI, 10.]** A certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body. They seized him, but he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.

**[CLXXXVII, 1.]** They led Jesus away to the chief priest. All the priests, the scribes, and the elders assembled.

**[CLXXXVIII, 4.]** Peter followed him from a distance, as far as inside the courtyard of the chief priest. He was sitting with the attendants [Note: [Col. 0605D] The words “by the fire” are recognized neither by the Greek text nor by our manuscripts], warming himself by the fire.

**[CLXXXVIX, 2.]** The chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus, in order to put him to death, but they found none. For many were giving false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree.

**[CXC, 6.]** Some stood up and bore false testimony against him, saying: “We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands.’” But even their testimony did not agree.

The chief priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying: “Do you have no answer to what these men are testifying against you?”

But he remained silent and answered nothing.

Again the chief priest questioned him and said to him: “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

Jesus said to him: “I am.

**[CXCI, 1.]** And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the power of God [Note: [Col. 0606D] Here too the name “God,” which the Greek text does not add, is absent from the same manuscripts], and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

**[CXCII, 6.]** The chief priest tore his garments and said:

**[CXCIII, 2.]** “What further need have we of witnesses? You have heard the blasphemy. What is your judgment?”

They all condemned him as deserving death.

**[CXCIV, 1.]** Some began to spit on him, cover his face, strike him with blows, and say to him: “Prophesy!” And the attendants struck him with open hands.

**[CXCV, 1.]** While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the chief priest came. When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said: “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”

But he denied it, saying: “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.”

**[CXCVI, 1.]** He went out in front of the courtyard, and the cock crowed.

When the servant girl saw him again, she began to say to those standing nearby: “This man is one of them.”

But he denied it again.

A little later, those standing there again said to Peter: “Surely you are one of them, for you are also a Galilean.”

But he began to curse and swear: “I do not know this man you are talking about.”

Immediately the cock crowed a second time.

**[CXCVII, 2.]** Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him: “Before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times.”

And he began to weep.

[Chapter XV. CXCVIII, 2.] And immediately, at daybreak, the chief priests, with the elders, scribes, and the whole council, having held a consultation, [CXCIX, 1.] bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate. [CC, 1.] And Pilate questioned him: “Are you the king of the Jews?” But he answered him, “You say so.” [CCI, 4.] And the chief priests accused him of many things. Pilate again questioned him, saying: “Do you not answer anything? See how many charges they bring against you!” But Jesus answered nothing further, so that Pilate was amazed. [CCII, 2.] Now on the feast day he used to release to them one prisoner, whichever one they requested. [CCIII, 4.] There was one called Barabbas, [Col. 0606C] who was imprisoned with the rebels, who had committed murder during the insurrection. And when the crowd had come up, it began to ask, just as he always did for them. Pilate answered them and said: “Do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?” For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy. [CCIV, 1.] But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he would release Barabbas to them instead. [CCV, 1.] Pilate again answered and said to them: “What then do you want me to do to the king of the Jews?” But they again shouted: “Crucify him!” Pilate, however, said to them: “For what evil has he done?” But they shouted even more: “Crucify him!” [CCVI, 1.] Pilate, wishing to satisfy the people, released Barabbas to them and handed Jesus over, scourged, to be crucified. [CCVII, 4.] The soldiers led him into the courtyard of the praetorium, and summoned the whole cohort; they clothed him in purple and placed upon him a crown of thorns, weaving it. And they began to greet him: “Hail, king of the Jews.” [CCVIII, 6.] And they struck his head with a reed, spat upon him, and, kneeling, worshiped him. And after mocking him, they stripped him of the purple and clothed him in their garments; and they led him out to crucify him. [CCIX, 1.] And they compelled a passer-by, a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross. [CCX, 1.] And they brought him to Golgotha, [Col. 0607A] a place which is interpreted as “the place of the Skull.” [CCXI, 4.] And they gave him wine mixed with myrrh to drink; but he did not accept it. [CCXII, 1.] And having crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots over them to determine what each should take. [CCXIII, 10.] Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him. [CCXV, 1.] And the inscription of his charge was written: “The king of the Jews.” [CCXV, 1.] And with him they crucified two robbers, one on his right and the other on his left. [CCXVI, 8.] And the Scripture was fulfilled which says: “And he was reckoned among the lawless.” [CCXVII, 6.] And those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads and saying: “Ah! [Note: One Regina manuscript has *qui destruxit* (“who destroyed”); another has *qui destruit* (“who destroys”); then, with equal agreement, *tribus diebus aedificat* (“in three days he builds”), and so forth.] You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save yourself by coming down from the cross.” [CCXVIII, 2.] Likewise the chief priests, mocking him, said to one another with the scribes: “He saved others; he cannot save himself. Let Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe.” [CCXIX, 2.] And those who had been crucified with him reviled him.

[CCXX, 2.] And when the sixth hour had come, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. [CCXXI, 6.] And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: “Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabacthani?”—which is interpreted: “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?” And some of those standing nearby, hearing this, said: “Look, he is calling Elijah.” [CCXXII, 2.] But one man ran and, filling a sponge with vinegar, put it around a reed and gave him a drink, saying: “Leave him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.” [CCXXIII, 1.] [Col. 0607C] But Jesus, uttering a loud cry, breathed his last. [CCXXIV, 2.] And the veil of the temple was torn in two, from the top [Alternative: from above] to the bottom. [CCXXV, 2.] Now when the centurion who stood opposite him saw that he had breathed his last while crying out in this way, he said: “Truly this man was the Son of God.” [CCXXVI, 6.] There were also women looking on from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joseph [Alternative: Joshua], and Salome. And when he was in Galilee, they followed him and ministered to him, as did many other women who had gone up with him to Jerusalem. [CCXXVII, 1.] And when evening had already come—for it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath—Joseph of Arimathea, a distinguished councillor, who himself was also awaiting the kingdom of God, came boldly to Pilate and [Col. 0607D] asked for the body of Jesus. Pilate was amazed that he had already died. And summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had already died. And when he had learned this from the centurion, [Col. 0608A] he granted the body to Joseph. [CCXXVIII, 1.] Joseph, having bought a linen cloth, took him down, wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a tomb that had been hewn out of rock; and he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb. [CCXXIX, 6.] Now Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joseph [Alternative: Joshua] were watching where he was laid.

[Chapter XVI. CCXXX, 8.] And when the sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary of James, and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint Jesus. [CCXXXI, 1.] And very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb after the sun had risen. And they said to one another: “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?” And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away. For it was very large. And entering the [Col. 0608B] tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were astonished. [CCXXXII, 2.] He said to them: “Do not be afraid. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Behold the place where they laid him. But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you into Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.” [CCXXXIII, 2.] But they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and terror had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

Having risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons. She went and announced it to those who had been with him, while they were mourning and weeping. And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe. [CCXXXIV, 8.] After this [Col. 0608C] he was revealed in another form to two of them as they were walking and going into the countryside. And they went and announced it to the rest; nor did they believe them. [CCXXXV, 10.] Finally, he appeared to the eleven as they were reclining, and reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him after he had risen. And he said to them: “Go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; but whoever does not believe will be condemned. These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them. They will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.” And the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up [Col. 0608D] into heaven and sits at the right hand of God. But they went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word by the signs that followed.

[Col. 0607] The Gospel according to Mark ends.

[Col. 0607]

THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE BEGINS.

[Col. 0607D] [Chapter I, I, 10.] [Note: Many printed books, together with not a few manuscript codices, place this first chapter of Luke below, at verse 5, beginning with the words: “There was in the days of Herod, king of Judaea, a certain priest,” and so forth. But they assign the preceding preface neither to any chapter nor to any canon. How incorrect this is may be understood from the fact that it seems to imply that the aforesaid preface is not the genuine work of the evangelist Luke, nor inspired by God. It is impious to say this. We have restored these matters in accordance with the evidence of the manuscripts of our library at Saint-Germain, numbers 4, 19, and 24. Another copy of the same excellent library, number 18, could easily be added to these.
