In it, together with the notation of the first chapter—which nowhere appears in what follows—the whole beginning of Luke up to the aforesaid words of verse 5, “There was in the days of Herod,” and so forth, exclusively, has been excised. MART.] Since many have undertaken [Col. 0608D] to arrange an account of the events that have been fulfilled among us [Col. 0609A], just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word delivered them to us, it seemed good to me also, having followed [Note: More closely conforming to the Greek, our manuscripts read *assecuto a principio omnibus diligenter* (“having diligently followed all things from the beginning”): in Greek, *Ἔδοξε κᾀμοὶ, παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς κ. τ. λ.* (“It seemed good to me also, having accurately followed all things from the beginning,” etc.). Moreover, see Martianay’s discussion of this Preface in the Notes.] everything carefully from the beginning, to write it out for you in orderly sequence, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may recognize the truth of the matters about which you have been instructed.

There was in the days of Herod, king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah; and his wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth. Now both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in years.

And it happened, when he was serving as priest [Note: Two Regina manuscripts insert the name “Zechariah” here, and some Greek copies likewise retain it.] in the order of his division before God, according to the custom of the priesthood, that he was chosen by lot to offer incense, entering [Col. 0609B] the temple of the Lord. And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense. Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him. But the angel said to him: “Do not fear, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John. And there will be joy and exultation for you, and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord; he will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb. And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. He himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers toward the children, and the unbelieving [Note: Again, two Regina manuscripts prefer *incredibiles* (“unbelieving”) instead of *incredulos* (“those who do not believe”).] toward the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare [Col. 0609C] for the Lord a perfected people.”

And Zechariah said to the angel: “How shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in years.” And the angel answered and said to him: “I am Gabriel, who stand before [Col. 0610A] God, and I have been sent to speak to you and announce these good things to you. And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day when these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”

And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were wondering why he was delayed in the temple. But when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he was making signs to them and remained mute. And when the days of his service had been completed, he went to his home. After these days, his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she hid herself for five months, saying: “Thus the Lord has dealt with me in the days when he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among people.”

[II, 5.] [Note: There is great disagreement here among both manuscript and printed books. For many manuscripts place the second chapter above, at verse 19, with these words: “And the angel answered and said to him: I am Gabriel, who stand before God, and I have been sent to speak to you and announce these good things to you.” Since these words are assigned to the fifth canon, they ought to correspond with the third canon of Matthew’s Gospel: “Now the generation of Christ was thus: When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.” But it is clear that there is no agreement between these passages, since the former concerns the conception of John the forerunner, whereas the latter concerns the conception of Christ. This is an error, or rather the carelessness of copyists, who, when they saw in copies—as also in the Saint-Germain manuscript number 18, which in this matter we rightly follow as the most corrected and most consistent with reason, and prefer to all the others—that the second chapter of Luke was marked at the words of verse 26, which are found here in the text, namely: “Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent,” where the angel Gabriel is mentioned, just as in the other passage of verse 19 cited above, imprudently took one place for the other. This was especially likely because in certain codices, as in our manuscript of Saint-Germain number 19, those two passages in two columns of the same page correspond almost perfectly with one another on the same line. Not noticing this, all the printed books, with no manuscript codex among those we have at hand supporting them, separate the present second chapter into the following chapter at verse 26, with the words: “And it happened, when they were there, that the days were fulfilled for her to give birth, and she bore her firstborn son and wrapped him in swaddling clothes”—although these words describe the birth of Christ, not his conception, as in the parallel passage in Matthew. MART.]

Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a [Col. 0610B] city of Galilee named Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary. [III, 10.] And the angel entered to her and said: “Hail, full of grace; the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.” When she heard this, she was troubled at his saying and considered what sort of greeting this might be. And the angel said to her: “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God. Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father. And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end.”

And Mary said to the angel: “How will this happen, since I do not know a man?” And the angel answered and said to her: [Col. 0610C] “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who will be born [Note: The Regina manuscripts entirely lack the words *ex te* (“from you”), which are also found only rarely in Greek copies.] from you will be called the Son of God. And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has also conceived a son in her old age; [Col. 0611A] and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren, because no word will be impossible with God.”

And Mary said: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.

And Mary arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, to a city of Judah. And she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. And it happened that when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the infant leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. And she cried out with a loud voice and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And from where is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, as the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed is she who believed [Note: The same manuscripts read: “Blessed is she who believed,” and consistently continue: “because there will be fulfillment of the things spoken to her by the Lord,” closer also to the Greek: *ἡ πιστεύσασα, ὅτι ἔσται τελείωσις τοῖς λελαλημένοις αὐτῇ παρὰ Κυρίου*, “she who believed, because there will be fulfillment of the things spoken to her by the Lord.”], because the things spoken to you [Col. 0611B] by the Lord will be fulfilled.”

And Mary said:

“My soul magnifies the Lord,

and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

For he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid; behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

For he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name.

And his mercy is from generation to generation [Note: Two Regina manuscripts read: “through generations and generations.”] for those who fear him.

He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.

He has brought down the powerful from their throne and exalted the humble.

He has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent away empty.

He has received Israel, his servant, remembering [Col. 0611C] his mercy [Note: The same manuscripts read “to remember his mercy,” again closer to the Greek *μνησθῆναι ἐλέους*.],

as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his offspring forever.”

And Mary remained with her about three months, and she returned to her home.

Now Elizabeth’s time to give birth was fulfilled, and she bore a son. And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her. And it happened that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him by the name of his father, Zechariah. But his mother answered and said: “Not so; he shall be called John.” And they said to her: “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.” And they made signs to his father, asking what he wanted him to be called. And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote, [Col. 0611D] saying: “John is his name.” And they were all amazed. Immediately his mouth and tongue were opened, and he spoke, blessing God. And fear came upon all their neighbors, and throughout all the hill country of Judaea all these things were being reported. And all who heard them kept them in their heart, saying: [Note: With equal agreement, the same manuscripts read: “What, do you suppose,” corresponding to the Greek *Τί ἄρα*, “What then.”] “Who, do you suppose, will this child be?” For the hand of the Lord was with him.

And Zechariah his father [Col. 0612A] was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:

“Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and accomplished redemption for his people.

And he has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,

as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets who have existed from of old:

salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,

to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,

the oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant us

that, delivered from the hand of our enemies without fear, [Col. 0612B] we might serve him

in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,

to give knowledge of salvation to his people for the forgiveness of their sins,

through the tender mercies of our God, by which the dawn from on high has visited us,

to shine upon those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”

Now the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day of his manifestation to Israel.

[Col. 0612C] [Chapter II.] And it happened in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered. This registration was first made [Note: One of our manuscripts and another belonging to Crassus, in Martianay’s possession, read: “This registration was made while the governor,” and so forth, without the particle *a*; this also gives a more coherent sense in accordance with the Greek, *ἐγένετο ἡγεμονεύοντος τῆς Συρίας Κυρηνίου*, “it occurred while Quirinius was governing Syria.”] when Quirinius was governor of Syria. And all went to be registered, each to his own city. Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David, to be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was pregnant.

And it happened that while they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth. And she bore her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging.

And there were shepherds in that region, keeping watch and guarding the watches of the night over their flock. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood [Col. 0612D] beside them, and the brightness of God shone around them, and they were struck with great fear. And the angel said to them: “Do not fear. For behold, I announce to you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people: for today a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David. And this will be a sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger.”

And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, [Col. 0613A] praising God and saying: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.”

And it happened that when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another: “Let us go as far as Bethlehem and see this event that has happened, which the Lord has shown us.” And they came with haste and found Mary, Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger. And when they saw this, they recognized the matter that had been spoken to them about this child. And all who heard it were amazed at the things that had been told them by the shepherds. But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart. And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.

And when the eight days had been completed [Col. 0613B] for the circumcision of the child, [Note: The word *puer* (“child”), which is also absent from the better Greek manuscripts, is entirely absent from one Regina manuscript; in the other it was added by a second hand.] his name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses had been fulfilled, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.” And they were to offer a sacrifice according to what was said in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. And he had received an answer from the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. And he came in the Spirit into the temple.

[Col. 0613C] And when the parents of the child Jesus brought him in, to do for him according to the custom of the law, he himself took him into his arms, blessed God, and said:

“Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace,

for my eyes have seen your salvation,

which you have prepared before the face of all peoples,

a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.”

And his father and mother were amazed at the things that were said about him. And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: “Behold, this one is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be opposed. And a sword will pierce your own [Col. 0613D] soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”

And there was Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days, and had lived with her husband for seven years after her virginity. And she was a widow until eighty-four years of age. She did not depart from the temple, serving with fastings and prayers night and day. And she, arriving at that very hour, gave thanks to the Lord and spoke about him to all who were awaiting the redemption of [Note: In our manuscripts, “Jerusalem” is read instead of “Israel,” as also in most Greek books, *Ἱερουσαλήμ*.] Israel.

And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth. [Col. 0614A] And the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was in him.

And his parents went every year to Jerusalem for the solemn feast of Passover. And when he was twelve years old, while they were going up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast, and when the days had been completed, as they were returning, the child Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it. Supposing him to be in the traveling company, they came a day’s journey and sought him among their relatives and acquaintances. And when they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him. And it happened that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, listening to them and questioning them. [IV, 2.] And all who heard him were astonished at his understanding and his answers [Col. 0614B]. And when they saw him, they were amazed.

[V, 10.] And his mother said to him: “Son, why have you done this to us? Behold, your father and I have been searching for you in sorrow.” And he said to them: “Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be in the things that belong to my Father?” And they did not understand the word that he spoke to them. And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was subject to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart. And Jesus advanced in wisdom, age, and favor with God and human beings.

[Chapter III. VI, 3.] Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governing Judaea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene, under the chief [Col. 0614C] priests Annas and Caiaphas, the word of the Lord came upon John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness. [VII, 1.] And he came into all the region of the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, as it is written in the book of the sayings of Isaiah the prophet:

“The voice of one crying in the wilderness:

Prepare the way of the Lord;

make his paths straight.

Every valley shall be filled,

and every mountain and hill shall be brought low,

and the crooked places shall become straight,

and the rough ways into smooth roads;

and every flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

[VIII, 5.] Therefore he said to the crowds who were coming out to be baptized by him: “Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the coming wrath? Produce, therefore, fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say: ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God is able from these [Col. 0614D] stones to raise up children for Abraham. For already the axe has been placed at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

[IX, 10.] And the crowds questioned him, saying: “What then shall we do?” He answered and said to them: “Whoever has two tunics should give to one who has none; and whoever has food should do likewise.” Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him: “Teacher, what shall we do?” But he said to them: “Do nothing more than what has been appointed for you.” And soldiers also questioned him, [Col. 0615A] saying: “And what shall we do?” And he said to them: “Do violence to no one, and bring no false accusation; and be content with your wages.”

Now while the people were expecting, and all were reasoning in their hearts about John, whether perhaps he himself was the Christ, John answered, saying to all: [X, 1.] “I baptize you with water, but one stronger than I is coming, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire. [XI, 5.] His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will cleanse his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his granary, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”

And with many other exhortations he preached the good news to the people.

[XII, 2.] But Herod the tetrarch, when he was reproved by him concerning Herodias, the wife of his brother, and concerning all the evil things [Col. 0615B] that Herod had done, added this also to them all: he shut John up in prison.

[XIII, 1.] Now it happened, when all the people had been baptized, and when Jesus also had been baptized and was praying, that heaven was opened. And the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”

[XIV, 5.] And Jesus himself was beginning to be about thirty years old, as was supposed, the son of Joseph, who was the son of Heli, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Janne, the son of Joseph, the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Hesli, the son of Nagge, the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semei, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah, the son of Joanna, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of [Col. 0615C] Neri, the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosan, the son of Elmadan, the son of Er, the son of Jesus, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonah, the son of Eliakim, the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David, the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon, the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah, the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor, the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah, the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech, the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of [Col. 0615D] Jared, the son of Mahalaleel [Manuscript: Maleel], the son of Cainan, the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.

## [Chapter IV. XV, 2.]

Now Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness for forty days, and was tempted by the devil. [XVI, 5.] And he ate nothing during those days; and when they were completed, he was hungry. The devil said to him: “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.” [Col. 0616A] And Jesus answered him: “It is written: ‘Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”

And the devil led him [Note: [Col. 0615D] The words “to a high mountain,” which are also lacking in certain Greek books, are absent from both Regina manuscripts.] onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in an instant of time. And he said to him: “I will give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if you worship before me, all will be yours.” And Jesus answered and said to him: “It is written:” [Note: [Col. 0615D] The Regina manuscripts insert “God,” a name also retained by the Greek copies. A little earlier the Sixtine Edition has the additional words [Col. 0616D] “if, falling down, you worship me.”] “You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.”

And he led him into Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him: “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. For it is written that he has commanded his angels concerning you, to preserve you; and that they will bear you up in their hands, lest you perhaps strike your foot against a stone.” And Jesus answered and said to him: [Col. 0616B] “It has been said: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’” And when every temptation had been completed, the devil departed from him until an opportune time.

### [XVII, 1.]

And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report about him went out through the whole region. And he taught in their synagogues, and was glorified by all.

### [XVIII, 10.]

And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. According to his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read. And the book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. When he had unrolled the book, he found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; for this reason he has anointed me. He has sent me to proclaim good news to the poor, [Note: [Col. 0616D] Here again the words “to heal the brokenhearted,” which are omitted by certain Greek manuscripts, are absent from both Regina manuscripts; in the second Vatican manuscript, however, they were added by a later correction.] to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord [Col. 0616C] and the day of recompense.”

And when he had folded up the book, he returned it to the attendant and sat down. And the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed upon him. Then he began to say to them: “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”

### [XIX, 1.]

And all bore witness to him and marveled at the words of grace that proceeded from his mouth, and they said: “Is this not Joseph’s son?”

### [XX, 10.]

And he said to them: “Surely you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we have heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in your homeland.’”

### [XXI, 1.]

And he said: “Amen, I say to you, no prophet is acceptable in his homeland. In truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were shut up for three years and six months, when there was a great famine throughout the whole land; yet Elijah was sent to none of them except to Zarephath of Sidon, to a widowed woman. And there were many lepers in Israel under the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman [Ms. Neman] the Syrian.”

And all in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard this. And they rose up and drove him outside the city, and led him to the brow of the mountain on which their city had been built, in order to throw him down. But he, passing through the midst of them, went on. [Col. 0617A]

### [XXIII, 8.]

And he went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and there he taught them on the Sabbaths.

### [XXIV, 2.]

And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word was with authority.

### [XXV, 8.]

And in the synagogue there was a man who had an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying: “Let us alone! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—[Note: [Col. 0617D] In Greek, τίς εἶ—“who you are”—in the Regina manuscript.] the Holy One of God.”

And Jesus rebuked him, saying: “Be silent, and come out of him.” And when the demon had thrown him down in the midst, it came out of him and did him no harm. And terror came upon everyone, and they spoke with one another, saying: “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.” And a report about him spread into every place of the region. [Col. 0617B]

### [XXVI, 2.]

And rising from the synagogue, he entered Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was held by a severe fever, and they appealed to him on her behalf. And standing over her, he rebuked the fever, and it left her. And immediately she rose and served them.

When the sun had set, all who had the sick with various diseases brought them to him. And he laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.

### [XXVII, 8.]

And demons came out from many, crying out and saying: “You are the Son of God.” And rebuking them, he would not permit them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.

### [XXVIII, 8.]

And when day came, he went out and proceeded to a deserted place. And the crowds sought him, and [Note: [Col. 0617D] Without the negative particle, the Regina manuscripts have “and they came as far as him,” in agreement with nearly all the Greek copies.] did not come all the way to him; and they detained him so that he would not leave them. But he said to them: [Col. 0617C] “I must proclaim the kingdom of God to the other cities also, because for this I was sent.”

And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.

## [Chapter V. XXIX, 10.]

And it happened that, while the crowds were pressing upon him to hear the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesareth. And he saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen had gone down and were washing their nets. And getting into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, he asked him to put out a little from the shore. And sitting down, he taught the crowds from the boat.

### [XXX, 9.]

When he had ceased speaking, he said to Simon: “Put out into the deep, and lower your nets for a catch.” And Simon answered and said to him: “Master, having labored throughout the whole night, we caught nothing; but at your word I will lower the net.”

And when they had done this, they enclosed a very large quantity of fish, and their net was breaking. And they beckoned to their companions who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that [Note: [Col. 0618D] The adverb “almost,” which is not found in the better Greek books, is entirely absent from the Regina manuscript.] they almost sank.

### [XXXI, 10.]

When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees, saying: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.” For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him because of the catch of fish that they had taken; and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners.

### [XXXII, 2.]

And Jesus said to Simon: “Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching human beings.” And when they had brought the boats to land, leaving everything, they followed him.

### [XXXIII, 2.]

And it happened that, while he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying: “Lord, if you are willing, you can cleanse me.” And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I am willing. Be cleansed.” And immediately the leprosy left him.

And he ordered him to tell no one: “But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

### [XXXIV, 1.]

But the report about him spread all the more, and great crowds gathered to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses.

### [XXXV, 2.]

But he was in the wilderness and praying.

### [XXXVI, 2.]

[Col. 0618B] And it happened that on one of the days he was sitting and teaching. And Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.

### [XXXVII, 1.]

And behold, men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they sought to bring him in and place him before him. And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the crowd, they went up onto the roof and lowered him through the tiles, together with the bed, into the midst before Jesus.

When he saw their faith, he said: “Man, your sins are forgiven you.” And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason, saying: “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”

But when Jesus recognized their thoughts, he answered and said to them: [Col. 0618C] “Why are you reasoning in your hearts? Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say: ‘Rise and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—“I say to you, rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.”

And immediately he rose up before them, took up the bed on which he had been lying, and went to his house, glorifying God. And astonishment seized them all, and they glorified God. And they were filled with fear, saying: “We have seen extraordinary things today.”

### [XXXVIII, 2.]

And after these things he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him: “Follow me.” And leaving everything, he rose and followed him.

### [XXXIX, 2.]

And Levi made a great feast for him in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining at table with them. [Col. 0618D] And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured, saying to his disciples: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

### [XL, 2.]

And Jesus answered and said to them: “Those who are well do not need a physician, but those who are ill. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

And they said to him: “Why do the disciples of John fast frequently and offer prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”

And he said to them: “Can you make the children of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”

And he also told them a parable: “No one puts a patch from a new garment onto an old garment; otherwise he tears the new one, and the patch from the new does not match the old. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled, and the wineskins will perish. Rather, new wine must be put into new wineskins, and both are preserved. And no one who has drunk old wine immediately wants new, for he says: ‘The old is better.’”

## [Chapter VI. XLI, 2.]

And it happened that on the second-first Sabbath, as he was passing through the grainfields, his disciples were plucking ears of grain and eating them, rubbing them in their hands. But some of the Pharisees said to them: [Col. 0619B] “Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbaths?”

And Jesus answered them and said: “Have you not even read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him—how he entered the house of God, took the bread of the Presence, ate it, and gave it to those who were with him, although it is not permitted for anyone to eat it except the priests?”

### [XLII, 2.]

And he said to them: “The Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

And it happened on another Sabbath that he entered the synagogue and taught. And there was a man whose right hand was withered. The scribes and the Pharisees were watching to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find a charge against him.

But he knew their thoughts, and he said to the man who had the withered hand: “Rise and stand in the midst.” And he rose and stood. Then Jesus said to them: [Col. 0619C] “I ask you whether it is permitted on the Sabbaths to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?”

And after looking around at them all, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored. But they were filled with folly, and they discussed with one another what they should do to Jesus.

### [XLIII, 2.]

And it happened in those days that he went out onto the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to God.

### [XLIV, 2.]

And when day came, he called his disciples, and chose twelve of them—whom he also named Apostles: Simon, whom he surnamed Peter, and Andrew his brother; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus; and Simon, who is called the Zealot; and Judas of James; and Judas Iscariot [Col. 0619D] [Ms. Scarioth], who was the betrayer.

### [XLV, 1.]

And coming down with them, he stood on a level place, together with a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon, who had come to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses. And those who were troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

And the whole crowd sought to touch him, because power went out from him and healed them all.

### [XLVI, 5.]

And he, lifting his eyes toward his disciples, said: “Blessed are you who are poor, because yours is the kingdom of God.” [Col. 0620A]

### [XLVII, 5.]

“Blessed are you who hunger now, because you will be filled.”

### [XLVIII, 5.]

“Blessed are you who weep now, because you will laugh.”

### [XLIX, 5.]

“Blessed will you be when people hate you, and when they exclude you, reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, on account of the Son of Man. Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven; for their fathers did the same things to the prophets.

### [L, 10.]

“But woe to you who are rich, because you have your consolation. Woe to you who are filled, because you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.

### [LI, 10.]

“Woe when all people speak well of you [Note: [Col. 0619D] The Vatican and Regina manuscripts have “when all people speak well of you,” and this “all” is also present in the original Greek text according to most copies: πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι. Then two Regina manuscripts have “their fathers did these things to the prophets” [Col. 0620D], which has been repeated from the immediately preceding verse; for here the text most correctly calls them false prophets, and in the second correction in the other Regina manuscript the wording has likewise been restored.] for their fathers did the same things to the false prophets.

### [LII, 5.]

“But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you. Bless those who curse you, and pray for those who slander you.

### [LIII, 5.]

“To the one who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other also. And from the one who takes away your garment, do not withhold your tunic either. Give to everyone who asks you, and from the one who takes away what is yours, do not demand it back.

### [LIV, 5.]

“And just as you wish people to do to you, do the same to them. And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.

### [LV, 5.]

“And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do this. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners, in order to receive an equal return.

“But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return. And your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and evil. Therefore be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

### [LVI, 2.]

“Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven. Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing, they will pour into your lap. For with the same measure with which you measure, it will be measured back to you.

### [LVII, 5.]

And he also told them a parable: “Can a blind person lead a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?

### [LVIII, 3.]

“A disciple is not above his teacher; but everyone who is perfected will be like his teacher.

### [LIX, 5.]

[Col. 0620D] “Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother: ‘Brother, let me remove the splinter from your eye,’ while you yourself do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the splinter from your brother’s eye.

### [LX, 5.]

“For there is no good tree that produces bad fruit, nor a bad tree producing good fruit. For every tree is known by its fruit. [Col. 0621A]

### [LXI, 5.]

“For they do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.

### [LXII, 5.]

“A good person brings forth good from the good treasure of his heart, and an evil person brings forth evil from the evil treasure. For from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

### [LXIII, 3.]

“Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say?

### [LXIV, 5.]

“Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and does them—I will show you whom he is like. He is like a man building a house, who dug deeply and laid its foundation on rock. When a flood occurred, the river struck that house but could not shake it, because it had been founded on rock.

“But the one who hears and does not act is like a man building his house on the ground without a foundation. When the river struck it, it immediately collapsed, and the ruin of that house was great.” [Col. 0621B]

## [Chapter VII. LXV, 3.]

When he had completed all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum. A certain centurion’s servant, who was ill, was close to death; he was precious to him. And when he heard about Jesus, he sent to him the elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.

And when they had come to Jesus, they earnestly appealed to him, saying: “He is worthy that you should grant this to him. For he loves our nation, and he himself built our synagogue for us.”

And Jesus went with them. And when he was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying: “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof. For this reason I did not consider myself worthy even to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.

“For I also am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

When Jesus heard this, he marveled. And turning to the crowds following him, he said: “Amen [Note: [Col. 0621D] One Regina manuscript repeats “Amen,” as it is also retained in most Greek copies; in one or two copies it is said only once.] I say to you, I have not found such faith even in Israel.”

### [LXVI, 5.]

And those who had been sent, when they returned to the house, found the servant who had been ill healthy.

### [LXVII, 10.]

And it happened afterward that he went to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd were going with him. And as he approached the gate of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother; and she was a widow, and a large crowd from the city was with her.

When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her: “Do not weep.” [Col. 0621D] And he approached and touched the bier—and those carrying it stood still—and he said: “Young man, I say to you, arise.”

And the dead man sat up and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother. Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying: “A great prophet has arisen among us,” and “God has visited his people.”

### [LXVIII, 10.]

And this report about him went out throughout all Judea and the entire surrounding region. [Col. 0622A]

### [LXIX, 5.]

And John’s disciples reported all these things to him. And John summoned two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus, saying: “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?”

When the men had come to him, they said: “John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying: ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?’”

At that very hour he healed many of illnesses, afflictions, and evil spirits, and he granted sight to many blind people.

And he answered and said to them: “Go and report to John what you have heard and seen: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, the poor receive good news; and blessed is whoever is not scandalized by me.”

And when John’s messengers had departed, [Col. 0622B] he began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see—a reed shaken by the wind? [Note: [Col. 0621D] The Vatican manuscript and two Regina manuscripts have “a reed being shaken by the wind?” The Greek has κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον, “a reed being shaken by the wind.”]

“But what did you go out to see—a man dressed in soft garments? Behold, those who are in splendid clothing and luxury are in kings’ houses.

“But what did you go out to see—a prophet? Indeed, I say to you, and more than a prophet:

### [LXX, 2.]

“This is the one of whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send my angel before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’

### [LXXI, 5.]

“For I say to you, among those born of women no prophet is greater than John the Baptist. But the one who is lesser in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

### [LXXII, 10.]

And all the people who heard, including the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John. But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected God’s counsel with respect to themselves, not having been baptized by him. [Col. 0622C]

[Note: [Col. 0621D] The words “but the Lord said,” which are also lacking in certain Greek copies, are absent from our manuscripts.]

But the Lord said:

### [LXXIII, 5.]

“To what, then, shall I compare the people of this generation, and to what are they like? They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, saying: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we mourned, and you did not [Note: [Col. 0622D] One Vatican manuscript has “and you did not lament”; the Greek is καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε, “and you did not weep.”] weep.’

“For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: ‘He has a demon.’ The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say: ‘Behold, a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ And wisdom was justified by all her children.”

### [LXXIV, 1.]

A certain Pharisee was asking him to eat with him. [Note: [Col. 0622D] Here, along with the Vatican manuscript, one Regina manuscript has “asked” instead of “was asking”; shortly afterward, all agree in reading “he reclined,” instead of “he would recline.”]

And he entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at table. And behold, there was a woman in the city who was a sinner. When she learned that he had reclined in the Pharisee’s house, she brought an alabaster jar of ointment. And standing behind him at his feet, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head; and she kissed his feet and anointed them with ointment.

When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself: “If this man were a prophet, he would surely know who and what sort of woman this is who touches him [Col. 0623A], for she is a sinner.” [Note: [Col. 0622D] The same manuscript has “who and what sort of woman she was,” and so forth.]

And Jesus answered and said to him: “Simon, I have something to say to you.” And he said: “Teacher, speak.”

“There were two debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they had nothing with which to repay, he forgave both of them. Which of them, then, will love him more?”

Simon answered and said: “I suppose the one to whom he forgave more.”

And he said to him: “You have judged correctly.”

And turning toward the woman, he said to Simon: “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave me no kiss, but she, from the time she entered, has not ceased kissing my feet. You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.

“Therefore I say to you: [Note: [Col. 0623D] One Vatican manuscript and another Regina manuscript prefer the future form, “They will be forgiven,” instead of “They are forgiven.”] Her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much. But the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.”

And he said to her: “Your sins are forgiven.”

And those reclining at table with him began to say among themselves: “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”

And he said to the woman: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

## [Chapter VIII. LXXV, 10.]

And it happened afterward that he journeyed through cities and villages, proclaiming and announcing the kingdom of God; and the Twelve were with him, together with certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, who is called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out; and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward; and Susanna; and many others who ministered to him from their resources. [Col. 0623C]

### [LXXVI, 2.]

And when a very large crowd had gathered, and people from the cities were hurrying to him, he spoke by means of a parable:

“The sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and was trampled, and the birds of the sky devoured it. And some fell upon the rock, and when it had sprouted, it withered because it had no moisture. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns that sprang up with it choked it. And some fell into good soil, and when it had grown, it produced a hundredfold harvest.”

As he said this, he cried out: “Whoever has ears for hearing, let him hear.”

And his disciples asked him what this parable meant. And he said to them: “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, [LXXVII, 1.] but to the others in parables, so that, seeing, they may not see, and hearing, they may not understand.

[Col. 0623D] ### [LXXVIII, 2.]

“Now this is the parable: The seed is the word of God. Those beside the road are the ones who hear; then the devil comes and takes the word from their heart, so that, believing, they may not be saved.

“Those upon the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but these have no roots: they believe for a time, and at the time of testing they fall away.

“As for what fell among the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, but as they go on their way they are choked by anxieties, riches, and pleasures of life, and they do not bring forth fruit.

“As for what fell into good soil, these are the ones who, hearing the word with a good and excellent heart, retain it and bear fruit with perseverance. [Col. 0624A]

### [LXXIX, 2.]

“No one who lights a lamp covers it with a vessel or places it under a bed; rather, he places it on a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.

### [LXXX, 2.]

“For nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest, nor concealed that will not be known and come into the open.

### [LXXI, 5.]

“Therefore, see how you hear. For to the one who has, it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he supposes himself to have will be taken away from him.

### [LXXXII, 2.]

And his mother and his brothers came to him, and they could not approach him because of the crowd. And it was reported to him: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see you.”

But he answered and said to them: “My mother and my brothers are these: those who hear the word of God and do it.”

### [LXXXIII, 2.]

And it happened on one of the days that he got into a boat, and his disciples with him, and he said to them: “Let us cross over to the other side of the lake.” And they set out.

And as they were sailing, he fell asleep. And a windstorm descended upon the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger. They approached and woke him, saying: “Master, we are perishing.”

But he rose and rebuked the wind and the tempest of the water, and it ceased, and there was calm. And he said to them: “Where is your faith?”

But, being afraid, they marveled among themselves, saying: “Who, then, is this, that he commands even the winds and the sea, and they obey him?”

And they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee. And when he had gone ashore, a certain man who had a demon for a long time met him. He wore no clothing and did not remain in a house, but among the tombs.

When he saw Jesus, he fell before him and, crying out with a loud voice, said: “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For it had seized him many times, and he had been bound with chains and fetters and kept under guard; but breaking the bonds, he was driven by the demon into deserted places.

Jesus asked him, saying: “What is your name?”

And he said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.

And they begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.

Now there was there a large herd of pigs feeding on the mountain. And they begged him to permit them to enter into them. And he permitted them.

The demons therefore came out of the man and entered the pigs. And the herd rushed down the steep slope into the lake and was drowned.

When those who were tending them saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the villages. And they went out to see what had happened, and came to Jesus. And they found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting, clothed and in his right mind, at his feet; and they were afraid.

Those who had seen it also reported to them how the man who had been possessed by the legion had been healed. And the whole multitude of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to depart from them, because they were seized by great fear. [Col. 0625A]

### [LXXXIV, 8.]

But he got into the boat and returned. And the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to be with him. But Jesus dismissed him, saying: “Return to your house and recount how much God has done for you.”

And he went throughout the whole city, proclaiming how much Jesus had done for him.

### [LXXXV, 2.]

And it happened that when Jesus had returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him. And behold, a man named Jairus came, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. And he fell at Jesus’ feet, begging him to enter his house, because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying.

And it happened that, as he went, the crowds were pressing upon him. And a certain woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years, and had spent all her means on physicians, and could not be healed by anyone, approached from behind and touched the fringe of his garment. And immediately the flow of her blood stopped.

And Jesus said: “Who touched me?”

But while everyone was denying it, Peter and those who were with him said: “Master, the crowds are pressing upon you and afflicting you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

And Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I know that power has gone out from me.”

When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell before his feet. And she declared before all the people for what reason she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.

But he said to her: “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

While he was still speaking, someone came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house and said to him: “Your daughter has died; do not trouble him.”

But when Jesus heard this word, he answered the girl’s father: [Col. 0625C] “Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved.”

And when he had come to the house, he did not permit anyone to enter with him except Peter, James, and John, and the girl’s father and mother.

Now everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said: “Do not weep; she is not dead [Note: [Col. 0625] The manuscripts used here do not add “the girl”; this noun also occurs here in only very rare Greek copies.] but sleeping.”

And they laughed at him, knowing that she was dead.

But he, taking her hand, cried out, saying: “Girl, arise.”

And her spirit returned, and she immediately rose. And he ordered that food be given to her.

And her parents were astonished, and he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.

[Chapter IX. LXXXVI, 2.] Having summoned the twelve Apostles, he gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases. And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick. [Column 0625D]

[LXXXVII, 2.] And he said to them: “Take nothing for the journey, neither staff, nor bag, nor bread, nor money; and do not have two tunics. And into whatever house you enter, stay there, and do not leave from there.

[LXXXVIII, 2.] And whoever does not receive you, when you leave that city, shake even the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.”

[LXXXXIX, 8.] Having gone out, they went about through the villages, preaching the Gospel and healing everywhere.

[XC, 2.] Now Herod the tetrarch heard all that was being done by him, [Column 0626A] and he was perplexed, because some were saying, “John has risen from the dead”; others, “Elijah has appeared”; and still others, “One of the ancient prophets has risen.” But Herod said: “I beheaded John. Who, then, is this about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.

[XCI, 8.] When the Apostles returned, they told him everything they had done.

[XCII, 3.] And taking them with him, he withdrew privately to a deserted place, which is Bethsaida. When the crowds learned this, they followed him; and he received them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed treatment.

[XCIII, 1.] Now the day had begun to decline. And the twelve approached and said to him: “Dismiss the crowds, so that, going into the surrounding villages and farms, they may lodge and find food, because here [Column 0626B] we are in a deserted place.”

But he said to them: “You give them something to eat.” They replied: “We have no more than five loaves and two fish—unless perhaps we ourselves should go and buy food for all this crowd.” For there were about five thousand men.

But he said to his disciples: “Make them sit down in groups of fifty.” And they did so, and made them all sit down. Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and distributed them to his disciples to set before the crowd. And they all ate and were satisfied. And what remained over was collected: twelve baskets of fragments.

[XCIV, 1.] And it happened that, while he was alone praying, the disciples were with him. And he questioned them, saying: “Who do the crowds say that I am?” [Column 0626C]

They answered and said: “John the Baptist; but others say Elijah; and still others that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”

And he said to them: “But who do you say that I am?”

Simon Peter answered and said: “The Christ of God.”

[XCV, 2.] But he rebuked them and ordered them to tell this to no one, saying: “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise again.”

[XCVI, 2.] And he said to all: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world, [Column 0626D] but loses or forfeits himself?

[XCVII, 2.] For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his own majesty, and that of the Father and of the holy angels.

[XCVIII, 2.] But I tell you truly: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”

Now about eight days after these words, he took Peter, James, and John and went up the mountain to pray. And while he was praying, the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing white and shining. And behold, two men were speaking [Column 0627A] with him. They were Moses and Elijah, seen in glory, and they spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.

But Peter and those who were with him were weighed down with sleep. When they awoke, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him. And it happened that, as they were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus: “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah”—not knowing what he was saying.

And as he was saying this, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud. And a voice came from the cloud, saying: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

And when the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen. [Column 0627B]

[XCIX, 2.] On the following day, as they were coming down from the mountain, a great crowd met them. And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying: “Master, I beg you, look upon my son, because he is my only child. And behold, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, throws him down, and convulses him with foaming; and he scarcely leaves him after tearing him apart. I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”

Jesus answered and said: “O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and endure you? Bring your son here.”

And as he approached, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and returned him to his father.

[C, 8.] And all were astonished at the greatness of God. [CI, 2.] While everyone was marveling at all that he did, he said to his disciples: “Put these words into your hearts: the Son of Man is destined to be delivered into the hands of men.”

But they did not understand this saying, and it was veiled from them, so that they would not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

[CII, 2.] And a thought entered among them as to which of them was the greatest. But Jesus, seeing the thoughts of their hearts, took a child, set him beside himself, and said to them: “Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For the one who is least among you all is the greatest.”

[CIII, 8.] John answered and said: “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us.”

And Jesus said to him: “Do not stop him. For whoever is not against you is for you.”

[CIV, 10.] Now when the days of his being taken up were being fulfilled, he set his face firmly toward going to Jerusalem. And he sent messengers ahead of him. As they went, they entered a Samaritan town to make preparations for him. But they did not receive him, because his face was directed toward Jerusalem.

When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: “Lord, do you wish us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?” [Note: Greek copies add, “just as Elijah also did,” ὡς καὶ Ἠλίας ἐποίησε.]

But he turned and rebuked them, saying: “You do not know of what spirit you are. [Column 0628A] For the Son of Man did not come to destroy lives, but to save them.”

And they went to another village.

[CV, 5.] And as they were traveling along the road, someone said to him: “I will follow you wherever you go.”

Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to recline his head.”

And he said to another: “Follow me.”

But he said: “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”

And Jesus said to him: “Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but you go and announce the kingdom of God.”

[CVI, 10.] And another said: “I will follow you, Lord, but first permit me to take leave of those who are at home.”

Jesus said to him: “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

[Chapter X. CVII, 10.] After this the Lord appointed another seventy-two [Column 0628B] and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and place where he himself was about to come.

[CVIII, 5.] And he said to them: “The harvest is indeed abundant, but the laborers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send laborers into his harvest.

[CIX, 5.] Go. Behold, I send you like lambs among wolves.

[CX, 2.] Carry neither purse, nor bag, nor sandals, and greet no one along the road.

[CXI, 5.] Into whatever house you enter, first say: ‘Peace to this house.’ And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it will return to you.

[CXII, 5.] Remain in that same house, eating and drinking what they have, for the laborer is worthy of his wages.

[CXIII, 10.] Do not move from house to house. And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you; heal the sick who are in it, and say to them: ‘The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.’ [Column 0628C]

[CXIV, 2.] But into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say: ‘Even the dust that clings to us from your city we wipe off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has drawn near.’ I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom on that day than for that city.

[CXV, 5.] Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes. Nevertheless, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.

And you, Capernaum, exalted to heaven, you will be brought down to hell. [Column 0628D]

[CXVI, 1.] “Whoever hears you hears me; and whoever rejects you rejects me. But whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”

[CXVII, 10.] The seventy-two returned with joy, saying: “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name.”

And he said to them: “I was watching Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; and nothing will harm you.

Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” [Column 0629A]

[CXVIII, 5.] At that hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said: “I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little ones. Yes, Father, because this was pleasing before you.

[CXIX, 3.] “All things have been handed over to me by my Father. And no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.”

[CXX, 5.] And turning to his disciples, he said: “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see. For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.”

[CXXI, 2.] And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, testing him, and saying: “Master, what must I do to possess eternal life?”

But he said to him: “What is written in the Law? How do you read it?” [Column 0629B]

He answered and said: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”

And he said to him: “You have answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”

[CXXII, 10.] But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus: “And who is my neighbor?”

Jesus took up the question and said: “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They also stripped him, inflicted wounds upon him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

Now it happened that a certain priest was going down the same road; and when he saw him, he passed by. Likewise, a Levite, when he was near the place and saw him, passed by.

But a certain Samaritan, while traveling, came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion. He approached, bound his wounds, pouring in oil and wine; then he placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

The next day he brought out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying: ‘Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.’

Which of these three seems to you to have been a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”

He said: “The one who showed mercy toward him.”

And Jesus said to him: “Go, and you do likewise.”

Now it happened, as they were traveling, that he entered a certain village. And a woman named Martha welcomed him into her house. And she had a sister named Mary, who also sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to his word.

But Martha was occupied with extensive service. She stood and said: “Lord, is it no concern to you that my sister has left me alone to serve? Tell her, therefore, to help me.”

And the Lord answered and said to her: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things. But one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the better portion, which will not be taken away from her.”

[Chapter XI. CXXIII, 5.] And it came to pass, when he was praying in a certain place, that, when he had ceased, one of his disciples said to him: “Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.” And he said to them: “When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be your name. May your kingdom come.” [Note: [Column 0629D] In most Greek codices there is also added that clause, “May your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth,” γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Further, two manuscripts, one Vatican and the other of the Queen, read “give us daily” instead of “give us today”; in Greek it is usually τὸ καθ` ἡμέραν.] “Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our sins, since we ourselves also forgive everyone indebted to us. And do not lead us into temptation.”

[CXXIV, 10.] And he said to them: “Which of you will have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him: ‘Friend, lend me three loaves, because a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’; and he from within will answer and say: ‘Do not trouble me; the door is already shut and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give you anything’? Even if he persists in knocking, I tell you, though he will not rise and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needs. [Column 0630B]

[CXXV, 5.] “And I say to you: Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened. Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent instead of a fish? Or if he asks for an egg, will offer him a scorpion? If you, then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father from heaven give a good spirit to those who ask him!”

[CXXVI, 5.] And he was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When he had cast out the demon, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were astonished.

[CXXVII, 2.] But some of them said: “He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons.” [Column 0630C]

[CXXVIII, 5.] And others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.

[CXXIX, 2.] But he, seeing their thoughts, said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste [Note: [Column 0630D] At once, our manuscripts prefer; the Greek also has ἐρημοῦται, ‘is laid waste’.], and house will fall upon house. And if Satan too is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub. But if I cast out demons by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges. But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, then surely the kingdom of God has come upon you. When a strong man, fully armed, guards his courtyard, his possessions are in peace; but if one stronger than he comes upon him and conquers him, he takes away all his armor in which he trusted and distributes his spoils. Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.” [Column 0630D]

[CXXX, 5.] “When an unclean spirit has gone out from a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest; and, finding none, it says: ‘I will return to my house from which I came.’ And when it comes, it finds it swept clean and [Note: [Column 0630D] Again two manuscripts, one Vatican and the other the older Queen manuscript, omit this word ‘adorned,’ which nevertheless occurs in nearly all Greek books.] adorned. Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and, entering, they dwell there. And that person’s last state becomes worse than the first.” [Column 0631A]

[CXXXI, 10.] Now as he was saying these things, a certain woman from the crowd raised her voice and said to him: “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked.” But he said: “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”

[CXXXII, 5.] As the crowds were gathering, he began to say: “This generation is an evil generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so will the Son of Man be to this generation. The Queen of the South will rise in the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, one greater [Note: [Column 0631D] In the same codices: ‘one greater than Solomon is here.’] than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh will rise in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.” [Column 0631B]

[CXXXIII, 1.] “No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place or under a bushel, but on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.

[CXXXIV, 5.] Your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light; but if it is evil, your body too will be in darkness. Therefore see to it that the light in you is not darkness. If, then, your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a shining lamp gives you light.”

[CXXXV, 5.] And while he was speaking, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He entered and reclined. But the Pharisee began to say within himself, wondering why he had not washed before dinner. And the Lord said to him: “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but within you are full of robbery and wickedness. Fools! Did not he who made the outside also make the inside? Nevertheless, give as alms what remains, and behold, all things are clean for you.” [Column 0631C]

[CXXXVI, 5.] “But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over judgment and the love of God. These things you ought to have done, without omitting those.

[CXXXXVII, 2.] Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the first seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplace.

[CXXXVIII, 5.] Woe to you, because you are like unmarked tombs, and people walking over them do not know it.”

[CXXXIX, 5.] Then one of the lawyers answered and said to him: “Master, by saying these things you insult us also.” But he said: “Woe to you lawyers also, because you load people with burdens that they cannot carry, while you yourselves do not touch the loads with one of your fingers.” [Column 0631D]

[CXL, 5.] “Woe to you who build the tombs of the prophets, while your fathers killed them. Certainly you testify that you approve the deeds of your fathers, since they killed them, while you build their tombs.

[CXLI, 5.] Therefore also the wisdom of God said: ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles, and they will kill and persecute some of them,’ so that the blood of all the prophets shed from the foundation of the world may be required of this generation, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation. [Column 0632A]

[CXLII, 5.] Woe to you lawyers, because you have taken away the key of knowledge. You yourselves did not enter, and you hindered those who were entering.”

[CXLIII, 10.] And while he was saying these things to them, the Pharisees and lawyers began vehemently to press him and to provoke him to speak on many matters, lying in wait for him and seeking to catch something from his mouth in order to accuse him.

[Chapter XII.] Meanwhile, when countless crowds had gathered, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his disciples: [CXLIV, 2.] “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, [Column 0632B] which is hypocrisy.

[CXLV, 5.] Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known. Therefore, what you have said in darkness will be spoken in the light, and what you have whispered in private rooms will be proclaimed upon the rooftops. But I say to you, my friends: Do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do. I will show you whom you should fear: fear him who, after he has killed, has authority to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I say to you, fear him. Are not five sparrows sold for two asses, and not one of them is forgotten before God? Indeed, even all the hairs of your head are numbered. Therefore do not fear: you are worth more than many sparrows. [Note: [Column 0631D] All our manuscripts omit the pronoun ‘you,’ which the Greek text retains. [Column 0632D]] I say to you: everyone who confesses me before people, the Son of Man also will confess before the angels of God. [Column 0632C]

[CXLVI, 2.] But whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.

[CXLVII, 2.] And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but to one who has blasphemed against the Holy Spirit it will not be forgiven.

[CXLVIII, 2.] When they bring you before synagogues and magistrates and authorities, do not be anxious how or what you should answer or what you should say; for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you ought to say.”

[CXLIX, 10.] Then someone from the crowd said to him: “Master, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.” But he said to him: “Man, who appointed me a judge or divider over you?” And he said to them: “See to it, and beware of every kind of covetousness, because one’s life does not consist in the abundance of one’s possessions.” [Column 0632D] And he told them a parable: “A rich man’s field yielded abundantly, and he reasoned within himself, saying: ‘What shall I do?
