I have nowhere to store my crops.’ And he said: ‘I will do this: I will tear down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my produce and goods; and I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, feast.’ But God said to him: ‘Fool, this night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’ So it is with one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.” [Column 0633A]

[CL, 5.] And he said to his disciples: “Therefore I say to you: Do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. Life is more than food, and the body more than clothing. Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap; they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than they! Which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature? If, then, you cannot do even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest? Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin; yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass that is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith! And do not seek what you are to eat or what you are to drink, and do not be lifted up in anxiety; for all these things the nations of the world seek. But your Father knows that you need them. Nevertheless, seek [Note: [Column 0633D] In accordance with the Greek text, two of our manuscripts omit the adverb ‘first’; and, immediately after, all unanimously reject the words ‘and his righteousness,’ with the Greek archetype supporting them.] first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

[CLI, 10.] Do not fear, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.

[CLII, 2.] Sell what you possess and give alms.

[CLIII, 5.] Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

[CLIV, 10.] Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning [Note: [Column 0633D] The words ‘in your hands’ are added neither by the Greek text [Column 0634D] nor by the Latin manuscripts which we use.] in your hands, and be like people awaiting their master’s return from the wedding, so that, when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him. [Column 0633C]

[CLV, 5.] Blessed are those servants whom the master, when he comes, finds watching. Amen I say to you, he will gird himself, make them recline, and, passing by, serve them. And if he comes in the second watch, and if he comes in the third watch, and finds them so, blessed are those servants.

[CLVI, 2.] But know this: if the householder knew at what hour the thief would come, he would surely watch and would not allow his house to be broken into. You too be ready, because at an hour when you do not expect it, the Son of Man will come.

[CLVII, 5.] Peter said to him: “Lord, do you say this parable to us, or also to everyone?” And the Lord said: “Who then is the faithful and prudent steward whom the master will appoint over his household, to give them their measure of wheat at the proper time? [Column 0633D] Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, finds doing so. [Note: [Column 0634D] The pronoun ‘his’ is added here both in the Greek text and in our manuscripts.] Truly I say to you, he will appoint him over all that he possesses.

[CLVIII, 5.] But if that servant says in his heart: ‘My master delays his coming,’ and begins to beat [Note: [Column 0634D] With the same sense, but closer to the Greek word παῖδας, our manuscripts read ‘boys’ rather than ‘servants’.] servants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk, that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unbelievers. [Column 0634A]

[CLIX, 10.] Now the servant who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows; but the one who did not know and did things deserving blows will be beaten with few. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from him to whom they have entrusted much, they will demand more.

[CLX, 5.] I came to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I desire but that it be kindled? But I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how I am constrained until it is accomplished! Do you think that I came to give peace on earth? No, I tell you, but division. For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three: father against son and son against his father; mother against daughter and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.

[CLXI, 5.] [Column 0634B] He also said to the crowds: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say: ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens. And when you see the south wind blowing, you say that there will be heat, and it happens. Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of earth and sky; how is it that you do not discern this time? And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

[CLXII, 5.] When you go with your adversary to a magistrate, make every effort on the way to be released from him, lest he drag you before the judge, the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison. I tell you, you will not get out from there until you have paid even the last mite.”

[Chapter XIII. CLXIII, 10.] At that very time some were present who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. And [Column 0634C] he answered and said to them: “Do you think that these Galileans were sinners beyond all Galileans because they suffered such things? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish. Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they too were debtors beyond all the people dwelling in Jerusalem? No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.

[CLXIV, 10.] And he told this parable: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none. Then he said to the keeper of the vineyard: ‘Behold, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down. Why should it also occupy the ground?’ But he answered and said to him: ‘Lord, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put in manure. If indeed it bears fruit—but if not, you will cut it down in the future.’” [Column 0634D]

Now he was teaching in their synagogue on the Sabbaths. And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and could not at all straighten herself. When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said: “Woman, you are released from your infirmity.” And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she was made straight [Column 0635A] and glorified God.

But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the crowd: “There are six days on which one ought to work; therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”

[CLXV, 2.] The Lord answered him and said: “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it away to water it? And ought not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound—behold, for eighteen years—to be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?”

[CLXVI, 10.] As he said these things, all his adversaries were put to shame, and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things being done by him.

[CLXVII, 2.] Therefore he said: “What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it? It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his garden; it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of heaven rested in its branches.” [Column 0635B]

[CLXVIII, 5.] And again he said: “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God? It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened.”

[CLXIX, 2.] And he went through cities and villages, teaching and making his way toward Jerusalem.

[CLXX, 5.] Someone said to him: “Lord, are there few who are saved?” But he said to them: “Strive to enter through the narrow gate, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.

[CLXXI, 5.] After the householder has entered and shut the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying: ‘Lord, open to us.’ And he will answer and say to you: ‘I do not know where you are from.’ Then you will begin to say: [Column 0635C] ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’ And he will say to you: ‘I do not know where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’ There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth,

[CLXXII, 5.] when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves cast out. And they will come from east and west and north and south, and recline in the kingdom of God.

[CLXXIII, 2.] And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”

[CLXXIV, 10.] On that same day some Pharisees approached, saying to him: “Go out and depart from here, because Herod wants to kill you.” And he said to them: “Go and tell that fox: ‘Behold, I cast out demons and accomplish healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am perfected.’ Nevertheless, I must journey today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem. [Column 0635D]

[CLXXV, 5.] Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I wished to gather your children, as a bird gathers her nest under her wings, and you would not! Behold, your house will be left to you desolate. But I tell you, you will not see me until the time comes when you say: ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

## [Chapter XIV]

**[CLXXVI, 10.]** And it happened that, when Jesus entered the house of one of the leading Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him. And behold, a certain man suffering from dropsy was before him.

**[CLXXVII, 2.]** And Jesus, responding, said to the lawyers and Pharisees: “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” **[Col. 0636A]** But they kept silent. And he took hold of him, healed him, and dismissed him. And responding to them, he said: “Which of you, if his donkey or ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?” And they were unable to answer him concerning these things.

**[CLXXVIII, 10.]** And he also told those who had been invited a parable, observing how they chose the places of honor, saying to them: “When you are invited to a wedding, do not recline in the place of honor, lest someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him; and the one who invited you and him comes and says to you, ‘Give this man your place’; and then you begin, with shame, to occupy the lowest place. But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that, when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all those reclining with you; **[CLXXIX, 5.]** for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

**[CLXXX, 10.]** And he also said to the one who had invited him: “When you prepare a luncheon or a dinner, do not invite your friends, or your brothers, or your relatives, or wealthy neighbors, lest they too invite you in return, and it become repayment for you. But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind; and you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

When one of those reclining with him heard this, he said to him: “Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.”

**[CLXXXI, 5.]** But he said to him: “A certain man prepared a great dinner and invited many. And at the dinner hour he sent his servant to say to those invited that they should come, because everything was now ready. And they all began together to make excuses.

“The first said to him, ‘I have bought a farm, and I must go out and see it; I ask you to consider me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them; I ask you to consider me excused.’ And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’

“And the servant returned and reported these things to his master. Then, becoming angry, the master of the household said to his servant, ‘Go quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring here the poor, the disabled, the blind, and the lame.’ And the servant said, ‘Master, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room.’ And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out onto the roads and along the hedges, and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled. For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.’”

**[CLXXXII, 5.]** And great crowds were traveling with him. Turning, he said to them: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters—and even his own life—he cannot be my disciple. And whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.

**[CLXXXIII, 10.]** “For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost required, to see whether he has enough to complete it? Otherwise, after he has laid the foundation and is unable to finish it, all who see it may begin to mock him, saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’ Or what king, going to engage another king in war, does not first sit down and consider whether he can meet with ten thousand the one who comes against him with twenty thousand? Otherwise, while he is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for the terms of peace.

**[CLXXXIV, 5.]** “So therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses cannot be my disciple.

**[CLXXXV, 2.]** “Salt is good. But if the salt has become tasteless, with what will it be seasoned? It is useful neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; it will be thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

[Note: **[Col. 0637D]** In one Vatican manuscript and another of the Regina manuscripts, as also in several Greek codices: “But if the salt also,” and so forth.]

## [Chapter XV]

**[CLXXXVI, 2.]** Now tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him. And the Pharisees and scribes were grumbling, saying: “This man receives sinners and eats with them.”

**[CLXXXVII, 5.]** And he told them this parable, saying: “Which man among you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost until he finds it? And when he has found it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing; and when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.’ I tell you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance.

**[CLXXXVIII, 10.]** “Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp, sweep [MS: “turn upside down”] the house, and search carefully until she finds it? And when she has found it, she calls together her women friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I had lost.’”

[MS: *evertit* (“turns upside down”).]

**[CLXXXIX, 5.]** “So I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.

**[CXC, 10.]** “A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided the property between them. And not many days later, after gathering everything together, the younger son departed to a distant region, and there he squandered his property by living extravagantly.

“And after he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred in that region, and he began to be in need. And he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that region, who sent him to his farm to feed pigs. And he longed to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him any.

“But coming to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants in my father’s house have bread in abundance, while I am perishing here from hunger! I will arise **[Col. 0637D]** and go to my father, and I will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants.’

“And he arose and went to his father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with compassion; he ran and fell upon his neck and kissed him. And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

“But the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly, bring out the first robe and dress him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet. And bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate, because this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.’ And they began to celebrate.

“Now his older son was in the field. And when he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing. And he called one of the servants and asked **[Col. 0638D]** what these things were. And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and sound.’

“But he became angry and did not want to go in. Therefore his father came out and began to plead with him. But he answered and said to his father, ‘Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I have never transgressed your commandment; yet you have never given me a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends. But when this son of yours came, who has devoured your property with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

“And he said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours. But it was necessary to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.’”

[Note: **[Col. 0638D]** In our manuscripts: “what these things were.”]

## [Chapter XVI]

And he also said to his disciples: “There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this man was accused before him of having squandered his possessions. And he called him and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’

“And the steward said within himself, ‘What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am unable to dig, and I am ashamed to beg. I know what I will do, so that, when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.’

“And summoning each of his master’s debtors, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’ And he said, ‘A hundred casks of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your written account, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

“Then he said to another, ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your written account and write eighty.’

“And the master praised the dishonest steward because he had acted prudently; for the sons of this age are more prudent in their generation than the sons of light. And I say to you: Make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of iniquity, so that, when it fails, they may receive you into eternal dwellings.

“Whoever is faithful in very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is unjust in very little is unjust also in much. If, therefore, you have not been faithful with unrighteous mammon, who will entrust the true riches to you? And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?

**[CXCI, 5.]** “No servant can serve two masters. For either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will cling to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.”

**[CXCII, 10.]** Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and they ridiculed him. And he said to them: “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among men is an abomination before God.

**[CXCIII, 5.]** “The Law and the Prophets lasted until John; from that time the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone presses into it.

**[CXCIV, 5.] [Col. 0639A]** “But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of the Law to fall.

**[CXCV, 2.]** “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries a woman divorced by her husband commits adultery.

**[CXCVI, 10.]** “There was a certain rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day. And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, covered with sores, longing to be satisfied with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table, **[Col. 0639D]** and no one gave him anything. But even the dogs came and licked his sores.

“And it happened that the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried in hell. And lifting up his eyes while he was in torments, he saw Abraham far away and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried out and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering in this flame.’

“And Abraham said to him, ‘Son, remember that you received good things during your life, and Lazarus likewise bad things; but now he is comforted here, while you are suffering. And in all these things a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who wish to cross from here to you cannot, nor can they cross from there to us.’

“And he said, ‘Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers, so that he may testify to them, lest they too come to this place of torment.’

“And Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.’

“But he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

“And he said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they believe if someone rises from the dead.’”

[Note: **[Col. 0639D]** The words “and no one gave him,” which are also absent from the Greek archetype, are not found in the manuscripts that we consulted.]

## [Chapter XVII]

**[CXCVII, 2.]** And he said to his disciples: “It is impossible that stumbling blocks should not come; but woe to the one through whom they come. It would be more advantageous for him if a millstone were placed around his neck and he were thrown into the sea than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

**[CXCVIII, 5.]** “Pay attention to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

**[CXCIX, 5.]** “And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turns back to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive him.”

**[CC, 5.]** And the Apostles said to the Lord: “Increase our faith.” And the Lord said: “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, **[Col. 0639D]** you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and be transplanted into the sea,’ and it would obey you.”

[Note: **[Col. 0639D]** In all our manuscripts the reading is *diceretis* (“you would say”), and the Greek has ἐλέγετε.]

**[CCI, 10.]** “But which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, would say to him when he returns from the field, ‘Come at once and recline,’ and would not instead say to him, ‘Prepare what I may eat, gird yourself, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk; and after this you shall eat and drink’? Does he perhaps thank that servant because he did what had been commanded him? I do not think so.

“So you also, when you have done everything that has been commanded you, say: ‘We are useless servants; we have done what we were obliged to do.’”

And it happened, while he was going to Jerusalem, that he passed through the middle of Samaria and **[alternative reading: also]** Galilee. And as he entered a certain village, ten leprous men met him, standing at a distance. And they raised their voices, saying: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”

And when he saw them, he said: “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And it happened that, as they went, they were cleansed.

Now one of them, when he saw that he had been cleansed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice. And he fell on his face at his feet, giving thanks; and he was a Samaritan.

Then Jesus responded and said: “Were not ten cleansed? And where are the nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this foreigner?” And he said to him: “Rise, go; your faith has saved you.”

**[CCII, 5.]** And when he was questioned by the Pharisees: **[Col. 0640B]** “When does the kingdom of God come?” he answered them: “The kingdom of God does not come with observation; nor will they say, ‘Behold, here!’ or ‘There!’ For behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”

**[CCIII, 10.]** And he said to his disciples: “Days will come when you will long to see one day of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.

**[CCIV, 2.]** “And they will say to you, ‘Behold, here!’ and ‘Behold, there!’ Do not go out, and do not follow them.

**[CCV, 5.]** “For just as lightning, flashing from beneath the sky, shines upon the things that are beneath the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.

**[CCVI, 2.]** “But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

**[CCVII, 5.]** “And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so will it also be in the days of the Son of Man. They were eating and drinking; they were marrying and being given in marriage, until the day on which Noah entered the ark. And the flood came **[Col. 0640C]** and destroyed them all.

**[CCVIII, 10.]** “Likewise, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building; but on the day when Lot went out from Sodom, fire and sulfur rained from heaven and destroyed them all. So will it be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.

**[CCIX, 2.]** “On that hour, let the one who is on the rooftop, with his belongings in the house, not go down to take them; and likewise, let the one in the field not turn back.

**[CCX, 10.]** “Remember Lot’s wife.

**[CCXI, 3.]** “Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will preserve it alive.

**[CCXII, 5.]** “I tell you: On that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other will be left. Two will be grinding together; one will be taken and the other will be left. Two will be in the field; one will be taken **[Col. 0640D]** and the other will be left.”

**[CCXIII, 5.]** In response they said to him: “Where, Lord?” And he said to them: “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will gather.”

## [Chapter XVIII]

**[CCXIV, 10.]** And he also told them a parable about the necessity of always praying and not losing heart, saying: “There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear God and did not respect man. And there was a certain widow in that city, and she came to him, saying, ‘Vindicate me against my adversary.’ And he was unwilling for a long time.

“But afterward **[Col. 0641A]** he said within himself, ‘Although I do not fear God and do not respect man, nevertheless, because this widow is troublesome to me, I will vindicate her, lest she finally come and wear me out.’”

And the Lord said: “Hear what the unjust judge says. And will God not vindicate his elect, who cry out to him day and night, and will he be patient with them? I tell you that he will vindicate them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, do you suppose he will find faith on the earth?”

And he also spoke this parable to certain people who trusted in themselves as righteous and despised others: “Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

“The Pharisee, standing, prayed this within himself: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other men—robbers, unjust, adulterers—or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I possess.’

“But the tax collector, standing far away, did not even want to raise his eyes toward heaven; instead, he beat his breast, saying: ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’

“I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; **[CCXV, 5.]** for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

**[CCXVI, 2.]** And they were bringing infants to him so that he might touch them. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked them. But Jesus, calling them together, said: “Allow the children to come to me, and do not forbid them; for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

**[CCXVII, 2.]** “Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.”

**[CCXVIII, 2.]** And a certain ruler questioned him, saying: **[Col. 0641C]** “Good Teacher, what must I do to possess eternal life?”

But Jesus said to him: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone. You know the commandments: ‘You shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor your father and mother.’”

And he said: “I have kept all these things from my youth.”

**[CCXIX, 2.]** When Jesus heard this, he said to him: “One thing is still lacking in you: sell everything that you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”

**[CCXX, 2.]** When he heard this, he became sorrowful, because he was very rich. And when Jesus saw that he had become sorrowful, he said: “How difficult it is for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God! For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

And those who heard this said: **[Col. 0641D]** “Then who can be saved?”

He said to them: “The things that are impossible with men are possible with God.”

And Peter said: “Behold, we have left everything and followed you.”

**[CCXXI, 2.]** And he said to them: “Amen, I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children, for the sake of the kingdom of God, who will not receive many times more in this present age, and in the coming age eternal life.”

**[CCXXII, 2.]** And Jesus took the Twelve and said to them: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that has been written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be accomplished. For he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, and spat upon; and after they have scourged him, they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”

**[CCXXIII, 10.]** And **[Col. 0642A]** they understood none of these things; this saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was being said.

**[CCXXIV, 2.]** And it happened that, as he approached Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging. And when he heard the crowd passing by, he asked what this was. And they told him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.

And he cried out, saying: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.” And those who were going ahead rebuked him, so that he should be silent. But he cried out all the more: “Son of David, have mercy on me.”

And Jesus, standing still, ordered him to be brought to him. And when he had drawn near, he asked him, saying: “What do you want me to do for you?”

And he said: “Lord, that I may see.”

And Jesus said to him: “See; your faith has saved you.” And immediately he saw, and followed him, glorifying **[Col. 0642B]** God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

## [Chapter XIX]

**[CCXXV, 10.]** And entering Jericho, he was passing through it. And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus; he was a chief tax collector, and he himself was rich. And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd, since he was short in stature.

And running ahead, he climbed a sycamore tree in order to see him, because he was going to pass that way. And when he came to the place, Jesus looked up and saw him and said to him: “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, because today I must remain at your house.”

And he hurried down and welcomed him joyfully. And when they all saw this, they grumbled, saying that he had gone in to stay with a sinful man.

And Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord: “Behold, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor; and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I repay fourfold.”

Jesus said to him: “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.

**[CCXXVI, 5.]** “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.”

**[CCXXVII, 10.]** As they were listening to these things, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and because they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.

**[CCXXVIII, 2.]** Therefore he said: “A certain nobleman went to a distant region to receive a kingdom for himself and then return.

**[CCXXIX, 5.]** “And calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them: ‘Engage in business until I come.’

“But his citizens hated him, and they sent a delegation after him, saying: ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’

“And it happened that, after receiving the kingdom, he returned and ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be summoned, so that he might know what each had gained through business.

“The first came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten minas.’ And he said to him, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’

“And another came, saying, ‘Master, your mina has produced five minas.’ And he said to him, ‘And you, be over five cities.’

“And another came, saying, ‘Master, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a cloth. For I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man: you take what you did not deposit, and you reap what you did not sow.’

“He said to him: ‘I will judge you from your own mouth, wicked servant. You knew that I am a severe man, taking what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow; **[Col. 0643A]** why, then, did you not put my money in the bank, so that when I came I might have collected it with interest?’

“And he said to those standing by: ‘Take the mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’

“And they said to him: ‘Master, he has ten minas.’

**[CCXXX, 2.]** “I tell you that to everyone who has, more will be given, **[Col. 0643D]** and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”

[Note: **[Col. 0643D]** The Vatican manuscript and the older Regina manuscript do not add “and he will have abundance”; these words occur only in the other Regina manuscript, and indeed were supplied there in a second correction. In the Greek text they are entirely absent.]

**[CCXXXI, 5.]** “But those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them—bring them here and kill them before me.”

**[CCXXXII, 2.]** And after saying these things, he went ahead, ascending toward Jerusalem. And it happened that, when he drew near Bethphage and Bethany, at the mountain called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying: “Go into the village opposite. As you enter it, you will find a colt of a donkey tied up, on which no human being has ever sat. Untie it and bring it. And if anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say this to him: ‘Because the Lord needs it.’”

**[CCXXXIII, 2.]** Those who had been sent went away and found the colt standing, just as he had told them. As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: “Why are you untying the colt?”

And they said: “Because the Lord needs it.”

And they led it to Jesus. And throwing their garments over the colt, they placed Jesus upon it. And as he went, they spread their garments on the road.

**[CCXXXIV, 1.]** And when he was already approaching the descent of the Mount of Olives, all the crowds of the disciples began joyfully to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty deeds that they had seen, **[Col. 0643C]** saying: “Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.”

[Note: **[Col. 0644D]** In place of *discipulorum* (“of the disciples”), all our manuscripts prefer *descendentium* (“of those descending”), as does the Greek copy at Cambridge that had belonged to Bede, which has τῶν καταβαινόντων (“of those descending”) instead of τῶν μαθητῶν (“of the disciples”).]

**[CCXXXV, 5.]** And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him: “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”

And he said to them: “I tell you, if these should be silent, the stones would cry out.”

**[CCXXXVI, 10.]** And when he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it, saying: “If you too had known—and indeed on this your day—the things that make for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.

“For days will come upon you when your enemies will surround you with a rampart and hem you in; they will press you hard on every side, and they will cast you and your children within you **[CCXXXVII, 1.]** down to the ground; and they will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.”

**[CCXXXVIII, 1.]** And entering the temple, he began to drive out those selling in it and those buying, saying to them: “It is written: ‘My house is a house of prayer.’ But you have made it a den of robbers.”

**[CCXXXIX, 1.]** And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests, the scribes, and the leaders of the people were seeking to destroy him, and they could not find what they might do to him. For all the people were hanging upon his words, listening to him.

## [Chapter XX]

**[CCXL, 2.]** And it happened that, on one of the days, while he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up and said to him: “Tell us, by what authority you do these things? Or who is it that gave you this authority?”

But Jesus answered and said to them: “I too will ask you one question. Answer me: Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men?”

But they reasoned among themselves, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us; for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”

And they answered that they did not know where it was from.

And Jesus said to them: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

**[CCXLI, 2.]** And he began to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenant farmers, and he himself went abroad for a long time. And at the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, so that they might give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.

“And he proceeded to send another servant. But they beat this one also, treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty-handed. And he proceeded to send a third; and they wounded him too and threw him out.

“Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps, when they see him, they will show respect.’

“But when the tenants saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.’

“And they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them? He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others.”

When they heard this, they said to him: “May it never be!”

But he looked at them and said: “What, then, is this that is written: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the cornerstone’? Everyone who falls upon that stone will be shattered; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

**[CCXLII, 1.]** And the chief priests and scribes sought at that very hour to lay hands on him, but they feared the people; for they understood that he had spoken this parable about them.

**[CCXLIII, 2.]** And watching him, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in his speech and hand him over to the authority and power of the governor. And they questioned him, saying: “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and that you do not show partiality, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar or not?”

But, perceiving their deceit, he said to them: “Why do you test me? Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?”

They answered: “Caesar’s.”

And he said to them: “Then give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”

And they were unable to criticize his statement before the people; and marveling at his answer, they fell silent.

Then some of the Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came and questioned him, saying: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us: ‘If someone’s brother dies, having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

“Now there were seven brothers. And the first took a wife and died childless. And the next took her, and he too died without a son. And the third took her. Similarly, all seven; and they left no offspring and died. Finally, the woman also died.

“Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as a wife.”

And Jesus said to them: “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage; but those who are considered worthy of that age and of the resurrection from the dead **[Col. 0645D]** neither marry nor are given in marriage. For they cannot die any longer, because they are equal to the angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.

“But that the dead rise, Moses also showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ Now he is not God of the dead but of the living, for all live to him.”

And some of the scribes responded and said: “Teacher, you have spoken well.”

[Note: **[Col. 0645D]** In accordance with the Greek text, οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ἐκγαμίζονται (“neither marry nor are given in marriage”), all our manuscripts that we use also read “neither marry nor take wives,” with one exception, Regina manuscript no. 14, which, in the first phrase only, has the future: “neither will they marry.”]

**[CCXLIV, 2.]** And they no longer dared to ask him anything.

**[CCXLV, 2.]** But he said to them: “How do they say that the Christ is the son of David, while David himself says in the Book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”’? Therefore David calls him Lord; how, then, is he his son?”

**[CCXLVI, 2.]** And while all the people were listening, he said to his disciples: “Beware of the scribes, who wish to walk about in robes and love greetings in the marketplace, the first seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets;

**[CCXLVII, 8.]** “who devour widows’ houses while making a pretense of lengthy prayer. They will receive the greater condemnation.”

## [Chapter XXI]

When he looked up, he saw those who were putting their offerings into the treasury: they were rich. He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two small coins. And he said: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others. For all these contributed to the offerings of God out of their abundance; but she, out of what she lacks, put in all the means of living that she had.”

[CCXLVIII, 2.] And when some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and votive gifts, he said: “These things that you see—days will come when not one stone will be left upon another that will not be destroyed.”

[CCXLIX, 2.] And they asked him, saying: “Teacher, when will these things happen, and what sign will there be when they are about to begin?” He said: “See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not therefore go after them. And when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified. For these things must happen first, but the end is not yet immediate.”

[Note: More exactly, the Greek has *οὐκ εὐθέως* (“not immediately”); one Vatican manuscript and another, older Regina manuscript have only *non statim* (“not immediately”) in place of *nondum* (“not yet”), etc.]

Then he said to them: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be great earthquakes in various places, and pestilences and famines; there will be terrors from heaven, and there will be great signs.

[Col. 0646A] [CCL, 1.] But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, dragging you before kings and governors because of my name. And this will happen to you for a testimony.

[CCLI, 2.] Therefore settle it in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how you will answer. For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict. You will be handed over by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death. You will be hated by everyone because of my name. Yet not a hair of your head will perish. By your endurance you will possess your souls.

[CCLII, 10.] But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its desolation has drawn near.

[Col. 0646B] [CCLIII, 2.] Then let those who are in Judaea flee to the mountains; let those who are in its midst depart; and let those who are in the surrounding regions not enter it. For these are days of vengeance, so that all the things that have been written may be fulfilled.

[CCLIV, 2.] Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing infants in those days.

[CCLV, 2.] For there will be great distress upon the earth, and wrath against this people.

[CCLVI, 10.] They will fall by the edge of the sword and will be led captive among all the nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations, until the times of the nations are fulfilled.

[CCLVII, 2.] And there will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, and upon the earth distress among the nations because of the confusion caused by the roaring of the sea and the waves. People will faint from fear and expectation of what is coming upon the whole world. For the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

[CCLVIII, 2.] And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty. But when these things begin to happen, look up and raise your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.

And he gave them this comparison: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees. When they are already producing fruit from themselves, you know that summer is near. So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

“Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until everything has happened. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.

[CCLIX, 10.] “Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts become weighed down with dissipation, drunkenness, and the cares of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly. For it will come like a snare upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth. Therefore keep watch, praying at all times that you may be considered worthy to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”

During those days he was teaching in the temple; at night he went out and stayed on the mountain called the Mount of Olives. And all the people came early to him in the temple to hear him.

## [Chapter XXII]

[CCLX, 1.] Now the feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was approaching.

[CCLXI, 1.] The chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might kill Jesus; but they feared the people.

[Col. 0647A] [Note: According to the Greek exemplar, *αὐτόν* (“him”), our manuscripts too prefer “him” (*eum*) rather than “Jesus”; the pronoun was inserted by a second hand in another Regina manuscript. Shortly afterward, instead of *Iscariotes*, all customarily read *Scarioth*.]

[CCLXII, 9.] Satan entered into Judas, who was surnamed Iscariot, one of the Twelve.

[CCLXIII, 2.] He went away and spoke with the chief priests and the officers about how he might hand him over to them. And they rejoiced and agreed to give him money. He promised, and he was seeking an opportunity to hand him over without the crowd.

The day of Unleavened Bread came, on which it was necessary to sacrifice the Passover. And he sent Peter and John, saying: “Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.”

They said to him: “Where do you want us to prepare it?”

And he said to them: “Behold, when you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters, and you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’ And he will show you a large upper room furnished; prepare it there.”

They went and found it as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover. When the hour came, he reclined at table, and the twelve apostles with him.

[CCLXIV, 10.] And he said to them: “With great longing I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

[CCLXV, 2.] For I tell you, from now on I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”

And taking the cup, he gave thanks and said: “Take this and divide it among yourselves. For I tell you that from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”

[CCLXVI, 1.] And taking bread, he gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying: “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

[Col. 0647C] [CCLXVII, 2.] Likewise, the cup after supper, saying: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which will be poured out for you.

[CCLXVIII, 2.] “Nevertheless, behold, the hand of the one who betrays me is with me at the table. For indeed the Son of Man goes according to what has been determined; nevertheless, woe to that man through whom he is betrayed.”

[CCLXIX, 1.] And they began to question one another about which of them would do this.

[CCLXX, 2.] A dispute also arose among them about which of them seemed to be the greatest. But he said to them: “The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors. But you are not to be so. Rather, let the greater among you become as the lesser, and the leader as the one who serves.

[CCLXXI, 10.] “For who is greater: the one reclining at table, or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am among you as one who serves.

“You are the ones who have remained with me in my trials. And I appoint for you a kingdom, just as my Father appointed one for me, so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom.”

[Col. 0647D] [Note: One Vatican manuscript has the pronoun *meo* (“my”), which is nevertheless present in the other books; another manuscript omits it at this point.]

[CCLXXII, 5.] “And you will sit upon thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

[CCLXXIII, 10.] “The Lord said: ‘Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded you, to sift you like wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail.

[CCLXXIV, 9.] “And you, once converted, strengthen your brothers.’”

[Col. 0648A] [CCLXXV, 1.] He said to him: “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.”

But he said: “I tell you, Peter, the cock will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know me.”

[CCLXXVI, 10.] And he said to them: “When I sent you without a purse, a bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said: “Nothing.”

Therefore he said to them: “But now, let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag. And whoever has none, let him sell his cloak and buy a sword.”

[CCLXXVII, 8.] “For I tell you that this Scripture must still be fulfilled in me: ‘And he was reckoned among the transgressors.’ For the things concerning me are reaching their end.”

[CCLXXVIII, 10.] They said: “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” He said to them: “It is enough.”

[CCLXXIX, 1.] And going out, he went according to his custom to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.

[Col. 0648B] [CCLXXX, 2.] When he had reached the place, he said to them: “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.”

[CCLXXXI, 1.] And he withdrew from them about a stone’s throw, and kneeling, he prayed, saying: “Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me.

[CCLXXXII, 1.] “Nevertheless, not my will but yours be done.”

[CCLXXXIII, 10.] And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him. And being in agony, he prayed more earnestly. And his sweat became like drops of blood falling upon the ground.

[CCLXXXIV, 2.] When he rose from prayer and came to his disciples, he found them sleeping from sorrow. And he said to them: “Why are you sleeping? Rise and pray, that you may not enter into temptation.”

[CCLXXXV, 1.] While he was still speaking, behold, a crowd; and the one called Judas, one of the Twelve, was going before them. He drew near to Jesus to kiss him.

[CCLXXXVI, 2.] Jesus said to him: “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”

[CCLXXXVII, 1.] When those around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him: “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?” And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.

But Jesus answered: “Let it be as far as this.”

[CCLXXXVIII, 10.] And touching his ear, he healed him.

[CCLXXXIX, 1.] Jesus said to the chief priests, the officers of the temple, and the elders who had come against him: “Have you come out with swords and clubs as against a robber? When I was with you every day in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour and the power of darkness.”

[CCXC, 1.] They seized him and led him to the house of the high priest.

[CCXCI, 1.] But Peter was following at a distance. When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and were sitting around it, Peter was sitting among them. A certain servant girl saw him sitting by the light, looked closely at him, and said: “This man too was with him?”

But he denied him, saying: “Woman, I do not know him.”

[CCXCII, 1.] A little later, another person saw him and said: “You are one of them too.” But Peter said: “Man, I am not.”

After an interval of about an hour, another man insisted, saying: “Truly, this man too was with him, for he is also a Galilean.”

Peter said: “Man, I do not know what you are saying.” And immediately, while he was still speaking, the cock crowed.

[Col. 0649A] [CCXCIII, 2.] And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, as he had said: “Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.” And going outside, Peter wept bitterly.

[CCXCIV, 1.] The men who were holding him mocked him, beating him. They blindfolded him and struck his face, asking him: “Prophesy: who is the one who struck you?” And they said many other blasphemous things against him.

[CCXCV, 2.] When day came, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the scribes assembled and led him into their council, saying: “If you are the Christ, tell us.”

[Col. 0649B] [CCXCVI, 10.] And he said to them: “If I tell you, you will not believe me; and if I ask you, you will neither answer me nor release me.

[CCXCVII, 1.] “From now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”

[CCXCVIII, 10.] They all said: “Then you are the Son of God?” He said to them: “You say that I am.”

[CCXCIX, 2.] They said: “Why do we need any further testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from his mouth.”

## [Chapter XXIII]

[CCC, 1.] Then the whole assembly of them rose and led him to Pilate.

[CCCI, 10.] They began to accuse him, saying: “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding the payment of taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”

[CCCII, 1.] Pilate questioned him, saying: “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him: “You say so.”

[CCCIII, 9.] Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds: “I find no case against this man.”

[CCCIV, 10.] But they pressed their charge, saying: “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judaea, beginning from Galilee as far as here.”

When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean. When he learned that he was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was himself in Jerusalem in those days.

When Herod saw Jesus, he was extremely glad, for he had long desired to see him, because he had heard many things about him and hoped to see him perform some sign. He questioned him at length, but he answered him nothing.

[CCCV, 2.] The chief priests and the scribes stood there, persistently accusing him.

[Note: In the Vatican manuscript, “The chief priests and the scribes also stood there.”]

[Col. 0649D] [CCCVI, 10.] Herod, with his soldiers, treated him with contempt and mocked him. He dressed him in a white robe and sent him back to Pilate.

Herod and Pilate became friends with each other on that very day; previously they had been enemies.

[CCCVII, 9.] Pilate, having summoned the chief priests, the officers, and the people, said to them: “You brought me this man as one who was turning the people away, and behold, after questioning him in your presence, I have found no case against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.

[CCCVIII, 10.] “Nor has Herod, for I sent you to him, and behold, nothing deserving death has been done by him. Therefore, after chastising him, I will release him.”

[CCCIX, 2.] Now he was obliged to release one prisoner to them at the feast.

[CCCX, 1.] But the whole crowd cried out together, saying: “Take this man away, and release Barabbas for us”—a man who had been imprisoned because of a certain insurrection that had occurred in the city and because of murder.

[CCCXI, 1.] Pilate spoke to them again, wishing to release Jesus. But they shouted back, saying: “Crucify him, crucify him!”

[CCCXII, 9.] He said to them a third time: “Why, what evil has this man done? I find no case deserving death in him. Therefore I will chastise him and release him.”

[CCCXIII, 1.] But they persisted with loud cries, demanding that he be crucified, and their cries grew stronger.

[CCCXIV, 1.] Pilate therefore gave sentence that their request should be carried out. He released to them the man who had been thrown into prison because of murder and insurrection, whom they had requested; but he handed Jesus over to their will.

[Col. 0650B] [CCCXV, 1.] As they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, and laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus.

[CCCXVI, 10.] A great multitude of the people and of women followed him; they were weeping and lamenting him. Jesus turned to them and said: “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me, but weep for yourselves and for your children. For behold, days will come when they will say: ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that have not borne, and the breasts that have not nursed.’ Then they will begin to say to the mountains: ‘Fall upon us,’ and to the hills: ‘Cover us.’ For if they do these things with the green wood, what will happen with the dry?”

[CCCXVII, 1.] Two other evildoers were also being led away with him to be put to death.

[CCCXVIII, 1.] When they came to the place called Calvary, there they crucified him;

[CCCXIX, 1.] and the criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.

[CCCXX, 10.] But Jesus was saying: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”

[CCCXXI, 1.] Dividing his garments, they cast lots. The people stood watching.

[CCCXXII, 2.] The rulers also mocked him with them, saying: “He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”

[CCCXXIII, 2.] The soldiers also mocked him, coming up to him and offering him vinegar, saying: “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.”

[CCCXXIV, 1.] There was also an inscription written above him in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew letters: “This is the king of the Jews.”

[CCCXXV, 2.] One of the criminals who were hanging there blasphemed him, saying: “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us.”

[CCCXXVI, 10.] But the other answered and rebuked him, saying: “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same condemnation? And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve; but this man has done nothing wrong.”

And he said to Jesus: “Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”

And Jesus said to him: “Truly I tell you: today you will be with me in paradise.”

[CCCXXVII, 2.] It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole earth until the ninth hour.

[Col. 0651A] [CCCXXVIII, 2.] The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in the middle.

[CCCXXIX, 1.] And crying out with a loud voice, Jesus said: “Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.” And saying this, he breathed his last.

[CCCXXX, 2.] When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying: “Truly, this was a righteous man.”

[CCCXXXI, 10.] And all the crowds who had gathered together for this spectacle and had seen what was happening returned, beating their breasts. All his acquaintances stood at a distance, as did the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching these things.

[CCCXXXII, 1.] And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man—he had not consented to their plan and actions—came from the city of Arimathea in Judaea. He too was awaiting the kingdom of God. He approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

[Col. 0651B] [CCCXXXIII, 1.] After taking it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed him in a tomb hewn from rock, in which no one had yet been laid.

[CCCXXXIV, 10.] It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning to dawn. The women who had come with him from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how his body had been placed.

[CCCXXXV, 8.] Returning, they prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they kept silence, according to the commandment.

## [Chapter XXIV]

[CCCXXXVI, 1.] But on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the tomb, carrying the spices they had prepared. They found the stone rolled away from the tomb. Entering, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

While they were perplexed about this, behold, two men stood beside them in shining garments.

[CCCXXXVII, 2.] As they were afraid and bowed their faces toward the ground, they said to them: “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you when he was still in Galilee, saying that the Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men, be crucified, and rise on the third day.”

And they remembered his words.

[CCCXXXVIII, 2.] Returning from the tomb, they announced all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.

[CCCXXXIX, 10.] They were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary of James, and the other women who were with them. They were telling these things to the apostles, but these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.

Peter, however, rose and ran to the tomb. Bending down, he saw only the linen cloths lying there, and he went away wondering to himself at what had happened.

[CCCXL, 8.] And behold, two of them were going that same day to a village that was sixty stadia from Jerusalem, named Emmaus. They were speaking with each other about all these things that had happened.

While they were talking and questioning one another, Jesus himself drew near and went with them; but their eyes were prevented from recognizing him.

And he said to them: “What are these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk, and why are you sad?”

One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: “Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem, and have you not learned the things that have happened there in these days?”

He said to them: “What things?”

And they said: “About Jesus of Nazareth, who was a man, a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people; and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to condemnation to death and crucified him.

“But we were hoping that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And now, in addition to all these things, today is the third day since these things happened.

[Note: The word *est* (“is”) is absent in one Vatican manuscript.]

“Moreover, some women from among us terrified us. They were at the tomb before daylight, and when they did not find his body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels who said that he was alive.

“Some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not find him.”

[Note: Our manuscripts, more correctly following the Greek archetype, have “they did not see” (*non viderunt* or *non vidimus*) instead of “they did not find.”]

And he said to them: “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and so enter into his glory?”

Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

They drew near to the village to which they were going, and he pretended that he was going farther. They urged him, saying: “Remain with us, because evening is approaching and the day is already declining.”

And he entered in to stay with them. And it happened, while he was reclining at table with them, that he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and handed it to them. Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.

And they said to one another: “Was not our heart burning within us while he spoke to us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

Rising at that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem. They found the Eleven gathered together, and those who were with them, saying: “The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon.”

And they were recounting what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized him in the breaking of the bread.

[CCCXLI, 9.] While they were saying these things, Jesus stood in their midst and said to them: “Peace to you; it is I. Do not be afraid.”

But they were troubled and terrified, thinking that they were seeing a spirit. And he said to them: “Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”

And after saying this, he showed them his hands and feet.

[CCCXLII, 9.] While they still did not believe, because of their joy, and were amazed, he said: “Do you have anything here to eat?”

They offered him a piece of broiled fish and a honeycomb. And when he had eaten before them, he took the remains and gave them to them.

[CCCXLIII, 3.] And he said to them: “These are the words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”

Then he opened their understanding, so that they might understand the Scriptures. And he said to them: “For thus it is written, and thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, and for repentance and the forgiveness of sins to be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.

“You are witnesses of these things. And I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. But remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”

Then he led them out as far as Bethany. And lifting up his hands, he blessed them. And it happened, while he was blessing them, that he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.

And they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy. They were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

[Col. 0653] The Gospel according to Luke ends.

# THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO JOHN BEGINS

[Col. 0653B] [Chapter I. I, 3.] In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made. In him was life, and the life was the light of men. And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.

[II, 3.] There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came for testimony, to bear witness to the light, so that all might believe through him. He was not the light, but he came to bear witness to the light.

[III, 3.] There was the true light that enlightens every person coming into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him.

[IV, 10.] He came to his own, and his own did not receive him. But to all who received him he gave power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name: who were born not from bloods, nor from the will of the flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God.

[V, 3.] And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. We saw his glory, glory as of the Only-Begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.

[VI, 1.] John bears witness to him and cries out, saying: “This was he of whom I said: ‘The one who comes after me has been placed before me, because he was before me.’”

[VII, 10.] And from his fullness we have all received, grace for grace. For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

[VIII, 3.] No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known.

[IX, 10.] This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him to question him: “Who are you?”

He confessed and did not deny; he confessed: “I am not the Christ.”

And they asked him: “What then? Are you Elijah?”

He said: “I am not.”

“Are you the prophet?”

He answered: “No.”

They therefore said to him: “Who are you, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”

[X, 1.] He said: “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”

[XI, 10.] Those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. They questioned him and said to him: “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”

[XII, 1.] John answered them, saying: “I baptize in water. But among you stands one whom you do not know.

[Note: Three manuscripts have “whom you do not know.”]

“He is the one who will come after me, who has been placed before me; I am not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandal.”

[XIII, 10.] These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said: “Behold, the Lamb of God; behold, the one who takes away the sin of the world.

[XIV, 1.] “This is the one about whom I said: ‘After me comes a man who has been placed before me, because he was before me.’ I did not know him; but so that he might be manifested in Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water.”

[XV, 1.] And John bore witness, saying: “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him. I did not know him; but the one who sent me to baptize in water said to me: ‘The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining—that is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ I have seen, and I have borne witness that this is the Son of God.”

[XVI, 10.] The next day John was standing there again, and two of his disciples. Looking at Jesus as he walked by, he said: “Behold, the Lamb of God.”

The two disciples heard him speaking, and they followed Jesus. Jesus turned and, seeing them following, said to them: “What are you seeking?”

They said to him: “Rabbi”—which, translated, means Teacher—“where are you staying?”

He said to them: “Come and see.”

They came and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him.

[XVII, 1.] He first found his brother Simon and said to him: “We have found the Messiah”—which is translated Christ. And he brought him to Jesus.

When Jesus looked at him, he said: “You are Simon, son of John; you will be called Cephas”—which is translated Peter.

[XVIII, 10.] The next day he wished to depart for Galilee and found Philip.

[Note: One Vatican manuscript has “On the next day, however, he wished to depart,” and so forth.]

[Col. 0655A] Jesus said to him: “Follow me.”

Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. Philip found Nathanael and said to him: “We have found the one about whom Moses wrote in the Law, and the prophets: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth.”

Nathanael said to him: “Can anything good come from Nazareth?”

Philip said to him: “Come and see.”

Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him: “Behold, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.”

Nathanael said to him: “From where do you know me?”

Jesus answered and said to him: “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”

Nathanael answered him and said: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the king of Israel.”

Jesus answered and said to him: “Because I told you, ‘I saw you under the fig tree,’ you believe? You will see greater things than these.”

And he said to him: “Truly, truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”

[Col. 0655B] ## [Chapter II]

On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Jesus and his disciples were also invited to the wedding.

When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him: “They have no wine.”

Jesus said to her: “What is this to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.”

His mother said to the servants: “Whatever he tells you, do it.”

Six stone water jars were standing there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding two or three measures.

Jesus said to them: “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim.

And Jesus said to them: “Now draw some out and take it to the steward.” And they took it.

When the steward tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from—but the servants who had drawn the water knew—the steward called the bridegroom and said to him: “Every person first serves the good wine; and when they have become drunk, the inferior. But you have kept the good wine until now.”

Jesus performed this beginning of signs in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

[XIX, 7.] After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they remained there for not many days.

[XX, 1.] The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

[XXI, 1.] He found in the temple those selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money-changers sitting there. And having made something like a whip from cords, he drove them all out of the temple, including the sheep and the oxen; he scattered the money-changers’ coins and overturned their tables.

[Col. 0655D] He said to those who were selling doves: “Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father’s house a house of commerce.”

[XXII, 10.] His disciples remembered that it was written: “Zeal for your house has consumed me.”

[XXIII, 4.] The Jews therefore answered and said to him: “What sign do you show us, since you do these things?”

[XXIV, 10.] Jesus answered and said to them: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

The Jews therefore said: “This temple was built in forty-six years, and you will raise it up in three days?”

But he was speaking about the temple of his body. Therefore, when he had risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this; and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

While he was in Jerusalem at Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, seeing the signs that he performed.

But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he knew them all, and because he had no need for anyone to testify about a person; for he himself knew what was in a person.

### [Chapter III]

There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. He came to Jesus by night and said to him: “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can perform these signs that you perform unless God is with him.”

Jesus answered and said to him [Col. 0656B]: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone has been born again,

[Note: [Col. 0655D] Our manuscripts have *born* instead of *born again*, more closely corresponding to the Greek text γεννηθῇ (*be born*). Likewise, shortly afterward, the same books read *enter* and *be born* instead of *be born again*.]

he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Nicodemus said to him: “How can a person be born when he is old? Surely he cannot enter his mother’s womb a second time and be born again?”

Jesus answered: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone has been born of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. What is born of flesh is flesh, and what is born of spirit is spirit. Do not marvel that I said to you: You must be born again. The Spirit breathes where it wills, and you hear its voice, but

[Note: [Col. 0656D] The same manuscripts read: “and you do not know from where it comes or where it goes.”]

you do not know from where it comes or where it goes; so it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit.”

Nicodemus answered and said to him: “How can these things happen?”

Jesus answered and said to him: “You are a teacher in Israel, and you do not understand these things? Amen, amen, I say to you: what we know, we speak, and what we have seen, we testify to; yet you do not accept our testimony. If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life.
