“For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not judged; but whoever does not believe has already been judged [Col. 0656D], because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.

“This is the judgment: that light has come into the world, and people loved darkness more than light, for their works were evil. Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed;

[Note: [Col. 0656D] Following the Greek exemplar, ὁ φαῦλα πράσσων (*the one who does evil*), our manuscripts also read *who does evil* instead of *evil*, etc.]

but whoever practices the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be revealed, because they have been done in God.”

After this Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea; there he stayed with them and baptized. [XXV, 3.] John was also baptizing at Aenon, near Salim, because there was much water there [Col. 0657A],

[Note: [Col. 0657D] Two manuscripts read *and they came*, a preposition that in one manuscript of the Regina edition was deleted in a second revision.]

and people came and were baptized. [XXVI, 4.] For John had not yet been sent into prison. [XXVII, 10.]

Now a dispute arose between John’s disciples and the Jews concerning purification. They came to John and said to him: “Rabbi, the one who was with you across the Jordan, to whom you bore witness—look, he is baptizing, and everyone is coming to him.”

John answered and said: “A person cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven. [XXVIII, 1.] You yourselves bear witness for me that I said: ‘I am not the Christ,’ but that ‘I have been sent before him.’ [XXIX, 10.] Whoever has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore this joy of mine has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.

“He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all. What he has seen and heard, he testifies to, and no one accepts his testimony. Whoever accepts his testimony has certified that God is truthful. For the one whom God sent speaks the words of God; for God does not give the Spirit by measure. [XXX, 3.]

“The Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hand. [XXXI, 10.] Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; but whoever is disobedient to the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.”

### [Chapter IV]

When Jesus therefore learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—although Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples—[Col. 0657C] [XXXII, 7.] he left Judea and went again into Galilee. [XXXIII, 10.]

It was necessary for him to pass through Samaria. So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the estate that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Jacob’s well was there. Jesus, therefore, wearied from the journey, was sitting thus beside the well. It was about the sixth hour.

A woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her: “Give me a drink.” (For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food.)

The Samaritan woman therefore said to him: “How is it that you, though a Jew, ask me for a drink, though I am a Samaritan woman?” For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.

Jesus answered and said to her: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you perhaps would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

The woman said to him: “Lord, you have nothing with which to draw, and the well is deep. From where, then, do you have living water? Surely you are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his livestock?”

Jesus answered and said to her: “Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks from the water that I will give him will never thirst. Rather, the water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.”

The woman said to him: “Lord, give me this water [Col. 0658A], so that I may not thirst or come here to draw water.”

Jesus said to her: “Go, call your husband, and come here.”

The woman answered and said: “I have no husband.”

Jesus said to her: “You have spoken well, ‘I have no husband.’ For you have had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband; in this you have spoken truly.”

The woman said to him: “Lord, I see that you are a prophet. Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where one must worship.”

Jesus said to her: “Woman, believe me, because the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.”

[Note: [Col. 0658D] In our manuscripts, *because it will come*. The Greek text itself, however, has the present form ἔρχεται (*it is coming*).]

“You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews. But the hour is coming—and now is—when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For the Father also seeks such people to worship him. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”

The woman said to him: “I know that the Messiah is coming” (who is called Christ). “When he comes, he will announce everything to us.”

Jesus said to her: “I am he, the one speaking with you.”

And immediately his disciples came, and they marveled that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said: “What are you seeking?” or “Why are you speaking with her?”

The woman therefore left her water jar and went into the city, and said to those men: “Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Surely he is the Christ?”

So they went out of the city and came to him.

Meanwhile the disciples were asking him, saying: “Rabbi, eat.”

But he said to them: “I have food to eat of which you do not know.”

The disciples therefore said to one another: “Surely someone has brought him something to eat?”

Jesus said to them: “My food is to do the will of the one who sent me, and to complete his work. Do you not say that there are still four months, and the harvest is coming? [Al.: *is*] Look, I say to you: Lift up your eyes and see the regions, because they are already white for the harvest.

“And the one who reaps receives a reward and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together. For in this the saying is true: ‘One is the sower, and another is the reaper.’ I sent you to reap what you did not labor for; others labored, and you entered into their labor.”

Now many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the word of the woman who testified: “He told me everything I have done.” [Col. 0658D.]

When the Samaritans therefore came to him, they asked him to remain there. And he stayed there two days. And many more believed in him because of his word.

And they said to the woman: “We no longer believe because of your speech; for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this man is truly the Savior of the world.”

[XXXIV, 7.] After two days he departed from there and went into Galilee. [XXXV, 1.] For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.

[XXXVI, 10.] When therefore they came into Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen everything he had done in Jerusalem on the feast day; for they too had gone to the feast.

So he came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water wine. [XXXVII, 4.]

There was a certain royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son, for he was beginning to die.

Jesus therefore said to him: “Unless you see signs and wonders, you do not believe.”

The royal official said to him: “Lord, come down before my son dies.”

Jesus said to him: “Go; your son lives.”

The man believed the word that Jesus had spoken to him and went away.

Now as he was going down, his servants met him and announced that his son was alive. So he asked them the hour at which he had improved.

They said to him: “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”

The father therefore realized that it was at that hour when Jesus had said to him: “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, along with his entire household.

This was again the second sign that Jesus performed when he came from Judea into Galilee.

### [Chapter V. XXXVIII, 1.]

After this there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. There is in Jerusalem a Sheep Pool, called in Hebrew Bethsaida, having five porticoes.

In these lay a great multitude of the sick, blind, lame, and withered, waiting for the movement of the water. For an angel of the Lord descended into the pool at a certain time, and the water was stirred. And whoever entered the pool first after the stirring of the water was healed of whatever illness afflicted him.

There was a certain man there who had been ill for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had already been ill for a long time, he said to him: “Do you want to become well?”

The sick man answered him: “Lord, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred; for while I am coming, another goes down before me.”

Jesus said to him: “Rise, take up your pallet, and walk.”

And immediately the man became well, and he took up his pallet and walked.

Now it was the Sabbath on that day. The Jews therefore said to the man who had been healed: “It is the Sabbath; it is not permitted for you to carry your pallet.”

[XXXIX, 10.] He answered them: “The one who made me well, he said to me: ‘Take up your pallet and walk.’”

They therefore asked him: “Who is the man who said to you: ‘Take up your pallet and walk?’”

But the man who had been healed did not know who it was. For Jesus had withdrawn from the crowd gathered in that place.

Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: “Look, you have become well; do not sin any longer, so that something worse may not happen to you.”

The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.

For this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.

But Jesus answered them: “My Father is working until now, and I am working.”

For this reason the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only was breaking the Sabbath, but also was calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

Jesus therefore answered and said to them [Col. 0660A]: “Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son can do nothing from himself except what he sees the Father doing. For whatever he does, the Son likewise does. For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself does; and he will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel.

“For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whomever he wishes. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. [XL, 1.] Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.

[ XLI, 10.] “Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death [Col. 0660B] into life.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming—and now is—when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live. For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has also granted the Son to have life in himself. And he has given him authority to exercise judgment, because he is the Son of Man.

“Do not marvel at this, because the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God. And they will come forth: those who have done good, into the resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, into the resurrection of judgment.

“I can do nothing from myself. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just [XLII, 1.], because I do not seek my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.

[XLIII, 10.] “If I testify concerning myself, my testimony is not true. There is another who testifies concerning me, and I know that the testimony by which he testifies concerning me is true.

“You sent to John, and he bore witness to the truth. But I do not receive testimony from a human being; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved. He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing for a time to rejoice in his light.

“But I have testimony greater than John’s. For the works that the Father gave me to complete—the very works that I do—testify concerning me that the Father sent me. And the Father who sent me has himself testified concerning me. [XLIV, 4.] You have never heard his voice, nor have you seen his form. [XLV, 10.]

“And you do not have his word remaining in you, because you do not believe the one whom he sent. Search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and they are the ones that testify concerning me. Yet you are unwilling to come to me so that you may have life.

“I do not receive glory from human beings. But I know you, that you do not have the love of God in yourselves. I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, you will receive him.

“How can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?

“Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; there is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you hope. For if you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me also, for he wrote about me. But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?”

[Col. 0661A] ### [Chapter VI. XLVI, 1.]

After this Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee, which is that of Tiberias. A great multitude followed him, because they saw the signs that he performed upon those who were sick.

[XLVII, 3.] Jesus therefore went up onto the mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.

[XLVIII, 1.] Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.

[XLIX, 1.] When Jesus had therefore lifted up his eyes and seen that a very great multitude was coming to him, he said to Philip: “Where shall we buy bread so that these people may eat?”

He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.

Philip answered him: “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, so that each might receive even a little.”

One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him: “There is one boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these among so many?”

Jesus therefore said: “Have the people sit down.”

Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, about five thousand in number.

Jesus therefore took the loaves, and when he had given thanks, he distributed them to those who were seated; likewise also from the fish, as much as they wanted.

When they had been filled, he said to his disciples: “Gather up the fragments that remain, so that they may not be lost.”

They therefore gathered them and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley loaves that remained after those who had eaten.

[L, 10.] When those people had seen the sign that Jesus had performed, they said: “This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world.”

Jesus therefore, when he realized that they were about to come and seize him to make him king, fled again to the mountain, alone.

[LI, 4.] When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea. And having embarked in a boat, they crossed the sea toward Capernaum. It had already become dark, and Jesus had not come to them.

The sea was rising because a strong wind was blowing. When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near to the boat, and they were afraid.

But he said to them: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

They therefore wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the land toward which they were going.

[LII, 10.] The next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there had been no other boat there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples, but that his disciples alone had departed. Other boats, however, had arrived from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

When the crowd therefore saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

When they had found him across the sea, they said to him: “Rabbi, when did you come here?”

Jesus answered them and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you: you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the loaves and were satisfied. Work not for food that perishes, but for food that remains unto eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For the Father—God—has set his seal upon him.”

They therefore said to him [Col. 0662A]: “What shall we do, so that we may perform the works of God?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “This is the work of God: that you believe in the one whom he sent.”

[LIII, 4.] They therefore said to him: “What sign, then, do you perform, so that we may see and believe you? What do you work?”

[LIV, 10.] “Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”

Jesus therefore said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: Moses did not give you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is the one who descends from heaven and gives life to the world.”

They therefore said to him: “Lord, always give us this bread.”

[LX, 1.] Jesus then said to them: “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst. But I told you that you have both seen me and do not believe.

[LVI, 10.] “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will not cast out. [LVII, 1.] For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of the one who sent me. [LVIII, 10.]

“And this is the will of the Father who sent me: that I lose nothing of everything he has given me, but raise him up on the last day. And this is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.”

[LIX, 1.] The Jews therefore murmured about him because he had said: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven.”

[Note: [Col. 0661D] Our manuscripts do not add *living*, an epithet that is likewise not found here in the Greek text.]

And they said: “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How, then, does he say: ‘I have come down from heaven?’”

[Col. 0662C]

[Note: [Col. 0662D] One Vatican manuscript reads *he has come down* instead of *I have come down*.]

[LX, 10.] Jesus therefore answered and said to them: “Do not murmur among yourselves. No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day.

“It is written in the prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me.

[LXI, 3.] “Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.

[LXII, 10.] “Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life.

[LXIII, 1.] “I am the bread of life.

[LXIV, 10.] “Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness, and they died. This is the bread descending from heaven, so that if anyone eats of it, he may not die.

[LXV, 1.] “I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh for the life of the world.”

[LXVI, 10.] The Jews therefore argued among themselves, saying: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”

Jesus therefore said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.

[LXVII, 1.] “For my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink.

[LXVIII, 10.] “Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him. Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me will also live because of me.

“This is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the bread your fathers ate and they died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.”

He said these things while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.

Many of his disciples, therefore, when they heard this, said: “This is a hard saying; who can hear it?”

But Jesus, knowing within himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, said to them: “Does this scandalize you?

[LXIX, 1.] “What, then, if you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before?”

[Note: [Col. 0663D] Instead of the word *is*, two of our manuscripts insert the obelus ÷, though less correctly.]

[LXX, 4.] “It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing.

[LXXI, 10.] “The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life. But there are some among you who do not believe.”

[LXXII, 4.] For Jesus knew from the beginning who the unbelievers were, and who would betray him.

[LXXIII, 10.] And he said: “For this reason I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to him by my Father.”

From this point many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him.

Jesus therefore said to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to leave?”

[LXXIV, 1.] Simon Peter therefore answered him: “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Christ, the Son of God.”

[LXXV, 10.] Jesus answered them: “Did I not choose you Twelve? And one of you is a devil.”

He was speaking of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon [Al.: *Scariothem* and *Scariothis*]; for he was going to betray him, although he was one of the Twelve.

[Col. 0663C] ### [Chapter VII]

After this Jesus was walking in Galilee; for he did not wish to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

Now the Jewish feast of Booths was near. His brothers therefore said to him: “Leave here and go into Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works that you do. For no one acts in secret while seeking to be known publicly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.”

For not even his brothers believed in him.

Jesus therefore said to them: “My time has not yet arrived, but your time is always ready. The world cannot hate you, but it hates [Mart.: *hears*] me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.

“You go up to this feast; I am not going up to this feast, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.”

When he had said these things, he remained in Galilee.

But when his brothers had gone up, then he too went up to the feast, not openly but as if in secret.

The Jews therefore were looking for him during the feast and saying: “Where is he?”

There was much murmuring about him among the crowd. For some were saying: “He is good.” Others were saying: “No, but he leads the crowds astray.”

Yet no one spoke openly about him, because of fear of the Jews.

When the feast was already halfway over, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.

The Jews were amazed, saying: “How does this man know letters, though he has never studied?”

Jesus answered them and said: “My teaching is not mine, but that of the one who sent me. If anyone wishes to do his will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I speak from myself.

“Whoever speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truthful, and there is no injustice in him.

“Did Moses not give you the law? Yet none of you observes the law. Why do you seek to kill me?”

The crowd answered and said: “You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?”

Jesus answered and said to them: “I performed one work, and you are all amazed. For this reason Moses gave you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.

“If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made an entire man well on the Sabbath?

“Do not judge according to appearance, but judge a just judgment.”

Some people from Jerusalem were saying: “Is this not the man whom they seek to kill?”

[Note: [Col. 0663D; Col. 0664D] Two of our manuscripts omit the particle *and*; a third, Vatican manuscript deletes it in a second revision. Shortly before this, instead of *from Jerusalem*, the Greek has ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμιτῶν, *from the Jerusalemites*.]

“And look, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ? But we know where this man is from; when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.”

[LXXVI, 3.] Jesus therefore cried out in the temple while teaching and saying: “You know me, and you know where I am from. Yet I have not come from myself; rather, the one who sent me is true, whom you do not know. I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”

[LXXVII, 1.] They therefore sought to seize him, and no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.

[LXXVIII, 10.] Many from the crowd believed in him and said: “When the Christ comes, will he perform more signs than this man has performed?”

The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things about him, [LXXIX, 1.] and the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to seize him.

[LXXX, 10.] Jesus therefore said to them: “I am with you for a little while longer, and I am going to the one who sent me.

[LXXXI, 10.]

[Note: [Col. 0664D] Some manuscripts less correctly have *then* here and shortly afterward, *you seek* instead of *you will seek*.]

“You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.”

The Jews therefore said among themselves: “Where is this man going, that we will not find him? Surely he is not going to the dispersion among the Gentiles and teaching the Gentiles?

“What is this saying that he has spoken: ‘You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come’?”

On the last and great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying: “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me—as the Scripture says—rivers of living water will flow from his belly.”

He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were going to receive; for the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.

[LXXXII, 7.] From that crowd, therefore, when they had heard these words of his, some said: “This is truly the Prophet.”

Others said: “This is the Christ.”

[LXXXIII, 7.] But some said: “Does the Christ come from Galilee? Does not the Scripture say that the Christ comes from the offspring of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”

[LXXXIV, 10.] A division therefore arose in the crowd because of him.

[LXXXV, 1.] Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.

[LXXXVI, 10.] The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees. And they said to them: “Why did you not bring him?”

The officers answered: “Never has anyone spoken as this man speaks.”

The Pharisees therefore answered them: “Have you too been led astray? Has any one of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in him? But this crowd, which does not know the law, is accursed.”

Nicodemus said to them—the one who had come to him by night, who was one of them: “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears him and learns what he does?”

They answered and said to him: “Are you also from Galilee? Search

[Note: [Col. 0665D] Our manuscripts do not add *the Scriptures*, nor does the Greek text itself: ἐρεύνησον, καὶ ἴδε, *search, and see*.]

and see that no prophet arises from Galilee.”

And each of them returned to his own house.

## Chapter VIII

Jesus went on to the Mount of Olives. At dawn he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him; and he sat down and taught them.

The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, set her in the midst, and said to him: “Teacher, this woman has just been caught in adultery. Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say?”

They were saying this to test him, so that they might have grounds to accuse him. But Jesus, bending down, wrote with his finger on the ground. When they persisted in questioning him, he straightened up and said to them: “Let the one among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.” And bending down again, he wrote on the ground.

When they heard this, they went out one by one, beginning with the elders. And Jesus was left alone [Note: Here our manuscripts, and certain older Greek copies, omit the name “Jesus.”], with the woman standing in the midst. Jesus straightened up and said to her: “Woman, where are they who accused you? Has no one condemned you?”

She said: “No one, Lord.”

And Jesus said: “Neither will I condemn you. Go, and from now on do not sin any more.”

Again Jesus spoke to them, saying: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.”

The Pharisees therefore said to him: “You bear witness about yourself; your witness is not true.”

Jesus answered and said to them: “Even if I bear witness about myself, my witness is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going. You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one. And even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me. And in your law it is written that the testimony of two people is true. I am the one who bears witness about myself, and the Father who sent me bears witness about me.”

They therefore said to him: “Where is your Father?”

Jesus answered: “[LXXXVII, 3.] You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, perhaps you would also know my Father. [LXXXVIII, 1.] Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, while teaching in the temple; and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come. [LXXXIX, 10.]”

Jesus therefore said to them again: “I am going away, and you will seek me [Note: Two manuscripts read “you seek,” in the present tense, as noted above], and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

The Jews therefore said: “Surely he will not kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

And he said to them: “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world. I therefore told you that you will die in your sins. For if you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sin.”

They therefore said to him: “Who are you?”

Jesus said to them: “The Beginning—the one who also speaks to you.” [Manuscript reading: “because I speak to you.”]

“I have many things to say and to judge concerning you. But the one who sent me is truthful, and what I heard from him, these things I speak in the world.” And they did not understand that he was speaking to them of the Father.

Jesus therefore said to them: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but speak these things just as the Father taught me. And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, because I always do what is pleasing to him.”

As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

Jesus therefore said to the Jews who had believed him: “If you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth has set you free.””

They answered him: “We are Abraham’s offspring and have never been enslaved to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”

Jesus answered them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin. Now a slave does not remain in the household forever, but the son remains forever. Therefore, if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.

“I know that you are Abraham’s children; but you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no room in you. What I have seen with my Father I speak; and you do what you have seen with your father.”

They answered and said to him: “Our father is Abraham.”

Jesus said to them: “If you are Abraham’s children, do the works of Abraham. But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this. You do the works of your father.”

They therefore said to him: “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, God.”

Jesus therefore said to them: “If God were your father, you would certainly love me, for I proceeded from God and came. Indeed, I did not come of myself, but he sent me. Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word.

“You are from the father, the devil, and you want to carry out the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from what belongs to him, because he is a liar and its father.

“But because I speak the truth, you do not believe me. Which of you will convict me of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe me? Whoever is from God hears the words of God. This is why you do not hear: because you are not from God.”

The Jews therefore answered and said to him: “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

Jesus answered: “I do not have a demon; rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me. But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death.”

The Jews therefore said: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets did too; yet you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will never taste death.’ Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets also died. Whom do you make yourself?”

Jesus answered: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, whom you say is your God [Note: In two of our manuscripts, “because he is our God,” in agreement with certain Greek copies: ὅτι Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστι.]—and you have not known him. But I know him. And if I said that I did not know him, I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.

“Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

The Jews therefore said to him: “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”

Jesus said to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham came to be, I am.”

Therefore they picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

## Chapter IX

As Jesus passed by, he saw a man blind from birth. And his disciples asked him: “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he should be born blind?”

Jesus answered: “Neither did this man sin nor his parents, but so that the works of God might be manifested in him. I must work the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work. As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud from the spittle, and smeared the mud on his eyes. And he said to him: “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which is translated “Sent”).

He therefore went, washed, and came back seeing.

The neighbors and those who had previously seen him, because he was a beggar, said: “Is this not the man who used to sit and beg?”

Some said: “It is he.”

Others said: “No, but he resembles him.”

But he said: “I am he.”

They therefore said to him: “How were your eyes opened?”

He answered: “The man who is called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ I went, washed, and I see.”

[Note: Our manuscripts are closer to the Greek archetype: “I washed, and I saw.” Other copies read, “They therefore said to him,” as does the Greek: νιψάμενος, ἀνέβλεψα (“having washed, I saw”); εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ (“they therefore said to him”).]

And they said to him: “Where is he?”

He said: “I do not know.”

They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees. Now it was a sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes. Again the Pharisees questioned him about how he had come to see.

But he said to them: “He put mud on my eyes; I washed, and I see.”

Some of the Pharisees therefore said: “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the sabbath.”

But others said: “How can a sinful man perform such signs?” And there was a division among them.

They therefore said again to the blind man: “What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?”

He said: “He is a prophet.”

The Jews therefore did not believe about him that he had been blind and had come to see, until they summoned his parents—the man who had come to see—and questioned them, saying: “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”

His parents answered them and said: “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind. But how he now sees, we do not know; nor do we know who opened his eyes. Ask him. He is of age; let him speak for himself.”

His parents said this because they feared the Jews. For the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed him to be the Christ, he would be expelled from the synagogue. For this reason his parents said: “He is of age; ask him.”

They therefore summoned again the man who had been blind and said to him: “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”

He therefore said to them: “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

They therefore said to him: “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

He answered them: “I have already told you, and you heard. Why do you want to hear it again? Surely you also want to become his disciples?”

They reviled him and said: “You are his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses. We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know where he is from.”

The man answered and said to them: “This is astonishing: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes. Now we know that God does not hear sinners. But if anyone worships God and does his will, him he hears. From the beginning of the world it has not been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind. If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”

They answered and said to him: “You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?” And they cast him out.

Jesus heard that they had cast him out, and when he had found him, he said to him: “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

He answered and said: “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”

And Jesus said to him: “You have both seen him, and the one speaking with you is he.”

He said: “I believe, Lord.” And falling down, he worshiped him.

And Jesus said: “For judgment I came into this world: so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”

Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him: “Surely we are not blind also?”

Jesus said to them: “If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say, ‘We see.’ Your sin remains.”

## Chapter X

“Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs in by another way, is a thief and a robber. But whoever enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice [Note: Our manuscripts add the pronoun “his,” with the Greek exemplar φωνῆς αὐτοῦ.]; and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out. And when he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice. They do not follow a stranger, but flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”

Jesus told them this proverb, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.

Jesus therefore said to them again: “Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep. All who came are thieves and robbers, [Note: Our manuscripts read, closer to the Greek, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἤκουσαν, “but the sheep did not hear them.”] and the sheep did not hear them. I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; and he will enter and go out and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal, slaughter, and destroy. I came so that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.

“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep. But the hired man, who is not the shepherd and whose sheep are not his own, sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees; and the wolf snatches and scatters the sheep. The hired man flees because he is a hired man and has no concern for the sheep.

“I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and my own know me, [XC, 3.] just as the Father knows me and I know the Father; [XCI, 4.] and I lay down my life for my sheep. [XCII, 10.] And I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.

“For this reason the Father loves me: because I lay down my life so that I may take it up again. No one takes it from me; rather, I lay it down of myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. I received this commandment from my Father.”

Again there was a division among the Jews because of these words.

Many of them were saying: “He has a demon and is insane; why do you listen to him?”

Others said: “These words are not those of one who has a demon. Surely a demon can open the eyes of the blind?”

The Feast of the Dedication took place in Jerusalem, and it was winter. Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s portico.

The Jews therefore surrounded him and said to him: “How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”

Jesus answered them: “I speak to you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name bear witness about me. But you do not believe [Note: One or two of our manuscripts add mihi, “me,” although this pronoun is neither in the Greek text nor in the very ancient Latin manuscript of Reginae], because you are not of my sheep. My sheep hear my voice; I know them, and they follow me. And I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them from my hand. What my Father has given me is greater than all, and no one can snatch them from the hand of my Father. I and the Father are one.”

The Jews therefore picked up stones to stone him.

Jesus answered them: “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of these works are you stoning me?”

The Jews answered him: “We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because, though you are a man, you make yourself God.”

Jesus answered them: “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’? If he called those gods to whom the word of God came—and Scripture cannot be annulled—do you say to the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You are blaspheming,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’? If I do not perform the works of my Father, do not believe me. But if I do perform them, even if you do not wish to believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.”

[XCIII, 4.] They therefore sought to seize him, but he went out of their hands. And he went away again across the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptizing, and he remained there.

[Note: In accordance with the authority of our manuscripts and of other editors, which consistently have “baptizing,” corresponding to the Greek ὁ βαπτίζων, we have restored this reading; previously, following Martianaeus, the text had “was baptized.”]

[XCIV, 10.] Many came to him and said: “John indeed performed no sign, but everything John said about this man was true.” And many believed in him.

## Chapter XI

There was a certain sick man, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha her sister. (Mary was the one who anointed the Lord with perfume and wiped his feet with her hair; her brother Lazarus was sick.)

His sisters therefore sent to him, saying: “Lord, behold, the one whom you love is sick.”

When Jesus heard this, he said: “This illness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

Jesus loved Martha, her sister Mary, and Lazarus. When he heard, therefore, that he was sick, he then remained in the same place for two days.

After this he said to his disciples: “Let us go again into Judea.”

The disciples said to him: “Rabbi, the Jews were just now seeking to stone you, and you are going there again?”

Jesus answered: “Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world. But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.”

He said these things, and afterward said to them: “Lazarus our friend is sleeping, but I am going to awaken him from sleep.”

[Note: Two of our manuscripts read “to raise him up”; a third simply reads “to raise,” with the preposition having been deleted by later correction.]

His disciples therefore said: “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will be safe.”

But Jesus had spoken of his death, while they thought that he was speaking about ordinary sleep.

Then Jesus said to them plainly: “Lazarus has died, and I rejoice for your sake, so that you may believe, because I was not there. But let us go to him.”

Thomas, who is called Didymus, therefore said to his fellow disciples: “Let us also go, so that we may die with him.”

Jesus therefore came and found that he had already been four days in the tomb. (Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.)

Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother.

When Martha heard that Jesus had come, she went to meet him; but Mary was sitting at home.

Martha therefore said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”

Jesus said to her: “Your brother will rise again.”

Martha said to him: “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.”

Jesus said to her: “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live; and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

She said to him: “Yes, Lord; I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God, who has come into this world.”

When she had said this, she went away and secretly called her sister Mary, saying: “The Teacher is here and is calling you.”

When she heard this, she rose quickly and came to him. Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.

The Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw that Mary had quickly risen and gone out, followed her, saying: “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”

When Mary had come to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, he groaned in spirit and troubled himself, and said: “Where have you laid him?”

They said to him: “Lord, come and see.”

And Jesus wept.

The Jews therefore said: “See how he loved him.”

But some of them said: “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the man born blind, have caused this man not to die?”

[Note: The word “born”—referring to one born blind—is absent from our manuscripts and from most Greek copies of better quality.]

Jesus therefore, groaning again within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone had been placed over it.

Jesus said: “Take away the stone.”

Martha, the sister of the one who had died, said to him: “Lord, by now there is an odor, for it has been four days.”

Jesus said to her: “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”

They therefore took away the stone. Jesus, lifting his eyes upward, said: “Father, I give you thanks because you have heard me.

[Note: Nearly all Latin and Greek manuscripts add the adverb “indeed” or “truly” here.]

“I knew that you always hear me, but because of the crowd standing around I said this, so that they may believe that you sent me.”

When he had said this, he cried out in a loud voice: “Lazarus, come out!”

Immediately the man who had died came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth, and his face wrapped in a cloth.

Jesus said to them: “Unbind him and let him go.”

Many of the Jews who had come to Mary and Martha, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in him.

[Note: The name “Jesus” is absent from our manuscripts and from some Greek manuscripts.]

But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

The chief priests and Pharisees therefore gathered a council and said: “What are we doing? For this man performs many signs. If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

One of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: “You know nothing at all, nor do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation should not perish.”

[Note: “For us” is found in most Greek manuscripts, and our manuscripts unanimously prefer it as well.]

He did not say this of himself. Rather, because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation, and not only for the nation, but also to gather into one the children of God who were scattered abroad.

[XCV, 4.] From that day therefore they planned to kill him.

Jesus therefore no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away from there to the region near the desert, to a city called Ephraim, and there he remained with his disciples.

[XCVI, 1.] Now the Passover of the Jews was near. [XCVII, 10.] Many went up to Jerusalem from the region before the Passover, to purify themselves.

They were seeking Jesus and speaking with one another as they stood in the temple: “What do you think? Surely he will not come to the feast?”

The chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, so that they might seize him.

## Chapter XII

Jesus therefore, six days before the Passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus had been, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.

[XCVIII, 1.] [Note: This chapter, John XCVIII, must be referred not only to canon 1, in which it agrees with Matthew CCLXXVI, Mark CLVIII, and Luke LXXIV, but also to canon 4, in which it corresponds with Matthew CCLXXVII and Mark CLIX. We are content to have noted these matters and have reproduced faithfully what is found in the manuscripts. MART.]

They made him a supper there, and Martha served; Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.

Mary therefore took a pound of costly perfume of pure nard, anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.

One of his disciples, Judas Iscariot [manuscript: Scariothis], who was about to betray him, said: “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”

He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and, having the money box, carried away what was put into it.

[Note: Two of our manuscripts read “carried away” with the preposition, exportabat. Then, closer to the Greek archetype, they read “Leave her” rather than “Let her,” using the singular form sin[e] for sinite.]

Jesus therefore said: “Leave her, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial. For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”

[XCIX, 10.] The large crowd of Jews therefore learned that he was there, and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

The chief priests therefore planned to kill Lazarus as well, because many of the Jews were going away on his account and believing in Jesus.

[C, 1.] On the next day the large crowd that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm trees, went out to meet him, and cried out: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”

[CI, 7.] Jesus found a young donkey and sat upon it, as it is written: “Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your king is coming, seated on a donkey’s colt.”

[CII, 10.] At first his disciples did not understand these things. But when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things to him.

The crowd that had been with him, when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead, bore witness.

For this reason the crowd also went out to meet him, because they had heard that he had performed this sign.

The Pharisees therefore said among themselves: “Do you see that we are accomplishing nothing? Behold, the whole world has gone after him.”

Now there were some Gentiles among those who had gone up to worship at the feast. These therefore approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.”

Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip in turn told Jesus.

[CIII, 4.] Jesus answered them, saying: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”

[Note: In one Vatican manuscript, “so that he may be glorified” occurs instead of “to be glorified.”]

[CIV, 10.] “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falling into the ground dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

[CV, 3.] Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.

[CVI, 10.] If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also my servant will be. If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.

[CVII, 4.] Now my soul is troubled. And what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour.

[CVIII, 10.] But it was for this reason that I came to this hour. Father, glorify your name.”

A voice therefore came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

The crowd standing there and hearing it said that thunder had occurred. Others said: “An angel has spoken to him.”

Jesus answered and said: “This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours. Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.”

He said this to signify by what death he was going to die.

The crowd answered him: “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever. How then do you say, ‘The Son of Man must be lifted up’? Who is this Son of Man?”

Jesus therefore said to them: “For a little while longer the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not overtake you. Whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light.”

Jesus spoke these things, then went away and hid himself from them.

Although he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he said: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

[CIX, 1.] For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah said again: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they may not see with their eyes, understand with their heart, and turn, and I heal them.”

[CX, 10.] Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke about him.

Nevertheless, many even of the rulers believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, so that they would not be expelled from the synagogue. For they loved the glory of human beings more than the glory of God.

[CXI, 1.] Jesus therefore cried out and said: “Whoever believes in me does not believe in me but in the one who sent me. And whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.

[CXII, 10.] I have come into the world as light, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness. And if anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.

“Whoever rejects me and does not accept my words has one who judges him. The word that I have spoken—that will judge him on the last day. For I have not spoken of myself, but the Father who sent me himself gave me a commandment concerning what I should say and what I should speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore, what I speak, I speak just as the Father told me.”

## Chapter XIII

Before the feast of Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end.

[Note: Our manuscripts add the adverb “now,” which is also reflected in the Greek text, δέ.]

After supper, when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, to betray him,

[Note: Two of our manuscripts omit the name “Simon,” as do some Greek copies, but they unanimously and customarily read “Scariothis.”]

knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come forth from God and was going to God, he rose from supper, laid aside his garments, and, taking a towel, girded himself.

Then he poured water [Note: These same manuscripts read “poured” (misit) instead of “pours” (mittit).] into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.

He therefore came to Simon Peter. And Peter said to him: “Lord, are you washing my feet?”

Jesus answered and said to him: “What I am doing, you do not know now, but you will understand afterward.”

Peter said to him: “You shall never wash my feet.”

Jesus answered him: “If I do not wash you, you will have no share with me.”

Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.”

Jesus said to him: “The one who has been washed does not need to wash except his feet, but is wholly clean. And you are clean, but not all.”

For he knew who would betray him; therefore he said: “You are not all clean.”

After he had washed their feet and taken his garments, when he had reclined again, he said to them: “Do you know what I have done to you?”

[CXVI, 3.] “You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, for so I am.

[CXVII, 10.] If therefore I, Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, so that just as I have done to you, you also should do.

[CXVIII, 3.] Amen, amen, I say to you: a slave is not greater than his master, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

[CXIX, 10.] I am not speaking about all of you. I know whom I have chosen. But so that Scripture may be fulfilled: ‘The one who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me.’

“From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it has happened you may believe that I am he.

[CXX, 1.] Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever receives anyone whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.”

[CXXI, 1.] When Jesus had said these things, he was troubled in spirit, testified, and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you: one of you will betray me.”

[CXXII, 4.] The disciples therefore looked at one another, uncertain of whom he was speaking.

[CXXIII, 10.] One of his disciples was reclining on Jesus’ breast—the one whom Jesus loved.

Simon Peter therefore signaled to him and said to him: “Who is it of whom he speaks?”

When he had reclined upon Jesus’ breast, he said to him: “Lord, who is it?”

[Note: Our manuscripts read, “Jesus answered him.” Nearly all add the particle “then” in the passage where it says, “then Satan entered into him.” A little later these same manuscripts read, “Jesus says to him,” instead of “what he had said to him.”]

Jesus answered: “It is the one to whom I shall give the morsel after dipping it.”

[CXXIV, 9.] And when he had dipped the bread, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon. [Manuscript: Scariothis.] And after the morsel, Satan entered into him.

[CXXV, 10.] Jesus therefore said to him: “What you are doing, do quickly.”

But none of those reclining at table knew why he had said this to him. For some thought, because Judas had the money box, that Jesus had said to him: “Buy what we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.

When he had received the morsel, he went out immediately. And it was night.

When he had gone out, Jesus said: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him. If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.

“Little children, I am with you only a little longer. You will seek me; and just as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ so I say to you now.

“I give you a new commandment: that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

[CXXVI, 1.] Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, where are you going?”

Jesus answered: “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now, but you will follow afterward.”

Peter said to him: “Why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”

Jesus answered: “Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you: the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times.”

[Chapter XIV. CXXVII, 10.] “Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me. In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places. If it were otherwise, I would have told you, because I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be. And where I go, you know, and the way you know.” [Col. 0675D]

Thomas said to him: “Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?” Jesus said to him: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you had known me, you would certainly have known my Father also; and from now on you will know him, and you have seen him.” [Col. 0676A]

Philip said to him: “Lord, show us the Father, and that is enough for us.” Jesus said to him: “Have I been with you for so long a time, and you have not known me? Philip, he who sees me sees the Father also. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from myself. Rather, the Father dwelling in me himself performs the works. Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? Otherwise, believe because of the works themselves.

“Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.”

[Note: Our manuscripts perhaps follow the Greek more closely, reading “he who sees me sees the Father also,” etc. Then, more closely in the same text, they have “you do not believe” [singular] rather than “you do not believe” [plural].]

[CXXVIII, 4.] “And whatever you ask the Father in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it. If you love me, keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, so that he may remain with you forever: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. [Col. 0676B] But you will know him, because he will remain with you and will be in you.

[Note: At this point, in agreement with the Greek text, our manuscripts also have “you do not know,” rather than “you will not know.”]

“I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you. A little while longer, and the world will no longer see me. But you see me, because I live, and you will live. On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you. Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me.”

[CXXIX, 1.] “And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father; and I will love him and reveal myself to him.”

[CXXX, 10.] Judas—not Iscariot [manuscript: Scariothis]—said to him: “Lord, what has happened, that you are about to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?” [Col. 0676C]

Jesus answered and said to him: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words.

[CXXXI, 1.] “And the word that you have heard is not mine, but the Father’s, who sent me. I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you. [Col. 0676D]

[CXXXII, 10.] “But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and remind you of everything that I have said to you. I leave you peace; I give you my peace. I do not give it as the world gives. Let not your heart be troubled, and let it not be afraid.

“You have heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away, and I am coming to you.’ If you loved me, you would certainly rejoice, because I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I. And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.

“I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me. But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and that I do just as the Father commanded me: rise, let us go from here.”

[Chapter XV.] “I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he will remove; and every one that bears fruit, he will prune, so that it may bear more fruit. [Col. 0677A] You are already clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.

“Remain in me, and I in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.

“If anyone does not remain in me, he will be cast out like a branch and will wither; and they will gather it, throw it into the fire, and it burns.

[Note: Closer to the Greek ἐξηράνθη (“it withered”), two of our manuscripts also read *aruit* (“it withered”), rather than *arescet* (“it will wither”).]

[CXXXIII, 4.] “If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, whatever you wish, ask, and it will be done for you.

[CXXXIV, 10.] “In this my Father is glorified: that you bear very much fruit and become my disciples. As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Remain in my love. [Col. 0677B] If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

“I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be complete. This is my commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you.

[CXXXV, 4.] “No one has a greater love than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends.

[CXXXVI, 10.] “You are my friends if you do what I command you. I will no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you.

“You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, and for your fruit to remain,

[CXXXVII, 4.] “so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.” [Col. 0677C]

[CXXXVII, 10.] “I command these things to you: love one another. If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you. If you were of the world, the world would love what belonged to it. But because you are not of the world, and I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.

[CXXXIX, 3.] “Remember my word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’

[CXL, 10.] “If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

[CXLI, 1.] “But they will do all these things to you because of my name,

[CXLII, 3.] “because they do not know him who sent me.

[CXLIII, 10.] “If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.” [Col. 0677D]

[Note: The same manuscripts, omitting the word *quidem* (“indeed”), have here a reading closer to the Greek text: *non credunt* (“they do not believe”), πιστεύουσιν; shortly afterward, consistently, they have “you do not see” rather than “you will not see.”]

[XLIV, 1.] “Whoever hates me hates my Father also.

[CXLV, 10.] “If I had not done among them works that no one else has done, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father. But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’

“But when the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father—he will bear witness concerning me. And you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.”

[Chapter XVI.] “I have spoken these things to you so that you may not be scandalized. They will expel you from the synagogues. [Col. 0678A]

[CXLVI, 1.] “But the hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he is offering service to God. And they will do these things to you because they have not known the Father or me. But I have spoken these things to you so that, when their hour comes, you may remember that I told you.

[CLXVII, 10.] “I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’ But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.

“But I tell you the truth: it is expedient for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment: concerning sin, indeed, because they did not believe in me; concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see me; concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has already been judged. [Col. 0678B]

“Still I have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when that Spirit of truth comes, he will teach you all truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the things that are to come. He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.

[CXLVIII, 3.] “Everything that the Father has is mine.

[CXLIX, 10.] “Therefore I said that he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.

“A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me, because I am going to the Father.”

Then some of his disciples said to one another: “What is this that he says to us: ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me,’ and, ‘Because I am going to the Father’?” [Col. 0678C]

So they said: “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he is saying.”

Jesus knew that they wanted to question him, and he said to them: “Are you asking one another about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me’? Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

“A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her hour has come. But when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers her distress because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world. So you too now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you. [Col. 0678D]

“And on that day you will ask me nothing.

[CL, 4.] “Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything in my name, he will give it to you. Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.

[CLI, 10.] “I have spoken these things to you in figures. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will announce the Father to you openly. [Col. 0679A] [Manuscripts omit *In* (“On”).] On that day you will ask in my name. And I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you, for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me [manuscript: “you love me”] and believed that I came forth from God.

“I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again I am leaving the world and going to the Father.”

His disciples said to him: “Behold, now you are speaking openly and saying no figure. Now we know that you know everything, and you have no need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came forth from God.”

[CLII, 4.] Jesus answered them: “Do you believe now? Behold, the hour is coming—and has already come—when you will be scattered, each to his own, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

[CLIII, 10.] “I have spoken these things to you so that you may have peace in me. In the world you will have distress; but take courage: I have conquered the world.”

[Chapter XVII.] Jesus spoke these things; and, lifting his eyes to heaven, he said: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you, just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he might give eternal life to all whom you have given him. [Col. 0679B]

“And this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent. I glorified you on earth; I completed the work that you gave me to do. And now, Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory that I had with you before the world existed.

“I have manifested your name to the human beings whom you gave me from the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word. Now they know that everything that you have given me is from you, because I gave them the words that you gave me; and they received them and truly knew that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me.

“I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you gave me, because they are yours. And everything that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I have been glorified in them. [Col. 0679C]

“And now I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, whom you gave me, so that they may be one, as we are.

“When I was with them, I kept them in your name. I guarded those whom you gave me, and none of them perished except the son of perdition, so that Scripture might be fulfilled.

“But now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I gave them your word, and the world hated them because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

“I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil. They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world. [Col. 0679D]

“Sanctify them in the truth. Your word is truth. Just as you sent me into the world, I also sent them into the world. And for their sake I sanctify myself, so that they too may be sanctified in truth.

“I do not pray for these alone [manuscripts: *his* for *eis*], but also for those who will believe in me through their word, so that all may be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so that they too may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.

“And I have given them the glory that you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one. I in them, and you in me, so that they may be perfected into one; and so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me. [Col. 0680A]

“Father, I desire that those whom you gave me may also be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me, because you loved me before the foundation of the world.

[CLIV, 3.] “Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you;

[CLV, 10.] “and these have known that you sent me. And I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”

[Chapter XVIII. CLVI, 1.] When Jesus had said these things, he went out with his disciples across the torrent of Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he entered, he and his disciples. [Col. 0680B]

[CLVII, 10.] Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with his disciples.

[CLVIII, 1.] Therefore Judas, having received a cohort, and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.

[CLIX, 10.] Jesus, therefore, knowing everything that was about to happen to him, went forward and said to them: “Whom are you seeking?”

They answered him: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

Jesus said to them: “I am he.” Judas, who betrayed him, was also standing with them. When he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground.

Then he asked them again: “Whom are you seeking?”

They said: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

Jesus answered: “I told you that I am he. Therefore, if you are seeking me, let these men go,” so that the word might be fulfilled which he had spoken: “Of those whom you gave me, I have not lost any.”

[CLX, 1.] Simon Peter, therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the chief priest, cutting off his right ear. [Col. 0680C] The servant’s name was Malchus.

[CLXI, 10.] Jesus therefore said to Peter: “Put your sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?”

[Note: Our manuscripts do not have the pronoun “your,” which some Greek codices also omit.]

[CLXII, 1.] Then the cohort, the tribune, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him.

[CLXIII, 10.] And they led him first to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year. Caiaphas was the one who had given the Jews the counsel: “It is expedient that one man die for the people.”

[CLXIV, 4.] Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus.
