[CLXV, 10.] That disciple was known to the high priest, and he entered with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard.

[CLXVI, 1.] But Peter was standing outside at the door.

[CLXVII, 1.] Therefore the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in. [Col. 0680D]

[CLXVIII, 1.] The maidservant who was the doorkeeper said to Peter: “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?”

He said: “I am not.”

[CLXIX, 10.] Now the servants and officers were standing beside a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter too was with them, standing and warming himself.

The high priest therefore questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.

[CLXX, 1.] Jesus answered him: “I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather; I have said nothing in secret.

[CLXXI, 10.] “Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Behold, they know what I said.” [Col. 0681A]

[CLXXII, 1.] When he had said this, one of the officers standing nearby struck Jesus on the face, saying: “Is that how you answer the high priest?”

[CLXXIII, 10.] Jesus answered him: “If I have spoken wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if I have spoken rightly, why do you strike me?”

[CLXXIV, 1.] And Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.

[CLXXV, 1.] Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. Therefore they said to him: “Are you also one of his disciples?”

He denied it and said: “I am not.”

One of the servants of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said to him: “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”

[Note: Our manuscripts omit the pronoun “to him,” which is likewise not represented in the Greek text.]

Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately the cock crowed.

[CLXXVI, 1.] Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium. It was morning. [Col. 0681B]

[CLXXVII, 10.] They themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled, but so that they might eat the Passover. Therefore Pilate went outside to them and said: “What accusation do you bring against this man?”

They answered and said to him: “If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you.”

Pilate therefore said to them: “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.”

The Jews therefore said to him: “It is not lawful for us to kill anyone,” so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he had spoken, signifying by what death he was going to die.

[CLXXVIII, 1.] Pilate therefore entered the praetorium again, called Jesus, and said to him: “Are you the king of the Jews?”

Jesus answered: “Do you say this from yourself, or have others told you about me?”

[CLXXIX, 10.] Pilate answered: “Am I a Jew? Your nation and the chief priests have handed you over to me. What have you done?”

Jesus answered: “My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my officers would certainly fight so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.” [Col. 0681C]

[CLXXX, 4.] Pilate therefore said to him: “So you are a king?”

Jesus answered: “You say that I am a king.”

[CLXXXI, 10.] “For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.”

Pilate said to him: “What is truth?”

[Note: Thus all exemplars assign this chapter of John, CLXXX, to the fourth canon and join it with chapter CCCXXI of Matthew, chapter CCXXI of Mark, and chapter CXCII of the same John, with which, however, it has almost nothing in common. It ought rather to be assigned to the first canon and joined with chapter CCCXX of Matthew, chapter CC of Mark, chapter CCCII of Luke, and likewise chapter CLXXVIII of the same John, with which it agrees in every respect. But against the testimony of all the codices we permit ourselves nothing. MART.]

[CLXXXII, 9.] And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them: “I find no case against him.”

[CLXXXIII, 4.] “But you have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at the Passover. Do you therefore want me to release the king of the Jews to you?”

[CLXXXIV, 1.] Then they all cried out again, saying: “Not this man, but Barabbas.” Now Barabbas was a bandit.

[Chapter XIX. CLXXXV, 4.] Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him. And the soldiers, weaving a crown from thorns, placed it on his head and clothed him in a purple garment. They came to him and said: “Hail, king of the Jews!” And they struck him on the face. [Col. 0682A]

[CLXXXVI, 9.] Pilate therefore went outside again and said to them: “Behold, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no case against him.”

([CLXXXVII, 4.] Then Jesus went out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.)

And he said to them: “Behold, the man!”

[CLXXXVIII, 1.] When the chief priests and officers saw him, they cried out, saying: “Crucify him! Crucify him!”

[Note: Like most Greek exemplars, our manuscripts also omit the pronoun “him.”]

[CLXXXIX, 10.] Pilate said to them: “Take him yourselves and crucify him;

[CXC, 9.] “for I find no case against him.”

[CXCI, 10.] The Jews answered him: “We have a law, and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”

[CXCII, 4.] When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid. And he entered the praetorium again and said to Jesus: “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. [Col. 0682B]

[CXCIII, 10.] Pilate therefore said to him: “Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you, and authority to release you?”

Jesus answered: “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”

From that point Pilate sought to release him. But the Jews cried out, saying: “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”

When Pilate heard these statements, he brought Jesus outside and sat on the tribunal, at the place called the Pavement—*Lithostrotos* [manuscript: *Lithostrotus*]—but in Hebrew, *Gabbatha*. It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And he said to the Jews: “Behold, your king!” [Col. 0682C]

[CXCIV, 1.] But they cried out: “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!”

[CXCV, 10.] Pilate said to them: “Shall I crucify your king?”

The chief priests answered: “We have no king except Caesar.”

[CXCVI, 1.] Then he handed him over to them to be crucified.

[CXCVII, 1.] They therefore took Jesus and led him away. And carrying his own cross, he went out to the place called the Place of the Skull, but in Hebrew, *Golgotha*, where they crucified him,

[CXCVIII, 1.] and with him two others, one on either side, with Jesus in the middle.

[CXCIX, 1.] Pilate also wrote a title and placed it on the cross. It was written: “Jesus the Nazarene, King of the Jews.” [Col. 0682D]

[CC, 10.] Therefore many of the Jews read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. And it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.

The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate: “Do not write, ‘King of the Jews,’ but that he himself said, ‘I am King of the Jews.’”

Pilate answered: “What I have written, I have written.”

[CCI, 1.] Therefore, when the soldiers had crucified him, they took his garments—and made four portions, a portion for each soldier—and also the tunic. The tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout. [Col. 0683A]

They therefore said to one another: “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be,” so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says: “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.”

And the soldiers indeed did these things.

[CCII, 10.] Standing beside the cross of Jesus were his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple standing whom he loved, he said to his mother: “Woman, behold, your son.”

Then he said to the disciple: “Behold, your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his own household.

[CCIII, 4.] After this, knowing that everything had been accomplished, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, Jesus said: “I thirst.”

A vessel full of vinegar was standing there. They, having placed hyssop around a sponge full of vinegar, held it to his mouth. [Col. 0683B]

[CCIV, 1.] When Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: “It is finished.” And bowing his head, he gave up the spirit.

[CCV, 10.] Since it was the day of Preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath—for that Sabbath was a great day—the Jews asked Pilate that their legs be broken and that they be taken away.

Therefore the soldiers came: they broke the legs of the first man and of the other who had been crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs. Instead, one of the soldiers opened his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

And the one who saw it has borne witness, and his testimony is true. And he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you too may believe. For these things happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: “You shall not break a bone of him.” [Col. 0683C]

And again another Scripture says: “They will look upon him whom they pierced.”

[CCVI, 1.] After this, Joseph of Arimathea, because he was a disciple of Jesus, though secretly for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate to take away the body of Jesus. And Pilate permitted it. Therefore he came and took the body of Jesus.

[CCVII, 10.] Nicodemus also came—the man who had first come to Jesus at night—bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.

[CCVIII, 1.] Therefore they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with spices, as is the Jews’ custom for burial.

Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been placed. There, because it was the Jews’ day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus.

[Chapter XX. CCIX, 1.] On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came early to the tomb, while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been removed from the tomb. [Col. 0683D]

[CCX, 10.] Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them: “They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have placed him.”

Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out and came to the tomb. The two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead more quickly than Peter and came first to the tomb. And when he had bent down, he saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not enter.

Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there, and the cloth that had been over his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but wrapped separately in one place. [Col. 0684A]

Then the other disciple also entered—the one who had come first to the tomb—and he saw and believed. For they did not yet know the Scripture, that he had to rise from the dead.

Then the disciples went away again to their own homes.

[CCXI, 1.] But Mary was standing outside at the tomb, weeping. As she wept, she bent down and looked into the tomb. And she saw two angels in white, sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been placed.

[CCXII, 10.] They said to her: “Woman, why are you weeping?”

She said to them: “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have placed him.” [Col. 0684B]

When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, but she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her: “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?”

Thinking that he was the gardener, she said to him: “Lord, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have placed him, and I will take him.”

Jesus said to her: “Mary.”

She turned and said to him: “Rabboni”—which means “Teacher.”

Jesus said to her: “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and say to them: ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.’”

Mary Magdalene came announcing to the disciples: “I have seen the Lord,” and that he had said these things to her.

[CCXIII, 9.] When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were closed where the disciples were gathered because of fear of the Jews, [Col. 0684C] Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them: “Peace be with you.”

And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side.

[CCXIV, 10.] Therefore the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.

Then he said to them again: “Peace be with you. Just as the Father sent me, I also send you.”

When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them: “Receive the Holy Spirit.

[CCXV, 7.] “Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven them; and whose you retain, they are retained.”

[CCXVI, 10.] But Thomas, one of the twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. Therefore the other disciples said to him: “We have seen the Lord.”

But he said to them: “Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

[Note: Perhaps more correctly according to the Greek, τὸν τύπον (“the mark” or “figure”), our manuscripts also read *figuram* (“the mark/figure”) rather than *fixuram* (“the piercing”).]

[CCXVII, 9.] And after eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came when the doors were closed, stood in the midst, and said: “Peace be with you.” [Col. 0684D]

Then he said to Thomas: “Put your finger here and see my hands; bring your hand and put it into my side. And do not be unbelieving, but believing.”

[CCXVIII, 10.] Thomas answered and said to him: “My Lord and my God!”

Jesus said to him: “Because you have seen me, Thomas, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”

Jesus also performed many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book. But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, believing, you may have life in his name. [Col. 0685A]

## Chapter XXI

**[CCXIX, 9.]** After this Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias.

[Note: [Col. 0685C] Two of our manuscripts do not add “to the disciples”; certain Greek copies also omit the name Jesus.]

He revealed himself in this way. Simon Peter, Thomas, who is called Didymus, Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together. Simon Peter said to them: “I am going fishing.” They said to him: “We are coming with you.” They went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing.

When morning came, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus. Jesus therefore said to them: “Children, do you have anything to eat?” They answered him: “No.” He said to them: “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find something.” So they cast it, and now they were unable to haul it in because of the quantity of fish.

**[CCXX, 10.]** Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter: “It is the Lord.”

[Note: [Col. 0685C] The name “Peter,” which is nevertheless found in almost all Greek books, is absent from one or two of our manuscripts.] When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girded his tunic around himself—for he was naked—and threw himself into the sea. The other disciples came in the boat—for they were not far from land, but about two hundred cubits away—dragging the net of fish.

**[CCXXI, 9.]** When they had come down onto the land, they saw burning coals laid out, with a fish placed upon them, and bread. Jesus said to them: “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.”

**[CCXXII, 9.]** Simon Peter went up and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three. And although there were so many, the net was not torn.

**[CCXXIII, 9.]** Jesus said to them: “Come, eat.”

**[CCXXIV, 10.]** None of those reclining at table dared to ask him, “Who are you?” because they knew that it was the Lord.

**[CCXXV, 9.]** Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and likewise the fish.

**[CCXXVI, 10.]** This was now the third time that Jesus had revealed himself to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.

When they had eaten, Jesus said to Simon Peter: “Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.”

**[CCXXVII, 9.]** He said to him: “Feed my lambs.”

**[CCXXVIII, 10.]** He said to him again: “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.”

**[CCXXIX, 9.]** He said to him: “Feed my lambs.”

**[CCXXX, 10.]** He said to him a third time: “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was distressed because he had said to him a third time, “Do you love me?” and he said to him: “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.”

[Note: [Col. 0685C] At the first occurrence also, two of our manuscripts prefer *you know all things* (*tu omnia scis*) to our reading *you know* (*nosti*).]

**[CCXXXI, 9.]** He said to him: “Feed my sheep.”

**[CCXXXII, 10.]** “Amen, amen, I say to you: When you were younger, you girded yourself and walked wherever you wished; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish to go.” He said this to signify by what death he would glorify God. And when he had said this, he said to him: “Follow me.”

Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following—the one who also reclined at supper upon his breast and said: “Lord, who is the one who will betray you?” When Peter had seen him, he said to Jesus: “Lord, but what about this man?” Jesus said to him:

[Note: [Col. 0685C] There is an ancient scribal error in which, instead of the conditional particle *if* (*si*), they wrote *thus* (*sic*), contrary to the Greek text, where ἐὰν is read; the Syriac and Arabic likewise follow it. In our manuscript no. 19 the passage was corrected in both places, where *sic* had been written; but another hand restored what had been corrected. Another manuscript, no. 15, having first read “Thus I want him to remain, etc.,” nevertheless later added: “But if I want him to remain thus until I come, what is that to you?” The others consistently read *sic*. MART. —The Codex Reginae, no. 14, also said formerly to have belonged to Saint Wenceslaus, a manuscript indeed of good antiquity and reputation, reads *if* (*si*) in both places, in accordance with the Greek text ἐὰν, instead of *thus* (*sic*). Since it is not relevant to our purpose to reopen the customary controversy on this matter, we recommend that you consult the sacred critics, as well as our Jerome, Book I *Against Jovinianus*, and what we have noted concerning that passage.]

“Thus I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

Therefore this saying spread among the brothers: that that disciple does not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him, “He does not die,” but: “Thus I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”

This is the disciple who bears witness to these things and who wrote them; and we know that his testimony is true. There are also many other things that Jesus did; if they were written down one by one, I do not think that the world itself could contain the books that would have to be written.

**The Gospel according to John ends here.**

# Apostolic Order

Containing: the Acts of the Apostles, the Epistles of Paul, the Catholic Epistles, and the Apocalypse.

[Col. 0687]

# The Book of the Acts of the Apostles Begins

Edited according to the Vatican exemplar with the utmost fidelity.

## Chapter I

I composed the first account, O Theophilus, concerning all the things that Jesus began to do and to teach, until the day on which, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up. To them also he presented himself alive after his passion by many proofs, appearing to them for forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.

And while eating with them, he ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to await the promise of the Father, “which,” he said, “you have heard from my mouth; for John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”

Therefore, when they had assembled, they asked him, saying: “Lord, will you restore the kingdom to Israel at this time?” But he said to them: “It is not for you to know the times or moments that the Father has placed in his own authority. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the farthest ends of the earth.”

And when he had said these things, while they were watching, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him from their eyes. And as they were gazing into heaven while he went away, behold, two men stood beside them in white clothing. They also said: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven.”

Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey away. And when they had entered the upper room, they went up to where Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James were staying.

All these persevered unanimously in prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.

In those days Peter, rising in the midst of the brothers—there was a crowd of about one hundred and twenty persons altogether—said: “Men, brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became the leader of those who seized Jesus. He was numbered among us and received a share in this ministry.

“Now this man acquired a field from the reward of his wickedness, and, hanging headlong, burst open in the middle, and all his innards spilled out. This became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their language *Haceldama*, that is, ‘Field of Blood.’

“For it is written in the Book of Psalms:

‘Let their dwelling become desolate,
and let there be no one who inhabits it’;

and:

‘Let another take his office.’

“Therefore, from these men who have accompanied us throughout the whole time in which the Lord Jesus entered and went out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which he was taken up from us, one of these must become with us a witness to his resurrection.”

And they put forward two: Joseph, who was called Barsabbas, surnamed Justus, and Matthias. And praying, they said: “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two you have chosen to receive the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas departed to go to his own place.” And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

## Chapter II

When the days of Pentecost were completed, they were all together in the same place. And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like that of a violent wind approaching, and it filled the entire house where they were sitting.

And divided tongues appeared to them, as if of fire, and one rested upon each of them. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in various languages, as the Holy Spirit gave them utterance.

Now there were Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven. When this sound occurred, the multitude gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.

They were all amazed and wondered, saying: “Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans? And how is it that we each hear our own language in which we were born? Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and inhabitants of Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and Roman visitors, Jews also and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own languages the great works of God.”

They were all amazed and wondered, saying to one another: “What can this mean?” But others, mocking, said: “They are full of new wine.”

But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and addressed them: “Men of Judea and all you who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen to my words. For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is the third hour of the day. Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:

‘And it shall be in the last days, says the Lord,
that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh;
and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy,
and your young men shall see visions,
and your elders shall dream dreams.

“‘Indeed, upon my male servants and my female servants, in those days, I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy. And I will give wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes. And it shall be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.’

“Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarean, a man accredited by God among you through mighty deeds, wonders, and signs, which God performed through him in your midst, as you yourselves know—this man, handed over by the predetermined plan and foreknowledge of God, you killed by the hands of lawless men, fastening him to the cross. God raised him up, having loosed the pains of Hades, since it was impossible for him to be held by it.

“For David says concerning him:

‘I foresaw the Lord always before me,
because he is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.
Therefore my heart rejoiced,
and my tongue exulted;
moreover, my flesh also shall rest in hope,
because you will not abandon my soul in Hades,
nor will you allow your Holy One to see corruption.
You have made known to me the paths of life;
you will fill me with joy in your presence.’

“Men, brothers, let me speak boldly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day. Therefore, since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that he would set one of the fruit of his loins upon his throne, foreseeing this, he spoke about the resurrection of Christ: that he was neither abandoned in Hades nor did his flesh see corruption.

“God raised up this Jesus, and of this we are all witnesses. Therefore, exalted at the right hand of God and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he poured out this Spirit, whom you see and hear.

“For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself says:

‘The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.’

“Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with absolute certainty that God has made both Lord and Christ this Jesus whom you crucified.”

When they heard this, they were pierced in heart and said to Peter and the other apostles: “What shall we do, men, brothers?”

Peter said to them: “Repent,” he said, “and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you and for your children, and for all who are far away, all whom the Lord our God will call.”

With many other words he also bore witness and exhorted them, saying: “Save yourselves from this corrupt generation.” Therefore those who received his word were baptized, and about three thousand persons were added on that day.

They persevered in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers. Fear came upon every person, and many wonders and signs were performed through the apostles in Jerusalem, and great fear was upon them all.

All who believed were together and held everything in common. They sold their possessions and goods and distributed them to everyone according to each person’s need. Every day they continued unanimously in the temple, and breaking bread in their homes, they received food with gladness and simplicity of heart, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added daily to their number those who were being saved.

## Chapter III

Peter and John were going up to the temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer. And a certain man who had been lame from his mother’s womb was being carried; they placed him daily at the temple gate called Beautiful, so that he might ask alms from those entering the temple.

When he saw Peter and John beginning to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms. But Peter, looking at him with John, said: “Look at us.” He looked intently at them, hoping to receive something from them. But Peter said: “I have neither silver nor gold; but what I have, this I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarean, rise and walk.”

And taking him by his right hand, he lifted him up, and immediately his legs and feet were strengthened. Leaping up, he stood and walked; and he entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.

All the people saw him walking and praising God. They recognized him as the one who had sat at the Beautiful Gate of the temple asking for alms, and they were filled with astonishment and amazement at what had happened to him.

As he held on to Peter and John, all the people ran to them at the portico called Solomon’s, in astonishment. When Peter saw this, he addressed the people:

“Men of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Or why do you look at us as though by our own power or authority we had made this man walk? The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his Son Jesus, whom you indeed handed over and denied before Pilate’s face, when he had decided to release him.

“But you denied the Holy and Just One and asked that a murderer be granted to you; but you killed the author of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.

“By faith in his name, his name strengthened this man whom you see and know; and the faith that comes through him gave him this complete health in the presence of you all.

“And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your rulers. But God fulfilled in this way what he had foretold through the mouth of all the prophets: that his Christ would suffer.

“Therefore repent and turn back, so that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshment may come from the presence of the Lord, and he may send the one who was proclaimed to you, Jesus Christ, whom heaven must indeed receive until the times of the restoration of all things that God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old.

“Moses indeed said:

‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet from among your brothers, like me; you shall listen to him according to everything he says to you.’

“And it shall be that every person who does not listen to that Prophet shall be exterminated from the people.

“And all the prophets, from Samuel onward, who spoke, also announced these days. You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God established with our fathers, saying to Abraham:

‘And in your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed.’

“God, having raised up his Son, sent him to you first, blessing you so that each person might turn away from his wickedness.”

## Chapter IV

As they were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them, distressed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming the resurrection from the dead in Jesus. They laid hands on them and placed them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.

Many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men became about five thousand.

On the following day their rulers, elders, and scribes assembled in Jerusalem, together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and all who were of the high-priestly family. Having placed them in the midst, they asked: “By what power or in what name have you done this?”

Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: “Rulers of the people and elders, hear this. If we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a sick man, by what means this man has been healed, let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarean, whom you crucified and whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you healthy.

“He is the stone rejected by you builders, which has become the cornerstone. And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among human beings by which we must be saved.”

When they saw Peter’s and John’s boldness and discovered that they were uneducated and ordinary men, they were amazed and recognized them as having been with Jesus. Seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they could say nothing in reply.

They ordered them to withdraw outside the council and conferred with one another, saying: “What shall we do with these men? For a notable sign has certainly been performed through them, known to all who dwell in Jerusalem; it is manifest, and we cannot deny it. But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them, so that they speak no longer in this name to anyone.”

Calling them, they ordered them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. But Peter and John answered them: “Judge for yourselves whether it is right in the sight of God to obey you rather than God. For we cannot fail to speak about what we have seen and heard.”

But they, after threatening them, released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since everyone was glorifying what had happened in the event that had taken place. For the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old.

After being released, they went to their own people and reported everything that the chief priests and elders had said to them. When they heard this, they raised their voice unanimously to God and said:

“Lord, you are the one who made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them, who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David, your servant, said:

‘Why did the nations rage,
and the peoples devise vain things?
The kings of the earth stood by,
and the rulers gathered together
against the Lord and against his Christ?’

“For truly they gathered together in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed: Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, to do whatever your hand and your counsel had decreed would happen.

“And now, Lord, look upon their threats and grant your servants to speak your word with complete boldness, while you stretch out your hand for healings, and signs and wonders are performed through the name of your holy Son Jesus.”

And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered was shaken. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.

The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul. No one claimed that any of the things he possessed was his own, but they held everything in common. With great power the apostles gave testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus Christ, and great grace was upon them all.

For no one among them was in need. All who owned fields or houses sold them, brought the proceeds of what they had sold, and laid them at the apostles’ feet. It was distributed to each person according to his need.

Joseph, who was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles—which is translated “Son of Consolation”—a Levite and a Cypriot by birth, having a field, sold it, brought the proceeds, and laid them at the apostles’ feet.

## Chapter V

A certain man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a field and, with his wife’s knowledge, kept back part of the price of the field; bringing a portion, he laid it at the apostles’ feet.

But Peter said: “Ananias, why has Satan tempted your heart, so that you should lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the field? While it remained, did it not remain yours, and when sold, was it not in your control? Why did you put this matter in your heart? You have not lied to human beings but to God.”

When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and expired. And great fear came upon all who heard. The young men rose, removed him, carried him out, and buried him.

After an interval of about three hours, his wife entered, unaware of what had happened. Peter said to her: “Tell me, woman, did you sell the field for this amount?” She said: “Yes, for that amount.”

Peter said to her: “Why did you agree together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”

Immediately she fell at his feet and expired. When the young men entered, they found her dead; they carried her out and buried her beside her husband. And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.

Through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were performed among the people. They were all together in Solomon’s portico. None of the others dared to join themselves to them, but the people magnified them.

The multitude of believers in the Lord increased still more, both men and women, so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and placed them on beds and pallets, so that, when Peter came, at least his shadow might overshadow some of them and they might be delivered from their illnesses.

A multitude from the neighboring cities of Jerusalem also came together, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits; and they were all healed.

But the high priest rose, and all who were with him—that is, the sect of the Sadducees—were filled with zeal. They laid hands on the apostles and placed them in the public prison.

But an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors during the night, led them out, and said: “Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.”

When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and were teaching. The high priest and those who were with him arrived, convened the council and all the elders of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

When the officers arrived and, having opened the prison, did not find them, they returned and reported: “We found the prison securely locked, with the guards standing before the doors; but when we opened it, we found no one inside.”

When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these reports, they were perplexed about what this might become. Then someone arrived and announced to them: “Behold, the men whom you placed in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”

Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, without force; for they feared the people, lest they be stoned. After bringing them, they set them before the council. The high priest questioned them, saying:

“By giving you strict orders, we ordered you not to teach in this name; and behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.”

But Peter and the apostles answered: “We must obey God rather than human beings. The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree. God exalted him by his right hand as Leader and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. And we are witnesses of these words, as is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”

When they heard this, they were enraged and planned to kill them. But a Pharisee named Gamaliel rose in the council, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, and ordered that the men be taken outside for a short time.

He said to them: “Men of Israel, take care concerning these men and consider what you are about to do. For before these days Theudas arose, claiming to be someone, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was killed, and all who believed him were scattered and reduced to nothing.

“After him Judas the Galilean arose in the days of the enrollment and drew the people after him. He too perished, and all who consented to him were dispersed.

“And now I say to you: Withdraw from these men and leave them alone. For if this plan or work is from human beings, it will be destroyed; but if it is from God, you will not be able to destroy it, lest you perhaps be found even to be opposing God.”

They agreed with him. And having summoned the apostles, they flogged them, ordered them not to speak at all in the name of Jesus, and released them.

They went away from the presence of the council rejoicing, because they had been deemed worthy to suffer dishonor for the name of Jesus. Every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming Christ Jesus.

## Chapter VI

In those days, as the number of the disciples increased, there arose a complaint by the Greeks against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.

The Twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said: “It is not right for us to abandon the word of God and serve tables. Therefore, brothers, select from among yourselves seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this task. But we will devote ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

The saying pleased the entire multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicholas, a convert from Antioch. They set them before the apostles, and after praying, they laid hands on them.

The word of the Lord grew, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly. A large crowd of priests also obeyed the faith.

Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people. Some from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, and some of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen. They could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.

Then they suborned men who claimed that they had heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and against God. They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; and rushing upon him, they seized him and brought him before the council.

They set up false witnesses who said: “This man does not cease speaking words against this holy place and the law. For we have heard him say that this Jesus the Nazarean will destroy this place and change the traditions that Moses handed down to us.”

And all who were sitting in the council, looking at him, saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

## Chapter VII

The high priest said, “Are these things so?” He replied:

“Men, brothers, and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran, and said to him: ‘Go out from your land and from your kindred, and come into the land that I will show you.’ Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. From there, after his father had died, he brought him into this land in which you now dwell. He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot’s breadth, but promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his offspring after him, although he had no child.

“God spoke to him as follows: ‘His offspring will be resident aliens in a foreign land, and they will enslave and mistreat them for four hundred years. And the nation that they serve I myself will judge,’ said the Lord; ‘and after this they will come out and serve me in this place.’ And he gave him the covenant of circumcision. Thus he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day; and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

“Then the patriarchs, moved by jealousy, sold Joseph into Egypt; but God was with him. He rescued him from all his afflictions and granted him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who appointed him governor over Egypt and over all his household.

“Now a famine came upon all Egypt and Canaan, and great distress, and our fathers could find no food. When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers there first. On the second occasion Joseph was recognized by his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh. Then Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his kindred, seventy-five persons. And Jacob went down into Egypt, and he himself died, as did our fathers. They were transferred to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem.

“But as the time of the promise that God had made to Abraham was approaching, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph. He took advantage of our race and oppressed our fathers, so that they exposed their infants, in order that they might not be preserved alive.

“At that time Moses was born, and he was pleasing to God. He was nourished for three months in his father’s house. When he had been exposed, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up and raised him as her own son. Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and in his deeds.

“When he had reached the age of forty, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel. When he saw one of them being wronged, he defended him and avenged the injured man by striking down the Egyptian. He supposed that his brothers would understand that God was granting them deliverance through his hand, but they did not understand.

“On the following day he appeared to them while they were quarreling and was reconciling them in peace, saying: ‘Men, you are brothers; why do you harm one another?’ But the man who was wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying: ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me, just as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’

“At this saying Moses fled and became a resident alien in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons. When forty years had been completed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in the flame of a burning bush. When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to examine it, the voice of the Lord came to him, saying: ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’

“Moses, trembling, did not dare to look. But the Lord said to him: ‘Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground. I have indeed seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to deliver them. And now, come: I will send you to Egypt.’

“This Moses, whom they had rejected, saying, ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge?’, this man God sent as ruler and redeemer, with the hand of the angel who had appeared to him in the bush. He led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.

“This is the Moses who said to the children of Israel: ‘God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; you shall listen to him.’ This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; he received living words to give to us.

“Our fathers were unwilling to obey him, but rejected him and turned back in their hearts to Egypt, saying to Aaron: ‘Make gods for us to go before us. For this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’

“And they made a calf in those days and offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands. But God turned away and handed them over to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets:

“‘Did you offer me victims and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel? And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, images that you made in order to worship them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.’

“Our fathers had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, just as God ordained for them when he spoke to Moses, telling him to make it according to the pattern he had seen. Our fathers, in turn, brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations whom God drove out before our fathers, until the days of David. He found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling-place for the God of Jacob. But Solomon built him a house.

“Yet the Most High does not dwell in things made by hands, as the prophet says:

“‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What house will you build for me,’ says the Lord, ‘or what is the place of my rest? Did not my hand make all these things?’

“Stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Just One, of whom you have now been the betrayers and murderers—you who received the law through the disposition of angels and did not keep it.”

When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart and gnashed their teeth at him. But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. And he said: “Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”

But crying out with a loud voice, they covered their ears and rushed upon him together. They drove him outside the city and stoned him. The witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul. And they stoned Stephen as he called upon the Lord and said: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”

Then, falling on his knees, he cried out with a loud voice, saying: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. Saul, meanwhile, was consenting to his death.

## Chapter VIII

On that day a great persecution arose against the Church in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Devout men took care of Stephen and made great mourning over him.

But Saul was ravaging the Church. Entering house after house and dragging out men and women, he handed them over to custody.

Those, therefore, who had been scattered went from place to place, proclaiming the word of God. Philip went down to a city of Samaria and preached Christ to them. The crowds paid close attention with one accord to what Philip said, hearing and seeing the signs that he performed. For many of those who had unclean spirits had them come out, crying with a loud voice. Many paralytics and lame people were healed. And there was great joy in that city.

Now there was a certain man named Simon, who had previously practiced magic in the city and bewildered the people of Samaria, claiming that he was someone great. Everyone, from the least to the greatest, listened to him, saying: “This man is the power of God that is called Great.” They paid attention to him because for a long time he had bewildered them with his magic arts.

But when they had believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, men and women alike were baptized. Then Simon himself also believed; and after he had been baptized, he remained with Philip. And when he saw the signs and the great miracles that were being performed, he was astonished and amazed.

When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. When they arrived, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit, for he had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

When Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money, saying: “Give me this power also, so that whoever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”

But Peter said to him: “May your money perish with you, because you thought that the gift of God could be acquired with money. You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God. Therefore repent of this wickedness of yours and pray to God, if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.”

Simon answered and said: “Pray for me to the Lord, so that none of these things you have spoken may come upon me.”

After testifying and speaking the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, evangelizing many regions of the Samaritans.

Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: “Rise and go toward the south, to the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza; this is desert.” And he rose and went.

And behold, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, an official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasures, had come to Jerusalem to worship. He was returning, seated in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.

The Spirit said to Philip: “Approach and join yourself to this chariot.” Philip ran up and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah, and said: “Do you think you understand what you are reading?”

He replied: “And how could I, unless someone guides me?” And he asked Philip to come up and sit with him. The passage of Scripture that he was reading was this:

“Like a sheep he was led to slaughter; and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation judgment was taken away from him. Who will recount his generation? For his life will be taken from the earth.”

The eunuch answered Philip and said: “I ask you, of whom does the prophet say this—of himself or of someone else?”

Then Philip opened his mouth and, beginning from this Scripture, proclaimed Jesus to him.

As they went along the road, they came to some water. And the eunuch said: “Behold, here is water. What prevents me from being baptized?”

Philip said: “If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted.”

He answered: “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.”

And he ordered the chariot to stop. Both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him. When they had come up from the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch no longer saw him. He went on his way rejoicing.

But Philip was found at Azotus, and as he passed through, he proclaimed the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

## Chapter IX

Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, approached the high priest and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to this Way, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

As he was traveling, it happened that he was approaching Damascus. Suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him. Falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”

He said: “Who are you, Lord?”

And he replied: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goad.”

Trembling and astonished, he said: “Lord, what do you want me to do?”

And the Lord said to him: “Rise and enter the city, and there you will be told what you must do.”

The men who were traveling with him stood astonished. They heard the voice but saw no one. Saul rose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. Leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus.

For three days he was unable to see, and he neither ate nor drank.

Now there was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. In a vision the Lord said to him: “Ananias!”

He replied: “Here I am, Lord.”

And the Lord said to him: “Rise and go to the street called Straight, and seek in the house of Judas a man named Saul of Tarsus. For behold, he is praying.”

And he saw a man named Ananias entering and laying his hands on him so that he might regain his sight.

But Ananias answered: “Lord, I have heard from many about this man—how much harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem. And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call upon your name.”

But the Lord said to him: “Go, for this man is an instrument chosen for me, to carry my name before the nations and kings and the children of Israel. For I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.”

And Ananias went and entered the house. Laying his hands on him, he said: “Saul, brother, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, has sent me so that you may see and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he regained his sight. He rose and was baptized. After taking food, he regained his strength.

He stayed for several days with the disciples who were in Damascus. And immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that he is the Son of God.

All who heard him were astonished and said: “Is this not the man who was ravaging in Jerusalem those who called upon this name, and who had come here for the purpose of bringing them bound before the chief priests?”

But Saul grew ever stronger and confounded the Jews who lived in Damascus, asserting that this is the Christ.

When many days had passed, the Jews conspired together to kill him. Their plot became known to Saul. They were also guarding the gates day and night in order to kill him. But the disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

When he arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple. Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how, on the road, he had seen the Lord, that he had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had acted boldly in the name of Jesus.

He was with them, coming and going in Jerusalem and acting boldly in the name of the Lord. He also spoke and disputed with the Greeks; but they sought to kill him. When the brothers learned this, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the Church throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace. It was being built up, walking in the fear of the Lord, and was filled with the consolation of the Holy Spirit.

Now it happened that, as Peter was passing through all the regions, he came down to the saints who lived in Lydda. There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a pallet for eight years, for he was paralyzed.

Peter said to him: “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Rise and make your bed.” And immediately he rose.

All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

Now in Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas. She was full of good works and alms that she performed.

It happened in those days that she fell ill and died. After washing her, they placed her in an upper room. Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, asking: “Do not delay in coming to us.”

Peter rose and went with them. When he arrived, they led him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the tunics and garments that Dorcas used to make for them.

After putting everyone outside, Peter knelt and prayed. Then, turning toward the body, he said: “Tabitha, rise.”

She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up. He gave her his hand and raised her. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her alive.

This became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord. He remained for many days in Joppa, with a certain Simon, a tanner.

## Chapter X

Now there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called Italian, devout and fearing God with all his household, giving many alms to the people and always entreating God. He clearly saw in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God entering to him and saying: “Cornelius.”

He gazed at him and, seized with fear, said: “What is it, Lord?”

He said to him: “Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God. And now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter. He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea. He will tell you what you must do.”

When the angel who was speaking to him had departed, he called two of his household servants and a soldier who feared the Lord, from among those who attended him. After telling them everything, he sent them to Joppa.

On the following day, while they were traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up to the upper room to pray, about the sixth hour. As he became hungry, he wanted to taste something. While they were preparing food, a trance came over him. He saw heaven opened and a certain vessel descending, like a great linen cloth, being let down by its four corners from heaven to earth. In it were all kinds of four-footed animals, reptiles of the earth, and birds of the sky.

And a voice came to him: “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.”

But Peter said: “By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common or unclean.”

And the voice spoke to him a second time: “What God has cleansed, you must not call common.”

This happened three times, and immediately the vessel was taken back up into heaven.

While Peter was inwardly perplexed about what the vision he had seen might mean, behold, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having searched out Simon’s house, stood at the gate. They called out and asked whether Simon, who is called Peter, was lodging there.

While Peter was reflecting on the vision, the Spirit said to him: “Behold, three men are seeking you. Rise, go down, and go with them without hesitation, for I have sent them.”

Peter went down to the men and said: “Behold, I am the one you seek. For what reason have you come?”

They said: “The centurion Cornelius, a just man who fears God and has a good reputation among the entire Jewish nation, received a response from a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you.”

So he brought them in and received them as guests.

On the following day he rose and set out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him. On the next day he entered Caesarea.

Cornelius was waiting for them, having summoned his relatives and close friends. When Peter entered, Cornelius came to meet him and, falling at his feet, worshiped him. But Peter raised him up, saying: “Rise; I too am a human being.”

And speaking with him, he entered and found many gathered there. He said to them: “You know how abhorrent it is for a Jewish man to join or approach a foreigner. But God has shown me that I should call no person common or unclean. Therefore I came when summoned, without hesitation. I ask, then, for what reason did you summon me?”

Cornelius said: “Four days ago, up to this hour, I was praying at the ninth hour in my house. And behold, a man stood before me in a shining garment and said: ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered in the sight of God. Therefore send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He is lodging in the house of Simon the tanner beside the sea.’

“So I immediately sent for you, and you have done well to come. Now, therefore, we are all here in your presence, to hear everything that has been commanded you by the Lord.”

Then Peter opened his mouth and said:

“In truth I have discovered that God is not a respecter of persons, but in every nation whoever fears him and practices righteousness is acceptable to him. He sent the word to the children of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ—he is Lord of all.

“You know what happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism that John proclaimed: Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power; he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.

“And we are witnesses of all that he did in the region of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree. God raised him on the third day and granted that he be made manifest—not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by God: to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

“And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives remission of sins through his name.”

While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the word. The faithful from the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished, because the grace of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out upon the nations. For they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God.

Then Peter answered: “Can anyone forbid water, so that these people who have received the Holy Spirit as we have should not be baptized?”

And he ordered them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain with them for several days.

## Chapter XI

The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the nations also had received the word of God. When Peter went up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision disputed with him, saying: “Why did you enter to uncircumcised men and eat with them?”

Peter began to explain the matter to them in order, saying:

“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain vessel descending, like a great linen cloth, being let down by its four corners from heaven, and it came as far as me. Looking into it, I examined it and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the sky.

“I also heard a voice saying to me: ‘Rise, Peter; kill and eat.’

“But I said: ‘By no means, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

“The voice answered a second time from heaven: ‘What God has cleansed, you must not call common.’

“This happened three times, and everything was taken up again into heaven.

“And behold, immediately three men stood at the house in which I was, sent to me from Caesarea. The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s house.

“He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying to him: ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He will speak words to you by which you and your entire household will be saved.’

“When I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as upon us at the beginning. And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said: ‘John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’

“If, therefore, God gave them the same grace as he gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?”

When they heard these things, they became silent and glorified God, saying: “Then God has also granted repentance to the nations for life.”

Those who had been scattered because of the persecution that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews. But some of them—men from Cyprus and Cyrene—when they entered Antioch, spoke also to the Greeks, announcing the Lord Jesus.

And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of believers turned to the Lord.

The report about them reached the ears of the Church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch. When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to remain with steadfast purpose of heart in the Lord, because he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. And a great multitude was added to the Lord.

Then Barnabas departed for Tarsus to seek Saul. When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For an entire year they met there in the Church and taught a great crowd, so that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch. One of them, named Agabus, rose and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine was about to occur throughout the whole world; this took place under Claudius.

The disciples, according to each person’s means, determined individually to send assistance to the brothers living in Judea. They did this, sending it to the elders through the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

## Chapter XII

At that same time King Herod began to mistreat some members of the Church. He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword. When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter as well.

It was during the days of Unleavened Bread. After arresting him, he put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of soldiers for guard duty, intending to bring him before the people after Passover. So Peter was kept in prison, but prayer was being made for him without ceasing by the Church to God.

When Herod was about to bring him out, on that very night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while guards before the door were keeping watch over the prison.

And behold, an angel of the Lord stood near, and a light shone in the chamber. Striking Peter’s side, he woke him, saying: “Rise quickly.” And the chains fell from his hands.

The angel said to him: “Gird yourself and put on your sandals.” He did so. And he said to him: “Wrap your garment around you and follow me.”

Going out, he followed him, and he did not know that what was being done through the angel was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.

After passing the first and second guard posts, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened for them of its own accord. They went out and proceeded along one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

Peter, coming to himself, said: “Now I truly know that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting.”

After considering the matter, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered and praying.

When he knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhoda came to listen. When she recognized Peter’s voice, she did not open the door for joy, but ran inside and announced that Peter was standing before the door.

They said to her: “You are out of your mind.”

But she insisted that it was so. They replied: “It is his angel.”

Peter continued knocking. When they opened the door, they saw him and were astonished. He motioned to them with his hand to be silent and told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. Then he said: “Report these things to James and the brothers.” And going out, he departed to another place.

When day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers about what had happened to Peter. After Herod had searched for him and failed to find him, he conducted an inquiry into the guards and ordered them to be led away. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and remained there.

He was angry with the Tyrians and Sidonians. They came to him with one accord, and having persuaded Blastus, who was in charge of the king’s chamber, they sought peace, because their regions were supplied with food from his country.

On an appointed day, Herod, dressed in royal clothing, sat upon the tribunal and addressed them. The people shouted: “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”

Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he had not given glory to God. And, consumed by worms, he breathed his last.

But the word of the Lord grew and multiplied.

Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem after completing their ministry, taking with them John, who was called Mark.

## Chapter XIII

Now there were in the church at Antioch prophets and teachers, among whom were Barnabas, and Simon who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, [Col. 0704D] and Manaen, the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul. While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them: “Set apart for me Saul and Barnabas for the work to which I have appointed them.” Then, after fasting and praying and laying their hands upon them, they sent them away.

They, indeed, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia; and from there they sailed to Cyprus. When they had arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John as their assistant. Having traversed the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain Jewish man, a magician and false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus, who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. [Col. 0705A] He summoned Barnabas and Saul and desired to hear the word of God.

But Elymas the magician—for that is how his name is interpreted—resisted them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith. Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit and looking intently at him, said: “O man full of every deceit and every fraud, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord? And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.” And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking someone to give him his hand.

Then, when the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, marveling at the teaching of the Lord. After Paul and those who were with him had sailed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John, withdrawing from them, returned to Jerusalem.

[Col. 0705B] They, however, passing through Perga, came to Antioch in Pisidia; and entering the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down. After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying: “Men and brothers, if there is among you a word of exhortation for the people, speak.”

Then Paul rose, and indicating silence with his hand, said: “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen. The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they were sojourners in the land of Egypt; and with an uplifted arm he led them out of it. For about forty years he endured their conduct in the wilderness. And having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he distributed their land to them by lot, after about four hundred and fifty years. After this he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet. [Col. 0705C] And thereafter they asked for a king; and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years. Having removed him, he raised up David as king for them; and bearing witness to him, he said: ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who will do all my will.’

“From this man’s seed, according to his promise, God brought forth Jesus as Savior for Israel, with John proclaiming beforehand, before his coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel. As John was completing his course, he said: ‘Who do you suppose me to be? I am not he; but behold, one is coming after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

“Men and brothers, sons of the race of Abraham, and those among you who fear God: to you the word of this salvation has been sent. For those who dwelt in Jerusalem, and their rulers, not recognizing him or the voices of the prophets, which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by judging him. [Col. 0705D] Though they found no cause of death in him, they asked Pilate to have him killed. And when they had accomplished everything that had been written about him, taking him down from the tree, they laid him in a tomb. But God raised him from the dead on the third day. He was seen for many days by those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem; they are now his witnesses to the people.

“And we announce to you the promise made to our fathers, [Col. 0706A] that God has fulfilled this for our children by raising Jesus, as it is also written in the second Psalm: ‘You are my Son; today I have begotten you.’ And that he raised him from the dead, never again to return to corruption, he said in this way: ‘I will give you the holy and faithful things of David.’ Therefore he says also elsewhere: ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see corruption.’ For David, after serving God’s purpose in his own generation, fell asleep and was laid with his fathers, and he saw corruption. Therefore let it be known to you, men and brothers, that through him forgiveness of sins is announced to you, and that from all things from which you could not be justified by the Law of Moses, everyone who believes is justified in him.

“Therefore beware lest what is spoken in the Prophets come upon you: ‘Behold, you despisers, and wonder, and perish; for I am doing a work in your days, a work that you will not believe, if someone should tell it to you.’”

As they were going out, [Col. 0706B] they begged that these words might be spoken to them on the following Sabbath. When the synagogue had been dismissed, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking with them, persuaded them to remain in the grace of God.

On the following Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of God. But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted what was spoken by Paul, blaspheming. Then Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly: “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles. For thus the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have appointed you as a light to the Gentiles, that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth.’”

When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word [Col. 0706C] of the Lord; and all who had been appointed to eternal life believed. The word of the Lord was spread throughout the whole region.

But the Jews incited devout and honorable women and the leading men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas; and they drove them out of their territory. But they shook the dust from their feet against them and came to Iconium. And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

## Chapter XIV

Now it happened at Iconium that they entered the synagogue of the Jews together and spoke, so that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.
