But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been manifested, testified to by the law and the prophets. The righteousness of God is through faith in Jesus Christ, for all and upon all who believe in him; for there is no distinction. For all have sinned and lack the glory of God.

They are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as an expiation through faith in his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness because of the remission of former sins in God’s forbearance; to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so that he himself may be righteous and the one who justifies the person who is of the faith of Jesus Christ.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript does not add “of Christ” (*Christi*), and the Greek text likewise omits the name here.]**

Where, then, is your boasting? It has been excluded. By what law? By that of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we consider that a person is justified by faith without works of the law.

Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also the God of the Gentiles? Indeed, of the Gentiles also. For there is one God, who justifies circumcision by faith and uncircumcision through faith.

**[Note: The same manuscript has *qui justificavit*—“who justified”—a customary prophetic mistake for *justificabit*—“who will justify,” corresponding to the Greek δικαιώσει (*dikaiōsei*, “will justify”).]**

Do we then destroy the law through faith? Certainly not; rather, we establish the law.

## [Chapter IV]

What, then, shall we say that Abraham our father found according to the flesh? For if Abraham was justified by works, he has glory—but not before God.

For what does Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.”

Now to the one who works, the reward is not counted according to grace but according to debt; but to the one who does not work, yet believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness, according to the purpose of the grace of God.

**[Note: The words “according to the purpose of the grace of God” are entirely absent from the Palatine manuscript. Most Greek books also lack them, and I think they arose only from Valesius’s readings.]**

As David also speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God credits righteousness without works:

“Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven,
and whose sins have been covered.
Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin.”

Does this blessedness, then, remain only in circumcision, or also in uncircumcision? For we say that faith was counted to Abraham as righteousness.

How, then, was it counted? In circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript has more here: “when he was in circumcision, or also in uncircumcision.” The Greek reads ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ—“when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision.”]**

And he received the sign of circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith that was in uncircumcision, so that he might be the father of all believers through uncircumcision, so that righteousness might be counted to them also; and so that he might be the father of circumcision—not only of those who are of circumcision, but also of those who follow the footsteps of the faith that was in the uncircumcision of our father Abraham.

For the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he should be heir of the world was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise abolished. For the law produces wrath; for where there is no law, neither is there transgression.

**[Note: Here the Palatine manuscript lacks only the two words *tantum manet* (“remains only”), in accordance with the Greek text in most manuscripts of better quality.]**

Therefore it is from faith, so that the promise may be firm according to grace for all the seed—not only for the one who is of the law, but also for the one who is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.

As it is written: “I have appointed you the father of many nations”—before God, in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls those things that are not as though they were.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript has “in whom you believed” instead of “in whom he believed.” A little later it adds, “so your seed will be like the stars of heaven,” words that likewise do not appear in the Greek text according to copies of better quality.]**

Against hope, he believed in hope, so that he might become the father of many nations, according to what had been said to him: “So shall your seed be.”

And he was not weakened in faith, nor did he consider his own body, already dead—for he was nearly a hundred years old—or the deadness of Sarah’s womb. He did not hesitate in distrust at the promise of God, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God, fully convinced that whatever he had promised, he was also able to do.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript adds the name “God,” which is nevertheless absent here from the Greek archetype.]**

Therefore it was also counted to him as righteousness. But it was not written only for his sake, that it was counted to him, but also for our sake, to whom it will be counted if we believe in him who raised Jesus Christ our Lord from the dead.

**[Note: Here the Palatine manuscript omits the name “Christ,” although it appears in the Greek exemplar.]**

He was handed over because of our offenses and raised because of our justification.

## [Chapter V]

Therefore, having been justified by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we also have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we glory in the hope of the glory of the children of God.

**[Note: More closely following the Greek wording, the Palatine manuscript reads “access by faith into grace.”]**

And not only this, but we also glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces endurance; endurance, testing; testing, hope; and hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.

For why did Christ die for the ungodly at the appointed time, when we were still weak? For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous person; perhaps someone might dare to die for a good person.

But God demonstrates his love toward us, because while we were still sinners, Christ died for us at the appointed time.

**[Note: The words “at the appointed time,” which are not found in the Greek text, are entirely absent from the Palatine manuscript.]**

Much more, therefore, having now been justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved in his life.

And not only this, but we also glory in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

Therefore, just as through one man sin entered this world, and through sin death, and so death passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned—for until the law sin was in the world, but sin was not imputed when there was no law—

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “sin is not imputed” in the present tense, when there is no law; the Greek text likewise supports this reading.]**

Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a type of the one to come.

But the gift is not like the offense. For if the many died through the offense of one, much more did the grace of God and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abound to the many.

And the gift is not like what came through one who sinned.

**[Note: More closely following the Greek exemplar, the Palatine manuscript has “through one who sinned” instead of “through one sin.” The Greek reads δι’ ἑνὸς ἁμαρτήσαντος—“through one who sinned.” Immediately afterward it omits “For the judgment was from one.”]**

For the judgment indeed came from one offense resulting in condemnation, but the gift came from many offenses resulting in justification.

For if death reigned through the offense of one, through that one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one Jesus Christ.

Therefore, just as through one offense judgment came upon all human beings for condemnation, so also through one act of righteousness came upon all human beings for justification of life.

For just as through the disobedience of one man the many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of one the many will be constituted righteous.

The law entered in so that the offense might abound. But where the offense abounded, grace abounded even more, so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness unto eternal life, through Jesus Christ our Lord.

## [Chapter VI]

What, then, shall we say? Shall we remain in sin so that grace may abound? Certainly not. We who died to sin—how shall we still live in it?

Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? Therefore we were buried with him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.

For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall also be united with his resurrection. Knowing this, that our old person was crucified together with him, so that the body of sin might be destroyed and we might no longer serve sin.

For the one who has died has been justified from sin. But if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live together with Christ, knowing that Christ, having risen from the dead, dies no more; death no longer rules over him.

For in that he died, he died to sin once for all; but in that he lives, he lives to God. So you too must consider yourselves dead to sin but alive to God, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

**[Note: Some Greek manuscripts also omit the words “our Lord”; the Palatine manuscript likewise does not contain them.]**

Therefore, let sin not reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires. Nor should you present your members as weapons of unrighteousness to sin; rather, present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as weapons of righteousness to God.

For sin will not rule over you, since you are not under the law but under grace.

What then? Shall we sin because we are not under the law but under grace? Certainly not. Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey—whether of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?

But thanks be to God that although you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over. Having been freed from sin, you became slaves of righteousness.

I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and iniquity leading to iniquity, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification.

For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness. What fruit, then, did you have at that time in those things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.

**[Note: The same Palatine manuscript does not contain the two words “in those things”; this is also closer to the Greek wording.]**

But now, having been freed from sin and having become slaves of God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and your end is eternal life. For the wages of sin are death, but the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

## [Chapter VII]

Or do you not know, brothers—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?

For the woman who is under a husband is bound by law to her husband while he lives; but if her husband dies, she is released from the law of her husband. Therefore, while her husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she is with another man; but if her husband dies, she is freed from the law of her husband, so that she is not an adulteress if she is with another man.

Therefore, my brothers, you too were put to death with respect to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another—the one who rose from the dead—in order that we might bear fruit for God.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “so that we might bear fruit,” in accordance with the Greek exemplar, ἵνα καρποφορήσωμεν (*hina karpophorēsōmen*).]**

For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins that were through the law worked in our members, so that they bore fruit for death. But now we have been released from the law of death in which we were held, so that we may serve in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter.

What, then, shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not. But I did not know sin except through the law. For I would not have known covetousness unless the law had said, “You shall not covet.”

But sin, having taken an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetousness. For without the law sin was dead. I was once alive without the law; but when the commandment came, sin revived. I died, and the commandment that was intended for life was found by me to be for death.

For sin, having taken an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me. Therefore the law is indeed holy, and the commandment holy, righteous, and good.

What, then? Did what is good become death to me? Certainly not. But sin, so that it might appear to be sin, worked death in me through what is good, so that sin might become exceedingly sinful through the commandment.

For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin. For I do not understand what I do. For I do not do the good that I want, but I do the evil that I hate.

**[Note: The Palatine manuscript has simply “I do not do what I want, but I do what I hate.” It does not contain the words “the good” and “the evil” at this point; these are likewise absent from the Greek text, but were introduced into Greek books from Valesius’s readings, or from the corresponding passage in the following isocolon four verses later.]**

But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good. Now, however, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells in me.

For I know that good does not dwell in me—that is, in my flesh. For the willing is present in me, but I do not find the ability to accomplish the good. For I do not do the good that I want, but I do the evil that I do not want.

But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin that dwells in me.

**[Manuscript: *jam* (“now”) is omitted.]**

Therefore I find this law: when I want to do good, evil lies close at hand. For I delight in the law of God according to the inner person, but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in my members.

Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Therefore I myself, with my mind, serve the law of God; but with the flesh, the law of sin.

## [Chapter VIII]

There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and death. For what was impossible for the law, weakened as it was through the flesh, God did: sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and, on account of sin, condemning sin in the flesh, so that the just requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

For those who are according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, but those who are according to the Spirit attend to the things of the Spirit. For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace.

[Col. 0735C] For the wisdom of the flesh is hostile to God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can it be. Those who are in the flesh cannot please God. But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to him.

But if Christ is in you, although the body is dead because of sin, the spirit is alive because of righteousness.

[Note: [Col. 0735D] In the Palatine manuscript, instead of *lives* (*vivit*) there is *is life* (*est vita*), as also in the Greek text, ζωή.]

And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you.

[Manuscript: *gave life* (*vivificavit*) instead of *will give life* (*vivificabit*).]

Therefore, brothers, we are debtors—not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh. For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

[Col. 0735D] For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.

[Manuscript: *they* is omitted.]

For you did not receive a spirit of slavery again for fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption as sons, in whom we cry, “Abba, Father.” For the Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. And if children, then heirs—heirs indeed of God, but fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him.

[Col. 0736A] For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy of comparison with the future glory that will be revealed in us. For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God. For creation was subjected to futility, not willingly but because of him who subjected it in hope,

[Note: [Col. 0736D] Here the Palatine manuscript omits the pronoun *it* (*eam*), and shortly afterward it has the noun *of God* where the text reads “awaiting the adoption of the sons of God”; in both respects it follows the Greek archetype more closely.]

because creation itself will also be set free from the slavery of corruption into the freedom of the glory of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groans and labors in childbirth until now. And not only it, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we await the adoption of sons, the redemption of our body.

For in hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what one sees?

[Manuscript: *who* (*qui*) instead of *what* (*quid*).]

But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it with patience.

[Col. 0736B] Likewise the Spirit also helps our weakness; for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself pleads for us with inexpressible groanings. And he who searches the hearts knows what the Spirit desires, because he pleads for the saints according to God.

We know, moreover, that all things work together for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose. For those whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. And those whom he predestined, he also called; and those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.

What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who is against us? He who did not spare even his own Son, but delivered him up for us all—how will he not also grant us everything with him?

[Note: [Col. 0736D] More correctly, in accordance with the Greek, the Palatine manuscript reads in the future tense, “will grant.”]

Who will bring an accusation against God’s elect? God, who justifies? Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus, who died—rather, who was also raised—who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.

Who therefore will separate us from the love of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or persecution, or sword? As it is written: “For your sake we are being put to death all day long; we have been reckoned as sheep for slaughter.”

But in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. For I am certain that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither things present nor things to come, neither powers,

[Note: [Col. 0736D] As in most Greek manuscripts, οὔτε δυνάμεις, “nor powers,” the words *nor virtues* are likewise absent from the Palatine manuscript.]

neither height nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

## [Chapter IX]

I speak the truth in Christ; I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit: that I have great sorrow and continual pain in my heart. For I myself could wish to be accursed and separated from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh. They are Israelites, [Col. 0737A] to whom belong the adoption as sons, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises; to them belong the fathers, and from them, according to the flesh, is the Christ, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.

But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israelites.

[Note: [Col. 0737D] The same manuscript omits the word *are* here; shortly afterward it reads *nor because* instead of *nor who*, following the Greek exemplar, Οὐδ’ ὅτι.]

Nor are all Abraham’s descendants his children; rather, “In Isaac shall your offspring be named.” That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are reckoned as offspring. For the word of promise is this: “At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.”

And not only this, but Rebecca also, having conceived by one man, Isaac our father—for when they had not yet been born or done anything good or bad, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain, it was said to her, not on the basis of works but through him who calls: “The elder shall serve the younger.” As it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

What then shall we say? Is there injustice with God? Certainly not. For he says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show compassion to whom I show compassion.”

[Manuscript: *to whom* (*cui*) instead of *of whom* (*cujus*) in both instances.]

Therefore it depends not on the one who wills or on the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.

For Scripture says to Pharaoh: “For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might show my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.”

[Manuscript: *and* is omitted.]

Therefore he has mercy on whom he wishes, and he hardens whom he wishes.

You will say to me, then: “Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?” O human being, who are you to answer back to God? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it, “Why did you make me like this?” Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?

[Col. 0737C] But what if God, wishing to show his wrath and make known his power, endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, in order to make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory?

And these he also called—us, not only from the Jews but also from the nations. As he says in Hosea:

“I will call ‘My people’ those who were not my people,
and ‘Beloved’ her who was not beloved;
and in the place where it was said to them,
‘You are not my people,’
there they will be called sons of the living God.”

Isaiah, however, cries out concerning Israel:

“If the number of the sons of Israel were like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved. For the Lord will complete and shorten the word in righteousness, because the Lord will execute a shortened word upon the earth.”

[Col. 0737D] And as Isaiah had foretold:

“Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom and would have been made like Gomorrah.”

What then shall we say? That the nations, who were not pursuing righteousness, obtained righteousness—the righteousness that comes from faith. But Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain the law of righteousness. Why? Because it was not from faith but as though from works. For they stumbled over the stone of stumbling, as it is written:

“Behold, I place in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.”

[Col. 0738A]

## [Chapter X]

Brothers, the desire of my heart and my supplication to God for them is for their salvation. For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. For, being ignorant of God’s righteousness and seeking to establish their own, they were not subject to God’s righteousness. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.

For Moses writes that the person who practices the righteousness that comes from the law will live by it. But the righteousness that comes from faith speaks in this way:

“Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’”—that is, to bring Christ down. Or, “Who will descend into the abyss?”—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.

But what does Scripture say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart”—that is, the word of faith that we proclaim. For if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made for salvation.

For Scripture says: “Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.” For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, since the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him. For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.

How then will they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without someone preaching? And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written:

“How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace,
of those who proclaim good things!”

But not all obey the Gospel. For Isaiah says:

“Lord, who has believed our report?”

So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.

But I ask: Have they not heard? Indeed, “Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.”

But I ask: Did Israel not understand? Moses is the first to say:

“I will provoke you to jealousy by a people who is not a people; I will send you into anger by an unintelligent nation.”

Isaiah, however, dares to say:

“I was found by those who were not seeking me; I became manifest to those who were not asking about me.”

But to Israel he says:

“All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people.”

[Note: [Col. 0738D] The Palatine manuscript adds *to me* (*mihi*), a pronoun also found in a few Greek manuscripts.]

[Col. 0738D]

## [Chapter XI]

I ask, then: Has God rejected his people? Certainly not. For I myself am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew.

Or do you not know what Scripture says in the passage concerning Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?

“Lord, they have killed your prophets; they have dug up your altars; and I alone have been left, and they are seeking my life.”

But what does the divine response say to him?

“I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal.”

So therefore, at the present time also, a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace. But if it is by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.

What then? What Israel was seeking, it did not obtain; but the elect obtained it. The rest were blinded, as it is written:

“God gave them a spirit of compunction,
eyes so that they might not see,
and ears so that they might not hear,
to this very day.”

And David says:

“Let their table become a snare
and a trap,
a stumbling-block
and a recompense for them.
Let their eyes be darkened,
so that they may not see,
and keep their back continually bent.”

I ask, then: Did they stumble in order to fall? Certainly not. But through their trespass salvation has come to the nations, in order to make them jealous. Now if their trespass is the wealth of the world, and their diminishing the wealth of the nations, how much more will their fullness be?

[Col. 0739B] For I speak to you nations: insofar as I am indeed the apostle of the nations, I will honor my ministry, if somehow I may provoke my flesh to jealousy and save some of them. For if their loss is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be except life from the dead?

And if the first portion is holy, so is the whole lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches. But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though you were a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the root and richness of the olive tree, do not boast against the branches.

But if you boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root that bears you. Then you will say, “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.” Quite so: they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand through faith. Do not be arrogant, but fear. For if God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either.

[Col. 0739C] See, then, the kindness and severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God’s kindness toward you, if you remain in kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off. And they also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

For if you were cut from the naturally wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted into a good olive tree, how much more will these, according to nature, be grafted into their own olive tree?

For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery—so that you may not be wise in your own estimation—that a hardening in part has happened to Israel until the fullness of the nations enters, and thus all Israel will be saved, as it is written:

“The one who delivers will come from Zion;
he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.
And this will be my covenant with them,
when I take away their sins.”

[Col. 0739D] With respect to the Gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with respect to election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers. For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

For just as you once disobeyed God but now have received mercy because of their disobedience, so they too have now disobeyed in consequence of the mercy shown to you, so that they themselves may also receive mercy. For God has enclosed all in disobedience, so that he may have mercy on all.

O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how inscrutable his ways!

“For who has known the mind of the Lord?
Or who has been his counselor?
Or who has first given to him,
so that he might be repaid?”

For from him, through him, and in him are all things. To him be glory forever.

[Manuscript: *for an age* instead of *forever*.]

Amen.

## [Chapter XII]

Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—your rational service. And do not conform yourselves to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.

For by the grace given to me I say to everyone among you: Do not think more highly than you ought to think, but think soberly, each according to the measure of faith that God has allotted.

[Col. 0740B] For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function, so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.

Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: if prophecy, according to the proportion of faith; if ministry, in ministering; if one teaches, in teaching; if one exhorts,

[Note: [Col. 0739D] More closely following the Greek text, the Palatine manuscript reads *in exhortation* (*in exhortatione*), instead of *in exhorting* (*in exhortando*).]

in exhortation; the one who gives, with simplicity; the one who presides, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

Love without dissimulation. Hating evil, clinging to good; loving one another with fraternal affection; anticipating one another in honor; not sluggish in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord; rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; devoted to prayer; sharing in the needs of the saints; pursuing hospitality.

Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse. Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep. Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own estimation. Repay no one evil for evil. Provide what is good, not only before God but also before all people.

If possible, insofar as it depends on you, live at peace with all people. Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath. For it is written:

“Vengeance is mine; I will repay,” says the Lord.

But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink. For by doing this you will heap burning coals upon his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

## [Chapter XIII]

[Col. 0739D] [Note: Following several Greek books, Πάσαις ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτάσσεσθε, the Palatine manuscript reads: “Be subject to all higher authorities.”]

Let every soul be subject to higher authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God. Therefore whoever resists authority resists God’s ordinance; and those who resist will bring condemnation upon themselves.

For rulers are not a terror to good conduct but to evil. Do you wish not to fear authority? Do what is good, and you will receive praise from it, for it is God’s servant for your good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword without cause. For it is God’s servant, an avenger for wrath against the one who does evil.

Therefore you must be subject, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience. For this reason you also pay taxes, since they are God’s ministers, serving precisely for this purpose. Give to everyone what is owed: to whom tribute, tribute; to whom revenue, revenue; to whom fear, fear; to whom honor, honor.

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for whoever loves the neighbor has fulfilled the law. For:

“You shall not commit adultery;
you shall not kill;
you shall not steal;
you shall not bear false witness;
you shall not covet”;

and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this saying:

“You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

Love of neighbor does no evil. Therefore love is the fullness of the law.

And know the time: it is already the hour for us to rise from sleep. For our salvation is nearer now than when we believed. The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.

Let us walk honorably as in the day—not in revelries and drunkenness, not in beds and debauchery, not in quarrels and jealousy—but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh in its desires.

[Note: [Col. 0741D] The Palatine manuscript reads, “but put on the Lord,” and so on; in Greek, ἀλλ’ ἐνδύνασθε Κύριον.]

## [Chapter XIV]

Receive the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions. One person believes that everything may be eaten; but the one who is weak eats vegetables.

[Manuscript: *holera*.]

Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat; and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God has welcomed him. Who are you to judge another’s servant? He stands or falls before his own master. And he will stand, for God is able to make him stand.

For one person judges one day to be above another; another judges every day alike. Let each be fully persuaded in his own mind. The one who observes the day observes it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God. And the one who does not eat abstains for the Lord, and gives thanks to God.

For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself. If we live, we live for the Lord; and if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord. For this is why Christ died and rose again: so that he might be Lord both of the dead and of the living.

But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother? For we shall all stand before the tribunal of Christ.

[Manuscript: *of God* instead of *of Christ*.]

[Col. 0741D] For it is written:

“As I live, says the Lord,
every knee shall bend to me,
and every tongue shall confess to God.”

Therefore each of us will give an account of himself to God.

Let us therefore no longer judge one another, but judge this rather: not to place a stumbling-block or an occasion of offense before a brother.

I know, and I am confident in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself, except for the one who considers something unclean; for that person it is unclean.

[Note: [Col. 0741D] The manuscript adds *is* (*est*), making the reading: “unless it is unclean to the one who considers something unclean.”]

For if your brother is distressed because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died. Therefore let our good not be blasphemed.

[Col. 0742A] For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. Whoever serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.

Therefore let us pursue the things that make for peace and the things that build one another up. Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for a person to eat through an offense.

It is good not to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother is offended, or is caused to stumble, or is weakened.

[Note: [Col. 0741D] The same manuscript reads *you offend* (*offendis*); the Greek has προσκόπτει, “is offended” or “stumbles.”]

Do you have faith? Keep it to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself in what he approves. But the one who doubts is condemned if he eats, because it is not from faith. And everything that is not from faith is sin.

## [Chapter XV]

We who are stronger ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak and not to please ourselves.

[Manuscript: *weakness* (*imbecillitatem*) instead of *weaknesses* (*imbecillitates*).] Let each of you please the neighbor for good, for edification.

[Note: [Col. 0741D] The Palatine manuscript reads differently: “Let each of you please the neighbor for good edification,” though the Greek text itself contradicts this reading.]

For Christ did not please himself, but as it is written:

“The reproaches of those who reproached you fell upon me.”

For whatever was written was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and consolation of the Scriptures we might have hope.

May the God of patience and consolation grant you to think the same thing toward one another according to Jesus Christ, so that with one mind and one mouth you may honor God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Col. 0742C] Therefore receive one another, just as Christ also received you, to the glory of God.

[Note: [Col. 0742D] The Palatine manuscript, with most Greek books, prefers *us* instead of *you*.]

For I say that Christ Jesus became a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made to the fathers; but the nations are to honor God for his mercy, as it is written:

“For this reason I will confess you among the nations, Lord,
and sing to your name.”

And again he says:

“Rejoice, nations, with his people.”

And again:

“Praise the Lord, all nations,
and magnify him, all peoples.”

And again Isaiah says:

“There will be a root of Jesse,
and the one who rises to rule the nations;
in him the nations will hope.”

May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope and in the power of the Holy Spirit.

I am confident, my brothers—and I myself am convinced concerning you—that you too are full of love, filled with all knowledge, so that you are able to admonish one another.

[Col. 0742D] I have written to you rather boldly, brothers, in part, as though reminding you, because of the grace given to me by God, so that I might be a minister of Christ Jesus among the nations, sanctifying the Gospel of God, so that the offering of the nations may be acceptable and sanctified in the Holy Spirit.

Therefore I have glory in Christ Jesus before God. For I would not dare to speak of anything that Christ did not accomplish through me for the obedience of the nations, by word and deed, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit,

[Col. 0743A] so that from Jerusalem and all around as far as Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the Gospel of Christ.

So I preached this Gospel—not where Christ has already been named,

[Note: [Col. 0743D] This pronoun is represented neither in the Greek nor in the Palatine manuscript.]

lest I build upon another’s foundation, but as it is written:

“Those to whom nothing was announced about him will see,
and those who have not heard will understand.”

For this reason I was hindered many times from coming to you.

[Note: [Col. 0743D] From the readings of Valesius there arose the Latin text “and I was prevented until now” (*et prohibitus sum usque adhuc*), but these words are entirely absent from the Palatine manuscript.]

But now, having no further place in these regions and having had the desire to come to you for many years, when I begin my journey to Spain I hope to see you in passing and to be sent on there by you, after I have first enjoyed your company in part.

But now I am setting out for Jerusalem to minister to the saints. For Macedonia and Achaia have decided to make some contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem. They decided to do so, and they are their debtors. For if the nations have shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to minister to them in material things.

When I have completed this and delivered this fruit to them, I will depart through your region toward Spain. And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the abundance of the blessing of the Gospel of Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0743D] The Palatine manuscript lacks *of the Gospel*, and the noun is also absent from some Greek manuscripts.]

I urge you, therefore, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Holy Spirit, to assist me in your prayers for me to God,

[Note: [Col. 0743D] Instead of “to assist me in your prayers for me,” the Palatine manuscript reads: “to impart your concern to me in prayers for me,” which is closer to the Greek text, συναγωνίσασθαί μοι ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν κ.τ.λ. (“to strive together with me in prayers for me to God,” and so forth).]

that I may be delivered from the unbelievers who are in Judea, and that my service-offering may be acceptable to the saints in Jerusalem, so that I may come to you with joy through the will of God and be refreshed together with you.

[Col. 0743C] May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

## [Chapter XVI]

I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is in the service of the Church at Cenchreae, so that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints and assist her in whatever matter she may need from you; for she herself also has been a helper to many, and to me personally.

Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, who for my life laid down their own necks; not only I give thanks to them, but also all the churches of the nations—and the church in their house.

[Manuscripts: *domestic Church* (*domestica Ecclesia*).]

Greet Epaenetus, beloved by me, who is the firstfruits of Asia in Christ. Greet Mary, who labored much among you.

[Col. 0744A] Greet Andronicus and Junia,

[Manuscripts: *Julius*.]

my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles and who were in Christ before me.

Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord. Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ Jesus,

[Note: [Col. 0744D] The Palatine manuscript, together with the Greek books, omits the name *Jesus* here.]

and Stachys, my beloved. Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those who are from the household of Aristobulus. Greet Herodion, my kinsman.

Greet those who are from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0744D] The Palatine manuscript does not add *household*, in accordance with the Greek text, though the noun is understood. Shortly afterward the same manuscript has *who labored much* (*quae multum laborant*), but the adverb was added there by a second hand, and the Greek text itself lacks it. Finally, it reads *Persida* instead of *Persidem*, and shortly afterward *Herman* instead of *Hermes*.]

Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the most distinguished woman, who labored much in the Lord. Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who is also mine.

Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Herma, Patrobas, Hermen, and the brothers who are with them. Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympias, and all the saints who are with them.

Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.

I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create dissensions and stumbling-blocks contrary to the teaching that you have learned, and turn away from them.

[Note: [Col. 0744D] More correctly, both in the Greek and in the Palatine manuscript, the reading is *from them* (*ab illis*) instead of *from others* (*ab aliis*). Shortly afterward the Palatine manuscript omits *our* in the phrase “Jesus Christ our Lord.”]

For such people do not serve Christ our Lord but their own belly; and through smooth speech and blessings they deceive the hearts of the innocent. For your obedience has become known everywhere. Therefore I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise in what is good and innocent in what is evil.

May the God of peace soon crush Satan beneath your feet. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord. Gaius, my host and the host of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, and Quartus, the brother.

May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

Now to him who is able to strengthen you according to my Gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through eternal ages—which was not made manifest through the Scriptures of the Prophets, according to the command of the eternal God, but made known among all nations for the obedience of faith—[Manuscript: *known alone* (*cognito solo*) instead of *to the only wise God* (*soli sapienti Deo*).]

To God, who alone is wise, through Jesus Christ, be honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

The Epistle of the blessed apostle Paul to the Romans ends.

[Col. 0745]

# The First Epistle of the Blessed Apostle Paul to the Corinthians Begins

[Col. 0745A] ## [Chapter I]

Paul, called an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother, to the Church of God that is at Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, together with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours.

Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

I give thanks to my God always for you, because of the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus: that in everything you have been enriched in him, in every word and in every knowledge, just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you, so that you lack nothing in any grace, as you await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

I urge you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing and that there be no divisions among you; but that you be perfected in the same mind and in the same judgment.

[Col. 0745C] [Note: Just as certain Greek manuscripts prefer γνώσει (“knowledge”) instead of γνώμῃ (“judgment”), so the Palatine manuscript here has *knowledge* instead of *judgment*. Shortly afterward it varies slightly as well, reading “that there are contentions among you,” and so forth.]

For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who belong to Chloe, that there are contentions among you. I mean this: each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” or “I to Apollos,” or “I to Cephas,” or “I to Christ.”

Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, so that no one may say that you were baptized in my name.

[Manuscript: *that you may be* instead of *that you were*.]

I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else. For Christ did not send me to baptize but to evangelize—not with wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.

For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved—that is, to us—it is the power of God. For it is written:

“I will destroy the wisdom of the wise,
and I will reject the understanding of the intelligent.”

Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe? Where is the investigator of this age? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?

For since the world did not know God through wisdom in the wisdom of God, it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe. For Jews ask for signs, and Greeks seek wisdom; but we preach Christ crucified: a stumbling-block to Jews, but foolishness to the nations; yet to those who are called, Jews and Greeks alike, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

For what is foolish of God is wiser than human beings, and what is weak of God is stronger than human beings.

[Col. 0746A] For consider your calling, brothers: not many are wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many noble. But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise, and God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong. God chose what is lowborn in the world and what is despised, what is not, to bring to nothing what is, so that no flesh might boast before him.

But from him you are in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom for us from God, and righteousness, sanctification, and redemption, so that, as it is written:

[Col. 0746B] “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”

## [Chapter II]

And I, when I came to you, brothers, came not with loftiness of speech or wisdom, announcing to you the testimony of Christ. For I judged myself not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified. And I was with you in weakness, and fear, and much trembling; and my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in a demonstration of the Spirit and of power [Note: [Col. 0745C] In the Palatine manuscript, *hic Dei* (“of God”) is added on a second revision, though incorrectly.]: so that your faith might not be in human wisdom but in the power of God.

But we speak wisdom among the mature—not indeed the wisdom of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing—but we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the wisdom hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory [Col. 0746C], which none of the rulers of this age knew. For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

But, as it is written: [Note: [Col. 0746C] In the Palatine manuscript, obeli have been placed before these two verses, quoted from Isaiah, chapter LXIV. You will easily understand why the copyist did this from Jerome himself in his Commentaries on that passage of Isaiah; if these matters are of sufficient importance, see also what we have noted.]

“What eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart, what God has prepared for those who love him.”

But God has revealed it to us through his Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God. For what human being knows the things of a human being except the human spirit that is in him? So also no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God. Now we have not received the spirit of this world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things given to us by God. We also speak of these things, not in words taught by human wisdom [Col. 0747A], but in teaching of the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.

But the natural person does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are examined spiritually. But the spiritual person judges all things, and he himself is judged by no one. For “who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

## [Chapter III]

And I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as carnal—as infants in Christ. I gave you milk to drink, not food, for you were not yet able; indeed, even now you are not able, for you are still carnal. For since there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not carnal and walking according to human ways? For when someone says, “I belong to Paul,” and another, “I to Apollos,” are you not human beings? [Col. 0747B]

What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Ministers of him in whom you believed, and each according to what the Lord gave. I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. Therefore neither the one who plants is anything, nor the one who waters, but God who gives the growth. The one who plants and the one who waters are one; but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor. For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s cultivation, God’s building.

According to the grace of God given to me, as a wise architect I laid a foundation, and another builds upon it. But let each one see how he builds upon it. For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.

But if anyone builds upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble [Col. 0747C], each one’s work will become manifest. For the Day of the Lord will declare it, because it will be revealed in fire; and the fire will test what sort of work each one’s is. If anyone’s work that he built upon it remains, he will receive a reward. If anyone’s work burns, he will suffer loss; yet he himself will be saved, but only as through fire.

Do you not know that you are God’s temple, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him. For God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

Let no one deceive himself [Ms. “you”]. If anyone among you seems to be wise in this age, let him become foolish, so that he may be wise. For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written: “I will seize the wise in their craftiness” [Col. 0747D]. And again: “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”

Therefore let no one glory in human beings. For all things are yours: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come—all things are yours; and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

## [Chapter IV]

In this way let a person regard us—as ministers of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries. Moreover, what is sought among stewards is that someone be found faithful. But it is a very small thing to me that I should be judged by you or by a human day [Col. 0748A]; indeed, I do not even judge myself. For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not thereby justified; the one who judges me is the Lord.

Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes. He will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and disclose the intentions of hearts; and then each one’s praise will come from God.

Now, brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn not to go beyond what is written, so that no one may be puffed up on behalf of one person against another. For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?

Already you are filled; already you have become rich; you reign without us—and indeed I wish that you did reign, so that we also might reign with you. For I think that God has displayed us apostles [Col. 0748B] as the last, as sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to human beings.

We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are prudent in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are noble, but we are ignoble. Until this present hour we are both hungry and thirsty, naked and beaten, unsettled and laboring, working with our own hands. We are cursed, and we bless; we are persecuted, and we endure; we are slandered, and we entreat. We have become like the refuse of this world, the offscouring of all things, up to the present.

I do not write these things to shame you, but I admonish you as my dearly beloved children. For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you do not have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, through the gospel, I begot you [Col. 0748C].

Therefore I urge you [Ms. “for”]: be imitators of me, [Note: [Col. 0747] The Palatine manuscript omits the words “as I also am of Christ,” which are likewise absent from the Greek text except in a few manuscripts.] as I also am of Christ.

For this reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my dearly beloved and faithful son in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways, which are in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.

As though I were not going to come to you, certain people have become puffed up. But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will discover not the speech of those who are puffed up but their power. For the kingdom of God is not in speech but in power. What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

## [Chapter V]

It is reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as does not even occur among the nations: that someone has his father’s wife. And you are puffed up, rather than mourning, so that the one who has done this deed might be removed from your midst [Col. 0748D].

For I, absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, the one who has acted in this way: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together, and my spirit with you, with the power of our Lord Jesus, to hand such a person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole lump? Purge out the old leaven, so that you may be a new batch, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed [Col. 0749A]. Therefore let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with fornicators—not at all meaning the fornicators of this world, or the greedy, or the rapacious, or those who serve idols; otherwise you would have had to leave this world. But now I wrote to you not to associate [Note: [Col. 0749D] The Palatine manuscripts have a considerably different reading: “Do not associate, if anyone who is called a brother among you is a fornicator,” and so forth. This reading may seem ancient, prior to the correction made by Jerome; yet it is also cited in some places in the epistles by Jerome himself.] with anyone who is called a brother if he is a fornicator, or greedy, or serves idols, or is abusive, or drunk, or rapacious—not even to eat with such a person.

For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those who are inside? But God will judge those who are outside. “Remove the evil person from among yourselves.”

## [Chapter VI]

Does any one of you, having a case [Col. 0749B] against another, dare to be judged before the unjust and not before the saints? Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Do you not know that we will judge angels—how much more matters of this life?

Therefore, if you have lawsuits concerning matters of this life, appoint as judges those who are despised in the church. I say this to your shame. Is there thus no wise person among you who could judge between his brother? But brother goes to court against brother—and this before unbelievers?

Already it is altogether a fault among you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why do you not rather suffer injustice? Why do you not rather suffer fraud? But you yourselves do injustice and defraud—and this to your brothers.

Or do you not know that the unjust will not possess the kingdom of God [Col. 0749C]? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idol-servants, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor men who have intercourse with males, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor abusers, nor rapacious people will possess the kingdom of God.

And such were some of you. But you were washed; but you were sanctified; but you were justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.

“All things are permitted to me,” but not all things are beneficial. “All things are permitted to me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything. Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food; but God will destroy both it and them [Ms. “it”]. The body, however, is not for fornication but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. God indeed raised up the Lord, and he will also raise us up by his power.

Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I therefore take Christ’s members [Col. 0749D] and make them members of a prostitute? Certainly not. Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body? For, he says, “the two will be one flesh.” But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit.

Flee fornication. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body; but the fornicator sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your members are the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and that you are not your own [Col. 0750A]? For you were bought at a great price. Therefore glorify and bear God in your body.

## [Chapter VII]

Now concerning the matters about which you wrote to me: “It is good for a man not to touch a woman.” But because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, and each woman her own husband. Let the husband render the due to his wife, and likewise also the wife to her husband. The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by mutual consent for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer; and come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control. But I say this by way of concession, not by command.

For I wish all of you to be as I myself am. But each has his own gift [Col. 0750B] from God, one in this way, another in that.

Now I say to the unmarried and to widows: it is good for them if they remain as I am. But if they cannot exercise self-control, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn.

But to those who are married I give this command—not I, but the Lord: that a wife should not separate from her husband; but if she has separated, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And let a husband not dismiss his wife.

But to the rest I say—not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, let him not dismiss her. And if any believing woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, let her not dismiss her husband. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through the believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through the believing husband [Note: [Col. 0750D] More closely following the Greek text, the Palatine manuscript has: “in the believing woman,” ἐν τῇ γυναικὶ, and so forth.]; otherwise [Col. 0750C] your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

But if the unbeliever departs, let him depart. A brother or sister is not enslaved in such circumstances; but God has called us in peace. For how do you know, woman, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

Nevertheless, as the Lord has distributed to each one, as God has called each one, so let him walk—and so I teach in all the churches.

Was someone called while circumcised? Let him not remove the circumcision. Was someone called while uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised. Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of God’s commandments.

Let each one remain in the calling in which he was called. Were you called as a slave? Do not let it concern you; but if you can become free, make use of the opportunity. For the one who was called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord’s freedman [Col. 0750D]; likewise, the one who was called as a free person is Christ’s slave. You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings.

Let each one, brothers, remain with God in whatever calling he was called.

Now concerning virgins I have no command of the Lord, but I give advice as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful. Therefore I think this to be good because of the present necessity: that it is good for a person to remain as he is.

Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife [Col. 0751A]. But if you take a wife, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such people will have trouble in the flesh, and I am sparing you.

This, then, I say, brothers: the time is short. It remains that those who have wives should be as though they had none; those who weep as though they did not weep; those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice; those who buy as though they did not possess; and those who use this world as though they did not use it. For the form of this world is passing away.

But I want you to be without anxiety. The unmarried person is concerned with the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord. But the married person is concerned with the things of the world, how he may please his wife, and he is divided.

The unmarried woman and the virgin think about the things of the Lord [Col. 0751B], so that she may be holy in body and spirit. But the married woman thinks about the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

Moreover, I say this for your benefit, not to throw a noose around you, but for what is honorable and what provides an opportunity to serve the Lord without hindrance [Ms. “to entreat”].

But if anyone thinks that he is acting dishonorably toward his virgin, because she is past marriageable age, and it ought to be so, let him do what he wishes: let her marry; he does not sin. But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity, and having authority over his own will, and having decided this in his heart—to keep his virgin—does well. Therefore both the one who gives his virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage does better.

A woman is bound to the law for as long as her husband lives. But if her husband dies [Col. 0751C], she is free to marry whom she wishes—only in the Lord [Note: [Col. 0751D] The Palatine manuscript does not add “to the law.” Nor do the other Latin manuscripts—the Corbeienses, Sangermanenses, and many others consulted by learned men—have this phrase here; nor is it found in most Greek manuscripts. It therefore appears to have been imported here from the preceding Epistle to the Romans, chapter VII, verse 2.].

But she will be happier if she remains as she is, according to my advice; and I think that I too have the Spirit of God.

## [Chapter VIII]

Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. If anyone thinks that he knows something, he has not yet known how he ought to know. But if anyone loves God, this person is known by him.

Now concerning the foods sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God except one. For even if there are those who are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—indeed there are many gods and many lords—yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we are unto him; and one [Col. 0751D] Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through him.

But knowledge is not in everyone. Some, through consciousness of the idol even until now, eat the food as idol-sacrifice; and their conscience, being weak, is defiled. But food does not commend us to God. For neither, if we eat, do we abound; nor, if we do not eat, do we lack.

But see to it that this freedom of yours does not somehow become a stumbling-block to the weak [Col. 0752A]. For if someone sees the one who has knowledge reclining in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be built up toward eating idol-sacrifices [Note: [Col. 0752D] In accordance with the Greek οἰκοδομηθήσεται, the Palatine manuscript also reads the future, “will be built up.”]?

And will the weak person perish through your knowledge—the brother for whom Christ died? Thus, by sinning against the brothers and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.

## [Chapter IX]

Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord? And if I am not an apostle to others, yet surely I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord. This is my defense before those who question me.

Do we not have authority [Col. 0752B] to eat and drink? Do we not have authority to take along a sister, a woman [Note: [Col. 0752D] The Palatine manuscript omits “sister,” although the word is present in the Greek text.] as a wife, as do the other apostles, the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas? Or do only I and Barnabas lack authority to do this?

Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of the flock’s milk? Do I say these things merely from a human standpoint? Or does the law not also say this? For it is written in the law of Moses: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.” Is God concerned about oxen? Or does he certainly say this for our sake [Note: [Col. 0752D] In the Palatine manuscript: “Or does he certainly say this for our sake?” followed by “Indeed, for our sake,” and so forth.]? For it was written for our sake: because the one who plows ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes in hope of sharing in the harvest.

If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap your material things? [Col. 0752C] If others share in your authority, why not rather we? But we have not used this authority; instead, we endure everything, so that we may not place any obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.

Do you not know that those who work in the sanctuary eat what comes from the sanctuary, and that those who serve at the altar share with the altar? So also the Lord ordained for those who announce the gospel to live from the gospel.

But I have used none of these things. Nor have I written this so that it should be done for me. For it is better for me to die than that anyone should deprive me of my glory. For if I preach the gospel, there is no glory for me; necessity is laid upon me. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel.

For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship. What, then, is my reward? That, when preaching the gospel [Col. 0752D], I may offer the gospel without cost, so as not to make use of my authority in the gospel.

For although I was free from all, I made myself a slave to all, so that I might win more. To the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews. To those under the law I became as though under the law—although I myself was not under the law—so that I might win those under the law. To those without the law I became as though without the law—although I was not without God’s law [Col. 0753A], but was within the law of Christ—so that I might win those without the law.

I became weak to the weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that I might save all. I do everything for the sake of the gospel, so that I may become a participant in it.

Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it. Everyone who competes in the contest exercises self-control in all things. They do this to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one.

Therefore I run in this way—not as uncertainly; I fight in this way—not as one beating the air. But I discipline my body and bring it into slavery, lest, after preaching to others, I myself should become disqualified.

## [Chapter X]

For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that [Col. 0753B] our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea; and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink—for they were drinking from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

Yet God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness. These things happened as figures of us [Ms. “for us”], so that we might not be desirous of evil things, as they desired them.

Nor become idolaters, as some of them did. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Nor let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day. Nor let us test Christ, as some of them [Col. 0753C] tested him and perished by serpents. Nor grumble, as some of them grumbled and perished by the destroyer.

Now all these things happened to them figuratively, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Therefore let the one who thinks he stands take care lest he fall.

No temptation has overtaken you except a human one. But God is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear; rather, with the temptation he will also provide a way through, so that you may be able to endure it.

Therefore, my beloved, flee from the worship of idols. I speak as to prudent people; judge for yourselves what I say.

The cup of blessing that we bless—is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? And the bread that we break—is it not a participation in the body of the Lord? [Note: [Col. 0753] The manuscripts of Curcelaeus add in Greek καὶ τοῦ ποτηρίου (“and of the cup”), which the Palatine manuscript also retains in Latin, “and of one cup.”]

Because [Col. 0753D] there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all share in the one bread. Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?

What then? Do I say that something sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything? But the things that the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to become partners with demons.

You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot share in the table of the Lord and the table of demons. Are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

“All things are permitted to me,” but not all things build up. Let no one seek his own advantage, but [Col. 0754A] that of the other.

Everything sold in the meat market, eat, asking no questions for the sake of conscience. “The earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”

If someone of the unbelievers invites you, and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience. But if someone says, “This was sacrificed to idols” [Ms. “sacrificial to idols”], do not eat it, for the sake of the one who disclosed it and for the sake of conscience. I mean not your own conscience, but that of the other.

For why should my freedom be judged by another’s conscience? If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I slandered for that for which I give thanks?

Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do everything for the glory of God. Be without offense to Jews, Greeks, and the church of God, just as I also please everyone in every way, not [Col. 0754B] seeking my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

## [Chapter XI]

Be imitators of me, as I also am of Christ. I praise you, brothers, because you remember me in everything and, just as I delivered them to you, hold fast to my instructions.

But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.

Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered disgraces his head. But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered disgraces her head; for it is one and the same as if she were shaved. For if a woman is not veiled, let her also be shorn. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her cover her head, because she is the image and glory of the man.

For man is not from woman, but woman from man. Indeed, man was not [Col. 0754C] created for the sake of woman, but woman for the sake of man. Therefore the woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.
