Therefore remember that formerly you Gentiles in the flesh, who are called the uncircumcision [Ms.: “were called”], by what is called circumcision in the flesh, made by hands [Col. 0779D]: that at that time you were without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope of the promise and without God in this world.

But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ [Col. 0780A]. For he himself is our peace, who made both one and, by abolishing the dividing wall of the barrier, the hostility in his flesh, nullified the law of commandments expressed in decrees, so that he might create the two in himself as one new man, making peace, and reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, killing the hostility in himself.

And coming, he proclaimed peace to you who were far away, and peace to those who were near. For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.

Therefore you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone. In him the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord; in him you too are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit [Ms. adds: “holy”] [Col. 0780B].

## [Chapter III]

For this reason I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles—if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of God’s grace that was given to me for you—that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote above briefly, so that, when you read, you may understand my insight into the mystery of Christ, which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men as it has now been revealed by the Spirit to his holy apostles and prophets:

that the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body, and fellow participants in his promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel. Of this I became a minister according to the gift of God’s grace, which was given to me according to the working of his power [Col. 0780C].

To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to proclaim among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ [Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “unsearchable,” a reading which recent critics insist is uniquely correct; yet the printed reading also seems equally sound, since it is derived from the verb *vestigo* (“to trace,” “to investigate).”], and to enlighten everyone concerning the stewardship of the mystery hidden from the ages in God, who created all things, so that through the Church the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places, according to the eternal purpose that he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.

In him we have boldness and access with confidence through faith in him. Therefore I ask that you not lose heart because of my tribulations for you, which are your glory.

For this reason I bend my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named, that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory [Col. 0780D], to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person, so that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts, rooted and grounded in love, so that you may be able, with all the saints, to comprehend what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge [Col. 0781A], so that you may be filled unto all the fullness of God.

Now to him who is able to do far more abundantly than all that we ask or understand, according to the power that works in us: to him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus, throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

## [Chapter IV]

Therefore I, a prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthily of the calling to which you were called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

One body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. One God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in us all [Col. 0781B].

But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ’s gift. Therefore he says:

“When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men.”

Now, “he ascended”—what does this mean except that he had also first descended into the lower regions of the earth? He who descended is also the one who ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.

And he himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets, others as evangelists, and others as shepherds and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ, until we all attain unity of faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.

Then we will no longer be children, tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine, in the wickedness of men, in craftiness directed toward the deception of error. Rather, speaking the truth in love, let us grow in every way into him who is the head, Christ. From him the whole body, joined and knit together through every supporting joint, according to the working in the measure of each individual member, produces the body’s growth for its own building up in love [Ms.: “building up”].

Therefore I say and testify in the Lord that you must no longer walk as the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their minds, having their understanding darkened, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their hearts. Having become desperate, they gave themselves over to indecency, for the working of every impurity, in greed [Col. 0781C] [Note: The same manuscript reads: “to every impurity in greed,” omitting the words “in the working of impurity,” apparently through the copyist’s carelessness; for the Greek text likewise has them.].

But you did not learn Christ in this way, if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, as the truth is in Jesus: to put off, with respect to your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted according to the desires of error. But be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who has been created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.

Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth, each one with his neighbor, because we are members of one another. Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down upon your anger. Do not give place to the devil. Let the one who was stealing steal no longer, but rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to give to the one in need.

Let no corrupt word proceed from your mouth, but only whatever is good for the building up of faith, so that it may give grace to those who hear. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and outcry and blasphemy be taken away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, compassionate, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you [Note: In agreement with some Greek books, the Palatine manuscript reads “forgave us,” rather than “forgave you.”].

## [Chapter V] [Col. 0782B]

Therefore be imitators of God, like beloved children, and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and gave himself for us as an offering and sacrifice to God for a pleasing fragrance.

But fornication and every impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints; nor obscenity, nor foolish talk, nor coarse joking, which does not belong to the matter, but rather thanksgiving.

For know this and understand: no fornicator, or impure person, or greedy person—which is the service of idols—has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God. Let no one deceive you with empty words; for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore do not become their partners.

For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light [Col. 0782C]. For the fruit of light consists in all goodness and righteousness and truth, testing what is pleasing to God. And do not participate in the unfruitful works of darkness; rather, expose them. For the things they do secretly are shameful even to speak of.

But everything that is exposed is made manifest by the light; for everything that is made manifest is light. Therefore he says:

“Awake, you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine upon you” [Note: The Palatine manuscript, rather insistently following the Greek, reads “Christ will shine upon you”: *epiphausei soi ho Christos* (“Christ will shine upon you”).].

Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as foolish people but as wise, making the most of the time, because the days are evil. For this reason do not become imprudent, but understand what the will of the Lord is.

And do not become drunk with wine, in which there is debauchery, but be filled with the Holy Spirit [Note: The epithet “holy,” which is also omitted in most Greek books, is not added in the Palatine manuscript.], speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord, always giving thanks for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God and the Father.

Be subject to one another in the fear of Christ. Let wives be subject to their husbands as to the Lord, because the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the Church. He is the savior of his body [Note: The pronoun “of it” is found neither in the better Greek books nor in the Palatine manuscript.]. But just as the Church is subject to Christ, so also let wives be subject to their husbands in everything [Col. 0783A].

Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the Church and gave himself for it, so that he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the washing of water in the word of life [Note: Here the Palatine manuscript, like the Greek text, does not have the words “of life.”], so that he might present the Church to himself in glory, not having spot or wrinkle or anything of this kind, but so that it might be holy and immaculate.

In the same way husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. For no one has ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the Church, because we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones.

For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh. This mystery is great; but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the Church.

Nevertheless, let each one of you love his wife as himself, and let the wife fear her husband [Col. 0783B] [Note: The Palatine manuscript also adds the particle “that,” in agreement with the Greek archetype.].

## [Chapter VI]

Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. “Honor your father and your mother”—which is the first commandment with a promise—“so that it may be well with you and you may live long upon the earth.”

And you, fathers [Note: The Palatine manuscript again omits the pronoun “you” here, as does the Greek text.], do not provoke your children to anger, but raise them in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.

Servants, obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your hearts, as you would Christ—not serving merely for appearances, as people-pleasers, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart, serving with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to human beings; knowing that whatever good each person does, he will receive this back from the Lord, whether servant or free.

And you, masters, do the same to them, giving up threats [Col. 0783C], knowing that both their Lord and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with him.

Finally, brothers, be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of his power. Put on the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.

Therefore take up the armor of God, so that you may be able to resist on the evil day and, having accomplished everything, to stand. Stand therefore, with your loins girded in truth and clothed with the breastplate of righteousness, and with your feet shod in readiness for the gospel of peace.

In all things take up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one [Col. 0784B]. And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit—which is the word of God—praying at every time with every prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and keeping watch in this very thing with all perseverance and supplication for all the saints.

And pray for me, that speech may be given to me in the opening of my mouth with boldness, to make known the mystery of the gospel, for which I am an ambassador in chains, so that in it I may dare to speak as I ought.

But so that you too may know what concerns me and what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything known to you. I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may know what concerns us and that he may comfort your hearts.

Peace to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord [Ms. adds: “our”] Jesus Christ. Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility. Amen.

*The Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Ephesians ends.*

[Col. 0783]

# THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE PHILIPPIANS BEGINS

## [Chapter I] [Col. 0783D]

Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

I give thanks to my God at every remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine making supplication with joy for all of you, because of your fellowship in the gospel [Note: The name “Christ,” absent from the Greek exemplar, is likewise absent from the Palatine manuscript.] from the first day until now.

I am confident of this very thing: that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion until the day of Christ Jesus. It is right for me to think this about all of you, because I have you in my heart, both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, as all of you are partners in my joy.

For God is my witness, how I long for all of you in the compassion of Jesus Christ. And this I pray: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge [Ms. adds: “all”] and in every perception, so that you may approve what is excellent, so that you may be sincere and without offense for the day of Christ, filled with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.

I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has turned out rather for the advancement of the gospel, so that my chains have become manifest in Christ throughout the whole praetorium and in all other places. And most of the brothers, trusting in the Lord because of my chains, dare much more fearlessly to speak the word of God.

Some indeed preach Christ because of envy and rivalry, but some also because of goodwill. Some do so out of love, knowing that I have been appointed for the defense of the gospel. Others proclaim Christ out of rivalry, not sincerely, supposing that they are raising up affliction for my chains.

What then? So long as Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether by pretense or by truth, in this I rejoice, and I will also rejoice. For I know that this will turn out for my salvation through your prayer and the assistance of the Spirit of Jesus Christ [Col. 0785B], according to my expectation and hope, that I will be put to shame in nothing, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.

For to me, living is Christ, and dying is gain. But if to live in the flesh is fruit of labor for me, then what I should choose I do not know. I am constrained by both: I have the desire to depart and to be with Christ, which is much better, but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.

And being confident of this, I know that I shall remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith, so that your rejoicing in Christ Jesus because of me may abound through my coming again to you.

Only live worthily of the gospel of Christ [Ms. adds: “in”], so that whether I come and see you or, being absent, hear about you, you are standing firm in one spirit, striving together for the faith of the gospel, in no way frightened by your adversaries. This is for them a cause of destruction, but for you of salvation—and this is from God. For it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him, engaged in the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear about me.

## [Chapter II]

Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, any consolation of love, any fellowship of the Spirit, any compassion and mercies [Note: In accordance with the Greek text—“and mercies”—the Palatine manuscript likewise prefers this reading], complete my joy by being of the same mind, having the same love, united in soul, thinking the one thing, doing nothing through rivalry or empty glory, but in humility considering one another superior to themselves, not each looking to his own interests but also to those of others.

Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus: who, although he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be seized, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of human beings and found in appearance as a human being.

He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, and death on a cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow—of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—and every tongue confess [Col. 0786A] that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

Therefore, my beloved—as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence but now much more in my absence—work out your salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God who works in you both to will and to accomplish, according to his good pleasure.

Do everything without murmuring and disputing, so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without reproach in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine like lights in the world, holding fast the word of life, for my glory on the day of Christ, because I did not run in vain or labor in vain.

But even if I am poured out upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and congratulate all of you. In the same way, you too rejoice and congratulate me [Col. 0786B].

I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I learn what concerns you. For I have no one so like-minded who will sincerely be concerned for you. For all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.

But you know his tested character: that as a son with his father, he served with me in the gospel. I therefore hope to send him to you as soon as I see what concerns me [Note: The words “to you,” omitted in most Greek books, are likewise absent from the Palatine manuscript.]. I trust in the Lord that I myself will also come to you soon.

But I considered it necessary to send Epaphroditus to you, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, but your apostle and minister of my need, since he was longing for all of you and was distressed because you had heard that he was ill. For indeed he was ill, nearly to the point of death; but God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.

Therefore I sent him more urgently, so that when you saw him you might rejoice again, and I might be without sorrow. Receive him therefore with all joy in the Lord, and hold such people in honor, because for the work of Christ he came near to death, risking his life so that he might complete what was lacking from you in service toward God.

## [Chapter III]

Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not burdensome for me, and it is necessary for you. Beware of dogs; beware of evil workers; beware of the mutilation.

For we are the circumcision, who serve God in the Spirit and glory in Christ Jesus and do not place confidence in the flesh [Col. 0786D]—although I myself have confidence even in the flesh.

If anyone else thinks he has confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee; according to zeal, persecuting the Church of God; according to the righteousness that is in the law, having lived without reproach.

But whatever things were gain to me, these I have considered loss because of Christ. Yet indeed I consider everything to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord [Col. 0787A]. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things and consider them rubbish, so that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ Jesus—the righteousness that is from God, based on faith—in order to know him and the power of his resurrection and the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death, if somehow I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.

Not that I have already received it or have already been perfected; but I pursue it, if somehow I may lay hold of that for which I have also been laid hold of by Christ Jesus [Note: In the Palatine manuscript: “if I may lay hold,” as in the Greek exemplar, *ei kai katalabō* (“if I may indeed lay hold”), with the word “somehow” omitted. This word is also absent from most other Latin manuscripts and from the Corbie Bibles of the Vulgate edition. Indeed, the ancient Latin Fathers do not know it; there is no need here to name them individually. One example among all is Augustine, *On the Merits and Forgiveness of Sins*, book II, chapter 13: “But I pursue it, if I may lay hold.”].

Brothers, I do not consider myself to have attained it. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead, I pursue the goal, toward the prize of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus [Col. 0787B].

Therefore, all who are perfect, let us think this way; and if you think differently in anything, God will reveal this to you also. Nevertheless, let us remain at the point to which we have attained, thinking the same thing and remaining within the same rule.

Be imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who walk in this way, as you have us for an example. For many walk—of whom I often told you, and now even with tears I say it—as enemies of the cross of Christ. Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame; they set their minds on earthly things.

But our citizenship is in heaven, from which we also await the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform the body of our humiliation, conforming it to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is also able to subject all things to himself.

## [Chapter IV] [Col. 0787C]

Therefore, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, beloved.

I urge Euodia and I entreat Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord. Yes, I also ask you, genuine companion, help them, women who labored with me in the gospel, together with Clement and my other fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.

Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice [Col. 0788A]. Let your gentleness be known to all people. The Lord is near. Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is chaste, whatever is just, whatever is holy, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good reputation—if there is any virtue and if there is any praise of discipline—think about these things. What you have learned and received and heard and seen in me, do these things; and the God of peace will be with you.

I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that at last you have flourished again in your concern for me, just as you were concerned before; but you were occupied [Col. 0788B]. I do not say this because of need, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am. I know how to be humbled, and I know how to abound; everywhere and in all things I have been instructed, both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to suffer need.

I can do all things through him who strengthens me. Nevertheless, you did well by sharing in my tribulation. You yourselves also know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in the account of giving and receiving except you alone, because even in Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my needs [Note: In Martianaeus’s edition, apparently through a typesetter’s error, it reads *qui misistis* (“you who sent”) in place of *mihi* (“to me”), and so forth.].

Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the abundant fruit credited to your account. I have everything and abound; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus what you sent, a fragrant odor, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.

And my God will fill every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus [Col. 0788C]. To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.

Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you. All the saints greet you, especially those from Caesar’s household. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

*The Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Philippians ends.*

[Col. 0787]

# THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE COLOSSIANS BEGINS

## [Chapter I] [Col. 0787D]

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the holy and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus who are at Colossae [Col. 0788D]. Grace to you and peace from God our Father [Note: The words “and the Lord Jesus Christ,” which most Greek copies also omit, are absent here from the Palatine manuscript.], and the Lord Jesus Christ.

We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you, having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love that you have for all the saints, because of the hope laid up for you in heaven, which you heard in the word of the truth of the gospel.

This gospel has come to you, just as it is in the whole world, and it bears fruit and grows, just as it does among you from the day on which you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth, as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ Jesus for you, and who also made known to us your love in the Spirit.

For this reason, from the day we heard, we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding, so that you may walk worthily, pleasing God in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God, strengthened with every power according to the might of his glory, with all strength and patience, with joy giving thanks to God the Father, who made us worthy to share in the lot of the saints in light.

He rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love, in whom we have redemption through his blood [Note: The same Palatine manuscript reads “we have redemption and forgiveness of sins,” omitting the intervening words “through his blood,” which likewise are not found in the better Greek codices.], forgiveness of sins.

He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation, because in him all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things were created through him and in him. And he is before all things, and all things hold together in him.

And he is the head of the body, the Church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead [Col. 0789C], so that he himself might hold first place in everything. For in him all fullness was pleased to dwell, and through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross, whether the things on earth or the things in heaven.

And you, when you were once alienated and enemies in mind, in evil works, he has now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and immaculate and blameless before him—if indeed you remain founded and steadfast in the faith and immovable from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which has been proclaimed in every creature under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.

Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and I complete in my flesh what is lacking in the sufferings of Christ for the sake of his body, which is the Church [Col. 0789D]. Of this I became a minister according to the stewardship of God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God: the mystery that was hidden from the ages and generations but has now been revealed to his saints.

To them God willed to make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. Him we proclaim, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus [Col. 0790A]. For this I labor, struggling according to his working, which he works in me with power.

## [Chapter II]

For I want you to know what great concern I have for you and for those who are in Laodicea and for all who have not seen my face in the flesh, so that their hearts may be comforted, instructed in love and in all the riches of the fullness of understanding, for the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ Jesus, in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.

I say this so that no one may deceive you with lofty speech. For although I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.

Therefore, just as you received Jesus Christ the Lord [Ms. adds: “our”], walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in him with thanksgiving [Col. 0790B].

See to it that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ. For in him the whole fullness of divinity dwells bodily, and you have been filled in him, who is the head of every principality and power.

In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ, having been buried with him in baptism, in which you also were raised through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.

And you, when you were dead in trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, forgiving you all trespasses, wiping out the written decree that stood against us, which was contrary to us. He removed it from our midst, fastening it to the cross, and stripping the principalities and powers, he led them away boldly, triumphing over them openly in himself.

Therefore let no one judge you concerning food or drink, or in respect of a festival or a new moon or Sabbaths, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.

Let no one defraud you, wishing to do so in humility and worship of angels, intruding into things he has not seen, vainly puffed up by the sense of his flesh, and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and built up through its joints and connections, grows with the growth of God.

Therefore, if you have died with Christ to the elements of this world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees: “Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle”—things which all perish through use, according to human commands and teachings?

These practices indeed have an appearance of wisdom in superstition and humility, and in not sparing the body [Note: The manuscript reads “and for not sparing it.” The Greek has *kai apheidōs* (“and unsparingly”).], not in any honor for the satisfaction of the flesh [Col. 0790D].

### [Chapter III]

Therefore, if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on the things that are above, not on those that are upon the earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ appears, your life, then you also will appear with him in glory.

Put to death, therefore, your members that are upon the earth: fornication, impurity, lust, evil desire, and greed, which is the service of idols. Because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. In these things you also once walked, when you were living in them. But now put away all these things as well: anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy, and shameful speech from your mouth. Do not lie to one another, stripping off the old man with his practices [Ms.: “his”], and putting on the new, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its creator.

Here there is no Gentile and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, Barbarian and Scythian, slave and free; but Christ is all things and in all.

Put on, therefore, as God’s elect, holy and beloved, compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against another. Just as the Lord forgave you, so also should you. Above all these things, have love, which is the bond of perfection. And let the peace of Christ rejoice in your hearts; into this peace you were also called in one body. And be thankful.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to God. Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter toward them. Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord. Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, lest they become discouraged. Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not serving merely for appearances, as pleasing men, but in sincerity of heart, fearing God. Whatever you do, work from the soul, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. Serve the Lord Christ. For the one who does wrong will receive what he has done unjustly, and there is no partiality with God.

Masters, provide your slaves with what is just and fair, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.

Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving. Pray at the same time for us also, that God may open for us a door for the word, so that we may speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also imprisoned, and that I may make it known as I ought to speak.

Walk wisely toward those who are outside, making the most of the time. Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.

Tychicus will make everything concerning me known to you, the most beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow slave in the Lord. I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that he may learn how things are with you and comfort your hearts, together with Onesimus, the beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything that is happening here.

Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, receive him. And Jesus, who is called Justus. These are the only ones from the circumcision who are my fellow workers for the kingdom of God; they have been a consolation to me.

Epaphras greets you, one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, always struggling for you in his prayers, so that you may stand perfect and fully assured in every will of God. For I bear him witness that he has much labor for you and for those who are in Laodicea and in Hierapolis.

Luke, the most beloved physician, greets you, as does Demas. Greet the brothers who are in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church that is in her house. When this letter has been read among you, arrange that it also be read in the church of the Laodiceans; and that you yourselves read the one from Laodicea. And say to Archippus: “See to the ministry that you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it.”

The greeting is by the hand of Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

The Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Colossians ends here.

[Col. 0791]

## THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE THESSALONIANS I BEGINS.

[Col. 0791D] [Chapter I]

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace.

We give thanks to God always for all of you, making mention of you continually in our prayers, remembering your work of faith, your labor of love, and your endurance in the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father. We know, beloved brothers of God, your election, because our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power, in the Holy Spirit, and with great fullness, just as you know what kind of people we were among you for your sake.

And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word amid great tribulation with the joy of the Holy Spirit, so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia. For the word of the Lord has sounded forth from you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith toward God has gone forth, so that we have no need to say anything.

For they themselves [Ms.: “concerning you”] report concerning us what kind of entrance we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God, and to await his Son from heaven—whom he raised from the dead—Jesus, who rescued us from the coming wrath.

### [Chapter II]

For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance among you, that it was not empty. But after we had previously suffered and been insulted—as you know—in Philippi, we had confidence in our God to speak to you the gospel of God amid much struggle [Note: In the Palatine manuscript, “much” was added in a later hand; the word is absent from the Greek text].

For our exhortation was not from error, nor from impurity, nor in deceit; but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing men, but God, who tests our hearts. For at no time did we use a speech of flattery, as you know, nor a pretext for greed—God is witness—nor did we seek glory from men, either from you or from others.

Although we could have been a burden to you as apostles of Christ, we became gentle in your midst, like a nurse cherishing her own children. So, longing for you, we were eager to impart to you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.

For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil: working night and day so as not to burden any of you, we proclaimed the gospel of God among you [Ms.: “for we proclaimed”]. You are witnesses, and God also, of how holy, just, and blameless we were toward you who believed. As you know, we exhorted and comforted each one of you, like a father his children, and testified that you should walk worthily of God, who called you into his own kingdom and glory.

For this reason we also give thanks to God without ceasing: because when you received from us the word of the hearing of God, you accepted it not as the word of men, but—as it truly is—the word of God, which is at work in you who believe.

For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus, because you too suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews, who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, persecuted us, and do not please God [Ms.: “did not please”], being opposed to all men. They prevent us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, thereby filling up their sins always. For the wrath of God has come upon them at last.

But we, brothers, being separated from you for a short time—in presence, not in heart—hastened all the more eagerly to see your face. For we wanted to come to you—I, Paul, both once and again—but Satan hindered us.

For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Are you not before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? For you are our glory and joy.

### [Chapter III]

Therefore, unable to endure any longer, we decided to remain alone in Athens, and we sent Timothy, our brother and God’s minister in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you concerning your faith, so that no one might be shaken by these tribulations. For you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.

Indeed, when we were with you, we foretold you that we were going to suffer tribulations, just as it happened, and you know it. For this reason, I too, unable to endure any longer, sent him to learn about your faith, lest perhaps the tempter had tempted you and our labor had become fruitless.

But now that Timothy has come to us from you and has announced your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, longing to see us just as we also long to see you, therefore, brothers, we were comforted concerning you in all our necessity and tribulation through your faith. For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.

For what thanksgiving can we render to God for you, in all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God, praying most earnestly night and day that we may see your face and complete what is lacking in your faith?

May God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ direct our way to you. And may the Lord multiply you and make your love [Note: The pronoun “your,” absent from the Greek text, is likewise omitted in the Palatine manuscript] abound toward one another and toward all, just as ours does toward you, so as to strengthen your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.

Amen.

### [Chapter IV]

Finally, brothers, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God, so you should walk, in order to abound more and more. For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus.

For this is the will of God: your sanctification—that you abstain from fornication, that each of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor, not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles who do not know God, and that no one transgress or defraud his brother in business. For the Lord is the avenger of all these things, as we told you beforehand and testified.

For God did not call us to impurity, but to sanctification. Therefore, whoever rejects these things rejects not man but God, who also gave his Holy Spirit within us.

Concerning brotherly love, we have no need to write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another. Indeed, you do this toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to abound more and more, to make it your aim to be quiet, to attend to your own affairs, to work with your hands, as we commanded you, and to walk honorably toward those who are outside, and to desire nothing from anyone.

We do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who sleep, so that you may not grieve like the rest who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.

For this we say to you by the word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, will not precede those who have fallen asleep. For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God. And the dead who are in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ [Note: The Palatine manuscript reads “the Lord,” closer to the Greek, Κυρίου] in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord.

Therefore comfort one another with these words.

### [Chapter V]

Concerning the times and moments, brothers, you have no need for us to write to you. For you yourselves know carefully that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction will come upon them, like labor pain upon a pregnant woman [Ms.: “a woman who is pregnant”], and they will not escape.

But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that that day might overtake you like a thief. For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness. Therefore, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us watch and be sober.

For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who are drunk, are drunk at night. But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of the hope of salvation. For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for the acquisition of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with him.

Therefore comfort one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.

We ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you, preside over you in the Lord, and admonish you, and to hold them in the highest regard in love because of their work. Be at peace with them.

And we ask you, brothers: admonish the disorderly, comfort the fainthearted, support the weak, and be patient toward all. See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone; but always pursue what is good toward one another and toward all.

Rejoice always. Pray without ceasing. Give thanks in everything, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for all of you. Do not extinguish the Spirit. Do not despise prophecies. Test everything; hold fast to what is good. Abstain from every form of evil.

May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, so that your spirit, soul, and body may be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Faithful is the one who called you; he will also accomplish it.

Brothers, pray for us. Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. I adjure you by the Lord that this letter be read to all the holy brothers.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you [Palatine manuscript likewise has “with all of you” instead of “with you”]. Amen.

The First Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Thessalonians ends here.

[Col. 0795]

## THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO THE THESSALONIANS II BEGINS.

[Col. 0795D] [Chapter I]

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace from our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing greatly and the love of each one of you toward one another is increasing, so that we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God, because of your endurance and faith [Note: The seemingly superfluous little word “and” is absent from both the Greek text and the Palatine manuscript] in all your persecutions and tribulations that you are enduring. These are evidence of God’s righteous judgment, so that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer.

Since it is indeed just with God to repay tribulation to those who trouble you, and to grant relief to you who are troubled, together with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of his power, in flaming fire, bringing vengeance upon those [Ms.: “concerning these”] who do not know God and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ [Note: The name “Christ” is omitted here in certain Greek copies and in the Palatine manuscript]. They will suffer the punishment of eternal destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he comes to be glorified in his saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed, because our testimony among you was believed on that day.

For this reason we also always pray for you, that our God may deem you worthy of his calling [The Palatine manuscript, along with several Greek books, omits “our”] and may fulfill every good purpose and work of faith in power, so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

### [Chapter II]

We ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him, that you not be quickly shaken from your mind or terrified, either by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter supposedly sent by us, as though the day of the Lord were imminent.

Let no one deceive you in any way, for unless the apostasy comes first and the man of sin, the son of perdition, is revealed—the one who opposes and exalts himself above everything that is called God or worshiped, so that he sits in the temple of God, presenting himself as though he were God—you do not remember that, when I was still with you, I told you these things? [The Palatine manuscript has the plural: “when we were still with you, we were telling you these things,” etc.]

And now you know what restrains him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of iniquity is already at work; only let the one who now restrains continue to restrain until he is removed from the midst. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming.

His coming is according to the working of Satan, with every power, signs, and lying wonders, and with every deceit of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. And for this reason God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe the lie [Ms.: “And therefore”; Greek likewise: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο], so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but consented to unrighteousness.

But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by God, because God chose you as firstfruits for salvation [Note: Here, and two verses later, the Palatine manuscript, together with certain Greek copies, reads “us” for “you”], in sanctification of the Spirit and belief in the truth. For this he also called you through our gospel, for the acquisition of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Therefore, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught, whether by word or by our letter.

May our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal consolation and good hope by grace, encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.

### [Chapter III]

Finally, brothers, pray for us, so that the word of God may run and be glorified, just as it is among you, and that we may be delivered from troublesome and evil men, for faith does not belong to all.

But God is faithful, who will strengthen you and guard you from evil [The Palatine manuscript, corrected in a later hand, reads “The Lord is faithful” instead of “God”; likewise the Greek has Κύριος]. We have confidence in you in the Lord that you are doing and will do what we command.

May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and the endurance of Christ.

We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw from every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the tradition that they received from us. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not disorderly among you. Nor did we eat anyone’s bread without paying for it; rather, with labor and toil, working night and day so as not to burden any of you.

This was not because we lacked authority, but so that we might give you an example for you to imitate us. For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: if anyone does not want to work, neither should he eat.

For we hear that some among you are walking disorderly, doing no work but meddling in other people’s affairs. To such persons we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ that, working quietly, they should eat their own bread.

But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good. If anyone does not obey our word through this letter, mark that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed. Do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.

May the Lord of peace himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with all of you.

The greeting is by the hand of Paul; this is the sign in every letter. Thus I write.

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.

The Second Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Thessalonians ends here.

[Col. 0797]

## THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO TIMOTHY I BEGINS.

[Col. 0797C] [Chapter I]

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope, to Timothy, a beloved son in faith. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

As I urged you to remain in Ephesus when I was going into Macedonia, so that you might command certain persons not to teach differently and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which produce disputes rather than God’s edification, which is in faith, 

The goal of the commandment is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and an unfeigned faith. Some, having strayed from these things, have turned aside to empty talk, wishing to be teachers of the law, understanding neither what they say nor concerning what they make assertions.

But we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, knowing this: that the law is not established for the righteous, but for the unrighteous and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the wicked and defiled, parricides and matricides, murderers, fornicators, men who lie with males, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine, which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.

I give thanks to him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he considered me faithful, appointing me to the ministry [Ms.: “who considered me”]. I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man; but I received the mercy of God [Note: The name “God” is omitted here in the Palatine manuscript, as also in the Greek text], because I acted ignorantly in unbelief. The grace of our Lord overflowed exceedingly, with faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.

The saying is trustworthy and worthy of all acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first. But for this reason I received mercy, so that Christ Jesus might first display in me all patience, as an example for those who would believe in him for eternal life [Ms. omits “Jesus”].

To the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen.

This command I entrust to you, Timothy my son, according to the preceding prophecies concerning you, so that you may wage the good warfare in them, holding faith and a good conscience. Some, rejecting this, have suffered shipwreck concerning the faith. Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan, so that they may learn not to blaspheme.

### [Chapter II]

Therefore, first of all, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and for all who are in positions of authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all piety and chastity.

For this is good and acceptable before God our Savior, who wishes all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humanity, the human being Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, a testimony at its proper times.

For this testimony I was appointed a herald and apostle—I speak the truth, I do not lie—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth [In the Palatine manuscript: “whose testimony,” as also in several Greek books, οὗ τὸ μαρτύριον. Shortly afterward, where it says “I speak the truth,” “in Christ” is added; these words are also present in the Greek text].

Therefore I wish men to pray in every place, lifting up pure hands without anger or dispute.

Likewise also women should adorn themselves in respectable clothing, with modesty and sobriety, adorning themselves not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly clothing, but—as is fitting for women professing godliness—through good works.

Let a woman learn in silence with all submission. I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to remain in silence. For Adam was formed first, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been deceived, came into transgression.

But she will be saved through childbearing, if she remains in faith, love, and sanctification with sobriety [Elsewhere the same translator consistently renders “sobriety” either as “with modesty,” as in the Epistle to Salvina, or as “with chastity,” as elsewhere. Indeed, after citing this verse in Book III Against Jovinianus—“if they remain in … sanctification with chastity”—he adds, as it is incorrectly found in Latin manuscripts: “sobriety is to be read, not chastity,” that is, σωφροσύνη].

### [Chapter III]

The saying is trustworthy: if anyone desires the office of bishop, he desires a good work. Therefore the bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, respectable, modest, hospitable, able to teach, not addicted to wine, not violent, but gentle; not quarrelsome, not greedy, governing his own household well, having children who are submissive with all chastity.

But if anyone does not know how to govern his own household, how will he care for the church of God? [The Palatine manuscript, in a later correction, reads “will you exercise care?”]

He must not be a recent convert, lest, being puffed up, he fall into the judgment of the devil. He must also have a good testimony from those who are outside, so that he does not fall into reproach and the devil’s snare.

Likewise, deacons must be respectable, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, and not pursuing dishonest gain. They must hold the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience. And let these also first be tested; then let them serve, being blameless.

Likewise, women must be respectable, not slanderers, sober, faithful in everything. Let deacons be husbands of one wife, governing their children and their own households well. For those who have served well acquire for themselves a good standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.

I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon. But if I delay, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the household of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

And plainly great is the mystery of piety: which was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was proclaimed among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, and taken up in glory.

### [Chapter IV]

Now the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith, giving attention to deceitful spirits and teachings of demons, through the hypocrisy of liars whose conscience has been seared, forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who know the truth.

For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving; for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.

By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of faith and of the good doctrine that you have followed. Avoid foolish and old-womanish myths; exercise yourself in piety.

For bodily exercise is useful for a little, but piety is useful for everything, holding the promise of life, both of the present and of the future. The saying is trustworthy and worthy of all acceptance.

For to this end we labor and are reproached, because we hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of believers.

Command and teach these things. Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the faithful in word, conduct, love, faith, and chastity. Until I come, attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching. Do not neglect the grace that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

Meditate on these things; be occupied with them, so that your progress may be evident to all. Pay attention to yourself and to the doctrine; persist in them. For by doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

### [Chapter V]

Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father; younger men as brothers; older women as mothers; younger women as sisters, with all chastity.

Honor widows who are truly widows. But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let her first learn to manage her own household and to repay her parents in kind, for this is acceptable before God.

But the woman who is truly a widow and desolate should hope in God and continue in supplications and prayers night and day. For she who lives in luxury is dead while she lives. Command these things also, so that they may be blameless.

But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

Let a widow be enrolled who is not less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one man, bearing witness through good works: if she has raised children, shown hospitality, washed the feet of the saints, assisted those suffering tribulation, and followed every good work.

But avoid younger widows. For when they have become wanton against Christ, they want to marry, incurring condemnation because they have set aside their first faith. At the same time they also learn to go around from house to house—not only idle, but also talkative and meddlesome, speaking about things that ought not to be said.

Therefore I want younger women to marry, bear children, manage households, and give the adversary no occasion for reproach. For some have already turned back after Satan.

If any believer has widows, let him provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may provide for those who are truly widows.

Let presbyters who preside well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and teaching. For Scripture says: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing” [The same manuscript prefers “You shall not bridle” instead of “You shall not bind”; Greek manuscripts also vary between φιμώσεις and κημώσεις]. And: “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”

Do not receive an accusation against a presbyter except on the testimony of two or three witnesses. Rebuke sinners before everyone, so that the others may also have fear.

I testify before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality. Do not lay hands quickly on anyone, nor share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.

Do not continue drinking only water, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.

The sins of some people are manifest, going before them to judgment; but some they also follow afterward. Likewise, good works are manifest, and those that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.

## [Chapter VI]

Let all who are slaves under the yoke regard their own masters as worthy of every honor, lest the name of the Lord and the teaching be blasphemed. Those who have believing masters must not despise them because they are brothers; rather, they must serve them all the more, because those who receive the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.

If anyone teaches otherwise and does not assent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the teaching that accords with godliness, he is proud, knowing nothing, but sickly over controversies and disputes about words. From these arise envy, quarrels, blasphemies, evil suspicions, and conflicts among people corrupted in mind and deprived of truth, who suppose that godliness is gain. But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and undoubtedly we can take nothing out of it. But having food and coverings, with these we are content.

For those who wish to become rich fall into temptation, into the devil’s snare, and into many useless and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction. For covetousness is the root of all evils; in seeking it, some have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains [Col. 0802C]. But you, man of God, flee these things; pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, gentleness. Fight the good fight of faith; seize eternal life, to which you were called and concerning which you made the good confession before many witnesses.

I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who made the good confession in his testimony before Pontius Pilate, that you keep the commandment spotless and irreproachable until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, which, at its proper times, the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords, will show: he alone possesses immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen [Note: [Col. 0802D] The Palatine manuscript and the Greek text omit the word “but.”] nor can see. To him be honor and everlasting dominion. Amen.

[Col. 0802D] Charge the rich of this age not to be high-minded and not to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who abundantly provides us with all things for enjoyment: to do good, to become rich in good works, to give readily, to share, storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, that they may lay hold of true life. O Timothy, guard the deposit entrusted to you, avoiding profane novelties of speech and the oppositions of falsely named knowledge; by professing it some have fallen away from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

Here ends the First Epistle of the Blessed Apostle Paul to Timothy.

[Col. 0803]

# THE SECOND EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO TIMOTHY BEGINS

[Col. 0803A] ## [Chapter I]

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus, to Timothy, beloved son: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

I give thanks to God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience, because [Ms. “whom”] I remember you without ceasing in my prayers night and day, longing to see you, mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy; recalling the unfeigned faith that is in you, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and, I am sure, in you also. For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands. For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power [Col. 0803B] and love and self-control.

Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but share in the labors of the Gospel according to the power of God, who saved us and called us with a holy calling, [Note: [Col. 0803C] In accordance with the Greek text, the Palatine manuscript omits the pronoun “his.”] not according to our works but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times. But it has now been made manifest through the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ, who indeed destroyed death but brought life and incorruptibility to light through the Gospel, for which I was appointed preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles. For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to guard my deposit until that day.

[Col. 0803C] Hold the pattern of sound words which you heard from me, in faith and love in Christ Jesus. Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. You know this: all who are in Asia have turned away from me, among them Phygelus and Hermogenes. May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain; rather, when he came to Rome, he diligently sought me and found me. May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord [Ms. “God”] on that day. And how much he ministered to me at Ephesus, you know better.

## [Chapter II]

Therefore, my son, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. What you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be competent to teach others also [Col. 0804A]. Labor as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No one serving as a soldier of God entangles himself in worldly business, so that he may please the one to whom he has proved himself. Likewise, one who competes in the contest is not crowned unless he has competed lawfully. The laboring farmer ought first to receive from the fruits. Understand what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.

Remember that the Lord Jesus Christ rose from the dead, of David’s seed, according to my Gospel, for which I labor even to chains, as though I were an evildoer; but the word of God is not bound. Therefore I endure all things for the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with heavenly glory. The saying is faithful: for if we died with him, we shall also live with him; if [Note: [Col. 0803C] The Palatine manuscript reads “if we endure,” as does the Greek, εἰ ὑπομένομεν.] we endure, we shall also reign with him; [Col. 0804B] if we deny him, he too will deny us; if we do not believe, he remains faithful: he cannot deny himself.

Remind them of these things, charging them before the Lord. Do not contend with words; it is useful for nothing except the overthrow of the hearers. Take care to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed worker, rightly handling the word of truth. But avoid profane, empty talk [Ms. “vain talk”], for it advances greatly into ungodliness, and their word spreads like a cancer. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus, who have fallen away from the truth, saying that the resurrection has already occurred, and [Note: [Col. 0804C] Again the same manuscript reads “in an instant,” and “they overthrew,” with the Greek καὶ ἀνατρέπουσι. Shortly afterward it reads “stood” for “stands,” and a little later “everyone who invokes” for “names,” less correctly in relation to the Greek.] have overthrown the faith of some. Yet the firm foundation of God stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,” and “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity.”

[Col. 0804C] In a great house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also wooden and earthenware ones; some indeed for honor, others for dishonor. If anyone therefore cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified and useful to the Lord, ready for every good work. Flee youthful desires; pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart. Avoid foolish and undisciplined questions, knowing that they produce quarrels. But the Lord’s servant must not quarrel; rather, he must be gentle toward all, apt to teach, patient, correcting with gentleness those who resist the truth, lest God perhaps grant them repentance unto knowledge of the truth, and they return to their senses [Col. 0805A] from the devil’s snare, by whom they are held captive [Ms. “captured”] for his will.

## [Chapter III]

But know this: in the last days perilous times will come. People will be self-loving, covetous, boastful, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without natural affection, without peace, slanderers, unrestrained, savage, without kindness, traitors, reckless, swollen with pride, lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God, having an appearance of godliness but denying its power. Avoid these also. For among them are those who creep into houses and lead captive little women burdened with sins, led by various desires, always learning and never able to come to knowledge of the truth.

As Jannes and Mambres [Col. 0805B] resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth: people corrupt in mind, disqualified concerning the faith. But they will proceed no further, for their folly will become evident to all, as theirs also was. But you have followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, patience, persecutions, sufferings—such as happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra; what persecutions I endured, and from them all the Lord delivered me. Indeed, all who wish to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. But evil people and deceivers will advance to worse, deceiving and being deceived. You, however, remain in what you learned and what was entrusted to you, knowing from whom you learned it, and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which can instruct you [Col. 0805C] for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. All Scripture, divinely inspired, is useful for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness, so that the person of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.

## [Chapter IV]

I testify before God and Jesus Christ, who is to judge the living and the dead, by [Col. 0806A] his appearing and his kingdom: preach the word; persist in season and out of season; reprove, entreat, rebuke, with all patience and teaching. For a time will come when they will not endure sound teaching, but, according to their own desires, will heap up teachers for themselves, with itching ears. They will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn aside to fables. But you, be watchful in all things, labor, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. Be sober.

For I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course; I have kept the faith. Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day—and not only to me, but also to all who love his appearing. Make haste to come to me soon. For Demas has deserted me, loving [Col. 0806B] this age, and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia. Luke alone is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry. But I sent Tychicus to Ephesus. When you come, bring the cloak which I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments. Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm; the Lord will repay him according to his works. You too must avoid him, for he strongly opposed our words.

At my first defense no one stood with me, but all deserted me; may it not be charged against them. But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be fulfilled and all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered from the lion’s mouth. The Lord delivered me from every evil work and will save me into his heavenly kingdom [Col. 0806C]. To him be glory for ages of ages. Amen. Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus. Erastus remained at Corinth; but I left Trophimus sick at Miletus. Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers greet you. The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

[Col. 0805] Here ends the Second Epistle of the Blessed Apostle Paul to Timothy.

[Col. 0805]

# THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL TO TITUS BEGINS

[Col. 0805D] ## [Chapter I]

Paul, servant of God and apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s elect and the knowledge of the truth which accords with godliness, in hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal times, but made manifest in his own times by the preaching of his word, which was entrusted to me by command of God our Savior: to Titus, beloved son according to a common faith, grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.

[Col. 0806D] For this reason I left you in Crete: that you might set right what remained unfinished and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you. If anyone is without accusation, husband of one wife, having faithful children, [Note: [Col. 0805] In accordance with the Greek text, the Palatine manuscript reads with the negative particle: “not under an accusation,” μὴ ἐν κατηγορίᾳ.] not under accusation of debauchery or insubordination. For a bishop must be without accusation, as God’s steward: not proud, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain; but hospitable, kind, sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled, [Col. 0807A] holding firmly to the faithful word which accords with the teaching, so that he may be able both to exhort in sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict.

For there are many [Note: [Col. 0807C] The Palatine manuscript likewise lacks the word “also,” which is absent from certain Greek books.] also who are disobedient, empty talkers, and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision, who must be rebuked; they overthrow whole households, teaching what ought not to be taught for shameful gain. One of them, their own prophet, said: “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.” This testimony is true. For this reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in faith, not attending to Jewish fables and commandments of people who turn away from the truth.
