Where is this written, unless in verse 7 of chapter 5 of the First Epistle of Saint John? Why is that testimony cited by Victor of Vita, Fulgentius, and other ancient writers? Will you say that they fabricated it, or adapted it to their own opinions, without being guilty of rashness? Our predecessors did not act in this way; they took care to collect from the Fathers many passages in confirmation of the testimony that they read in John’s Epistle.

A witness is the very ancient and excellent Corbie manuscript, which contains in one volume the Acts of the Apostles, the seven Canonical Epistles, and the Apocalypse of John; it is numbered 23 in our Saint-Germain Library. On its final page and outermost folio, the copyist of the volume appended the following testimonies, so that the authority of the Scripture about which we are now speaking might be confirmed. I found them written there as follows:

‘For there are three who bear witness on earth: the Spirit, the water, and the blood. And these three are one in Christ Jesus. And there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit. And these three are one.

‘Likewise: These are they who testify in heaven: the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.

‘Athanasius: There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, and the Word, and the Spirit; and in Christ Jesus they are one.

‘Fulgentius: There are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Spirit; and the three are one.’

We freely confess that the simple faith and diligence of this copyist pleased us more than all the elaborate apparatus of words of the recent critic, by which he strives to diminish the authority of the sacred text in the First Epistle of Blessed John.

And it is not without some sorrow of heart that we can see the author of the Catholic communion straining every nerve to prove that these words of the First Epistle of John, chapter 5, verse 7—‘For there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one’—were added through the rashness of ancient scribes and were not written by the sacred author.

Alas! Would the Church of God, the pillar and foundation of truth, thrust the additions of scribes upon us as sacred text, especially in those statements of Holy Scripture upon which the faith of the most holy Trinity depends? ‘But,’ he says, ‘the authority of the Church today imposes that testimony upon us as authentic Scripture.’ As though any authority of the Church of Christ could impose corruptions, interpolations, and so forth...
may turn copyists’ additions into the word of God and into canonical Scripture. Nothing is said more obtusely; nothing could be more destructive to faith in the divine Scriptures. Therefore we wish more sound counsels for the learned man who thought that, in his *Critical History of Sacred Scripture*, he had rendered a service to God—even though many things are found in his labors that undermine the traditions of the ancient Fathers and the authority of the Scriptures.”

[Col. 0821C] The order among the Greeks, who possess sound understanding in full and follow the right faith, is not the same as that found in the Latin manuscripts for the seven Epistles [Col. 0822C] now called Catholic. For, since [Mart.: “because”] Peter [Col. 0823A] is first in the number of the apostles, his Epistles too are first in the order of the others. But just as [Col. 0824A] some time ago we corrected the Evangelists in accordance with the line of truth, so, with God’s help, we have restored these Epistles to their proper order. [Col. 0825A] One of them is James’s, two are Peter’s, three are John’s, and one is Jude’s. If these had been translated into Latin speech by their interpreters as they had been arranged by them, faithfully as well, they would neither create ambiguity [Col. 0826A] for readers nor would the variety of expressions contend with itself [Al.: “the varieties would contend”]: especially [Col. 0828A] in that passage where we read that the unity of the Trinity is set forth in the First Epistle of John. In that passage as well we have discovered that much error was made by unfaithful [Col. 0829A] translators, contrary to the truth of the faith: [Note: [Col. 0830D] The manuscript of the Holy Cross has only the words for three things; others have “only the words for three things.” Then, in their own edition, they inserted them and immediately afterward omitted them.] they inserted only three terms, namely, [Col. 0830A] water, blood, and spirit, in their edition, while omitting the testimony of the Father, the Word, and the Spirit. In this testimony Catholic faith is especially strengthened, and the one divine substance of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is demonstrated. As for the other Epistles, how far the edition of others differs from ours I leave to the reader’s judgment. But you, virgin of Christ, Eustochium, while you earnestly seek from me the truth of Scripture, expose my old age, in a certain sense, to be gnawed by the teeth of the envious, who declare me a falsifier and corrupter of the holy Scriptures. But in such a work I neither fear the envy of my rivals nor will I deny the truth of holy Scripture to those who ask for it.

[Col. 0831]

## The Catholic Epistle of Blessed James the Apostle Begins

[Col. 0831B] **Chapter I.** James, servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes that are in the Dispersion: greetings. Consider it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance. And let endurance have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing. If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all and does not reproach anyone, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, without doubting; for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind. Therefore let that person not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord. A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.

But let the lowly brother glory in his exaltation, and the rich in his humiliation, [Col. 0831C] because he will pass away like the flower of grass. For the sun rises with its heat and dries up the grass; its flower falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So also will the rich man wither in his pursuits. Blessed is the man who endures temptation, because, when he has been tested, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love him. Let no one, when he is tempted, say, “I am being tempted by God.” For God is not a tempter of evil, and he himself tempts no one. Rather, each person is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire. Then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it has been completed, produces death.

Therefore, my most beloved brothers, do not be deceived. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or shadow caused by turning. For of his own will he begot us by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of first fruits of his creation.

You know this, my most beloved brothers. Let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger. For human anger does not accomplish the justice of God. Therefore, putting away all uncleanness and abundance of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which can save your souls. Be doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he will be compared to a man observing the face of his birth in a mirror: he observed himself, went away, and immediately forgot what he was like. [Col. 0832B] But the one who has looked into the perfect law of freedom and has persevered in it, not becoming a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, will be blessed in his deed.

If anyone thinks that he is religious but does not bridle his tongue, deceiving his own heart, that person’s religion is worthless. Religion pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself undefiled by this world.

**Chapter II.** My brothers, do not hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality. For if a man wearing a gold ring and splendid clothing enters your assembly, and a poor man in dirty clothing also enters, and you look upon the one wearing the splendid clothing and say to him, [Col. 0832C] “You sit here in a good place,” while you say to the poor man, “You stand there,” or, “Sit beneath my footstool,” are you not judging among yourselves and becoming judges with evil thoughts?

Listen, my most beloved brothers: has God not chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that God promised to those who love him? But you have dishonored the poor. Do not the rich oppress you by their power, and do they not themselves drag you into the courts? Do they not themselves blaspheme the good name that has been invoked over you?

If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scriptures, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well. But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors. For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all. For the one who said, “You shall not commit adultery,” also said, “You shall not kill.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.

So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom. For judgment is without mercy to the one who has not shown mercy; but mercy triumphs over judgment.

What benefit is it, my brothers, if someone says that he has faith but has no works? Can faith save him? If a brother or sister is naked and lacks daily food, and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; warm yourselves and be filled,” but you do not give them what the body needs, what benefit is it? So faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

[Col. 0833A] But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you my faith by my works. You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe, and they tremble. But do you wish to know, O empty man, that faith without works is dead? Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered his son Isaac upon the altar? You see that faith was working together with his works, and by works faith was brought to completion. And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.

You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone. Likewise, was not Rahab the prostitute justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out by another route? [Col. 0833B] For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead.

**Chapter III.** Do not become many teachers, my brothers, knowing that we shall receive a greater judgment. For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in speech, that person is perfect, able also to guide the whole body with a bridle. If we put bits into horses’ mouths so that they obey us, we guide their whole bodies. Look also at ships: although they are large and driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes. So also the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things.

See how great a fire sets alight how great a forest! And the tongue is a fire; the tongue is the universe of wickedness. [Col. 0833C] The tongue is placed among our members; it stains the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of our birth, being set on fire by Gehenna.

For every kind of beasts and birds, of reptiles and other creatures, is tamed and has been tamed by human nature. But no human being can tame the tongue: a restless evil, full of deadly poison. With it we bless God and the Father, and with it we curse human beings, who have been made in the likeness of God. From the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing. This ought not to be so, my brothers.

Can a spring from the same opening pour forth sweet and bitter water? Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce grapes, or a vine figs? So neither can salt water produce sweet water.

Who is wise and disciplined among you? Let him show his work by good conduct, in the meekness of wisdom. But if you have bitter jealousy and contention in your hearts, do not boast and be liars against the truth. This is not the wisdom descending from above, but earthly, natural, demonic. For where jealousy and contention are, there are instability and every evil work.

But the wisdom from above is first chaste, then peaceable, gentle, compliant, in agreement with what is good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging, without hypocrisy. The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

**Chapter IV.** From where do wars and quarrels arise among you? Are they not from this—from your desires that wage war in your members? You desire and do not have; you kill and are jealous and cannot obtain; you quarrel and wage war, and you do not have because you do not ask. You ask and do not receive because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your desires.

Adulterers, do you not know that friendship with this world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wishes to be a friend of this world makes himself an enemy of God. Or do you suppose that Scripture speaks in vain: “The spirit that dwells in you desires jealously”? But he gives greater grace. Therefore it says: “God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble.”

Submit yourselves, therefore, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, double-minded people. Be miserable, mourn, and weep; let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak evil of one another, brothers. The one who speaks evil of a brother or judges his brother speaks evil of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge. There is one lawgiver and judge, who can destroy and save. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

Now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to that city, spend a year there, conduct business, and make a profit,” you do not know what tomorrow will bring. For what is your life? It is a vapor that appears for a little while and then vanishes. Instead, you ought to say, [Col. 0834C] “If the Lord wills, and if we live, we shall do this or that.” But now you boast in your arrogance. Every such boasting is evil. Therefore, for one who knows how to do good and does not do it, it is sin.

**Chapter V.** Come now, rich people, weep and howl over your miseries that are coming upon you. Your riches have rotted, and your garments have been eaten by moths. Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wrath for yourselves in the last days.

Look: the wages of the laborers who harvested your fields, wages defrauded by you, cry out; and their cry has entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth. You have feasted upon the earth and nourished your hearts in luxury on the day of slaughter. You have condemned and killed the righteous, and he did not resist you.

Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look: the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, patiently enduring until he receives the early and late rain. You too must be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near. Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look: the judge stands before the door.

Take, brothers, as an example of suffering evil, labor, and patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord. Look: we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of Job’s endurance and have seen the Lord’s purpose, because the Lord is compassionate and merciful.

Above all, my brothers, do not swear, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your speech be, “Yes, yes,” and, “No, no,” so that you may not fall under judgment. Is any of you sorrowful? Let him pray. Is he cheerful? Let him sing psalms. Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him.

Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be saved. [Col. 0836A] For the continual prayer of a righteous person has great power. Elijah was a human being like us, subject to suffering; and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain upon the earth, and it did not rain for three years and six months. Then he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

My brothers, if anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back, he should know that whoever turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.

[Col. 0835] The Catholic Epistle of Blessed James the Apostle Ends.

[Col. 0835]

## The First Epistle of Blessed Peter the Apostle Begins

[Col. 0835B] **Chapter I.** Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect exiles of the Dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, for sanctification by the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace and peace be multiplied to you.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has regenerated us to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, to an incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading inheritance, kept in the heavens in you, [Col. 0835C] who are guarded by the power of God through faith for salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time. In this you will rejoice, though now, if necessary, you are grieved for a little while by various trials, so that the testing of your faith, much more precious than gold—which is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

Though you have not seen him, you love him; though you do not see him now, you believe in him, and, believing, you will rejoice with inexpressible and glorified joy, receiving the end of your faith, the salvation of your souls. Concerning this salvation the prophets searched and examined carefully, who prophesied of the grace destined for you, searching what time or what circumstances the Spirit of Christ within them was indicating, when he foretold the sufferings destined for Christ and the subsequent glories. To them it was revealed that they were serving not themselves but you with those things that have now been announced to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things into which angels desire to look.

[Col. 0835D] Therefore, girding the loins of your mind, being perfectly sober, hope in the grace being offered to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ. As obedient children, do not conform yourselves to the former desires of your ignorance; but, according to the one who called you, the Holy One, be holy yourselves in all your conduct, because it is written, “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”

And if you call upon as Father the one who judges impartially according to each person’s work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourn. Knowing that you were not redeemed from your vain conduct inherited from your ancestors with perishable things, gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of an unblemished and undefiled lamb, [Col. 0836B] foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world but manifested in the last times for your sake. Through him you are faithful in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.

Having purified your souls in obedience to love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart, as brothers. You have been born again, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God. For “all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls.” [Col. 0836C] But the word of the Lord remains forever. And this is the word that was preached to you.

**Chapter II.** Therefore, putting away all malice, all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and every slander, like newborn infants desire rational, guileless milk, so that by it you may grow into salvation, if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.

As you come to him, a living stone rejected by human beings but chosen and honored by God, you yourselves also, like living stones, are being built up into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Therefore Scripture contains this: “Behold, I place in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious; and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”

Therefore, honor belongs to you who believe. But for those who do not believe: “The stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner,” and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense” to those who stumble at the word and do not believe in that to which they were appointed.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for acquisition, so that you may proclaim the virtues of the one who called you from darkness into his marvelous [Col. 0837A] light. Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not obtained mercy, but now you have obtained mercy.

Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and pilgrims, to abstain from fleshly desires that wage war against the soul. Maintain good conduct among the nations, so that, in the matter in which they speak against you as evildoers, observing your good works, they may glorify God on the day of visitation.

Therefore submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human creature, whether to the king as supreme or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of the good. For this is the will of God: that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people, as having freedom as a veil for wickedness, but as servants of God. Honor everyone; love the brotherhood; fear God; honor the king.

Servants, submit yourselves with all fear to your masters, not only to the good and gentle but also to the difficult. For this is grace: if, because of consciousness of God, someone endures sorrows while suffering unjustly. For what credit is there if, when you sin and are beaten, you endure it? But if, when doing good, you patiently endure suffering, this is grace before God.

For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example so that you might follow his footsteps. He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth. When he was reviled, he did not revile in return; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but handed himself over to the one judging him unjustly. He himself bore our sins in his body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live for righteousness. By his bruise you have been healed. [Col. 0837C] For you were like wandering sheep, but now you have returned to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.

**Chapter III.** Likewise, let wives be subject to their husbands, so that even if some do not believe the word, they may be won without a word through the conduct of their wives, when they observe your chaste conduct in fear. Let their adornment not be outward—braiding of hair, wearing gold, or putting on garments—but the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptibility of a quiet and gentle spirit, which is precious in the sight of God.

For in this way formerly the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves, subject to their own husbands. Thus Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him “lord.” You have become her daughters by doing good and not fearing any disturbance.

Likewise, husbands, live together with your wives according to understanding, showing honor to the female vessel as to a weaker one, since they are also co-heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.

Finally, all of you be united, compassionate, loving the brotherhood, merciful, gentle, and humble, not repaying evil for evil or insult for insult, but, on the contrary, blessing, because you were called to inherit a blessing. For whoever wishes to love life and to see good days must restrain his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit. Let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are toward their prayers; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.

And who is there to harm you if you are zealous for what is good? But even if you suffer because of righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear their fear, and do not be troubled. Sanctify Christ the Lord in your hearts, always ready to make a defense to everyone who asks you for an account of the hope that is in you, but with gentleness and fear, keeping a good conscience, so that, in the matter in which they slander you, those who malign your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.

For it is better, if the will of God should will it, to suffer while doing good than while doing evil. For Christ also died once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, so that he might bring us to God, put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit. In that state he also went and preached to the spirits who were in prison, who formerly had been disobedient when God’s patience waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built. In it a few—that is, eight souls—were saved through water.

This baptism, corresponding to that figure, now saves you also: not the removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who is at the right hand of God, having swallowed up death so that we might become heirs of eternal life, having gone into heaven, with angels, authorities, and powers subjected to him.

**Chapter IV.** Therefore, since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same disposition, because whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sins, so as to live the remaining time in the flesh no longer for human desires but for the will of God.

For the past time is sufficient for carrying out the will of the nations, for those who walked in debauchery, desires, drunkenness, revelries, drinking bouts, and unlawful worship of idols. They are astonished that you do not run with them into the same flood of debauchery, and they blaspheme. They will give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

For this reason the gospel was preached even to the dead, so that, although they might be judged according to human standards in the flesh, they might live according to God in the spirit.

The end of all things has drawn near. Therefore be prudent and watchful in prayers. Above all, have constant mutual love among yourselves, because love covers a multitude of sins. Be hospitable to one another without grumbling. As each has received a gift, administer it to one another as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. If anyone speaks, let it be as the words of God; if anyone serves, let it be from the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.

Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal taking place among you for your testing, as though something strange were happening to you. Rather, rejoice insofar as you share in Christ’s sufferings, so that you may also rejoice and exult at the revelation of his glory. If you are reproached in the name of Christ, you will be blessed, because the Spirit of God, who is the Spirit of glory and power, rests upon you.

Let none of you suffer as a murderer, thief, slanderer, or coveter of what belongs to others. But if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; rather, let him glorify God in this name. For it is time for judgment to begin from the house of God. And if it begins first with us, what will be the end of those who do not believe the gospel of God? And if the righteous will scarcely be saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?

Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to a faithful Creator in good works.

**Chapter V.** Therefore I urge the elders among you—I who am a fellow elder and a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and also a participant in the glory that is to be revealed—[Col. 0839B] shepherd the flock of God that is among you, exercising oversight not under compulsion but willingly according to God; not for the sake of shameful gain but eagerly; not as domineering over the clergy but becoming examples to the flock from the heart. And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

Likewise, younger men, submit yourselves to the elders. All of you instill humility toward one another, because God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you at the time of visitation, casting all your anxiety upon him, because he cares for you.

Be sober and watchful. For your adversary the devil, like a roaring lion, prowls about, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being endured by your brotherhood throughout the world.

But the God of all grace, who called us into his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little, will himself perfect, strengthen, establish, and make you firm. To him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.

Through Silvanus, the faithful brother, as I consider him, I have written briefly to you, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand. The church that is chosen together with you in Babylon greets you, and so does Mark, my son. Greet one another with a holy kiss. Grace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

[Col. 0839] The First Epistle of Blessed Peter the Apostle Ends.

[Col. 0839]

## The Second Epistle of Blessed Peter the Apostle Begins

[Col. 0839C] **Chapter I.** Simon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained with us a faith equal in honor through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ. Grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus Christ our Lord.

Since his divine power has granted us everything pertaining to life and godliness through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue, through which he has given us the greatest and precious promises, so that through these you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption in the world caused by desire, apply every effort to supply virtue in your faith, knowledge in virtue, self-control in knowledge, endurance in self-control, godliness in endurance, brotherly affection in godliness, and love in brotherly affection.

For if these things are present and abound among you, they will not make you idle or fruitless in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For whoever does not possess these things is blind and groping with the hand, having received forgetfulness of the cleansing of his former sins.

Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election certain through good works; for if you do these things, you will never stumble. For in this way an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.

Therefore I will always begin to remind you of these things, although you know them and are established in the present truth. But I consider it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you, knowing that the putting off of my tent is soon to come, just as our Lord Jesus Christ also made clear to me.

And I will make every effort that, after my departure, you may frequently have occasion to remember these things. For we did not make known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ by following cleverly devised myths, but by becoming eyewitnesses of his majesty. For when he received honor and glory from God the Father, a voice such as this came to him from the majestic glory: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”

And we heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain. And we have the prophetic word made more certain, to which you do well to attend as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.

Understand this first: no prophecy of Scripture comes from its own interpretation. For prophecy was never brought forth by human will, but holy men of God, inspired by the Holy Spirit, spoke.

**Chapter II.** But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you, who will introduce destructive sects, even denying the Lord who bought them, bringing upon themselves swift destruction. Many will follow their debaucheries, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed. In greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their judgment has not been idle from long ago, and their destruction does not sleep.

For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but dragged them down with the cords of hell into Tartarus and committed them to be tortured and kept for judgment, and if he did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah, the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, while bringing the flood upon the world of the ungodly; and if he reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes and condemned them to destruction, setting them as an example of those who would act ungodly; and if he rescued righteous Lot, oppressed by the lawless behavior of the wicked—for that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day by seeing and hearing their lawless deeds—then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment.

He especially keeps those who walk after the flesh in the desire for defilement and despise authority. They are bold and self-willed; they do not fear bringing in sects and blaspheming, whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against them.

But these people, like irrational animals, creatures born for capture and destruction, blaspheming what they do not understand, will perish in their own corruption, receiving the reward of unrighteousness. They consider daytime pleasure a delight; they are stains and blemishes, overflowing in delights while feasting with you, having eyes full of adultery and unceasing sin, enticing unstable souls, having a heart trained in greed, children of a curse.

They have abandoned the straight way and gone astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the reward of unrighteousness. But he received a rebuke for his madness: a mute beast of burden, speaking with a human voice, restrained the prophet’s folly.

These are waterless springs and mists driven by storms, for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved. For while speaking proud words of vanity, they entice through the desires of the flesh and debauchery those who have barely escaped, who live in error. They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for whatever overcomes a person, to that he is enslaved.

For if, after escaping the defilements of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in these things and overcome, their latter state has become worse than the former. For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.

[Col. 0842A] What happened to them accords with the truth of the proverb: “A dog returns to its own vomit,” and, “A washed sow returns to wallowing in the mud.”

### [Chapter III]

Behold, beloved, I am writing this second letter to you, in which I arouse your sincere mind by way of reminder, so that you may remember the words formerly spoken by the holy prophets and the commandments of your apostles, of the Lord and Savior. Know this first: in the last days scoffers will come in mockery, walking according to their own desires and saying, “Where is the promise, or his coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it was from the beginning of creation.” For they deliberately overlook this: that the heavens existed of old, and the earth, formed out of water and through water by the word of God; through these the world that then existed was destroyed, being flooded with water. But the heavens and earth that now exist have been stored up by the same word, reserved for fire on the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly human beings.

But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some consider slowness; rather, he is patient toward you, not wishing any to perish but all to return to repentance. The day of the Lord will come like a thief; on it the heavens will pass away with a great rushing sound, the elements will be dissolved by heat, and the earth and the works in it will be burned up.

Since, then, all these things are to be dissolved, what kind of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of the Lord, because of which the burning heavens will be dissolved and the elements will melt in the heat of fire! But according to his promises we await new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

Therefore, beloved, while you await these things, make every effort to be found by him spotless and blameless, in peace. Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul wrote to you according to the patience given him, as he does also in all his letters when he speaks in them of these matters. In them there are certain things difficult to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort, as they do the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.

You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, keep watch, lest you be led astray by the error of the foolish and fall from your own steadfastness. Rather, grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory, both now and unto the day of eternity. Amen.

[Col. 0841] Here ends the Second Epistle of Blessed Peter the Apostle.

[Col. 0841]

## HERE BEGINS THE FIRST EPISTLE OF BLESSED JOHN THE APOSTLE

[Col. 0841D] [Chapter I]

What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked upon and our hands have touched, concerning the word of life—and the life was manifested, and we have seen it and bear witness, and proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and appeared to us—what we have seen and heard we proclaim to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and our fellowship may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ. And we are writing these things so that you may rejoice, and that your joy may be complete.

And this is the message that we have heard from him and proclaim to you: that God is light, and there is no darkness in him at all. If we say that we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanses us from every sin.

If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

### [Chapter II]

My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins—not for ours only, but also for those of the whole world.

And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says, “I know him,” but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him. But whoever keeps his word, truly in him the love of God has been perfected; and by this we know that we are in him. Whoever says that he remains in him ought himself also to walk as he walked.

Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment, which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you heard. Again, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.

Whoever says that he is in the light and hates his brother is in darkness still. Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him. But whoever hates his brother is in darkness, walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name’s sake. I am writing to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have conquered the evil one. I am writing to you, children, because you have known the Father. I am writing to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have conquered the evil one.

Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love is not in him, because everything that is in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away, and its desire; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.

Little children, it is the last hour; and just as you heard that Antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have arisen. From this we know that it is the last hour. They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us. But this happened so that it might be shown that not all are of us.

But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things. I have not written to you as though you did not know the truth, but as though you know it, and because no lie is from the truth. Who is the liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son. Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father; whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.

Let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father. And this is the promise that he himself promised us: eternal life.

I have written these things to you concerning those who are leading you astray. And as for you, let the anointing that you received from him remain in you; and you have no need for anyone to teach you. Rather, just as his anointing teaches you about everything—and is true and is not a lie—so remain in him, just as it taught you.

And now, little children, remain in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not be put to shame by him at his coming [Alternative: “in his coming”]. If you know that he is righteous, know also that everyone who practices righteousness has been born from him.

### [Chapter III]

See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God—and that is what we are. For this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know him. Beloved, now we are children of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we shall be. We know that when he is revealed, we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is. And everyone who has this hope in him sanctifies himself, just as he is holy.

Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness; and sin is lawlessness. And you know that he appeared in order to take away our sins, and there is no sin in him. Everyone who remains in him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him.

Little children, let no one lead you astray. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, just as he is righteous. Whoever commits sin is from the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. For this reason the Son of God appeared: to destroy the works of the devil.

Everyone born of God does not commit sin, because his seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God. By this the children of God and the children of the devil are revealed: everyone who is not righteous is not from God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. For this is the message that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another—not like Cain, who was from the evil one and killed his brother.

And why did he kill him? Because his works were evil, but those of his brother were righteous. Do not marvel, brothers, if the world hates you. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.

By this we have come to know love: that he laid down his life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. But whoever has the world’s goods, sees his brother in need, and closes his compassion against him—how does the love of God remain in him?

My little children, let us not love in word or tongue, but in deed and truth. By this we shall know that we are from the truth, and we shall persuade our hearts before him. For if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows everything.

Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God; and whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what is pleasing before him. And this is his commandment: that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us commandment. Whoever keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in that person; and by this we know that he remains in us: from the Spirit that he gave us.

### [Chapter IV]

Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God; and every spirit that dissolves Jesus [that is, denies or separates him] is not from God. And this is the Antichrist, of whom you heard that he is coming, and now he is already in the world.

You are from God, little children, and you have conquered them, because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world. They are from the world; therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them. We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. Everyone who loves has been born from God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

In this the love of God was revealed among us: God sent his only-begotten Son into the world so that we might live through him. In this is love: not that we loved God, but that he first loved us and sent his Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.

Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love is perfected in us. By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us from his Spirit.

And we have seen and bear witness that the Father sent his Son as the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God. And we have come to know and have believed the love that God has in us.

God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him. In this the love of God has been perfected with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so are we in this world.

There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment. Whoever fears has not been perfected in love. We therefore love God, because God first loved us.

If anyone says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar. For whoever does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God whom he does not see? And we have this commandment from God: that whoever loves God must love his brother also.

### [Chapter V]

Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God. And everyone who loves the one who begot loves also the one who has been begotten by him. By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God: that we keep his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome.

Because everything born from God conquers the world; and this is the victory that conquers the world: our faith. Who is the one who conquers the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not in water only, but in water and blood. And the Spirit is the one who bears witness, because the Christ is truth. For there are three [Note: [Col. 0845C] Thus, word for word, our three previously cited manuscripts also read. Concerning the others, there is scarcely anything on this passage that has not already been said. In one manuscript in the library of the canons of Verona, written for the most part in what are called majuscule letters and, another indication of considerable antiquity, divided by no division of chapters or verses, there are lacking not the heavenly witnesses, which have been so strongly urged, but the earthly witnesses—that is, the preceding isocolon: “There are three who bear witness on earth,” etc. I think that this plainly demonstrates by a new argument that the defect in those codices too, in which the heavenly witnesses—that is, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit—have been omitted, is to be ascribed solely to scribes’ haste and to the very common error that occurs where the same words recur. For since everyone will attribute the former to the copyist’s fault, no reason permits one not to attribute the latter in the same way in other books. Indeed, just as in that codex the copyist’s very error most clearly points to the recurrence of the other isocolon, so in the other Greek as well as Latin manuscripts it is manifestly evident that the error was committed in the heading where precisely the same explanation applies; for the fault could never have arisen except through the repetition of similar and almost identical words. Moreover, different persons err differently for that reason. In one manuscript of the Florentine Library of St. Mark, marked no. 35, the entire seventh verse is absent, while the sixth [Col. 0846C] ends thus: “And the Spirit is the one who bears witness, because Christ is truth”; but in the margin, in another hand, the seventh and eighth verses are supplied in reverse order: “Because there are three who bear witness on earth,” etc. In another Laurentian manuscript, pluteus VI, no. 10, this was formerly read at that place: “Because there are three who bear witness on earth, spirit, water, and blood, and the three are one. Just as there are three who bear witness in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and the three are one.” A later hand corrected this by erasing the words “on earth” in the first isocolon and then inserting “bear witness concerning heaven” in place of “bear witness,” etc. But as to the Hieronymian copy, I wonder how anyone could have persuaded himself that that clause concerning the witnesses testifying in heaven was absent. For since the two clauses correspond to one another in this way and are so closely joined to the following context that the sequence, if either one is absent, is altogether mutilated and gaping, the holy Father could not, if the error had already taken root in his own or other books, have failed to notice it. Besides, the testimonies of the African Fathers—Tertullian, Cyprian, Eugenius, Fulgentius, Vigilius, Victor, and the four hundred bishops in the profession of faith which they presented to the king of the Vandals—are known in support of the genuineness of this verse. Cassiodorus in the Complexiones is beyond every exception, since he belonged to the Roman, not the African, Church and was, moreover, an investigator of sacred codices more diligent than can be said. The distinguished editor of his book, Marquis Scipio Maffei, left nothing unaddressed in his notes on that passage which could contribute to that testimony. [Col. 0847B–0848B]] who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.

And there are three who bear witness on earth: the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and these three are one. If we receive human testimony, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, which is greater: that he has borne witness concerning his Son [Alternative addition: “his own Son”].

Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God within him. Whoever does not believe the Son makes him a liar, because he does not believe the testimony that God has borne concerning his Son. And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.

I have written these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have toward him: that whatever we ask according to his will, he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked of him.

If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life—for the one whose sin does not lead to death. There is sin leading to death; I do not say that one should pray concerning that. Every unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin leading to death.

We know that everyone born from God does not sin; rather, the birth from God preserves him, and the evil one does not touch him. We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the evil one. And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know the true God and be in his true Son. This is the true God and eternal life.

Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.

[Col. 0847] Here ends the First Epistle of Blessed John the Apostle.

[Col. 0847]

## HERE BEGINS THE SECOND EPISTLE OF BLESSED JOHN THE APOSTLE

[Col. 0847B] The elder to the elect lady and her children, whom I love in truth—and not I alone, but also all who have known the truth—because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever.

May grace, mercy, and peace be with you from God the Father and from Christ Jesus, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

I rejoiced greatly because I found some of your children walking in truth, just as we received commandment from the Father. And now I ask you, lady—not as though writing a new commandment to you, but the one that we had from the beginning—that we should love one another. And this is love: that we walk according to his commandments.

For this is the commandment: that, just as you heard [Alternative: “you heard” singular] from the beginning, you should walk in it. For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.

Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what you have worked for, but receive a full reward. Everyone who departs and does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son.

If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into the house, and do not say “Greetings” to him. For whoever says “Greetings” to him shares in his evil works.

Although I have many things to write to you, I did not wish to do so with paper and ink. For I hope to be with you and speak face to face, so that your joy may be complete. The children of your elect sister greet you.

[Col. 0847] Here ends the Second Epistle of Blessed John the Apostle.

[Col. 0847]

## HERE BEGINS THE THIRD EPISTLE OF BLESSED JOHN THE APOSTLE

[Col. 0847D] The elder to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth.

Beloved, I pray that in every respect you may prosper and be in good health, just as your soul prospers. I rejoiced greatly when the brothers came and bore witness to your truth, how you walk in truth. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in truth.

Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, and especially for strangers, who have borne witness to your love before the Church. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God. For they have gone out for the sake of his name, accepting nothing from the gentiles. Therefore we ought to receive such people, so that we may become fellow workers for the truth.

I might have written something to the Church, but Diotrephes, who loves to hold the first place among them, does not receive us. Therefore, if I come, I will call attention to the works he is doing, babbling maliciously against us. And as though these things were not enough for him, he himself does not receive the brothers, and he forbids those who would receive them and expels them from the Church.

Beloved, do not imitate evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God. Demetrius has received testimony from everyone and from the truth itself; and we also bear witness, and you know that our testimony is true.

I had many things to write to you, but I did not wish to write to you with ink and pen. I hope to see you soon, and we shall speak face to face.

Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

[Col. 0849] Here ends the Third Epistle of Blessed John the Apostle.

[Col. 0849]

## HERE BEGINS THE CATHOLIC EPISTLE OF BLESSED JUDE THE APOSTLE

[Col. 0849B] Jude, servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are beloved in God the Father, converted to Christ Jesus, and called: may mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

Beloved, while making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you, exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. For certain people have slipped in—those who long ago were designated for this judgment—ungodly people who turn the grace of our God into licentiousness and deny the only Master and our Lord Jesus Christ.

But I wish to remind you, although you know all things once for all, that Jesus, having saved the people from the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe. And the angels who did not keep their own principality but abandoned their dwelling, he has kept in eternal bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

As Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities, having in the same way committed fornication and gone after other flesh, have been set forth as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire, so also these people defile the flesh, reject dominion, and blaspheme majesties.

But when Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, argued over the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a judgment of blasphemy against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you.” Yet these people blaspheme whatever they do not understand; and whatever they know naturally, like irrational animals, in those things they are destroyed.

Woe to them, because they have gone in the way of Cain, and have poured themselves out in the error of Balaam for reward, and have perished in the rebellion of Korah.

These are stains in their love-feasts, feasting with you without fear, feeding themselves; waterless clouds carried about by winds; autumn trees, fruitless, twice dead, uprooted; wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the storm of darkness is reserved forever.

But Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied also concerning these people, saying: “Behold, the Lord came with his holy myriads, to execute judgment against all and to convict all the ungodly concerning all their ungodly deeds that they committed impiously, and concerning all the harsh things that ungodly sinners spoke against him.”

These are grumblers and complainers, walking according to their own desires; their mouths speak arrogant things, showing admiration for persons for the sake of gain.

But you, beloved, remember the words that were foretold by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ, who told you that in the last time there would be scoffers walking according to their own desires in ungodliness. These are the ones who separate themselves, sensual people who do not have the Spirit.

But you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ for eternal life. And rebuke those who have been judged; but save others by snatching them from the fire. On others have mercy with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh.

To him who is able to preserve you without sin and to set you before the presence of his glory blameless with exultation, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, before every age, and now, and unto all ages of ages. Amen.

[Col. 0849] Here ends the Catholic Epistle of Blessed Jude the Apostle.

[Col. 0851]

## HERE BEGINS THE APOCALYPSE OF BLESSED JOHN THE APOSTLE

[Col. 0851A] [Chapter I]

The revelation of Jesus [Note: Our manuscript, which we have at home, omits the name “Christ.”] Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must soon take place; and he made it known by sending it through his angel to his servant John. He bore witness to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ, to everything that he saw.

Blessed is the one who reads and hears the words of this prophecy [Manuscript: “and who hears”; “of this book”] and keeps what is written in it, for the time is near.

John to the seven Churches that are in Asia: grace to you and peace from him who is and who was and who is to come, and from the seven spirits that are before his throne, and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead and ruler of the kings of the earth.

To him who loved us and washed us from our sins in his blood, and made us a kingdom and priests to his God and Father—to him be glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Yes: Amen.

“I am Α and Ω, the beginning and the end,” says the Lord God, who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.

I, John, your brother and fellow participant in the tribulation, kingdom, and endurance in Jesus Christ, was [Note: The same manuscript reads, “I was in the Spirit on the island,” although the Greek text does not support this] on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus [Manuscript adds: “Christ”].

I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet, saying, “What you see, write in a book and send it to the seven Churches that are in Asia: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”

And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me. And when I had turned, I saw seven golden lampstands, and in the midst of the seven golden lampstands one like a son of man, clothed in a long robe and girded around the breasts with a golden sash. His head and hair were white like white wool and like snow; his eyes were like a flame of fire; his feet were like bronze, as though fired in a furnace; and his voice was like the sound of many waters.

He held seven stars in his right hand; and from his mouth came a sharp two-edged sword; and his face was like the sun shining in its strength. When I saw him, I fell at his feet as though dead. And he placed his right hand upon me, saying:

“Do not fear. I am the first and the last, and the living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive unto the ages of ages, and I have the keys of death and of Hades.

“Therefore write what you saw, what is, and what must take place after these things. The mystery of the seven stars that you saw in my right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven Churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven Churches.”

### [Chapter II]

To the angel of the Church at Ephesus write:

“These things says the one who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands. I know your works, your labor, and your endurance, and that you cannot tolerate evil people. You tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and found them to be liars. You have endurance and have borne up for my name’s sake, and you have not grown weary.

“But I have this against you: that you have abandoned your first love. Therefore remember from where you have fallen, repent, and do the first works. Otherwise I am coming to you and will move your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.

“But you have this in your favor [Note: Our manuscript has the additional words, “But you have this good thing,” though the Greek text gives no support for them]: that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.

“Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. To the one who conquers I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God.”

And to the angel of the Church at Smyrna write:

“These things says the first and the last, who was dead and came to life. I know your tribulation and your poverty [Manuscript omits “your”], but you are rich; and you are slandered by those who call themselves Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

“Do not fear any of the things that you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is going to cast some of you [Manuscript omits “some”] into prison, so that you may be tested; and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.

“Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. The one who conquers will certainly not be harmed by the second death.”

And to the angel of the Church at Pergamum write:

“These things says the one who has the sharp two-edged sword. I know where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. And you hold fast to my name and did not deny my faith, even in the days when Antipas, my faithful witness, was killed among you, where Satan dwells.

“But I have a few things against you: that you have there people who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to place a stumbling-block before the children of Israel, to eat [Note: Here indeed, in accordance with the Greek, φάγειν εἰδωλόθυτα, our manuscript too adds after the word “to eat”: “of sacrifices to idols,” etc.] and to commit fornication. So you also have people who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.

“Repent likewise. Otherwise I am coming to you soon, and I will fight against them with the sword of my mouth.”

[Manuscript adds: “if you do not repent.”]

“Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.”

And to the angel of the Church at Thyatira write:

“These things says the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire and whose feet are like bronze. I know your works, your faith, your love, your ministry, your endurance, and your last works, which are more numerous than the first.

“But I have a few things against you: that you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and teaches and deceives my servants to commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols.

“I gave her time to repent, but she does not wish to repent of her fornication. Behold, I will cast her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her will be in great tribulation unless they repent of her works. And I will strike her children with death, and all the Churches will know that I am the one who searches kidneys and hearts; and I will give to each of you according to your works.

“But I say to you and to the rest who are in Thyatira: all who do not hold this teaching, and who have not known the depths of Satan, as they say, I will not impose another burden upon you. Nevertheless, hold fast to what you have until I come.

“And to the one who conquers and keeps my works to the end, I will give authority over the nations; he will rule them with an iron rod, and they will be broken like a potter’s vessel, just as I also received from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.

“Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.”

[Col. 0853C] [Chapter III.] And to the angel of the church in Sardis write:

“Thus says he who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead. Be watchful and strengthen the rest, which were about to die. For I have not found your works complete before my God. Therefore keep in mind how you received and heard; keep it, and repent. If, then, you will not be watchful, I will come to you like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come to you.

“But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments; they will walk with me in white, because they are worthy. The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will not erase his name from the book of life; I will confess his name before my Father and before his angels. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

[Col. 0853D] And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write:

“Thus says the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts, who shuts and no one opens: I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut, because you have little strength [Ms. *modicum*, “a little”], and you have kept my word and have not denied my name. Behold, I will give [Ms. *tibi*, “to you”] some from the synagogue of Satan, who say that they are Jews and are not, but are lying. Behold, I will make them come and worship before your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.

“Because you have kept the word of my patience, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole inhabited world, to test those who dwell on the earth. Behold, I am coming soon; hold fast to what you have, so that no one may take your crown. The one who conquers I will make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will never go out again. I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which descends from heaven from my God [Ms. omits *Dei mei*, “of my God”], and my new name. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write:

“Thus says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, who is the beginning of God’s creation: I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were cold or hot! But because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to vomit you out of my mouth. For you say, ‘I am rich, I have become wealthy, and I need nothing’; and you do not know that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked.

“I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire, so that you may become rich; and white garments, so that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not appear; and anoint your eyes with eye-salve, so that you may see. I reprove and discipline those whom I love. Therefore be zealous and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door for me, I will enter in to him, and I will dine with him, and he with me.

“The one who conquers I will grant to sit with me on my throne, just as I also conquered and sat with my Father on his throne. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

[Chapter IV.]

After this I saw—and behold, a door was open in heaven—and the first voice that I had heard, like the voice of a trumpet speaking with me, said: “Come up here, and I will show you what must happen after this.” [Note: Our manuscript has, “I will show you what must happen soon,” etc.]

And immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne had been set in heaven, and one was seated upon the throne. And the one seated was like the appearance of a jasper stone and a sardius; and around the throne was a rainbow, like the appearance of an emerald. And around the throne were twenty-four seats; and upon the twenty-four thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white garments, with golden crowns upon their heads.

And from the throne came flashes of lightning, voices, and peals of thunder; and seven burning lamps were before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne was something like a glassy sea, resembling crystal. And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.

And the first living creature was like a lion, and the second living creature like a calf, and the third living creature had a face like that of a human being, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle. And the four living creatures, each of them having six wings, were full of eyes all around and within; and they had no rest day or night, saying:

“Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.”

And whenever the living creatures gave glory, honor, and blessing to the one seated upon the throne, who lives forever and ever, the twenty-four elders fell down before the one seated upon the throne and worshiped the one who lives forever and ever; and they cast their crowns before the throne, saying:

“You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory, honor, and power, because you created all things, and by your will they existed and were created.”

[Chapter V.]

And I saw in the right hand of the one seated upon the throne a book written within and on the outside, sealed with seven seals. And I saw [Ms. *audivi*, “heard”] a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice: “Who is worthy to open the book and to loosen its seals?”

And no one was able, neither in heaven nor on earth nor under the earth, to open the book or to look at it. [Note: The same manuscript inserts, “and to loosen its seals.”] And I wept greatly, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to see it.

And one of the elders said to me: “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, so as to open the book and to loosen its seven seals.”

And I saw—and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent into all the earth. And he came and took the book from the right hand of the one seated upon the throne.

And when he had opened the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying:

“You are worthy, Lord, to receive the book and to open its seals, because you were slain, and you redeemed us for God by your blood from every tribe and language and people and nation; and you made us a kingdom and priests for our God, and we shall reign upon the earth.”

[Col. 0855C] And I saw and heard the voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was thousands of thousands [Ms. omits *eorum*, “of them”], saying with a loud voice:

“Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power, divinity, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and blessing.”

And every creature that is in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and those that are in the sea and in it—all of them I heard saying:

“To the one seated upon the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and power forever and ever.”

And the four living creatures said: “Amen.” And the twenty-four elders fell upon their faces and worshiped the one who lives forever and ever. [Note: The words “the one who lives forever and ever,” which occur in some Greek books, are likewise absent from our manuscript.]

[Chapter VI.]

And when the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals [Col. 0855D], I heard one of the four living creatures saying [Ms. adds *mihi*, “to me”], like a voice of thunder: “Come and see.” [Note: This also begins again with “And I saw,” as in some Greek books; our manuscript omits it.]

And I saw—and behold, a white horse, and the one seated upon it had a bow; and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering, so that he might conquer.

And when he had opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: “Come and see.” And another horse went out, a red one; and to the one seated upon it was given the power to take peace from the earth, so that people might kill one another; and a great sword was given to him. [Col. 0856A]

And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: “Come and see.” And behold, a black horse; and the one seated upon it had a balance in his hand. And I heard something like a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying: “A two-pound measure of wheat for a denarius, and three two-pound measures of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the wine and the oil.”
