And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: “Come and see.” And behold, a pale horse; and the one seated upon it had the name Death, and Hades followed him. And authority was given to him over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, famine, death, and the beasts of the earth.

And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slain because of the word of God and because of the testimony that they had; and they cried out with a loud voice, saying:

“How long, Lord, holy and true, will you not judge and avenge our blood upon those who dwell on the earth?”

And white robes were given to each of them; and it was told them that they should rest for a little while longer [Note: Our manuscript has, “until the number of their fellow servants and their brothers who are to be killed, as they were, is completed,” etc.], until their fellow servants and their brothers who were to be killed as they had been were completed in number.

And I saw when he had opened the sixth seal—and behold, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black like a sackcloth garment, and the whole moon became like blood; and the stars of heaven fell upon the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind.

And the heaven withdrew like a scroll being rolled up; and every mountain and island was moved from its place. And the kings of the earth, the rulers, the tribunes, the rich, the mighty, and every slave and free person hid themselves in caves and among the rocks of the mountains. And they say to the mountains and rocks:

“Fall upon us and hide us from the face of the one seated upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb, because the great day of their wrath has come; and who will be able to stand?”

[Chapter VII.]

After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth [Ms. omits *terrae*, “of the earth”], so that they would not blow upon the earth or upon the sea or upon any tree.

And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it had been given to harm the earth and the sea, saying:

“Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the servants of our God upon their foreheads.”

And I heard the number of those sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed, from every tribe of the children of Israel:

From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand sealed.  
From the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.

After this I saw a great multitude, which no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. And they cried out with a loud voice, saying:

“Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.”

And all the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures; and they fell upon their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying:

“Amen. Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and strength be to our God forever and ever. Amen.”

And one of the elders answered and said to me: “These who are clothed in white robes—who are they, and from where have they come?”

And I said to him: “My lord, you know.”

And he said to me: “These are the ones who came from the great tribulation and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple; and the one seated upon the throne will dwell over them.

“They will hunger no more, nor thirst any more; neither will the sun fall upon them, nor any heat, because the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and lead them to springs of waters of life; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”

[Chapter VIII.]

And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. And I saw seven angels standing before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

And another angel came and stood before the altar, holding a golden censer [Note: The same manuscript adds, “in his hand”]. [Col. 0857C] And much incense was given to him, so that he might offer it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar that is before the throne of God. And the smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, rose from the angel’s hand before God.

And the angel took the censer and filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it upon the earth; and there were peals of thunder, voices, flashes of lightning, and a great earthquake.

And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound the trumpets.

And the first angel sounded his trumpet, and there was hail and fire mixed with blood, and it was thrown upon the earth. And a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees was burned up, and all green grass was burned up.

And the second angel sounded his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea. And a third of the sea became blood; and a third of the creatures in the sea that had souls died; and a third of the ships perished.

And the third angel sounded his trumpet, and a great burning star fell from heaven, like a torch; and it fell upon a third of the rivers and upon the springs of waters. And the name of the star is called Wormwood. And a third of the waters became wormwood; and many people died from the waters, because they had become bitter.

And the fourth angel sounded his trumpet, and a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck, so that a third of them was darkened; and a third of the day did not shine, and likewise a third of the night.

And I saw and heard the voice of one eagle flying through the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice:

“Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the remaining sounds of the trumpets of the three angels who are about to sound.”

[Chapter IX.]

And the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key of the pit of the abyss was given to it. And it opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke rose from the pit like the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.

And locusts came out of the smoke of the pit upon the earth, and power was given to them like the power of the scorpions of the earth. And they were commanded not to harm the grass of the earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree, but only those people who do not have the seal of God upon their foreheads. And it was given to them not to kill them, but to torture them for five months; and their torture was like the torture of a scorpion when it strikes a person.

And in those days people will seek death and will not find it; and they will desire to die, and death will flee from them.

And the forms of the locusts were like horses prepared for battle; and upon their heads were something like crowns resembling gold; and their faces were like human faces. And they had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like lions’ teeth. And they had breastplates like iron breastplates, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horses’ chariots running into battle.

And they had tails like scorpions, and there were stings in their tails; and their power was to harm people for five months. And over them they had as king the angel of the abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon [Ms. *Abdon*], and in Greek, *Apollyon*—in Latin, “Destroyer.”

The first woe has passed; and behold, two more woes are still coming after this.

And the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a voice from one of the four horns of the golden altar that is before the eyes of God, saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet:

“Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”

And the four angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour, day, month, and year, to kill a third of humankind. And the number of the mounted army was twenty thousand times ten thousand. And I heard their number.

And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and those seated upon them had breastplates of fire, hyacinth, and sulfur; and the heads of the horses were like lions’ heads; and from their mouths came fire, smoke, and sulfur. And by these three plagues a third of humankind was killed: by the fire, smoke, and sulfur that came from their mouths.

For the power of the horses is in their mouths [Note: In accordance with the Greek text, our manuscript omits the words “and in their tails”] and in their tails. For their tails were like serpents, having heads, and with these they cause harm.

And the rest of humankind, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk. Nor did they repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts.

[Chapter X.]

And I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven, clothed with a cloud; and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire. And he had in his hand a little open book. And he placed his right foot upon the sea and his left upon the earth, and he cried out with a loud voice, as when a lion roars.

And when he cried out, the seven thunders spoke their voices. And when the seven thunders had spoken their voices, I was about to write; and I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

“Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it.”

And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted his hand to heaven and swore by the one who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things in it, and the earth and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it:

“There will be no more delay, but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as he announced the good news through his servants the prophets.” [Note: Instead of “but in the days of the voice,” etc., our manuscript has, “and I saw at the end of the voice,” etc.]

And I heard the voice from heaven speaking with me again and saying:

“Go, take the open book from the hand of the angel standing upon the sea and upon the earth.”

And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the book. And he said to me:

“Take the book and devour it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet like honey.”

And I took the book from the angel’s hand and devoured it; and it was sweet like honey in my mouth, but when I had devoured it, my stomach became bitter. And he said to me:

“You must prophesy again concerning many peoples, nations, languages, and kings.”

[Chapter XI.]

And a reed like a rod was given to me, and I was told:

“Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar and those who worship [Ms. *habitantes*, “those who dwell”] in it. But the outer court of the temple, cast it outside and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.

“And I will give to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth. These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the Lord of the earth.

“And if anyone wants to harm them, fire will come out of their mouths and devour their enemies; and if anyone wants to injure them, he must be killed in this way. They have authority to shut the heaven, so that it may not rain during the days of their prophecy; and they have authority over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.

“And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that rises from the abyss will make war against them, and will conquer them and kill them. And their bodies will lie in the streets of the great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was also crucified.

“And people from the tribes, peoples, languages, and nations will see their bodies for three and a half days, and they will not allow their bodies to be placed in tombs. And those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwelt upon the earth.

“And after the three and a half days, the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon those who saw them. And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them:

“‘Come up here.’

“And they ascended into heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them. And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell; and seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake. And the rest were thrown into fear, and they gave glory to the God of heaven.

“The second woe has passed; behold, the third woe is coming soon.”

And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying:

“The kingdom of this world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he will reign forever and ever. Amen.”

And the twenty-four elders who sit upon their thrones before God [Ms. *Domini*, “the Lord”] fell upon their faces and worshiped God, saying:

“We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty, who are and who were and who are to come, because you have taken your great power and have begun to reign. And the nations were angry, and your wrath has come, and the time has come for the dead to be judged, and to give their reward to your servants the prophets and to the saints and to those who fear your name, the small and the great, and to destroy those who corrupt the earth.” [Ms. *corrumpunt*, “who corrupt”]

And the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was seen in his temple. [Note: Our manuscript omits the words “in his temple.”] And there were flashes of lightning, voices, an earthquake, and great hail.

[Chapter XII.]

And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars. And being pregnant, she cried out in labor and was tormented as she gave birth.

And another sign appeared in heaven; and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon its heads seven diadems. And its tail swept away a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth.

And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth, it might devour her child. And she gave birth to a male child who was to rule all the nations with an iron rod; and her child was caught up to God and to his throne. And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she had a place prepared by God, so that there they might feed her for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.

And there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and its angels fought; but they did not prevail [Ms. *praevaluerunt*, “they prevailed”], and no place was found for them any longer in heaven.

And that great dragon was thrown down, the ancient serpent, who is called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole inhabited world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying:

“Now salvation and power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of his Christ have come, because the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accused them before our God day and night. And they conquered him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony; and they did not love their lives even unto death.

“Therefore rejoice, heavens, and those who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and the sea, because the Devil has come down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has little time.”

And when the dragon saw that it had been thrown down to the earth, it pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child. And two wings of a great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.

And the serpent poured water like a river out of its mouth after the woman, so that it might cause her to be swept away by the river. But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had poured from its mouth.

And the dragon became angry with the woman and went away to make war against the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.

And it stood upon the sand of the sea.

[Chapter XIII.]

And I saw a beast rising from the sea, having seven heads and ten horns; and upon its horns were ten diadems, and upon its heads names of blasphemy. And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion.

And the dragon gave it its power and its great authority. And I saw one of its heads as though wounded unto death, and its mortal wound was healed. [Col. 0861C] And the whole earth marveled after the beast; and they worshiped the dragon that had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying:

“Who is like the beast, and who can fight against it?”

And a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies was given to it; and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months. And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme his name and his tabernacle and those who dwell in heaven.

And it was given authority to make war against the saints and to conquer them; and authority was given to it over every tribe, people, language, and nation. And all who dwell upon the earth worshiped it, whose names have not been written in the book of the life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.

If anyone has an ear, let him hear. If anyone leads into captivity, he goes into captivity; if anyone kills with the sword, he must be killed with the sword. Here is the endurance and faith of the saints.

And I saw another beast rising from the earth. It had [Ms. *habentem*, “having”] two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon. And it exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence; and it makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed. [Note: Our manuscript adds “and it lived,” a phrase drawn here from the later context.]

And it performs great signs, so that it even makes fire descend from heaven to earth in the presence of human beings. And it deceives those who dwell upon the earth because of the signs that were given it to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell upon the earth to make an image of the beast that had the wound of the sword and lived.

And it was granted to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might speak, and to cause all who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.

And it causes all—the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves—to receive a mark upon their right hand or upon their foreheads, so that no one may be able to buy or sell except the one who has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name.

Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a human being, and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.

[Chapter XIV.]

And I saw—and behold, the Lamb was standing upon Mount Zion, and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written upon their foreheads.

And I heard a voice from heaven like the voice of many waters and like the voice of great thunder. And the voice that I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps. And they were singing as though a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one was able to sing the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand who were purchased from the earth.

These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were purchased from humankind as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb. And no lie was found in their mouth; they are without blemish before the throne of God.

And I saw another angel flying through the midst of heaven, having an eternal Gospel, to proclaim the good news to those seated upon the earth and to every nation, tribe, language, and people, saying with a loud voice:

“Fear the Lord and give him honor, because the hour of his judgment has come; and worship the one who made heaven and earth, the sea, and the springs of waters.” [Note: Instead of the words “the sea and the springs of waters,” as in some Greek books, our manuscript likewise has *καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς*—“and everything that is in them.”]

And another angel followed, saying:

“Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, which gave all the nations wine to drink from the wine of the wrath of its fornication.”

And a third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice:

“If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives its mark upon his forehead or upon his hand, he too will drink from the wine of the wrath of God, which is mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of his wrath; and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and before the presence of the Lamb.

“And the smoke of their torments will rise forever and ever, and they have no rest day or night—those who worship the beast and its image, and anyone who receives the mark of its name.

“Here is the endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.”

And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

“Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. From now on, says the Spirit, let them rest from their labors, for their works follow them.”

And I saw—and behold, a white cloud, and seated upon the cloud one like a son of man, having upon his head a golden crown and in his hand a sharp sickle.

And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to the one seated upon the cloud:

“Send out your sickle and reap, because the hour to reap has come, for the harvest of the earth has dried up.”

And the one seated upon the cloud sent his sickle upon the earth, and the earth was reaped.

And another angel came out of the temple that is in heaven, himself also having a sharp sickle. And another angel came out from the altar, who had authority over the fire; and he cried out with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, saying:

“Send out your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.”

And the angel sent his sharp sickle upon the earth and gathered the vine of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God. And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress as high as the horses’ bridles, for one thousand six hundred stadia.

[Col. 0863B] [Chapter XV.]

And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, because in them the wrath of God is completed.

And I saw something like a glassy sea mixed with fire, and those who had conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name standing upon the glassy sea, holding the harps of God. And they were singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying:

“Great and marvelous are your works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are your ways, King of the ages. Who will not fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy; for all the nations will come and worship before you, because your judgments have been manifested.” [Ms. adds “all.”]

And after this I saw—and behold, the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened. And the seven angels who had the seven plagues came out of the temple, clothed in pure and shining linen [Ms. *lapide*, “stone”], and girded around their chests with golden belts.

And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever. And the temple was filled with smoke from the majesty of God and from his power; and no one was able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels had been completed.

## [Chapter XVI]

And I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels: “Go and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God upon the earth.” And the first went and poured out his bowl upon the earth, and a grievous and malignant sore came upon the people who had the mark of the beast, and upon those who worshiped its image [Col. 0863D].

And the second angel poured out his bowl upon the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead man; and every living soul in the sea died. And the third poured out his bowl upon the rivers and the springs of waters, and they became blood. And I heard the angel of the waters saying: “You are just, [Note: As in some Greek copies, so also in our Latin manuscript, ‘Lord’ is lacking here.] Lord, who are and who were, the Holy One, because you have judged these things. For they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and you gave them blood to drink; they deserve it.”

And I heard another [Col. 0864A] voice from the altar saying: “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are your judgments.” [Note: Again, our manuscript, together with several Greek books, lacks the words ‘from the altar.’]

And the fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was given to it to afflict people with heat and fire. And people were scorched by great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent, [Note: Our manuscript has more: ‘so that they would not worship demons,’ [Col. 0864D] ‘so that they might give him glory.’] so that they might give him glory.

And the fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and its kingdom became darkened; and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain [Ms. “ate”]. And they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores [Note: In this place and in the immediately following one, the same manuscript omits the pronoun ‘their’], and they did not repent of their deeds.

And the sixth angel poured out his bowl upon that great river, the Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun [Col. 0864B]. And I saw from the mouth of the dragon, and from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet [Note: Our manuscript adds ‘to have gone forth’; this is also found in some Greek copies, ἐξελθεῖν (to go forth)], three unclean spirits like frogs. For they are demonic spirits performing signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole earth to gather them for battle on the great day of Almighty God.

“Behold, I come like a thief. Blessed is the one who watches and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk naked and they see his shame.” And he will gather them into the place called in Hebrew Armageddon [Ms. “Hermageddon”].

And the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came from the temple, from the throne, saying: “It is done.” And there were flashes of lightning, voices, and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as had never occurred since people were upon the earth—such an earthquake, so great. And the great city was divided into three parts [Col. 0864C], and the cities of the nations fell. And Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the indignation of his wrath. And every island fled, and the mountains were not found. And great hail, like a talent, came down from heaven upon people; and people blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, because its plague was exceedingly great.

## [Chapter XVII]

And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying: “Come, I will show you the condemnation of the great prostitute who sits upon many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication, and those who inhabit the earth became drunk from the wine of her prostitution.”

And he carried me away in spirit into a desert. And I saw a woman sitting [Col. 0864D] upon a scarlet beast, full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns. And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, gilded with gold, precious stones, and pearls. She had a golden cup in her hand, full of abominations and the uncleanness of her fornication. And upon her forehead a name was written: “Mystery: Babylon the great, mother of fornications and of the abominations of the earth.”

And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints [Col. 0865A] and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. And I was greatly astonished when I saw her. And the angel said to me: “Why are you astonished? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.

“The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to rise from the abyss, and it will go into destruction. And the inhabitants of the earth will marvel—those whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world—when they see the beast that was and is not.

“And here is the meaning, for one who has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains upon which the woman sits, and they are seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain for a short time. And the beast that was and is not is itself the eighth [Col. 0865B]; it is one of the seven, and it goes into destruction.

“And the ten [Ms. omits ‘and the ten’] horns that you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but will receive authority as kings for one hour after the beast. These have one purpose, and they will hand over their power and authority to the beast. These will fight with the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because he is Lord [Note: In place of ‘of lords,’ our manuscript has a single word meaning ‘he rules’; Col. 0865D] of lords and King of kings, and those who are with him are called, chosen, and faithful.”

And he said to me: “The waters that you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples, nations, and languages. And the ten horns that you saw upon the beast: these will hate the prostitute, and will make her desolate and naked; they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire. For God has put it into their hearts to do what pleases him: to give their kingdom [Col. 0865C] to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled. And the woman whom you saw is the great city that has dominion over the kings of the earth.”

## [Chapter XVIII]

After these things I saw another angel descending from heaven, possessing great authority; and the earth was illumined by his glory. And he cried out [Note: “In strength,” together with our manuscript, is omitted by some Greek copies as well.] forcefully, saying: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! And it has become a dwelling place of demons, a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean and hateful bird, because all the nations drank from the wine of the wrath [Ms. “of the wrath”] of her fornication; and the kings of the earth committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth became rich through the power of her luxuries.

“And I heard another voice from heaven saying: ‘Come out of her, my people, so that you may not share in her sins [Col. 0865D] and receive none of her plagues. For her sins have reached as far as heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities. Repay her as she herself repaid you, and repay her double according to her deeds; in the cup in which she mixed the drink, mix her a double portion. As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, give her that much torment and mourning, because in her heart she says: “I sit as queen; I am not a widow, and I shall see no mourning.” Therefore, in one day her plagues will come: death, [Col. 0866A] mourning, and famine; and she will be burned with fire, because mighty is God who will judge her.’

“And the kings of the earth who committed fornication with her and lived in luxury will weep and mourn over her when they see the smoke of her burning. They will stand far away because of fear of her torment, saying: ‘Alas, alas, that great city, Babylon, that strong city! For in one hour your judgment has come.’

“And the merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo any longer: cargo of gold, silver, precious stone, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet [Ms. “scarlet-colored”]—and every kind of thyine wood, every vessel of ivory, every vessel of precious stone, bronze, iron, and marble, cinnamon [Note: Our manuscript has more: “and amomum, and spices,” etc., as also do some Greek copies, καὶ ἄμωμον, καὶ etc.], [Col. 0866B] and perfumes, ointment, frankincense, wine, oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and human lives. And the fruits desired by your soul have departed from you; all your rich and splendid things have perished from you, and they will never find them again.

“The merchants of these goods, who became rich from her, will stand far away because of fear of her torment, weeping and mourning, and saying: ‘Alas, alas, that great city, clothed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, gilded with gold, precious stone, and pearls! For in one hour such great wealth has been laid waste.’

“And every shipmaster, and everyone who sails on the lake, and sailors, and all who work at sea, stood far away and cried out when they saw the place of her burning, saying: ‘What city is like this great city?’ And they threw dust upon their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying: ‘Alas, alas, that great city, in which all who had ships at sea became rich from her prices! For in one hour she has been desolated.’

“Rejoice over her, heaven, and you saints, apostles, and prophets, because God has judged your judgment against her.”

And one mighty angel lifted up a stone like a great millstone and threw it into the sea, saying: “With such force Babylon, that great city, will be thrown down, and it will never be found again. And the sound of harpists, musicians, flute players, and trumpeters will never be heard in you again. No craftsman of any craft will ever be found in you again. The sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again. The light of a lamp will never shine in you again. The voice of bridegroom and bride will never again be heard in you, because your merchants were the rulers of the earth, because by your sorceries all the nations were led astray. And in her was found the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who were slain upon the earth.”

## [Chapter XIX]

After these things I heard what seemed to be the voice of many trumpets in heaven, saying: “Alleluia! Salvation, [Note: Our manuscript, together with most other Greek copies, lacks the words ‘and glory.’] and glory, and power belong to our God, because his judgments are true and just. For he has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth by her prostitution, and he has avenged [Col. 0867A] the blood of his servants from her hands.”

And again they said: “Alleluia!” And her smoke rises forever and ever.

And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits upon the throne, saying: “Amen, Alleluia.”

And a voice came out from the throne saying: “Praise our God, all his servants, and you who fear him, small and great.”

And I heard what seemed to be the voice [Note: The same manuscript has ‘of a trumpet’ in place of ‘of a crowd,’ agreeing with some Greek copies, in which σάλπιγγος (of a trumpet) occurs instead of ὄχλου (of a crowd).] of a great crowd, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunders, saying: “Alleluia, because the Lord our Almighty God has begun to reign. Let us rejoice and exult, and let us give him glory, because the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has prepared herself. And it was granted to her to clothe herself in shining and pure fine linen. For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.”

And he said to me: “Write: Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.” And he said to me: “These words of God are true.”

And I fell before his feet to worship him. And he said to me: “See that you do not do this. I am your fellow servant and the fellow servant of your brothers who possess the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse; and the one sitting upon it was called Faithful and True. And with justice he judges and fights. His eyes were like a flame of fire, and upon his head were many diadems. He had a name written which no one knows except himself. And he was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, and his name is called the Word of God.

And the armies that are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed in white and pure fine linen [Col. 0867C]. And from his mouth proceeds a sword sharp on both sides, so that with it he may strike the nations. And he himself will rule them with an iron rod, and he himself treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of Almighty God. And he has written upon his garment and upon his thigh: “King of kings and Lord of lords.”

And I saw one angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds flying through the midst of heaven: “Come and gather for the great supper of God, so that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of tribunes, and the flesh of mighty men; and the flesh of horses and of those who sit upon them; and the flesh of all free persons and slaves, small and great.”

And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to wage battle with the one sitting upon the horse and with his army. And the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet who performed signs before it, by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of burning fire and sulfur. And the rest were killed by the sword of the one sitting upon the horse, which proceeds from his mouth. And all the birds were filled with their flesh.

## [Chapter XX]

And I saw an angel descending from heaven, possessing the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand. And he seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years. And he threw him into the abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him, so that he might no longer deceive the nations until the thousand years were completed. After this he must be released for a short time.

And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those beheaded because of the testimony of Jesus and because of the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, nor received its mark upon their foreheads or upon their hands. And they lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.

The rest of the dead did not live until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is the one who has a share in the first resurrection. Over these the second death has no authority, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years.

And when the thousand years have been completed, Satan will be released from his prison. And he will go out and deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth—Gog and Magog—and gather them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the sea. And they went up over the breadth [Ms. “height”] of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city.

And fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them. And the Devil, who deceived them, was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet also will be tormented day and night forever and ever [Note: In accordance with the Greek text, καὶ βασανισθήσονται (and they will be tormented) is placed before the verb “were tormented” in our manuscript and others from the Corbie Library [Col. 0868D], and they read with a somewhat different meaning: “and they will be tormented day and night,” etc.].

And I saw a great white throne, and the one sitting upon it, from whose presence earth and heaven fled, and no place was found for them [Ms. “by them”]. And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the book of life. And the dead were judged from what was written in the books, according to their deeds.

And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, and death and the underworld gave up their dead who were in them; and each person was judged according to his deeds. And the underworld and death were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death [Note: The same manuscript repeats here the words “the lake of fire,” easily transferred from the margin into the text]. And whoever was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.

## [Chapter XXI]

And I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.

And I, John, saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, descending from heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard [Col. 0868D] a loud voice from the throne saying: “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with human beings, and he will dwell with them. And they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more; neither mourning, nor crying, nor pain will be any longer, because the former things have passed away.”

And the one sitting upon the throne said: “Behold, I make all things new.” And he said to me [Note: Our manuscript adds here the word “angel”]: “Write, because these words are utterly trustworthy and true.”

And he said to me: “It is done. I am Α and Ω: the beginning and the end. I will give the thirsty one water from the fountain of the water of life freely. The one who conquers will possess these things, and I will be his God, and he will be my son.

“But for the cowardly, unbelieving, accursed, murderers, fornicators, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars, their portion will be in the lake burning with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”

And one of the seven angels who had the bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying: “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.” And he carried me away in spirit to a great and high mountain [Ms. omits “and high”], and he showed me the holy city Jerusalem descending from heaven from God, possessing the glory of God. Its light was like a precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal.

And it had a great and high wall, with twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel. On the east, three gates; on the north, three gates; on the south, three gates; and on the west, three gates.

And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and upon them [Note: Neither the Greek text nor our manuscript repeats “twelve” here.] were twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

And the one speaking with me had a golden measuring rod, so that he might measure the city, its gates, and its wall. And the city was laid out as a square, and its length was as great as its width. And he measured the city with the golden rod, twelve thousand stadia; its length, height, and width were equal.

And he measured its wall, one hundred forty-four cubits, a human measure, which is also an angel’s. And the structure of its wall was jasper; but the city itself was pure gold, like pure glass. And the foundations of the city wall were adorned with every precious stone.

The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald; the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprase; the eleventh, hyacinth; the twelfth, amethyst.

And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, each gate being made from a single pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.

And I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty is its temple, and the Lamb. And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine upon it, for the glory of God illumined it, and its lamp is the Lamb.

And the nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their glory and honor into it [Col. 0870A]. And its gates will not be shut by day, for night will not be there. And they will bring the glory [Mss. add “their”] and honor of the nations into it.

Nothing defiled, or that practices abomination and falsehood, will enter it [Note: The manuscript reads: “Nothing defiled, or anything polluted, or that practices abomination,” etc.], except those who are written in the book of life [Ms. adds “and of”] of the Lamb.

## [Chapter XXII]

And he showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of its street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits and yielding its fruit each month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.

And no curse will be any longer [Note: A great number of Latin manuscripts have “and” instead of “but,” as in the Greek καί. Immediately afterward, “will be” should apparently be read in the singular, “will be,” as in the Greek.]; but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him. And they will see his face [Col. 0870B], and his name will be upon their foreheads [Note: Our manuscript has more: “his name written upon their foreheads,” etc., though the Greek text does not support this addition].

And night will be no more. And they will have no need of the light of a lamp or of the light of the sun, because the Lord God will illumine them, and they will reign forever and ever.

And he said to me: “These words are utterly trustworthy and true. And the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must happen soon. And behold, I am coming quickly. Blessed is the one who keeps [Note: Our manuscript reads “who will keep”] the words of the prophecy of this book.”

And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And after I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who showed me these things. And he said [Ms. “says”] to me: “See that you do not do this, for I am your fellow servant [Ms. omits “for”] and the fellow servant of your brothers the prophets and of those who keep the words [Note: Our manuscript, together with most other Latin manuscripts, omits “of the prophecy,” as does the Greek text itself] of the prophecy of this book. Worship God.”

And he said to me [Col. 0870C]: “Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near. Let the one who does harm continue to do harm; let the one who is filthy continue to be filthy; and let the one who is righteous continue to be justified [Note: The same manuscript reads, “and let the righteous be justified still”; many others have, “and let the righteous still practice righteousness.” Saint Cyprian twice quotes this passage as: “Let the righteous do still more righteous deeds”]; and let the holy person continue to be sanctified.

“Behold, I am coming quickly, and my reward is with me, to repay each person according to his deeds. [Note: Our manuscript lacks this entire verse: “I am Α and Ω, the first and the last, the beginning and the end,” although it is present in the Greek.] I am Α and Ω, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

“Blessed are those who wash their robes [Note: Our manuscript, together with most other ancient copies, omits the words “in the blood of the Lamb”; they are also absent from the Greek. Immediately afterward, some older Latin manuscripts, closer to the Greek, have “and by the gates” instead of “and through the gates”; our manuscript has “through the gates”] in the blood of the Lamb, so that they may have authority over the tree of life and may enter the city through the gates.

“Outside are dogs, sorcerers, sexually immoral persons, murderers, those who serve idols [Note: Our manuscript adds on its own “and fornicators”], and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.

“I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify these things to you in the churches. I am the root and offspring of David, the bright morning star.”

And the spirit [Ms. “bridegroom”] and the bride say: “Come.” And let the one who hears say: “Come.” And let the one who thirsts come; and let the one who wishes receive the water of life freely.

For I testify [Note: Our manuscript, together with most other Latin books, has “I” instead of “for”] to everyone who hears the words [Col. 0871A] of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues written in this book. And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his share from [Note: Older Latin books have “from the tree” instead of “from the book,” in accordance with the Greek ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου (from the tree)] the book of life, and from the holy city, and from the things [Col. 0872A] that are written in this book.

The one who testifies to these things says: “Yes, I am coming quickly.” Amen. Come, Lord Jesus. The grace of our Lord [Note: Our manuscript omits the words “and of Christ,” as well as the final two words “to you. Amen”; both Latin and some Greek books omit them] Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

[Col. 0871] Here ends the book of the Apocalypse of Blessed John the Apostle.

[Note: In this manner the manuscript of the sacred books of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, numbered 15, reads at the end of the Epistle to the Hebrews. For it does not, according to the custom of the other manuscripts, conclude the New Testament with the book of the Apocalypse, but with the Epistle to the Hebrews. After that Epistle, in the same very ancient and excellent manuscript, there follows the book of the Shepherd, which has come down to us mutilated through the injuries of time. Therefore let every student of the Divine Library of Saint Eusebius Jerome read in peace. To complete it in all its parts, we have added chronological and geographical tables as a concluding ornament. By “Chronology” I mean one previously unpublished, arranged in the time of Charlemagne by an anonymous author and copied in a Corbie manuscript, no. 2, at the end of the sacred books. For the geographical material we here use the maps of N. Sanson, because, if life permits, we shall present a geography drawn from Jerome’s works when we reach the book On Hebrew Places.]

READ IN PEACE THE LIBRARY OF JEROME, PRIEST OF BETHLEHEM.

[Col. 0871]

# APPENDIX TO THE DIVINE LIBRARY OF SAINT JEROME

[Note: This appendix refers to the Divina bibliotheca in volumes 28 and 29 of Patrologia Latina.]

# ABRIDGMENT OF THE CHRONICLE

## THE FIRST AGE

[Col. 0871C]

When Adam was 130 years old, he begot Seth. Seth, being 105 years old, begot Enos, while Adam was alive and was 235 years old. Enos, being 90 years old, begot Cainan, while Adam was alive and was 325 years old. Cainan, being 70 years old, begot Malaleel, while Adam was alive and was 395 years old. Malaleel, being 64 years old, begot Jared, while Adam was alive and was 360 years old. Jared, being 162 years old, begot Enoch, while Adam was alive and was 622 years old. Enoch, being 65 years old, begot Methuselah, while Adam was alive and was 687 years old. Methuselah, being 187 years old, begot Lamech, while Adam was alive and was 874 years old. Lamech, being 182 years old, begot Noah.

Noah, being 500 years old, begot Shem. When Shem was 100 years old, the Flood occurred. And here the total of 1,656 years is completed.

## THE SECOND AGE

[Col. 0871D]

In the second year after the Flood, Shem, aged 102 [Note: This does not agree with the sacred text], begot Arphaxad. Arphaxad, being 35 years old, begot Shelah. Shelah, being 30 years old, begot Eber. Eber, being 34 years old, begot Peleg. Peleg, being 30 years old, begot Reu. Reu, being 32 years old, begot Serug. Serug, being [Col. 0872C] 30 years old, begot Nahor. Nahor, being 29 years old, begot Terah. Terah, being 70 years old, begot Abraham.

Here the total of the second age ends, comprising 212 years. Together, the years of the two ages amount to 1,948.

## THE THIRD AGE

Abraham, being 100 years old, begot Isaac. Isaac, being 60 years old, begot Jacob. Jacob, being 90 years old, begot Joseph, who lived 110 years.

And from him until the departure of the children of Israel [Note: Read: “And from him until the departure of the children of Israel there were 145 years; and from the departure of the children of Israel until Joshua,” etc. This is clear from the sum of the years collected for this third age and for the three ages together. Although a certain copyist, deceived by this error, added his own figure, leaving this note in the margin: “From Adam until Moses, 2,808 years,” instead of 2,853.] until Joshua, there were 40 years.

From Joshua, therefore, until Othniel, there were 26 years. From Othniel until Ehud, 40 years. From Ehud until Deborah, 80 years. From Deborah until Gideon, 40 years. From Gideon until Abimelech, 40 years. From Abimelech until Tola, 3 years. From Tola until Jair, 23 years. From Jair until Jephthah, 22 years. From Jephthah until Abessan, 6 years [Col. 0872D]. From Abessa until Ajalon, 7 years. From Ajalon until Abdon, 10 years. From Abdon until Samson, 8 years. From Samson until Eli, 20 years. From Eli until Samuel, 40 years. From Samuel until Saul, 12 years. From Saul until David, 20 years.

Here the total of the third age is completed: 942 years [Col. 0873A]. Together, the years of the three ages amount to 2,890.

## THE FOURTH AGE

From David until Solomon, 40 years. From Solomon until Rehoboam, 40 years are counted. From Rehoboam until Abijah, 17 years. From Abijah until Asa, 3 years. From Asa until Jehoshaphat, 41 years. From Jehoshaphat until Joram, 25 years. From Joram until Azariah, 8 years. From Azariah until Athaliah, 1 year. From Athaliah until Joash, 6 years. From Joash until Amaziah, 40 years. From Amaziah until Uzziah, 29 years. From Uzziah until Jotham, 52 years. From Jotham until Ahaz, 16 years. From Ahaz until Hezekiah, 16 years. From Hezekiah until Manasseh, 29 years. From Manasseh until Amon, 55 years. From Amon until Josiah, 2 years. From Josiah [Col. 0873B] until Jehoiakim, 31 years. From Jehoiakim until Zedekiah, 11 years. From Zedekiah until Nebuchadnezzar, 11 years.

Here the total of the fourth age ends, comprising 463 years. The years of the four ages together amount to 3,363.

## THE FIFTH AGE

The years of the fifth age up to Cyrus are 30. From Cyrus until Cambyses, 30 years. From Cambyses until Darius, 9 years. From Darius until Xerxes, 36 years. From Xerxes until Artaxerxes, 21 years. From Artaxerxes until Darius, 40 years. From Darius until another Artaxerxes, 19 years. From Artaxerxes until another Artaxerxes, 40 years. From Artaxerxes until Arsaces, 26 years. From Arsaces until Darius, 4 years. From Darius until Alexander, 6 years. From Alexander until Ptolemy, 5 years. From Ptolemy until Philadelphus, 40 years [Col. 0873C]. From Philadelphus until Euergetes, 38 years. From Euergetes until Philopator, 26 years. From Philopator until Epiphanes, 17 years. From Epiphanes until Philometor, 24 years. From Philometor until another Euergetes, 35 years. From Euergetes until Soter, 29 years. From Soter until Alexander, 17 years. From Alexander until Ptolemy, 10 years. From Ptolemy until Dionysius, 8 years. From Dionysius until Cleopatra, 30 years. From Cleopatra until Julius Caesar, 2 years. From Julius until Octavian Augustus, 5 years. From Octavian Augustus until Christ, 42 years.

Here the fifth age ends, comprising 580 years [Read 589]. Together, the years of the five ages amount to 3,952.

## THE SIXTH AGE
From the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ to [Col. 0873D] Tiberius, twenty-four years are reckoned. [Note: “XIV” should be read, as can be gathered from Bede, from whom almost this entire chronology seems to have been taken.] From Tiberius to Christ’s Passion there are fifteen years [Read “eighteen,” from Bede]. From Christ’s Passion to Gaius there are five years. From Gaius to Claudius, four years. From Claudius to Nero, fourteen years. From Nero to Vespasian, fourteen years. From Vespasian to Titus, nine years. From Titus to Domitian, two years. From Domitian to Nerva, sixteen years. From Nerva to Trajan, one year. From Trajan to Hadrian, fourteen years [for nineteen]. From Hadrian to Antoninus, twenty-one years. From Antoninus to the other Antoninus, twenty-three years. From Antoninus to Commodus, nineteen years. From Commodus to Helvius Pertinax, thirteen years. From Helvius to Severus, one year. From Severus to Antoninus Caracalla, eighteen years. From Antoninus Caracalla to Macrinus, seven years. From Macrinus to Aurelius, one year. From Aurelius to Alexander, four years. From Alexander to Maximinus, thirteen years. From Maximinus to Gordian, three years. From Gordian to Philip, six years. From Philip to Decius, seven years. From Decius to Gallus and Volusianus, one year. From Gallus to Valerian, two years. From Valerian to Claudius, fifteen years. From Claudius to Aurelian, two years. From Aurelian to Tacitus, five years. From Tacitus to Probus, two years. From Probus to Carus, five years. From Carus to Diocletian, two years. From Diocletian to Constantine, twenty years. From Constantine to Constantius, thirty years. From Constantius to Julian, twenty-four years. From Julian to Jovian, two years. From Jovian to Valentinian, one year. From Valentinian to Valens, eleven years. From Valens to Theodosius, four years. From Theodosius to Arcadius, seventeen years. From Arcadius to Honorius, thirteen years. From Honorius to Theodosius, fifteen years. From Theodosius to Marcian, twenty-six years. From Marcian to Leo, six years. From Leo to the other Leo, twenty-seven years. Again, from Leo to Zeno, one year. From Zeno to Anastasius, sixteen years. From Anastasius to Justin, seventeen years. From Justin to Justinian, nine years. Again, from Justinian to Justin, thirty-nine years. Again, from Justin to Tiberius, thirteen years. From Tiberius to Maurice, four years. From Maurice to Phocas, twenty years. From Phocas to Heraclius, eight years. From Heraclius to [Note: “These words, destroyed by age, could not be read at all.] [lacuna] twenty-seven years. From Constantine to Justinian, seventeen years. From Justinian to the elder Pippin, two years. From the elder Pippin to Charles, twenty-seven years. From Charles to Pippin and Carloman, twenty-seven years. From Pippin and Carloman until Pippin was established as king, ten years. From Pippin to Charles and Carloman, seventeen years. From Charles and Carloman to Charles, four years. From that time Lord Charles alone assumed the kingdom and, under God’s protection, happily governs it to the present year, which is the forty-second year of his reign and the ninth of his empire. The total number of years from the beginning of the world to the present year is 5,761. [Note: This is the year of Christ 809. The remaining material appears to have been added.] From the Emperor Louis to Lothar, twenty-seven years. From the Emperor Lothar to Lothar his son, eighteen years.

## NOTICE CONCERNING THE COLLECTION OF VARIANT READINGS THAT FOLLOWS

[Col. 0875]

The following variant readings were gathered into a single body by the distinguished Blanchinus, a man of the highest standing in archaeological matters. Since we greatly desired that this new recension of the Divine Library should be enriched as much as possible, we did not hesitate to append here a document whose usefulness is clear from its title:

*The Divine Library, or Variant Readings of the Old Testament, translated according to the Hebrew truth, and of the New Testament, restored to the Greek faith, by Saint Eusebius Hieronymus, presbyter of Stridon, now issued for the first time from the most ancient manuscript codex of the Church of Toledo, written in Gothic letters, and most diligently prepared for comparison with the edition of the Sacred Bibles by Father John Hentenius of Nechlin, printed at Lyon in the year of the Lord 1569 by Guillaume Roville, under the Venetian Shield, and collated with that same edition in complete fidelity by the most learned master Christophorus Palomares. The autograph copy of this collation is preserved in the Vatican Library, no. 50.*

Having briefly set out the nature of the document, the judicious Collector places before us the preface that Christophorus himself prefixed to his copy, rightly judging that no clearer notice was needed. The celebrated preface is as follows:

> Behold, candid reader, from the library of the Church of Toledo, a very ancient manuscript copy of the Vulgate edition, written in Gothic letters. Although these letters have flowed from Latin elements, they have nevertheless degenerated so far from Latin elegance that, at first sight, they seem to resemble Hebrew or some foreign characters more than Latin ones, and are therefore extremely difficult to read. This difficulty is increased by the great similarity of certain letters to one another, by abbreviations of words, the joining of words, the rare division of sentences, and the almost complete absence of any system of orthography or punctuation. As a result, the reader is often forced to hesitate and doubt the true reading.
>
> I overcame all this difficulty through constant reading and diligent care. With complete fidelity I transcribed the readings of this copy into the margin of the present printed edition, then compared them with the manuscript again and corrected them, lest any false readings should have crept in. Some readings that differed too greatly from the printed text, or that might have seemed corrupt, I reviewed a second and third time, so that I might present to you that Gothic codex whole and sound.
>
> I also copied out many readings corrupted by a barbarous scribe entirely ignorant of the Latin language, just as I found them written; for from them it can often easily be conjectured what the pure and genuine reading once was. I made no judgment, however, on this matter, because when I undertook this task at the command of my illustrious lord, Gaspar de Quiroga, cardinal and archbishop of Toledo, he imposed on me only the duty of recording the Gothic readings that differ from the printed text. He left their examination and interpretation to the congregation established by our lord Sixtus V to revise and adorn the Vulgate edition, presided over by the most learned man, equally keen in intellect and mature in judgment, the illustrious Lord Cardinal Carafa.
>
> Indeed, however unfortunate and barbarous a recorder this codex may have found, by its antiquity it has preserved many readings of the greatest importance, readings that will be highly useful to those entrusted with the revision of the Sacred Scriptures, and that had perished through the injury of time in other codices.
>
> It cannot be known with certainty in what period it was written. This alone is certain: six hundred years ago a certain John, bishop of Córdoba, corrected this codex against other copies as an ancient manuscript, and, considering it a precious gift, gave it to the Church of Seville, as the same John wrote at the end of this copy in large Gothic characters, in these words:
>
> “In the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. The author and possessor of this book, in which the whole of the Old and New Testament is contained, was Servandus, of blessed memory. Since he was born and educated in the blessed see of Seville, he later deserved to hold the chair of the see of Bastigi. From that illustrious man this codex was granted to John, his intimate companion. John, after being nurtured in this distinguished see of Seville and educated by his uncle, Stephen, of blessed memory, the very wise and eloquent bishop of Seville, and after being ordained to the priesthood, was sent as bishop to the see of Carthage. From there he was transferred again and elected bishop of great and royal Córdoba. From that see, sound in body and mind, he resolved to offer this beautifully completed codex to the Lord God, in the aforesaid see of Seville, in memory of the ever-holy Virgin Mary, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January, in the year 1026 of the era, with this condition: that no cleric should dare [lacuna] or alter this codex from [lacuna] and from the aforesaid see. And if anyone should do so, which God forbid, let him be condemned by God, his angels, and all the saints.” Thus far he.
>
> We know that John corrected this codex from other copies, because he says that he is sending this book beautifully completed. Accordingly, from Genesis to the Apocalypse, some words are seen erased, some changed, and many others added in more recent Gothic letters between the lines or in the margin. The words thus changed or added are not of the sort that could be suspected of being glosses written in by some scholar—for there are no such glosses—but the passages themselves show that they are corrections made from other books. Wherever this occurs, I have indicated it with the words “is added” or “are added,” or have explained it at greater length.
>
> If I found anything written in the margin that was not a more recent correction, but that, from the color of the ink and the form of the characters, I recognized as something the same scribe had omitted through carelessness and then supplied, I neither noted nor changed it. I left it untouched as a certain and genuine reading.
>
> To accommodate brevity and the narrowness of the margin, I used certain signs, whose meaning is as follows. Whatever the Gothic codex lacks but the printed copy contains redundantly, I cut through with a line. If only one letter had to be removed, I pierced it with a transverse stroke `/`. If what is removed by these lines—which happens frequently—has been supplied by the aforesaid John in the margin or between the lines from other copies, I indicated this by placing a cross `+` over the first word and in the margin, with the words “is added” or “are added.”
>
> What the printed copy lacks but must be inserted into it from the manuscript, I indicated by this tailed pyramidal quadrilateral `*`, so that the reading marked with this sign in the margin may be inserted at the place where the same sign is fixed in the text and joined to the printed reading.
>
> I marked variant readings with an asterisk `+`, drawing a line beneath the printed words, so that in place of the words marked by the asterisk and line, those readings should be read which are likewise marked by an asterisk in the margin.
>
> When words alone must be transposed, so that those occupying the later position are read first, I drew a line beneath the later words, with two fragments of lines—`"`—fixed above the earlier word, and the same fragments placed between the words where the later words are to be read first.
>
> Finally, so that many small details might not escape notice, I prefixed this sign, `§`, to the printed lines. It indicates nothing other than that something in that line has either been removed or altered.
>
> In this manner the entire codex [Note: So that the reader might have a clear understanding of the signs used by Master Palomares in his copy annotated by hand, Blanchinus, a devoted friend of readers, explains them by the following examples. The practice of the notes or signs by which the Gothic codex is represented in this printed edition is as follows.]
>
> In Genesis, chapter 1, verse 24, the printed copy has *terrae secundum species* (“of the earth according to kinds”); the margin has *juxta species* (“according to kinds”), and both are underlined. This indicates that the Gothic codex differs from the printed copy at this place and reads *terrae juxta species*.
>
> In verse 26 the printed copy has *universae terrae* (“of the whole earth”); the *-que* is cut through by a stroke. This means that the *-que* is not present in the Gothic codex, which reads *universae terrae*.
>
> In verse 27 the printed copy has *et creavit Deus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem* (“and God created man in his image and likeness”); *imaginem* is also cut through by a line, and the margin says “are added.” This means that the words *ad imaginem* are not in the Gothic text, but were added later in Gothic letters by John, bishop of Córdoba, mentioned above in our preface. Thus the Gothic codex reads: *et creavit Deus hominem ad similitudinem* (“and God created man unto likeness”), and so forth.
>
> In Genesis, chapter 2, verse 19, the printed copy has *omne enim quod vocavit Adam* (“for every [creature] that Adam called”); the margin has *nomen* (“name”), marked with the tailed pyramidal quadrilateral. This means that the Gothic codex reads *omne enim nomen quod vocavit Adam* (“for every name that Adam called”).
>
> In Genesis, chapter 7, verse 2, the printed copy has *tolles septena et septena* (“you shall take seven and seven”); the second *et* is struck through by a transverse stroke. The stroke means that this *et* is not present in the Gothic codex, which reads *tolles septena septena* (“you shall take seven seven”). Transverse strokes or lines cutting through a letter or letters, words, or lines always signify that what is so pierced is absent from the Gothic codex.
>
> In Genesis, chapter 7, verse 17, the printed copy has *quadraginta diebus super terram* (“forty days upon the earth”), with the tailed quadrilateral placed before *super terram*. The margin has *et quadraginta noctibus* (“and forty nights”), with the same sign. My annotation says: “These words are written between the lines in more recent letters.” This means that the Gothic text agrees with the printed reading, while the words *quadraginta noctibus* were added between the lines or in the margin by the aforesaid John, so that the text reads: *quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus super terram* (“forty days and forty nights upon the earth”).
>
> In 1 Chronicles, chapter 9, verse 41, the printed copy has *Porro filii Micha, Phithon* (“Moreover, the sons of Micah: Phithon”), with *Phithon* preceded by the quadrilateral. The margin says “*filii* is added.” This means that the Gothic codex agrees with the printed copy, but that *filii* (“son”) was added in the margin by that John or someone else, so that the text reads: *Porro filii Micha, filii Phithon* (“Moreover, the sons of Micah: the sons of Phithon”).
>
> Similarly, in Romans 14, the printed copy has *scio et confido* (“I know and am confident”), with *et confido* likewise marked by the quadrilateral. The margin says “*enim* is added.” This means that the Gothic text agrees with the printed reading, but that *enim* (“for”) is added in the margin, so that the text reads: *scio enim et confido* (“for I know and am confident”).
>
> In 2 Corinthians, chapter 5, verse 12, the printed copy has *non iterum commendamus nos vobis* (“we do not again commend ourselves to you”). The fragments of lines indicate that these words are transposed in the Gothic codex, and that it should therefore be read: *non iterum nos commendamus vobis* (“we do not again commend ourselves to you”).
>
> This sign is an index indicating that something has been altered in the line to which it is prefixed. It should be observed that all the readings between the lines or in the margin of the Gothic codex are written in Gothic letters. Nevertheless, I often call them “more recent” in my annotations—not because they are not extremely ancient, but because they were not written by the scribe who wrote the entire codex, but by the aforesaid John or by someone else.]

I have therefore transcribed the entire codex with the greatest and most genuine fidelity demanded by so important a matter, except for the books of Baruch and the Psalms. For, as the titles of the Third and Fourth Books of Kings prefixed in this copy state, since this edition is from the translation of Saint Jerome, who admits in his preface to Jeremiah that he omitted Baruch, it is absent from this Bible. For the same reason, the Psalms in this copy do not agree with the version of the printed books, but derive from Saint Jerome’s translation circulated among his works; consequently, it was not worthwhile to record variant readings from the Psalms.

Receive, therefore, most kindly disposed reader, in the spirit in which it is offered to you, this ancient copy of the Vulgate edition. If, from this immense labor of ours, you restore even one word to its original purity, I shall be most grateful that I devoted so much care and effort to this work.

Toledo, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November, in the year 1588.

After he had completed this preface, and when the work was scarcely about to be committed to the press, the editor Palomares thought it appropriate to preface it anew for the reader as follows:

> I had already put the finishing hand to the work when I came upon two passages of Saint Jerome, from his letters to Lucinius of Baetica and to Theodora, his wife. From them it is clear that, while Saint Jerome was still alive, his works—which he had dictated up to that time, for he was already advanced in age—had reached Baetica in Spain, where this copy appears to have been written, as may be conjectured from the words quoted above of John of Seville, bishop of Córdoba. Since Seville and Córdoba are situated in Baetica, and since this edition is said in the same copy, as I noted in the preface, to be according to the translation of Saint Jerome, it is reasonable to believe that this codex was transcribed from the books of the aforesaid Lucinius, or from copies made from them and circulating in Baetica. I therefore thought I would oblige my reader by inserting here the words of Saint Jerome.
>
> “My little works,” he says in Letter 28, to Lucinius of Baetica, “which you say you desire, not because they deserve it but because of your kindness, I have given to your people to copy; and I frequently instructed them to compare and correct them carefully.”
>
> And later, near the end of the letter:
>
> “I have sent you and your sister the tokens of my poverty and the daily symbols of repentance: four little hair-shirts suited to your purpose and needs, and a book, namely the Visions of Isaiah, which I recently expounded in a historical interpretation.”
>
> In Letter 29, to Theodora, the wife of Lucinius of Baetica, praising Lucinius, he continues:
>
> “He scattered all his property and gave it to the poor, so that his righteousness might endure forever. Nor content with generosity toward his own country, he sent to the Churches of Jerusalem and Alexandria as much gold as could relieve the poverty of many. While many people admire and praise this, I shall praise in him above all his zeal and devotion to the Scriptures, by which he desired our little works so earnestly that, having sent six scribes—because in this province there is a scarcity of Latin speech and of scribes—he had everything we had dictated from our youth up to the present transcribed for him.”

  “I speak to you, and you shall keep my covenant; you shall be for me a people surpassing every nation; for the whole earth is mine, but you shall be for me a preserved kingdom and a holy nation. ## The Book of Leviticus

In Hebrew, *Vaicra*, that is, “And he called.”

### Chapter I

- v. 2: “You shall say” → “Say.”
- Ibid.: “sheep” → “from sheep.”
- v. 7: “pile up” → “prepare.”
- v. 10: “or from goats as a burnt offering; a year-old lamb and without, etc.” → “or from goats as a burnt offering; a year-old male without, etc.” The word *male* is added.
- v. 11: “the north” → “toward the north.”
- v. 14: “of birds for a burnt offering, etc.” → “a burnt offering of birds, etc.”
- v. 15: “he shall offer” → “let him offer.”
- Ibid.: “he shall do” → “you shall do.”
- v. 16: “near” → “because of.”
- v. 17: “having placed beneath” → “having arranged.”

### Chapter II

- v. 2: “he shall place” → “they shall place.”
- v. 4: “sprinkled” → “sprinkled portions.”
- v. 5: “sprinkled” → “sprinkled.”
- v. 6: “you shall divide it” → “you shall divide them.”
- Ibid.: “oil upon it” → “upon the oil.”
- v. 7: “fine flour” → “of fine flour.”

- v. 12: “shall be placed” → “shall be placed.”

If anyone offers a sacrifice by vow or willingly, it shall likewise be eaten on the same day; but if anything, etc.” These words are added in the margin, with three or four words erased from the text. # THE BOOK OF JOSHUA

[Column 0913]

[Column 0913C]

The Argument to the Book of Joshua, which begins “Jesus son of Nave,” etc., is not found in the Gothic codex.

Jerome’s Preface to Joshua, which begins “At last,” etc., is found in the codex.

The chapter-headings of the Second Book begin, according to some; for according to this edition of St Jerome, translated from the Hebrew, First and Second Samuel are reckoned as one book in the Canon.

# The Second Book of Samuel

Which we call the Second Book of Kings.

Thus it is found in the Gothic manuscript, in large letters, as also at the beginning of this book and the next:

> The book which according to the Septuagint is regarded as the Second is here concluded; but in this edition of Saint Jerome, which is from the Hebrew, the First and Second Books of Samuel are counted as one book in the canon.

# BOOK THREE OF KINGS

“The Third Book of Kings, according to the Hebrews the First of *Malachim*.” (Thus it is printed.) “Here begins the Third Book of Kings according to the Septuagint, but according to Saint Jerome the Second.” (Thus it is found in the Gothic manuscript, in large letters.)

*The Fourth Book of Kings according to the Septuagint ends here, namely, Malachin; according to this edition of blessed Jerome, it is the Second, because in the Hebrew canon the First and Second are one book. Likewise, the Third and Fourth are the same book.*

*(Here it appears in the Gothic exemplar in large letters. The prophet Isaiah follows in the same Gothic exemplar.)*
